বড়  ছিল যে আমার মনে  হয়, ১৫ থেকে ২০  টি জানলার সিট  অনায়াসেই কভার  করে নিয়েছে।  আমার সবচেয়ে  বেশি  উত্তেজনাপূর্ণ  লেগেছে এদের ইন- ফ্লাইট  এন্টারটেইনমেন্ট  স্ক্রিন।  এখানে প্রতিটি  সিটে তারা একটি  হেডফোন, কম্বল  এবং বালিশ  দিয়েছে। এই  এয়ারক্রাফটের  তিনটি জায়গায়  ক্যামেরা আছে।  একটি  এয়ারক্রাফটের  নিচে, একটি  সামনে এবং একটি  উপরে। এতে  আপনারা এই  তিনটি  ক্যামেরাই  অ্যাক্সেস  করতে পারতেন।  তো এটা আমার  কাছে সবচেয়ে  অবাক করা বিষয়  ছিল। আমরা  এন্টারটেইনমেন্ট  পরে দেখেছি,  কিন্তু  প্রথমেই আমরা  সব ক্যামেরা  চেক করছিলাম যে  কেমন দেখাচ্ছে । ক্যামেরার  ফুটেজ চেক করার  পর ভাবলাম, কেন  না এখন একটু  এন্টারটেইনমেন্ট  ট্রাই করা যাক।  আপনারা দেখতেই  পাচ্ছেন, এখানে  অনেক অপশন আছে— মুভি, টিভি,  পডকাস্ট, গান,  দুবাইয়ের  পর্যটন  কেন্দ্র এবং  আরও অনেক কিছু।  এখানে আপনারা  সব ধরণের  সিনেমার দেখা  পাবেন।  অ্যাকশন, হরর,  কমেডি,  রোমান্টিক এবং  আরও অনেক কিছু।  বাই দ্য ওয়ে,  আপনারা এখানে  ভারতের  আঞ্চলিক  সিনেমাও দেখতে  পারবেন। এর  পাশাপাশি  আপনারা  ফ্লাইটের সব  ডিটেইলস যেমন— আগমনের সময়,  গন্তব্য, গতি,  বাইরের  তাপমাত্রা—সহ  অনেক কিছু  এখানে  এক্সপ্লোর  করতে পারবেন।  ভাবলাম একটু  মজা করা যাক, আর  মজা করতে গিয়ে  মাথায় চোট  খেলাম। আমার  নিজের পরা  হেডফোনই আমার  মাথায় লাগল।  এমিরেটস সাথে  থাকলে, লাগেজের  চিন্তা ছাড়ুন।  আমরা একটি  এসএমএস পেলাম  যে আমাদের  ব্যাগগুলো  এয়ারক্রাফটে  লোড হয়ে গেছে।  এরা  এয়ারক্রাফটের  ভেতরে এক  অন্যরকম  পরিবেশ তৈরি  করেছিল। মানে  লাইটিংটা  একবার দেখুন।  খুবই উষ্ণ আবহ  ছিল। মনে  হচ্ছিল এই সফর  যেন শেষই না হয়।  ধন্যবাদ।  অবশেষে টেক  অফের সময় হয়ে  গিয়েছিল। আর  আমাদের সাথে  আরও অনেকেই  ক্যামেরা অন  করে দেখার  চেষ্টা করছিল  যে টেক অফের সময়  স্ক্রিনে কেমন  লাগে। অনেক  কিছু ঘুরে  দেখার পর এবার  পেট পূজোর সময়  হয়ে গিয়েছিল।  তো এখানে  আপনারা দেখতে  পাচ্ছেন যে  মেনু কার্ডটি  তিনটি ভাষায়  রয়েছে।  প্রথমটি  ইংরেজি,  দ্বিতীয়টি  হিন্দি এবং  তৃতীয়টি আরবি।  খাবার না আসা  পর্যন্ত  ভাবলাম কেন  একটি মারাঠি  সিনেমা দেখে  নেওয়া যাক।  আমরা নিরামিষ  খাবারই অর্ডার  করেছিলাম আর  নিরামিষে  পেয়েছিলাম  আচার, ফোরসান,  মাখন এবং মাউথ  ফ্রেশনার। এর  সাথেই ছিল  স্যালাড,  মিষ্টি, পনিরের  তরকারি, ভাত,  পাউরুটি, ফ্রুট  জুস এবং পানির  বোতল। রোস্টেড  কাজু বাদামের  সাথে ওরা  কাটলারি এবং  রিফ্রেশিং  টাওয়েলেটও  দিয়েছিল।  খাওয়া-দাওয়ার  পর, আমরা বাকি  মারাঠি  সিনেমাটি  দেখলাম। আর  এবার,  ল্যান্ডিংয়ের  সময় হয়ে  গিয়েছিল। আর  ল্যান্ডিংয়ের  সময়ও আমরা  ক্যামেরা অন  করেছিলাম এবং  সেই মুহূর্তটি  ক্যাপচার করার  চেষ্টা  করেছিলাম যার  জন্য আমরা অধীর  আগ্রহে  অপেক্ষা  করছিলাম। ও মাই  গড, এটা দারুণ  ছিল! বিশ্বাস  করুন বন্ধুরা,  এই অভিজ্ঞতাটা  আমি আপনাদের  বলে বোঝাতে  পারবো না। এটা  সত্যিই  স্বপ্নিল ছিল!  এই মিউজিকের  সাথে সাথে  আমাদের হৃদয়েও  যেন নাশিক ঢোল  বেজে উঠেছিল,  কারণ এখন আমরা  মুম্বাই পৌঁছে  গিয়েছিলাম।  ধন্যবাদ  এমিরেটস।  আমাদের  নিরাপদে  ল্যান্ড  করানোর জন্য  অনেক ধন্যবাদ।  আমরা সত্যিই  আপনাদের রাইড  উপভোগ করেছি।  মাত্র ৩ ঘণ্টার  সফর ছিল। ঘরে  ফেরার অনুভূতি  ভাষায় প্রকাশ  করা সম্ভব নয়।  নেভার এন্ডিং  কার্পেটের ওপর  দিয়ে হাঁটার  সময় এই  দৃশ্যগুলো  দেখার সুযোগ  হলো। এখানে  কিছু ইউনিক  জিনিস  ডিসপ্লেতে  রাখা ছিল যা খুব  সুন্দর। আর  ওখানে আপনারা  দেখতে পাচ্ছেন  আমার একটা  অ্যান্টিক  পিসও দাঁড়িয়ে  আছে। তো  এইভাবেই আমরা  মুম্বাই  পৌঁছালাম আর এই  জিনিসগুলো  দেখার জন্যই  আমরা ওপরে  এসেছিলাম।  আমাদের এই  ট্রিপ এখানেই  শেষ আর এখন বাড়ি  ফেরার সময়  বন্ধুরা।  ভিডিওটি দেখার  জন্য আপনাদের  অনেক ধন্যবাদ।  যদি এই ভিডিওটি  আপনাদের  ইনফরমেটিভ  লেগে থাকে, যদি  আপনারা নতুন  কিছু দেখে  থাকেন, তবে দয়া  করে লাইক করুন,  শেয়ার করুন,  কমেন্ট করুন,  সাবস্ক্রাইব  করুন এবং আপনার  বন্ধু ও  পরিবারের সাথে  শেয়ার করুন।  ভিডিওটি দেখার  জন্য অনেক অনেক  ধন্যবাদ। বাই  বাই, নিজের  খেয়াল রাখবেন  বন্ধুরা। দেখা  হবে পরের ব্লগে  আর এভাবেই  সাপোর্ট করতে  থাকুন এবং  ভালোবাসা  দেখাতে থাকুন।  অনেক ধন্যবাদ।

reviews.transcript_excerpt: फील्ड मार्शल सैयद आसिम अनीर की ईरानी…
reviews.transcript_full: फील्ड मार्शल सैयद आसिम अनीर की ईरानी सादर मसूदान से मुलाकात ईरान अमेरिका तनाज़ और वस्त में कशीदगी में मज़द इजाफे की रोकथाम अब हुबज़ दोबारा खोलने और तनाज़ के जल्द खात्मे के लिए अकामात पर तबादले ख्याल खबर एजेंसी रर्स के मुताबिक दौरे से काबिल फील्ड मार्शल आसिम अनीर की अमकी सदर डोनाल्ड ट्रंप और आला अमकी हुकाम से भी बातचीत हुई थी फील्ड मार्शल सैयद आसिम अनीर सुप्रीम नेशनल सिक्योरिटी काउंसिल में रहबर आला के नुमाइंद मोहसिन रजाई ईरानी पार्लियामेंट के स्पीकर बाकर खालिबाफ़ ईरानी वज़र खारजा और ईरानी वज़र दाखला सिकंदर मोमिनी से भी मुलाकातें हुई। फील्ड मार्शल के हमरा वज़र दाखला मोहसन नकवी भी मौजूद थे। वज़र खारजा इसाकदार तुर्की के वज़र खारजा हकान फैदान के दरमियान टेलीफ़ोनिक राब्ता दो तरफ ताल्लुकात इलाकाई सुरते हाल पर तबादले खयाल वज़ खारजा ने रीजनल फोर के आइंदा वज़ खारजा इजलास पर भी तबादले खयाल किया कसीर जहदी इजलासों और रवाबत से मुतालिक में दोनों वज़ खारजा में गुफ्तगू हुई बानी बीटीआई की अस्पताल मुंतकिरी के मामले पर रजिस्ट्रार सुप्रीम कोर्ट ऑफिस ने तौहीन अदालत की दरख्वास्त एतराज लगाकर वापस कर दी। जराय के मुताबिक फरीकैन पर तौहीन अदालत के इल्जामात की फहरिस्त फराहम नहीं की गई। अमेरिका का ईरान पर मजीद पाबंदियां आयद करने का ऐलान। अरे वज़रे खजाना स्कॉट बेसेंट की प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस कहा ईरान के डिजिटल असासों टेक्नोलॉजी सोने हवाबाजी और शिपिंग के शोबों पर नई पाबंदियां आयद की गई है। ईरान से तावुन करने वाले मुल्कों को अमकी गिर का सामना होगा। ईरानी वज़र इ्तारी हुर खजाना का अमेरिका की ईरान के खिलाफ नई पाबंदियों पर रद्दे अमल। कहा ईरान के खिलाफ इशारी पाबंदियां कोई नई बात नहीं जंग नहीं चाहते लेकिन इसदी हमले का मुकाबला करेंगे। हुकूमत ने ऐसी पाबंदियों से निपटने के पहले ही मंसूबाबंदी कर रखी है। शहर-शहर गलीगली ईद मिलाद नबी सल्लल्लाहहु अलैहि वही वसल्लम की तैयारियां उरूज पर गली मोहल्ले सड़कें इमारतें जगमगा उठी मिलाद और दूदो सलाम की महफिल का एतमाम मुल्क के बेशतर इलाकों में आज मौसम गर्म रहेगा। महकमा मौसमियात के मुताबिक दोपहर के बाद शुमाली इलाकों में मतला जुबी अब आलूद रहने का इमकान है। दरिया सिंध में कालाबाग पर पानी के दबाव में कमी आ गई। निचले दर्जे के सैलाब में तब तब्दील पानी की आमद कम होकर 331000 क्यूसिक रिकॉर्ड चश्मा बैराज, तौसा, गुड्डू और सख बैराज पर निचले दर्जे के सैलाब। फ्लड फॉरकास्टिंग डिवीजन लाहौर के मुताबिक मुल्क के बाकी दरियाओं में सुरते हाल मामूल पर है। वज़र दाखला मोहसिन नकवी का इस्लामाबाद में डिप्लोमेटिक इंक्लेव का दौरा जारी तरियाती कामों का जायजा लिया मोहसन नकवी के काम के दौरान एक भी तरफ ना काटने की हिदायत कहा डिप्लोमेटिक इंक्लेव को जदीद महफूज़ और खूबसूरत सिफ़ारसी ज़ोन बनाएंगे डिप्लो डिप्लोमेटिक इंक्लेव के रिहाशियों को आलमी मायार की सहूलित फराहम करना हमारी अवलीन तर्जी है। चेयरमैन सीडी ने डिप्लोमेटिक इंक्लेव में जारी तरकियाती कामों में पर ब्रीफिंग दी। डिप्टी कमिश्नर इस्लामाबाद और दीगर असरान भी इस मौके पर मौजूद थे। वज़र आला पंजाब मरियम नवाज का करप्शन के लिए बदनाम पुलिस अफसरों को एसएओ ना लगाने और बच्चों और खवातीन के खिलाफ जलायम में मुलविस अफराद के बारे में जीरो टॉलरेंस पॉलिसी अपनाने का हुकुम। मरियम नवाज ने कहा जिस जिले में जराइम की शरा ज्यादा होगी वहां डीपीओ से बासफरस की जाएगी। बच्चे और खवातीन मेरी रेड लाइन है। उनके खिलाफ जराइयम पर किसी को माफ नहीं किया जाएगा। मरियम नवाज की ज़रे सदादत इजलास में कैदी की वैन में जीपीएस और कैमरे नष्ट करने की मंजूरी। आईजी पंजाब ने ब्रिफिन में बताया कि जरा की मजमई सुरते हाल में वाज़ कमी का रुझान है। डकैती, कत्ल, चोरी और दीगर जराइयम में कमी आई है। पदीन के इलाके कठन में नौजवान की मुबना पुलिस मुकाबले में हलाकत के खिलाफ दरख्वास्त की समात आज सिंध हाई कोर्ट में होगी। वसा ने 26 जुलाई के पुलिस मुकाबले को जारी करार दिया है। पुलिस ने मुकाबले के बाद मुलजिम के बाएं हाथ में पिस्तौल वाली तस्वीर जारी की थी। वसा का मुतालबा है कि नौजवान की कब्र कशाई करके दोबारा पोस्टमार्टम किया जाए। देखा जाए कि मुबईना पुलिस मुकाबले के दौरान मुलजिम को लगी सात गोलियां कितने फासले से चलाई गई है। इस्लामाबाद के सेक्टर ई11 में घर से 13 साल के बच्चे की फंदा लगी लाश मिली। पुलिस के मुताबिक बच्चा घर में मुलाजिम था। पोस्टमार्टम रिपोर्ट के बाद मजीद तफ्तीश की जाएगी। बच्चा दो माह पहले ई1 में एक घर में मुलाजमत के लिए आया था। सरगोदा में बच्चों से मुबयना ज्यादती का वाकया मरकजी मुलजिम और उसकी अहलिया समेत नौ मुलजिमान के खिलाफ दो बच्चों के वालिद की मददयत में मुकदमा दर्ज। पुलिस का कहना है कि मुलजिमान की गिरफ्तारी के लिए छापे मार रहे हैं। माज़ के जुर्म की सजा नए कानून के मुताबिक नहीं दी जा सकती। लाहौर हाईकोर्ट ने बैलून मुल्क नौकरी का झांसा देकर रकम बटोरने वाले मुलजिम की जमानत मंजूर कर ली। अदालत ने रिमार्क्स दिए कि 2025 इमीग्रेशन तमीम मुलजिम के खिलाफ लागू नहीं हो सकती। मुलजिम पर एफआई ने एक साल की ताखर से एफआईआर दर्ज की। मुकदमे में मुबईना रकम की अदायगी। वक्त और जगह का कोई जिक्र नहीं। मुलजिम को मज़द जेल में रखना। ट्रायल से पहले सजा देने के मुतदि होगा। वज़रआला पंजाब मरियम नवाज चीन के चारों सरकारी दौरे पर रवाना चीन के काउंसिल जनरल ने वज़रआला को एयरपोर्ट पर अलविदा किया चीन के सूबे शन जियांग के पार्टी सेक्रेटरी की सरबराही में वफ वज़रला से मुलाकात करेगा वज़रला मरियम नवाज चीन के सरकारी मेहमान की हैसियत से शन जियांग स्टेट गेस्ट हाउस में कयाम करेगी पेट्रोलियम लेवी और महंगाई के खिलाफ लाहौर कराची और पेशावर में जमात इस्लामी के धरने का आज 10वां रोज़। लाहौर में फैसल चौक माल रोड पर धरने से खिताब में अमीर जमात इस्लामी हाफिज नमु रहमान ने कहा 13 रबुउल अव्वल को बाकायदा मुल्क गिर हड़ताल का ऐलान किया जाएगा। हड़ताल के साथ-साथ हमारा धरना भी जारी रहेगा। हमारा मुतालबा है कि पेट्रोलियम नेवी को खत्म किया जाए। यह मुतालबा हमारा नहीं 25 करोड़ आवाम का है। पारा चरार समेत जिले भर की बिजली तीसरे रोज भी मुतल टेस्को हुकाम के मुताबिक पड़ाव के इलाके में 132 केवी ट्रांसमिशन लाइन को टावर गिरने से बिजली मुतल है। तूफानी हवाओं के बायस मेन ट्रांसमिशन लाइन का टावर गिर गया। टावर की तसीबो मरम्मत के लिए सामान पहुंचा दिया गया। अमेरिका ने तकरीबन 47 बरस बाद शाम को दहशतगर्दी स्पोंसर करने वाली रियासतों के फैस से निकाल दिया। अमेरिकी वज़र खारजा मार्को रूबियो का कहना है यह फैसला शामी हुकूमत की जानिब से खुद को बेकवामी दहशतगर्दी की कारवाहियों से मुकम्मल तौर पर अलग करने के लिए किए गए इदामात के एतराफ में किया गया। फैसले से शामी आवाम को खुशहाली की जानिब रास्ता मिलेगा। शामी वज़र खारजा असद हसन अल शेबानी ने इस ऐलान को तारीख कदम करार देते हुए कहा कि शामी हुकूमत शफाफियत बाहमी मफादात और एतराम पर मबनी माहौल के कयाम के लिए काम जारी रखेगी। शाम 1979 से दहशतगर्दी स्पोंसर करने वाले मुालिक की अमकी फहरिस्त में मौजूद था। अब हुरम से कमोडिटी बहरी जहाजों की आमद तीन माह की कम तरीन सतह पर गुस्ता रोज सिर्फ एक कमोडिटी बहरी जहाज नेम उबूर किया जो 7 मई के बाद से सबसे कम तादाद है। इस्तंबोल से तेहरान के लिए ईरान की निजी एयरलाइन की परवाज में हंगामी सूरत हाल, हंगामी सुरते हाल पर तैयारी की तुर्की की जानिब वापसी एनका एयरपोर्ट पर बाहि हिफाजत उतर गया। और हरीपुर में मुबईना ज्यादती के बाद कत्ल की गई। पांच साला बच्ची की नमाज़ जनाजा अदा कर दी गई। पांच साला बच्ची 10 अगस्त को लापता हुई थी। बच्ची की लाश गुस्ता रोज वेयर हाउस के कुएं से मिली थी। पुलिस के मुताबिक तीन गिरफ्तार मुलजिमान ने बच्ची से ज्यादती का एतराफ किया है। गिरफ्तार तीनों मुलजिमान को जुडिशियल रिमांड पर जेल भेज दिया गया।

reviews.transcript_full: Everyone is stoked about the A220 right now. I mean, it's everywhere. But to be honest, I don't get the hype yet. So, let's take a look at the newly released Wait a minute. How much? I can't afford that. But what if I flew on the real thing instead? You know what? Let's do just that. So, today's A220 adventure takes us from London Gatwick to, drumroll, please, London Heathrow via Paris. That's right. Two flights, twice the chance to work out what the hype is all about. We'll take a look at the airplane, the cabin, and I'll even save a couple of geek tips for the end. But before we hop on board this Air France flight, let me tell you where the A220 really came from. So, Synaptic partnered with Inibuilds in Oops, sorry. That Yeah, that That's the virtual A220. Let's talk about the real one. So, the Airbus A220 wasn't even an Airbus to start with. Bombardier developed it as the C Series, a clean sheet 100 to 150 seat jet. But development was plagued by delays, engine problems, and huge costs. And then, Boeing threw another spanner in the works, challenging a major C Series deal with Delta in the United States. >> [music] >> And eventually, Airbus stepped in, taking control of the program in 2018 for a token one Canadian dollar. Nevertheless, the A220 is born. >> [music] >> So, that brings us to today, boarding Bombardier's passion project wearing Airbus colors. And honestly, the first impression is normal. For all the hype surrounding this aircraft, you could walk onto it and think you've just boarded another narrow-body. Until you look at the seating. The aisle sits slightly left of center, giving the A220 a 2-3 layout, which means there are no middle seats on the left. But naturally, I went for a window, 19F, because this is where the A220 starts to make a rather better case for itself. Look at these things. I've flown on plenty of A220s and 737s recently, the difference is immediately obvious. They're the closest thing I've seen to the 787's windows on a narrow-body, about 11 in wide and 16 in tall. And even the blind disappears into its own little recess, leaving the whole window unobstructed. And suddenly, the cabin doesn't feel quite so ordinary. But the A220's character isn't just visual, because this aircraft has sound. The pilots told me single-engine taxiing is pretty common on the A220, which introduces another little bit of A220 personality. The PTU. But sadly, it doesn't sound like the A220's barking dog. And for 15 minutes, you definitely know it's there. But it's not the only sound you'll come across. That unmistakable A220 spool up, a sort of mechanical wail. But of course, it's now time to take off. But now that we're up, let me just take a second to talk about the A220's really interesting engines. This is the Pratt & Whitney PW1500G. And unlike most monoliners, there's actually a gearbox sitting between the fan and the rest of the engine. And that makes the engine considerably more efficient. And while it has had its fair share of supply chain and operational problems, at low power, the airflow can create a vibration, a bit like blowing across an empty bottle. And with sounds like this, I'm kind of starting to get the hype behind the Airbus A220. But let's return to the real world for a moment. The Air France experience? Nothing overly special. Air vents and reading lights that the aisle seat on the right-hand side can't reach, so keep that in mind when choosing where to sit. USB outlets, a phone stand, reasonable legroom, and decent seat width. Even free Wi-Fi for Flying Blue members. Honestly, there's nothing to complain about whatsoever. And on this 40-minute flight, you might assume that that's where the service ends. But do you get catering? Yes, actually. A little packet of these herby bread bits, kind of like croutons, I guess. As well as the standard assortment of drinks, from coffees and teas to soft drinks, and even some little alcoholic beverages. Not exactly Michelin star dining, but for a 40-minute flight, honestly, pretty decent. And with that, it was finally time to land in the Paris's Charles de Gaulle. >> [music] >> And after a few days in Paris, it was time for round two. >> [music] >> Boarding in this time from a jet way was a nice upgrade, but more importantly, we were sitting further forward, just behind the emergency exits in row 15. And without repeating everything from the first flight, there was one thing that was really different, the sound. Only four rows ahead of where I'd been sat before, and the cabin was a whole lot quieter. It just goes to show how dramatically the A220's soundscape changes depending on where you're sitting. And after a lovely sunset departure from Charles de Gaulle, the skies over London Heathrow decided to put on an even better show. But enough being a passenger, let's look at what it's actually like to fly the thing. After each flight, I made my way to the flight deck to ask the crew about the A220. And while I didn't record them, they all gave me a pretty similar impression. It's recognizably an Airbus, but it's definitely [music] not your conventional Airbus. The heads-up displays, the controls, all the little quirks, there's a lot that's different. And seeing that weird little glowing cockpit in person was one of the highlights of the whole experience. So, if you're flying on an A220 yourself, here's what I recommend. Want to hear it? Sit around the rear of the wing. You'll get the whale, the engine noise, and potentially plenty of PTU. Want a quieter ride? Sit further forward, around the rows behind the emergency exits. And if you want to see the flight deck, just ask. The crew is normally more than happy to help. So now for the most important question of all. After having flown on the Airbus A220 twice, do I now get the hype? Yes. I do. Not the oh my god Synaptic release the A220 hype, but the overall real A220 hype. It's not overly revolutionary, but it's got character. The engines sound amazing, the windows are brilliant, and there's something genuinely clever underneath it all. A bit of Bombardier-Airbus Frankenstein. So don't forget to subscribe and help me afford the Synaptic A220, but for now, this is Flight Deck Focus. That was the A220, and I'll see you in the next one. >> [music]

reviews.transcript_full:
It's Turkish 787 Business Class today and I'm 
going for a 14-hour ultra long-haul which is   a serious test for any airline. I have reviewed 
Turkish twice on my channel and both times I was   impressed. So one may call me biased already, 
but if I like it - I will say so. But both of   those flights were not fully representative. A 
rare ex-Aeroflot A350 with suite cabin and an   older A330 business on European short-haul. Both 
were very good. But now I want to try the mainstay   of Turkish Business, the main new generation 
cabin used on both 787s and A350s. And now I'm a   bit scared. Can Turkish keep up impressing me? Or 
today I will have one of those "no one is perfect   moments"? But if I am to make my mind about 
Turkish, I have to try their core product. So,   let's explore together and let me know in comments 
if you agree with my verdict. My today's flight is   Istanbul to Mexico City. More than 11,000 km, 
14-hour journey on Boeing 787-9. I'm flying   from Istanbul airport again. But if my previous 
video, I was a shy guest flying to Shanghai with   China Eastern, now I feel like I'm at home as 
I fly Turkish Airlines, whose name is all over   the airport. Turkish doesn't wait for too long to 
show what it stands for here. You can see their   impressive business check-in zone from far away. 
It sends the right vibe immediately. Spacious,   stylish, no qeues and feels like an appetizer for 
the coming Turkish Lounge. Goes without saying   that check-in is smooth and takes less than 
a minute from "how are you" to "here is your   boarding pass" to "of course, I know where 
the lounge is". It's a late night flight,   which is common for Turkish long-haul. Despite 
the late hour, the airport is very active,   not like many European airports where most shops 
and cafes are shut down by 10 p.m. I'm walking   through Istanbul Shopping Mall, sorry, Istanbul 
Airport, and it's full of life. It got it all from   luxury fashion boutiques like that Louis Vuitton 
on steroids store to Turkish bazaar with all the   sweets and handicrafts and to massive "must have" 
multi-purpose duty-free stores. There are two very   similar Turkish Lounges here. But there is 
a catch. It's much better to take Business   Lounge rather than Miles and Smiles lounge as 
the later is much busier with all the status   flyers of Turkish and Star Alliance. Turkish 
Business Lounge is much more than a lounge. It's   an institution on its own from the older days of 
Istanbul Ataturk airport. There is hardly anything   else you can expect from the lounge. It got tons 
of comfortable seating, different zones - food,   work, relax, socialize, hotel-quality showers, and 
of course, food. Food and Turkish Airlines have   become synonyms in the last two decades, and the 
lounge shows it loud and clear. There are multiple   cooking stations where you can get hot meals and 
an amazing salad and meze bar. But I sense a smell   that draws me past them and towards the baking 
section where are two chefs are preparing pides,   a distant Turkish relative of pizza. I keep 
reminding myself "just a little" as I still have a   meal on board and go to my next favorite hot spot 
in the lounge, beverage station. Flying Turkish   and not having Turkish tea would be a heresy. So 
I pick a tulip-shaped glass and follow the ritual.   First very strong tea and then add water to your 
taste. And even if I managed to escape pide,   now I'm finally trapped by baklava. Well, it would 
be an offense to Turkish traditions if I didn't   try one. Who am I to disrespect this lounge? You 
can spend hours in this lounge. I have more about   it in my other Turkish videos, but for now I'm 
taking off to the gate. And getting there is quite   a walk, which actually might not be the worst 
idea before the 14-hour flight. Finally there and   time for the first confusion of this trip. Flight 
number is correct, but this gate boards a flight   to Cancun. That was a moment of scare, but then 
I realized that this flight does both. Goes first   to Mexico City and then continues to Cancun. This 
is what Turkish is practicing quite often. Mystery   solved. Otherwise, everything is by the book. 
Business has a separate lane and boarding priority   is very well observed. But then there is the 
usual hiccup in the airbridge. The plane is not   ready and we have to wait another 10 minutes. That 
happens all the time. And I keep wondering that at   the time when we learned how to send the signal 
into deep space, airlines still did not manage   to connect agents at the departure desks with the 
plane. Finally, aboard. Turkish 787s have 30 seats   in business with 1-2-1 configuration and direct 
aisle access for all seats. Interestingly, Turkish   is using forward-facing staggered rather than the 
more common reverse herringbone configuration. I'm   equally comfortable with both, but I know that 
some definitely prefer forward-facing seats.   Seats come with a heavy shell that gives a very 
cocoon-like feeling and a good level of privacy,   even if not the same as with suits with the 
doors. This is Stellia Symphony seat, which   is quite a rare product. The only other airline 
that I know of to use it is Singapore Airlines,   but they mostly use it for regional operations. 
Here I got 14-hour flight. Hm... interesting if   this seat got what it takes. The first experience 
is positive though. Everything looks and feels new   and very well put together using premium finishes 
and materials. This is clearly not of the rack   basic model. The seat was customized for Turkish 
Airlines and actually got an internal name,   Aurora. What I didn't realize when booking is 
that while all the seats are forward- facing,   some of the seats on the sides are closer to the 
aisle and some to the window. I got the former   which feels a bit more exposed. While those closer 
to the window have the console in between yourself   and the aisle that gives a feeling of more 
privacy. Well, next time. While everything is   definitely well designed, the seat does feel a bit 
tight space-wise. It makes me feel like in those   8 square meter rooms in Japanese hotels. You got 
everything, but you don't walk in that room. You   squeeze through. Though I might be just spoiled by 
Cathay Aria Suite. All in all, it looks good. But   the real conclusion should come in 14 hours, not 
now. There is still a lot to explore, but first   things first, let's fix my dinner plans, hopefully 
grab some views of night Istanbul during takeoff   and enjoy the signature meal of Turkish. At least 
those are my expectations. Turkish menu comes as   a fancy booklet immediately setting the mood and 
it's a hint that Turkish is paying attention to   small details that create experiences. Turkish 
definitely goes local on food. They use a lot   of local ingredients and proudly showcase 
them. I might never tell the difference,   but knowing that cheese comes from Canakkale 
or tea from Rize strangely makes me excited,   even if I have no idea where those places are. 
We will have a choice of three starters. Meze,   traditional Turkish appetizers, smoked salmon, 
carpaccio and prawns or a soup. Same three choices   for Main. Beef cutlets, sea bass and ricotta 
mezzelune, a kind of relative of ravioli. And   this would be followed by a cart with desserts, 
ice cream, and fruits. Sounds pretty good. And   I instantly make up my mind. Meze and beef! 
Some 10 hours later, this would be followed   by what sounds like a massive breakfast. Cheeses, 
ham, smoothie, fruits with a choice of omelette,   wrap, or pancakes. Well, for sure, I'm not going 
to get hungry on this flight. Our wine list is   an interesting blend of Turkish wines and a 
usual international mix. For whites, we have   two Turkish wines and Chablis. Red selection 
got two local names, French Medoc, Argentinian   Malbeck and Rioja. Nothing extravagant, 
but all solid names which retail for about   €20. Enough with anticipation of the meal. I start 
salivating already, and food is not likely to come   for another hour. By now, we already started 
taxiing, in Istanbul it could be notoriously   long. For a change, I choose orange juice rather 
than champagne for a pre-flight drink and cheer   for a good flight. While the flight is advertised 
as 14 hours, the navigation system shows that we   got 13 hours 20 minutes of flying time, which 
hints that at least half an hour of taxiing is   ahead of us. That's a big airport indeed. That's 
the part where I run my safety video competition,   comparing how airlines use this otherwise boring 
piece of info to tell who they are. Today,   I give Turkish a pass. I know their video and 
it's not going to score a lot. After years of   cool safety videos, somehow now they chose a 
very functional cartoonish approach which you   would hardly watch twice. Finally, engines 
whiz and we start accelerating on a runway.   As much as I wanted a fly over above night 
Istanbul, we are taking off towards the Black   Sea and away from the city, our flight path goes 
north, and I'm afraid my wishes for a nice view   have little impact here. I'm so hungry by now 
that the next 30 minutes are like a blur. There is   something behind the window and on the monitor in 
front of me, but all I can think is food. Drinks   come halfway. I feel adventurous and try Turkish 
Suvla Sur, a blend of Merlot and Cabernet which   turns out to be quite good. It's rich, smooth and 
with a clear dark fruity notes. No amuse-bouche   here but Turkish serves a nicely warmed up nut 
mix which does the job well. And here we are. The   meze arrives. If everything before, from the seat 
to all little touches was more or less in a very   solid territory, then dinner definitely takes 
things a notch above. Meze looks and tastes as   if we were in a fancy Istanbull restaurant rather 
than 30,000 ft above. And it's hardly a surprise.   This is where Turkish shines, winning for the last 
two years Skytrax best business class food award.   I'm not a food critic, so it's hard for me to 
describe the taste. You just have to take my word   that it was great. But what is much easier to see 
is how much thought they put into all the details.   Like this traditional Turkish candle light that 
makes it almost like a romantic dinner, especially   if you fly as couple. Or this oldest bread idea. 
Turkish recreating the recipe how bread was   baked 12,000 years ago in Anatolia from where it 
supposedly went out to the world. Can someone tell   that this is how it really was? Hardly. But does 
this give you a special feeling? For sure. Beef   cutlet comes next with asparagus, rocket salad, 
and some dried tomato on the side. And here,   probably for the first time, I make an aaahhh 
sound. It's too much on a well-done side and felt   a bit dry for my liking. A perfectly edible, just 
a little short of perfection, which I learned to   expect from Turkish food. That's always a problem 
of being great. The expectation is always high and   good is not always good enough. I finish all this 
with a perfect vanilla ice cream. As much as I was   seduced by desserts, I still keep in mind that 
big breakfast I want to try out tomorrow. The   big dinner makes me sleepy. But before I get some 
shuteye, I'm still to explore further my seat,   in-flight entertainment and amenities. Legspace 
first. New seat layouts brought a lot of privacy,   but all those new seats come with one common flaw, 
the narrow footwell. No one figured it out yet,   just some have it a bit better than the others. 
And here, Turkish is on "the others" side. My   legs feel a bit trapped and claustrophobic. While 
the seat is overall tight on space, there is a   decent storage space. A rather big console on 
my right with a personal storage compartment.   It hosts headphones, but you can easily put there 
your smartphone or some other things as it's quite   far from the aisle and seems to be reasonably 
secure. There is a standard bottle of water there   too rather than a fancy Voss or Fiji that some 
airlines like so much and which I think is really   a nonsense. A water is a water rather give me a 
better wine than a 20 euro water bottle. What's   next? Controls are right by my side. It's kind 
of cool how they light up with your touch. What   is smart is to have ono/off button for the screen 
here too. This is really convenient. The armrests   on both sides are retractable. This gives you more 
space when in flatbed position and more comfort   when upright. That's definitely a check. There 
also those additional vanity lights built into   the seat shell. Can be anything from a reading 
light to a kind of bedside light when you're in a   lie-flat position. And finally, a tray table 
which already got a full test drive during   the dinner. It's large and sturdy but not very 
adjustable. Can make you feel a bit trapped if   you got few extra pounds on yourself. Overall, 
nothing surprising, nothing disappointing. It's   definitely a very good seat even if some surfaces 
may feel a bit plasticky. But on the other hand,   you can see here the attention to details which 
I started sensing before and which comes across   the seat design as well. Some may tell its small 
things, but when you are in the air for 14 hours,   small things matter. Done with the seat and I 
switch my attention to in-flight entertainment.   The colors and resolution is good even if not 
4K, but it kind of becomes clear which side   Turkish takes in "does size matter?" argument. 
18 inch make it respectable, but hardly award   winning these days. Where Turkish shines is the 
content. It's endless. I would argue it's even   better than Emirates. Whatever your tastes are, I 
can confidently tell you will find something here   for yourself. What I also like is that they kept 
the interface conceptually the same for years.   Every time just refreshing the graphics but not 
changing the layout. So every time I fly Turkish,   I feel I can navigate through entertainment 
screen with my eyes closed. And this gives me   a strangely comforting feeling. To enjoy 
all that content Turkish provides Denon   headphones. It's still one of the few airlines 
that provides branded set and actually a good   and expensive one. Something in the range of 
€300 in retail. And as a cherry on the top,   there is onboard Wi-Fi and it's free in business. 
You get 1 GB of data and unlimited messaging,   which is more than adequate to stay in touch. 
Everyone talks about Turkish food, but I would   go further and put their in-flight entertainment 
as another thing where they are best-in-class,   if not simply the best. Let's see now how Turkish 
attention to details plays for amenities. Turkish   bedding set comes with a pillow and two blankets, 
a thinner cotton plaid and a thicker duvet style   blanket, which is actually quite nice as you never 
know if your flight is going to be hot or cold.   This is something as unpredictable for the 
airlines as box of chocolates for Forest Gump.   All looks good here. Hard to imagine otherwise 
given how big is Turkey on textiles. Surprisingly,   there were no mini-mattresses on our flight, which 
I thought to be a standard thing for Turkish. But   there is a set of sleepers, which for the moment I 
also expected to be some oldest or unique. But no,   for now it's usual. And the amenities bag itself. 
It looks quite big. So, who knows? Maybe I will   still find my mini mattress rolled up tightly in 
there. Turkish has a longtime cooperation with   Lanvin, one of the oldest French fashion house. It 
looks good on the outside, but inside it's a bit   on a simple side. A standard set that you can 
expect. Eye mask, toothpaste, and toothbrush,   and two tubes of hand cream and lip balm. But I 
kind of like those fluffy socks. Don't know why,   but they make me smile. I put them on with the 
thought that now I wear a French designer socks.   And with that, I'm done with my explorations and 
ready for what I hope to be good 8-9 hours of   sleep. Despite missing the mini mattress today, I 
slept surprisingly well and woke up exactly as per   plan, just in time for the breakfast. By now, I 
have 12 hours of flight behind. It's noon time in   Istanbul and I feel hungry again. So big breakfast 
no longer sounds like a strange idea. First plate   looks like a bit more simple than meze before, but 
it tastes just as good. It's very much in Turkish   style. Lots of small plates with different bites 
from cheese and ham to honey and butter. After   a bit of hesitation, I decide to order a cup 
of cappuccino instead of regular coffee. And   surprisingly, my gamble works. My cappuccino turns 
out to be almost proper. One of the better ones I   had at 30,000 ft. And again, I love those small 
details like this cardboard holder so that you   can comfortably hold the hot cup. The hot dish 
follows. It's a Turkish wrap with cheese and   what I think some combination of egg and potato. 
I would call it a cousin of breakfast burrito,   especially since we are flying to Mexico. 
Honestly, I wasn't entirely sure what I was   eating, but what I'm sure is that I properly 
enjoyed it. I'm quite impressed how Turkish   can make it look and taste as if it's just coming 
from the oven despite being served 12 hours into   a flight. And despite already having cappuccino, 
I obviously needed to get a glass of Cay, strong   Turkish tea. Without it, breakfast in Turkey is 
unthinkable. So, I better do it right. With that,   the breakfast is officially complete and I'm ready 
for the landing. Wait, not yet. A flight attendant   brings a small box with two pralines. I hesitate 
for the moment whether to keep it as a souvenir,   but tea seems to be a better companion for those 
pralines than my backpack. Now it's done. There   is about an hour left. Crew asks to open window 
shades and suddenly we are transferred from night   to day. Almost like walking out of a nightclub in 
the morning and realizing it's a daylight already.   Mexico City sits high in the mountains and 
there is a lot to see. I flew this approach   several times and each time enjoyed the views. Now 
I only have to look in the window and to conclude.   Or actually do both at the same time. I definitely 
like Turkish airlines and coming to this flight I   was a little worried if their mainstream business 
class would not be up to expectations I had after   experiencing their more of niche products 
before. And clearly there are some things to   pick here and there. But overall Turkish delivered 
a surprisingly solid and balanced business class   experience on this 787 flight. I would not call 
it the most luxurious, Emirates still probably   leads on this, but this doesn't make it any less 
worth. In a way, it's like comparing Bentley and   BMW. No one would argue which one is more 
luxurious, but it's a big question which   one you still like better. What I appreciated 
the most about Turkish is how balanced their   offer is. From the lounge and overall airport 
experience to the seat, food and entertainment,   they don't have anything which I could call a gap. 
Somewhere they were great, somewhere just good and   their food and in-flight entertainment I would 
put as best in class. And they never failed me in   anything throughout this journey. There are things 
which could be better - a bit more spacious seat,   some dishes were not born equal on the menu, some 
elements of the cabin have seen wear and tear. But   there was nothing where I would sigh "really, are 
you serious"? Which is what I actually did quite   a lot in the last few months from Lufthansa to 
Etihad to Air China. I confidently give "5-" once   again to this Turkish Airlines 787 business class 
flight. And with this, they firmly get on top of   my recommendation list. Whether a niche mini suite 
on just few A350s or mainstay 787 business cabin,   this is the airline I'm happy to fully 
endorse and to fly again and again. And   now I feel I should also check out their economy 
- since flying is not all about business class.

reviews.transcript_full:
Welcome to this review of Shanghai Airlines 
business class on their 787-9. Does this   automated security patrol giveaway where we 
are? We're in Japan at Kansai International,   in Osaka - shortly to travel to Shanghai. First, 
we were invited to the KIX lounge, and for more   on this lounge, see my separate review which I 
made last year. It will be linked at the end. This was my first time on Shanghai Airlines, 
which is wholly owned by China Eastern,   and you'll see the China Eastern logo 
pop up as we go through the video. My lovely wife managed to sneak ahead of me on 
the jet bridge as we approached the aircraft. So, here we go with our first look 
at the cabin. And look at this:   Closing door suites on a 2-hour regional flight. [Speaking to Crew] Okay. Thank you. 
Thank you very much. Thank you. Each seat has direct aisle 
access and loads of privacy. This seat is at a very high standard. I had 
no idea what to expect, so I was very pleased. So, there was storage space to my left. 
The seat itself was on the harder side,   but the leather gave it a premium feel. 
We'll look at the drinks menu in a moment.   This is the part of the console used 
for seat controls and the remote for   in-flight entertainment. There's also 
a universal power outlet, USB charging,   plus a headphone socket that appeared geared 
up for noise cancelling headphones. Of course,   the all important door latch, and 
a nice modern entertainment screen. Beneath the console are more seat 
controls and the tray table. And   the literature pocket was stuffed 
full of a bag containing slippers... Today's edition of China Daily... plus the safety card and also Wi-Fi instructions. 
Wi-Fi worked - It's free, but access is limited   as you might have experienced in China. Okay, 
that drinks menu - The alcohol choices were   simple. Red wine, white wine, or beer. No 
messing! I asked about a food menu, and the   crew member explained it would be a snack. That 
lowered my expectations! Cold towels and welcome   drinks from the menu were served, and there was a 
coaster to add to my collection, making it four! There was loads of leg room and 
two windows with a great view of   the engine and wing from my seat, which is 10 L. I almost forgot to mention the coat hook 
and this hidden cupboard with a mirror. This gadget, I think, is designed to hold things   in place. There was a branded bottle 
of water, but no individual air vents. On the floor was this sloping area leading up 
to the foot well, which itself had a mood light. The safety video played three times, first 
in Chinese, then Japanese, then English,   and I spotted this Cathay Pacific retro 
'lettuce leaf sandwich' livery on the   A350. [[Safety Video]Please ensure your 
portable electronic devices are switched   to flight mode]. While someone was engrossed 
in the China daily! [[Crew Announcement]ladies   and gentlemen, we are ready for takeoff. Please 
double check that your seat belt is fastened and   mobile phones should be switched off or 
switched to airplane mode. Thank you.] From Osaka Bay, we crossed 
Awaji Island and proceeded   over the Seto inland sea before clouds closed in. Looks like that China Daily is still 
on the go. Now, if you haven't seen   my China Eastern reviews, and I 
would recommend them obviously,   but my point is that entertainment was one of 
the weaknesses, and it was just the same here. There was nothing wrong with the 
responsiveness of the touch screen.   It was just the selections 
which were a bit lacking. I did like the virtual tour feature though where 
you could look around all parts of the cabin. Now that three pronged headphone socket 
turned out to be wasted, because the   headphones supplied were not noise cancelling 
and there is definite room for improvement here. Doors were put into use at cruising altitude. This   is only my second flight with 
a door and it's growing on me! Okay, it was time for the snack after drinks and 
nuts were served and then this box turned up. {{Message from Stephen}I hope you're enjoying 
the video. Can I please ask you to consider   subscribing? It's very important to me that 
I increase the number of subscribers to a   thousand by the end of January. I hope that you 
can help. Thank you.} Surely worth subscribing   just to get rid of messages like that!! So, 
this neat little snack box was a nice touch.   There were two sections with fruit, a sweet 
cake, and then at the front sandwiches and salad. Shanghai Airlines does have some much 
longer routes, so I'm not sure how   the food would change on those, but for 
this trip, this was definitely enough. Okay, I'll run through the amenities 
that were available at the seat. We had   the nice cloth bag with the slippers, 
and then there's that China Eastern   logo again - that was covering the 
blanket which was refreshingly thin! I didn't have time to put the seat flat,   but there was a comfortable recline, but 
we were already approaching Shanghai. Low cloud meant there were no spectacular views 
on the way in. And on arrival, we were going to   be heading off to the free transit hotel. If 
you're interested in that and how it works,   I do have a separate video going through 
the whole process from booking to sleeping. So, for this 2-hour trip 
between Osaka and Shanghai,   Shanghai Airlines did us proud. The highlight 
for me was the seat and the closing door.   Er the highlight for someone else was 
obviously the China Daily! Anyway,   here we are. I've got loads more videos 
on the channel and loads more planned.   Please click that subscribe button. I'd be 
really grateful. Thanks for watching today.

reviews.transcript_full: Emirates offers one of the most sought-after premium products in the world. Over the past 7 years, we've had the chance to experience business class with several different airlines. But does Emirates business class really live up to its reputation for luxury, service, and glamour? Today, we're going to find out aboard their brand new Airbus 350, an aircraft that has been in service for only 3 months. The business class cabin features 32 seats in a 1 2 1 configuration, giving every passenger direct aisle access. For window seats, the even-numbered rows are the best choice, as the seats are positioned closer to the window and offer more privacy. In the center, it's the opposite. The seats in the odd-numbered rows are positioned closer together, making them a great choice for couples. Since we're traveling as a couple, today we selected seats 5E and 5F. These two center seats are close together and slightly farther away from the aisles, giving us a little more privacy. If you're traveling alone, I would choose one of the center seats that are positioned farther apart, or an even row window seat for maximum privacy. There are three lavatories. One at the front dedicated to business class, and two more at the rear, shared with premium economy. Now, let's get on board. As soon as we step onto the aircraft, the first impression is excellent, an elegant modern cabin and a warm welcome from the smiling cabin crew. Before departure, we're offered orange juice, booster juice, or champagne. For me, I'll go with the orange juice. Emirates takes things a little further with a small mini bar near the seat, stocked with water, sparkling water, and a few snacks. Is it really necessary? Probably not, especially since you can order something almost anytime during the flight. But personally, I really appreciate this little extra touch. Next to the seat, you'll find everything you need to keep your devices charged. A power outlet, USB port, a fast charging USB-C port, and a built-in wireless charger. Business class is also equipped with a removable tablet that allows you to control the screen and the entire in-flight entertainment system. The amenity kit is very well equipped. It includes a Gillette razor, Bulgari products, earplugs, a toothbrush, a comb, and tissues. Emirates also provides very comfortable pajamas made from a blend of modal and elastane. Additional amenities are also available in the lavatories. Emirates in-flight entertainment system is probably one of the best, if not the best, we've experienced on any airline we've flown. The system is extremely responsive, and the selection of movies, TV shows, music, and other entertainment is simply impressive. In this category, Emirates is very hard to beat. Now, let's take a look at today's onboard menu and wine list. I found the menu quite good, but I was particularly impressed by the quality of the wines, which was excellent compared to what you typically find in business class. About 2 hours into the flight, I start my meal with a traditional Arabic mezze. For the main course, I choose the mixed grill followed by the chocolate pecan cake for dessert. After the meal, I take some time to listen to music and take my magnesium while my partner reads a book before we both try to get a few hours of sleep. After waking up, I take the opportunity to check out the premium economy cabin. And surprisingly, there are only about five passengers in the entire section. The cabin is also very elegant. The seats look comfortable and feature both a footrest and a calf rest. There's one thing to keep in mind, though. When the seat in front of you is fully reclined, the space can feel more restricted, especially if you're tall. To avoid this, I would probably choose the first row. The downside is that the entertainment screen is mounted on the bulkhead in front of you, which is a setup I personally like a little less. So, does Emirates new Airbus 350 business class live up to its reputation? There's no question that Emirates offers a luxurious and elegant cabin, an outstanding entertainment system, and very good service from the cabin crew. But the product isn't perfect. In my opinion, the food is still a step behind some other airlines, particularly Qatar Airways, where you can dine on demand and where the presentation is generally more refined. However, I would give Emirates a slight edge when it comes to the wine list, which I found a little more impressive than Qatar Airways. And of course, Qatar's Qsuites still have a major advantage with their closing doors, providing an extra level of privacy. For these reasons, I would place this new Emirates business class somewhere in the middle of our personal ranking of the business class products we've experienced. Of course, a lot also depends on the price you pay. Interestingly, one of the real sweet spots on the Emirates Airbus 350 might actually be premium economy. The cabin is elegant, the seats offer a respectable amount of recline, and you get both a footrest and a calf rest. On a long flight like Dubai to Montreal, those features can make a significant difference and help you arrive much more rested than you would in economy class. Thanks for watching. If you enjoyed this review, don't forget to subscribe to the channel and leave us a comment below. And I had this before during COVID, or just at the end of it, on a business class flight, and honestly, I didn't think it was that good. Food, entertainment, and even the bathroom to overall being ticked off my review checklist. Now, it's time to simply enjoy the rest of the flight. Cathay treats us with a beautiful LED lighting sequence from above, gradually changing the mood of the cabin, and helping everyone settle into the final part of the journey. Although, if I look slightly concerned, it's probably because the recline of the seat is surprisingly generous. This new premium economy seat offers around 8 in of recline, which is more than many of its competitors, and you'll definitely notice the difference when you're trying to relax. For the rest of the flight, I settled into the entertainment, and almost in perfect synchronization, the rest of the cabin closed their window shades. Well, nearly everyone. It's a simple thing, but it transforms what is an older aircraft frame into a much calmer and more comfortable environment. One final thing worth mentioning is the Wi-Fi. Cathay Pacific does offer connectivity, but at the moment it's only complimentary for business class, first class, and select top-tier frequent flyers. For everyone else, messages start around $4 for 30 MB package, while a 1-hour limited browsing pass is $9.95, and the full flight is $12.95. Whether that's good value is up to you, but personally I think the first two options difficult to justify. If I needed Wi-Fi, I'd probably go straight for the full flight package, or simply wait until landing. >> [music] >> I probably did pick the worst seat when it comes to the toilet, because if it's a long-haul flight, this will wake you up with the noise. However, there was a dedicated bathroom that's too frequently used, a little bit of a rarity. One final detail, and it's something I forgot to mention, and it's not just for the aviation enthusiasts. As a five-star airline, Cathay Pacific has added a high-resolution external camera to the aircraft, meaning even if you don't have a window seat, you can still enjoy the views from outside the plane. It's a small feature, but it's one of those touches that makes the flight feel a little bit more special, especially during the takeoff and landing, or when flying over somewhere scenic. So, there's probably a few areas which they could probably slightly improve on, but overall that is a really, really good seat. I'm just a little bit gutted that I didn't try it sooner. This now is not a little Japanese village, but it's the third floor of Haneda Airport. I think the main thing to take away is that the seat is really good, and it's a modern product with a big, beautiful screen, Bluetooth connectivity, and it is very, very comfortable with a lot of recline. And that is the main reason to fly on it. The fact they don't have glass cups like in the overlook, the headphones are quality and the cabin crew are just really good. I just think it's a shame that they run out of meals, but I can overlook that to be fair. Because I thought the dim sum was really good. Anyway, hope you've enjoyed the video. And safe travels.

reviews.transcript_full: (Transcribed by TurboScribe. Go Unlimited to remove this message.) Today we're back in Germany to ride the newest train in the country, and one that's not without its controversy. We'll be in first class on board this Taugo ICE-L for this three hour trip from Hamburg up to the unique island of Sylt. I will show you around all the classes, the on-board facilities and the dining car and talk about why this train has caused such a stir for Deutsche Bahn. So come along with me on another epic non-stop Euro trip. This journey starts in Hamburg in northern Germany. This is the second largest city in the country and the sixth largest in the EU with a population of around 2 million people. As far as big German cities go, I quite like it here. Especially as it's home to the world's biggest model railway, which is over 15km of track. Ok, let's head to the station. I was staying at the Ghana Hotel, right outside the eastern entrance. This fabulous station dates back to 1906 and houses 8 mainline, 4 S-Bahn commuter and 8 U-Bahn metro platforms. The entrance to the latter you can see straight ahead here. There is a multitude of different shops and food outlets across two levels. There is also a staff ticket office and travel centre here. I love the design, especially the wrought iron, glass walls and ceilings. The most impressive part however is the arched barrel train shed roof, which spans 70 metres across all mainline platforms. From the first floor balcony, you get wonderful views over Germany's largest unsupported train station canopy. Our train today is the 10.25am ICE 2074, which started in Berlin and is currently 16 minutes delayed. Let's check out the route. We will depart Hamburg and head north-west, making 4 planned intermediate stops on route before crossing the causeway over to the island of Silt. Ok, to the platform. These all have step-free access by lifts, if required. As I am just about to head down to the advertised platform 8, our train is switched over to platform 5. This was announced over the tannoy as well as the departure boards changing. And here comes our train for today, hauled by this Chesky Drahi Siemens Vektron Class 384 electric locomotive. This version has a top speed of 230kmph and a maximum power output of 6,400kW. They were meant to be hauled by DB's own new Talgo Class 105 locomotives, but these have yet to be delivered, just one of the many problems facing these trains' entry to service. Trailing is the brand new 17 coach rake of Talgo 230 ICEL coaches. These feature the iconic Talgo weight-saving design, where a single wheelset is shared between two coaches, but more on that later. There are 562 total seats, of which 477 are second class and 82 are first class, where we'll be travelling today. The rearmost coach is also a control car, which will allow for push-pull operation when they are eventually certified. I do think they look pretty smart though, what do you think? The L in ICEL stands for Low Floor. Level boarding is another Talgo feature, assuming correct platform height, such as here in Hamburg. The door next to the wheelchair spaces has a sliding step too, to bridge the small gap. The first class coaches are laid out in a 2 plus 1 configuration, and despite the greyness of the interior looking quite bland, the lighter coloured head cushions and armrests, along with the wooden tables, make the overall aesthetic quite pleasant. We will check them out in more detail once we get going. Staying connected while all is on the move can be complicated, but Holofly makes it incredibly simple. I am currently using Holofly's Global eSIM, giving me fast and unlimited data, without constantly changing SIM cards or worrying about expensive roaming charges. Coverage has been excellent throughout the past two weeks of this Euro trip, where I visited five countries, with the 4G and 5G seamlessly switching as I cross each international border. Holofly offers eSIMs for more than 200 destinations, including global coverage and over 15 regional packages, so you can choose the one that best suits your trip. Frequent travellers can also benefit from Holofly plans, which covers more than 160 destinations. There are unlimited data and 25GB light options with no contract, and you can cancel at any time. You'll also receive the All Was On benefit, providing 1GB of global backup data every month, from the moment your eSIM is installed. And if you need assistance, Holofly's support team is available 24x7 through web chat or WhatsApp. Use code NONSTOPEUROTRIP to get 5% off any Holofly eSIM, or 10% off a Holofly plans subscription for your first 12 months. Click my link above or in the description below to get connected with Holofly today. In the end we leave 18 minutes after the scheduled departure time at 10.43am. This journey from Hamburg to Esterland on the island of Sylt covers 240km, which is planned to take us 3 hours and 17 minutes of travel time. I booked about two weeks in advance and got my spa price ticket for €48.99, which is pretty good value in my opinion. This included an optional seat reservation fee of €6.90. With hindsight, I definitely didn't need to buy this, but you just never know with German trains. However, if you book earlier, then super spa price tickets start from €35.99 in first class, or from just €26.99 in second class. Various discounts for children up to the age of 14 are also applicable, see on screen now. All onboard announcements are made in both German and English. We warmly welcome you here. Shortly after departure, tickets are checked and the first class host comes around to take food or drinks orders. I passed on this as I want to visit the dining car myself later on. Luggage can be stored on the stacks near to the coach ends or on the overhead racks up above. The seat does look very stylish and although far from the most comfortable I've tried, had okay padding, a reasonable shape and a large winged headrest. There is a reading light built into this too. There are movable padded armrests and the seat can be reclined a bit using this button and sliding the base. Legroom is pretty good with the seat in front featuring an adjustable footrest too. This also has a small netted storage pocket and a large tray table with drinks indent. A small phone holder is at the top of the seat back. There is also a drinks holder in between the two seats and a litter bin down below. Two standard European style power sockets can be found just next to your own seat. Up above are both fixed and movable coat hooks and a very good window blind. Overall a reasonably comfortable first class product. You can scan the QR code on the seat back to connect to the ICE portal which includes free WiFi for all passengers. This was easy to connect to but was woefully slow. As we pick up a bit of speed you can really hear the Talgo ride quality come to light. While it is not as bad as some I have been on, there is just a constant background rattle with occasional big bumps. There are also some other interesting noises that the train makes like these strange hissing sounds. We are now on the approach to Itzyho, where our Czeski 3 Vektron locomotive will be swapped for a Deutsche Bahn bi-mode version for the rest of the route to Silt which is currently un-electrified. There is a scheduled 16 minute stop here for this to take place and we are just over 15 minutes late on arrival. Anyway, after sitting around for another 15 minutes, a man with a high-vis came down outside our coach and after some hands on heads, a few phone calls and a complete train reboot, we are on the move again at 11.54, now 38 minutes late. I have no idea what happened, there were no announcements made. Ok, let's go and check out the rest of the train now. These Talgo coaches are short, around half the length of a normal size train coach and due to this they don't have toilets in every one. There are 11 throughout the 17 coaches, including one which is fully accessible. Here is one of the regular ones. The water, soap and paper towels were all stocked up, as was the toilet roll. The toilet flush works and it was very clean overall. Now let's have a look at second class, which is in a 2 plus 2 layout with a mix of airline style and bay seating around a table. The seats are similar to mine in first class, however come with a reduced width and legroom as you'd expect. All the other amenities are the same with the exception of a shared centre armrest and no reading light. Honestly, if you could guarantee the train is as empty as it is today then I would go for second class every time. Moving through to the wheelchair spaces, of which there are three, all with two accompanying companion seats and all the facilities you get in the other classes. The fully accessible toilet along with baby changing facilities is in the adjacent vestibule, this was also very clean. A bit further and there are lots of amenities for families travelling with children. First, we have this compartment which features two sets of bay seating and a large central space for buggies and prams. More of the latter can be found in the next coach along, as well as plenty more seating dedicated to families which can be identified by the cartoon decorated walls. All of this is absolutely brilliant to see. Right down the far end there are eight vertical bike storage spaces. You must have a bike ticket to bring one on board, which start from €7.50 depending on distance. The bike space reservation is included with this ticket. We're now passing over the Kiel Canal which dates back to 1887. Every year around 32,000 ships use this 98km waterway which links the North and Baltic seas, reducing their transit distance by 460km. Although I am pretty impressed with most of the interior of this new Talgo ICE-L, the bistro dining car is where it's seriously let down. It has just 12 seats for the 17 coach train. There is also a vastly inferior menu to regular ICE services with just three hot options which is very disappointing. I went for the chilli con carne and bread roll along with a warm Coke Zero as they weren't chilled and they had no ICE. Ironic, eh? It wasn't exactly good value either with the total being €16.70. At Heide we pass a southbound service from Westerland to Berlin. This journey takes just over five and a half hours in total. After Hamburg heading eastbound, the train can use the high speed line to get up to its maximum speed of 230kmph. I'm going to have a moan now that Deutsche Bahn have branded this train as an ICE, which is their flagship high speed brand. There is no way that this train is anywhere close to on a par with the recently introduced 320kmph capable ICE3 Neo. I rode this not too long ago and the difference is night and day. I believe they have branded this Talgo set as an ICE to simply allow them to charge higher fares. We are now coming up to the most interesting part of today's route. Our destination at Westerland is on the holiday island of Silt, near to the Danish border in the far north of Germany. This island does not have a road connection to the mainland and as such the only way to reach it is by ferry or rail. And if you want to take your vehicle, then it will be loaded onto one of these auto-rack shuttle trains here at Niebuhr. This is a hugely popular service with holidaymakers, day-trippers and delivery drivers alike, with departures up to every half hour in peak summer season. To take your car over to Silt, prices start from €68 one way or €112 for a return journey which includes all passengers. At most times you can just turn up and go, but booking in advance in peak holiday season is definitely recommended as you can see how busy it gets. As well as these ICEL services, there is also the hourly RE6 regional train from Hamburg to Westerland. One of these trains can be seen over on the far platform here. I was about to say how well we are doing for time now with our delay still hovering around the same as before. However, all is about to go catastrophically wrong in a way only German railways can manage. We come to a rest at Klankspur, the last station on the mainland. We were not scheduled to stop here, which is never a good sign. I thought maybe it was due to some congestion on the single track sections ahead. But no, I will spare you the waiting around, but we were stationary for over 45 minutes while the train was restarted a number of times, with the AC, power sockets and carriage lights going on and off repeatedly during this period. Finally, and with the onboard information screen still not having caught up with our delay, I felt like cheering once we finally started moving again. This next 10 minutes is by far where you will see the best train window views of the journey. Leaving the German mainland, we must first pass through the Rickensbuller Kuge wetland nature reserve, before crossing the Hindenburg Dam, an 11km man-made causeway across to the island of Zilt, which opened in 1927. Dear guests, in a few minutes we have arrived at our last stop, Westerland. Today, 70 minutes delayed. At 40.41 we are there on platform 1. We say thank you and wish you a pleasant afternoon. We finally arrive at Westerland station at 2 .45pm, actually 74 minutes delayed. This entitles me to a 25% refund on my ticket price, which is easily claimed through the DB app. I had the money back to my card three days later. As we alight, let me summarise this journey from Hamburg to Westerland onboard the new DB Talgo ICE-L. Overall, it's a good train internally, well fitted out to a premium finish and quite comfortable. The price I paid was reasonable. It certainly doesn't live up to the ICE name, either in speed, ride quality or even the dining car offering. It's a shame that DB branded it as such, as I think Intercity would have been much more fitting. Have you been on a DB ICE-L in Germany yet? If so, what was your experience like? Let me know in the comments below. I will have a video coming soon on the nearly identical Danish version of this train, so stay tuned for that. Spoiler alert, it was way worse. Don't forget to subscribe. Thanks for watching to the end and I'll see you in the next video.

reviews.transcript_full:
Six hundred and fifty dollars, one way… Now, 
that's less than a lot of economy fares on the   full-service airlines. So, what's the catch?
Today's flight on this rather tired-looking   Boeing 787 Dreamliner takes me 
from Melbourne to Singapore.  Let's find out whether Scoot 
Plus is too good to be true,   or the best value premium seat 
leaving Australia right now
   I guess we can say Melbourne has beaten 
Sydney to the first project sunrise flight? And yea, that was our first-ever YouTube video. 
It is kind of scary to see how young we were. Back at the airport, I am off to 
find the Scoot check-in counter.  Scoot is Singapore Airlines’ low-cost 
arm and, at the time of recording,   operates 8 weekly flights to Melbourne.
Most of these are afternoon departures. Today’s   Sunday flight is an exception, departing at 9:35pm 
and arriving at an ungodly 4am in Singapore. The Scoot Plus fare includes priority check-in and   30kg of checked baggage. Both 
of which I made full use of. Through immigration and security pretty quickly,   and off to the lounge, I guess…
Except… there isn't one.  Scoot doesn’t provide any form 
of lounge access with its fares. So, I guess I will hang out at the airport. It's almost time to board, so I head 
to my gate — gate 16 today — where I   come face to face with my aircraft, 
a rather weary-looking Boeing 787. Priority boarding is another perk that comes with 
Scoot Plus, and one that was actually enforced Parked right next to us was a 
Singapore Airlines A350, and one that   looked like it had been polished that morning.
Anyway — let's take a look at today's seat map. Scoot has a fleet of 24 Boeing 
787 family aircraft. The Melbourne   flights are operated by the -9 variant.
The type features 375 seats in total.  The Scoot Plus cabin at the front 
has 35 seats in a 2-3-2 layout. So, this is the Scoot Plus cabin.  The 2-3-2 layout does mean a middle seat 
row, which you will probably want to avoid. The seat itself is a leather-covered 
recliner. With a seat width of 19.5”,   it feels reasonably wide, and despite 
its age, the leather still feels solid.  Legroom is outstanding too, 
with 38 inches of pitch.  The recline is generous as well, all 
controlled by these manual levers. And yes, there is no seat-back entertainment. 
All you get is a generous seat pocket.  There are AC power sockets in the centre console,   but you will be out of luck 
if you are after a USB port. Overall, it is a decent hard product that reminds 
me somewhat of the Jetstar business class seat. Pre-departure service was this cup 
of water. And… well, that's it.  Pushback was on time, followed by   a long taxi out to runway 34.
And then we were off.
   Not long after takeoff, the crew came around to 
confirm my pre-selected meal and drink choice.  I was also given this voucher 
for the inflight wifi. It came in handy, because Scoot 
doesn't offer IFE of any sort.  But you're better off downloading something before 
your flight — or paying some fairly ridiculous   prices for their wifi packages.
Fifty-five US dollars for a gigabyte.   The voucher that comes with Scoot Plus 
gives you 200 megabytes, which isn't a lot.  The speed was reasonable for plane 
internet, fine for messages, not much else. About an hour after departure, the meal arrived.  And this is it — the full Scoot 
Plus dining experience, on one tray. The main I preselected was a Curry Chicken 
Biryani Rice, served sealed with a label on   top telling you to peel back with care.
I took that warning very seriously,   considering my past history of spilling food 
on myself and the very dodgy tray table. I pre-selected this meal weeks ago when I booked.   These are some of the other meal choices provided.
Accompanying it was a drink, a chocolate muffin,   a Biscoff biscuit, a wet wipe and 
some plastic cutlery. That's the lot. The curry chicken and biryani rice 
were hot and filling. It was on par   with economy class offerings, 
but nothing more than that.  There's no alcohol included 
unless you paid for it. And that's it in terms of service for the 
flight. No second service, no snack later on,   nothing between here and Singapore.
If you want more, you're paying for   it. Scoot sells combo meals on 
board from around twelve dollars. Service was prompt, friendly and professional. 
Efficient rather than warm, but no complaints. I leaned back into my seat and tried to 
sleep through the rest of the flight.  And if you want a blanket or eye mask, be sure to 
bring your own as none will be provided for free. The rest of the flight was uneventful and some 
hours later, we were on approach to Singapore.  My watch reckoned I had managed 
almost five hours of sleep — broken,   but on an overnight in a recliner, I'll take it. So, time to look back at 
this Scoot Plus experience,   the hard product has a lot going for it.
Th seat’s generous pitch, width and recline   combined to provide a proper seat, almost as 
good as premium economy on other airlines.  The soft product is where it falls short. 
No lounge or inflight entertainment.   Two hundred megabytes of wifi and 
eye-watering prices if you want more.  One pre-selected meal. No blanket or eye mask. Put it next to even Jetstar's business 
class and Scoot gives you noticeably   less. In some ways it's thinner 
than a good premium economy product. But the question is what else six 
hundred and fifty dollars gets you   on this route. And most of the time, the 
answer is a seat down the back in economy.  Against that, this is totally worth it. Yes, 
you're paying for the seat, not the service.   If what you want is to arrive in Singapore 
having slept, that's the part that matters. Let me know what you think about 
Scoot Plus in the comments.  And if you want to see how this stacks 
up against the seat it reminds me of,   the Jetstar business class review is right here!
