reviews.transcript_full: Previously After checking out three different oneworld lounges at BKK we continue our journey and finally get to review Cathay Pacific's A350 Business Class and see what it's actually like If you haven't seen the previous episode I recommend giving it a quick watch first But without further ado let's continue our happy little journey Cathay Pacific Business Class Episode 2 of this four-part series Let's... 3 2 1 Take off ✈️ Hello everyone, I'm Ben That's right, we're already at the gate It feels a little weird starting the video here But... that's fine We get to see the plane right away Today's flight is Cathay Pacific Bangkok ✈️ Hong Kong CX704 A350-900 Cathay Pacific is the world's third-largest A350 operator Its fleet currently includes 18 A350-1000s and 30 A350-900s behind only SQ in first place and QR in second Their average age is around 8 years But today's aircraft B-LRI is a little older at almost 10 years old But... none of that matters The sunset today is absolutely gorgeous It looks incredible shining on the plane Business Class passengers happen to be boarding group 2 After passengers requiring assistance and the fancy elite members it's finally our turn to board Let's take a look at this aircraft's layout Cathay's A350-900 only has one seat configuration 38 Business Class seats 28 Premium Economy seats and 214 Economy seats in 1-2-1 2-4-2 and 3-3-3 configurations respectively Hehe~ After flying Cathay so many times I finally don't have to walk all the way to the back Today's seat is 17K The seat itself is the classic reverse herringbone Safran Cirrus III Seat As soon as we get to the seat we can already see a comfy pillow waiting for us and on the side table there's also a physical menu We'll take a closer look at those later Let's look at some numbers first First up, the legroom is pretty insane For reference, I'm comparing this to EVA Air's 777 Business Class because that's... pretty much the only Business Class I've flown that I can compare this to With 45 inches of seat pitch and a seat width of 20.2 inches both are slightly better than EVA Air But honestly... they're all about the same to me My legs can't reach the end anyway But Cathay definitely does feel noticeably more spacious This extra space on the inside for someone who likes sleeping on their side and curling up their legs like me is extremely ergonomic And of course, this compartment opens up too .... Wait a second Isn't this... our old friend Surfshark? (LMAO) Did I just shark you Did I just shark you when you least expected it? Our good friend Surfshark is basically an online teleportation device For someone like me who's constantly traveling around the world like a weird human being it's actually incredibly useful When I'm traveling whether at airports, hotels, or cafés I'm almost always connected to public Wi-Fi It's definitely convenient but public Wi-Fi isn't as safe as you might think But once you turn on Surfshark it encrypts your connection giving you an extra layer of protection Together with its strict no-logs policy you can feel a little more secure when using public Wi-Fi The new email scam checker can also identify emails containing phishing threats giving me all-around online protection And then some websites or streaming platforms have regional restrictions that prevent you from accessing them That's when Surfshark can instantly activate teleportation mode and teleport you to another country With over 140 locations worldwide and more than 4,500 servers wherever you want to go it's pretty much just one click away Plus one account works on unlimited devices and there's 24/7 customer support With all that, what are you waiting for? Just click the link now or use my promo code and you'll get an extra 4 months of Surfshark Yay~ Thank you, everyone~ And thank you to Schrödinger's Surfshark for sponsoring this video So, we... where were we again...? Oh, right Storage Perfect timing Let's take a look at the other storage spaces too The side table is right here Let me show you And if we open this compartment here inside you'll find a bottle of water over-ear noise-cancelling headphones a little mirror that pops up and a small pocket Slightly awkwardly you have to dig everything out before you can find all the ports inside There's USB a universal power outlet and a headphone jack Personally, I don't find this particularly convenient But... it's fine I get to sit up front so who am I to complain? Moving over to the side this is your little control panel a reading light with adjustable brightness the PSP for the entertainment system and... the seat adjustment controls We'll play with those later when I'm being lazy For now, let's look over by the aisle There's a coat hook up top and a literature pocket underneath Inside you'll find the safety card an airsickness bag and the inflight magazine There's not a whole lot in there But at least on both sides your arms each have a comfy little home It's just that the one on my left was ridiculously stuck It took me forever to finally pop it up But... once I got it up it was like I'd unlocked a secret compartment There's a hidden spot for a water bottle underneath I have to say the storage on this seat is genuinely pretty impressive Perfect for people with lots of little things Okay, very nice What else do we have? Let's take a look at this big screen up front The entertainment screen can be stowed away You might need a very long arm to reach it but just push it back like this and there you go It's an 18-inch HD screen running Cathay's latest entertainment system There's really not much to complain about here Although it's still missing a few features found on the new Aria Suite I'll show you those in Episode 4 But Cathay's entertainment system is excellent as always Every time I fly Cathay, I look forward to seeing what new movies they have TV shows news music games shopping the flight map and cameras on the plane's butt and head It's all here Don't worry I think it's basically impossible to get bored on this flight Very nice~ Alright, back to the seat Is there anything else we haven't covered? The seat itself has a headrest that adjusts up, down, left, and right And one thing I really like is there's a small privacy shield on the aisle side It's not as fancy as having a door but honestly, it's a very cost-effective way of providing some privacy And if that little reading light isn't bright enough there are also overhead lights And Cathay is generous enough to let you turn both of them on unlike energy-saving champion EVA Air which only lets you turn on one And that's it That's Cathay Pacific's A350 Business Class seat I really like it At least personally, I think it slightly beats EVA's 777 What do you guys think? The flight attendants were also very attentive As soon as we boarded they came around with hot towels welcome drinks and asked what we'd like for our meal Let's start with a little champagne to ceremoniously kick off this journey Not long after the safety video started playing and we pushed back right on time That's also when I secretly discovered another little light underneath the side table This trip to Bangkok was short but very enjoyable Hopefully I'll be back soon to visit my friends But for now, let's take off It's a little dark but let's still take a moment to enjoy this beautiful engine view See you in a bit~ Okidoki Welcome back~ Once we reached cruising altitude the flight attendant proactively came over to ask if I wanted a blanket I said yes and then she just tucked me right in Peasant Ben had absolutely no idea how to react But anywayz it's time to check out the Wi-Fi After flying Cathay so many times in my life I've finally gotten to use Cathay's Wi-Fi for free When it comes to Cathay this is pretty impressive every aircraft in their fleet has inflight Wi-Fi But if you want to use it for free only First Class Business Class Diamond and Gold status members and members flying Premium Economy are eligible Yep As for the speed it was pretty decent in actual use I'll put my speed test screenshot here too Coverage also seems to be almost worldwide so there's really not much to complain about Hopefully one day in Economy we can at least get free Wi-Fi for messaging Think about it, Cathay~ Alright After playing around with the PSP for a bit next up is of course what I've been looking forward to most meal time! The tray table pulls out from here and as you can see, it folds out You can also easily push it forward so if you need to get out while eating you still have a little room and won't be held hostage by your food Speaking of food what options are on the menu? For drinks alcohol takes up a big part of the menu red wine white wine cocktails whisky beer you can order them all But if you're like me and don't really drink much there's also juice soft drinks coffee and tea plus some special options like Hong Kong milk tea and hot chocolate Now onto the food There are two choices for the main course five-spice chicken with fermented red bean curd and what I chose this time fried tiger prawns with tamarind sauce Ta-da! And here's the food! Look at this~ Don't these colors make it look incredibly appetizing? The bottom-left corner is empty because... the flight attendant soon came by with a basket of warm bread to fill that empty spot Garlic bread—you can't go wrong So let's hurry up and dig in! Okay, first up, the drinks It comes with a glass of water and I ordered the Cathay classic Cathay Delight Don't judge me but this is actually my first time trying it kiwi juice + coconut milk + mint leaves Mmmmm That's pretty good~ Nice and milky No, I'm not swearing but with a refreshing touch to it Delicious! If I had to name one downside I'd say this... isn't the best drink to pair with a meal So next time, I might order this as my welcome drink I think that would work better Next up, the appetizer Thai grilled pork neck salad It doesn't look like much but there's actually quite a lot of meat underneath Drizzle on that sweet and sour Thai dressing Ohhh~ So good Nice and tangy just like the ulcer in my mouth absolutely exploding in there Ughhh Annoying I'll just have to endure it Let's move straight on to today's main course Prawns, rice, and veggies OOOKKAYYY Very generous Five prawns and none of them are particularly small Take a bite and it's packed with meat Very satisfying But I also have to say the flavors are definitely pretty intense Towards the end it got a little spicy, but that's fine because I have absolutely zero spice tolerance But the sauce is also quite salty and oily so you really need to eat it with rice But if you watched the previous episode, you'll know my stomach right now is basically on the verge of exploding So I ended up in this awkward situation where I wanted to eat... but physically couldn't eat anymore The veggies on the side are pickled cabbage with scrambled eggs Pretty interesting It's just a shame that I didn't find it particularly refreshing so this entire main course felt... a little difficult to finish Let's just have some fresh fruit instead This is exactly what I want right now Ohhh~ Cold and sweet Even the pineapple isn't sour at all Very refreshing APPLE-solutely AMAZING! 🤣🤣🤣 But then I got hit with another attack that garlic bread from earlier with some butter CRAPPP So good, but... so fattening 🐷 Whatever, let's not worry about that Let's just enjoy this rare Business Class experience Making myself feel guilty about it would just be unfair to myself And of course how could we finish the meal without Cathay's classic Häagen-Dazs? It was served after everyone had mostly finished eating This time, I got vanilla Nom nom So happy Getting ice cream on a plane is pure happiness I think it's time for a quick summary Overall, I thought the inflight meal was... pretty good Aside from the main course being a bit salty and heavy I really don't have much to complain about They were very generous with the prawns The appetizer fruit bread and drinks were all great The plates and cutlery also made the meal feel quite special I personally really enjoyed it I think the bigger problem was... before I even got on the plane my stomach was already about to explode I... I blame my friend So I think if my stomach had been a little emptier when I ate this meal I might've felt differently Who knows But either way the food is already in my stomach Let's get up and move around and check out Cathay's Business Class bathroom while we're at it Cathay's A350 Business Class has three bathrooms in total shared between 38 passengers That's a great ratio so you rarely have to wait The bathroom is also well stocked with amenities Bamford hand wash body lotion face mist and for some reason, there's also an unbranded hand wash Maybe they want you to use less of the expensive one Then you've got the usual baby changing table two coat hooks a full-length mirror toilet seat covers sanitary pads cups and air vents Not bad It's got everything you need What's more unusual is you can also find a window in the bathroom so you can relieve yourself under the stars I don't even know what I'm saying anymore Anyways, that's about it Let's head back and lie down Before we arrive in Hong Kong let's relax and do absolutely nothing for a bit By the way I noticed the pillowcase actually has a Bamford logo on it so I'll just assume it's a fancy pillow Over on the aisle side there's another section that can pop up but it seemed a little broken so I ended up pulling it up by hand giving you just a tiny bit more room to wiggle around And with my legs fully stretched out my feet reach about here As you can see, there's still plenty of room for me to be a happy little caterpillar Wa wa And that's it From there, we flew all the way back to Hong Kong Sad sad But... it's time to wrap things up When we arrived in Hong Kong I was a little sad The time went by way too quickly But Cathay's A350 Business Class was... really good~ I can't really bring myself to complain much After all, I cherish every chance I get to fly Business Class But the storage is excellent the seat goes fully flat the service is excellent and the food is pretty good Does this seat feel outdated? Of course if you really compare it with the latest Business Class products out there it definitely feels a little dated But is it actually outdated? I think even today with competition this intense it's still a very solid product I think it can easily hold up for a few more years Add in the fast-track service from Bangkok and the lounge experience and overall, it's still a great experience So if you get the chance I'd definitely recommend giving it a try I don't think you'll be disappointed Mhm And that's it That's everything for this episode~ If you enjoy these airline review videos don't forget to like, share, save, and subscribe And once again, thank you to all my lovely supporters for supporting my channel ❤️ If everything goes according to plan the next episode picks up after we arrive in Hong Kong at Hong Kong Airport Cathay's home turf for some lounge hopping We're only halfway through the journey So I'll see you in the next episode~ Biboo

reviews.transcript_full: What started as a single flight from Melbourne turned into the biggest adventure Joe and I have ever taken. Over 83 days, we traveled through 10 countries, through thousands of kilometers, and experienced everything from Arctic landscapes and ancient cities to incredible food, unforgettable hotels, and some amazing surprises. This is a start of that journey. >> [music] [music] >> Welcome back to Maximo's Travels. Over the coming months, Joe and I are taking you on our biggest adventure yet. 83 days traveling throughout Malaysia, Finland, Estonia, Turkey, Germany, Belgium, England, Scotland, Iceland, and France. Along the way, I'll be sharing honest airline reviews, hotel reviews, airport lounges, train journeys, day trips, local food, and practical travel tips to help you plan your own adventures. Everything you see is completely self-funded, so every review is based on our own experience and honest opinion. Our adventure begins at Melbourne Airport, where we're boarding Malaysian Airlines flight MH148 to Kuala Lumpur aboard one of their newest aircraft, the Airbus A330-900neo. We've chosen extra legroom economy seats, and in this review, I'll show you exactly what the experience is like from check-in and boarding through the seats, meals, entertainment, comfort, and service. But, this isn't just a one-way review. After traveling for 12 weeks, we'll board Malaysian Airlines flight MH129, giving us the perfect opportunity to see whether the experience is just as good on the journey back home. So, how does Malaysia Airlines stack up on one of its flagship routes? Are the extra legroom seats in economy worth paying for? And is it the perfect airline to begin our 83-day adventure around the world? Come with us. Our journey starts now. But first, a little context. Why fly to Malaysia if we intend to fly to Europe? Well, the answer is twofold. Firstly, we wanted to break up the 24-hour plus journey flying from Melbourne to Europe. And secondly, we had accumulated enough Qantas Frequent Flyer points for two business class return trips from Southeast Asia to Europe. It was far, far easier to book a business class flight using points from Southeast Asia on one of Qantas's partners rather than try and book a Qantas flight from Australia to Europe. We'd had one or two bad experiences flying economy on long-haul routes. So, we decided to book Malaysian Airlines and their Airbus A330-900neo, one of their newest aircraft in their fleets. And we decided to book extra legroom seats as well. So, we found ourselves at Melbourne Airport at a very respectable 10:00 a.m. ready to check in for a 1:25 p.m. departure. Malaysian Airlines check-in opened at least 3 hours before departure. However, it did take around 30 minutes to check in. This is largely due to delays in handling luggage at the airport. Although the amount of luggage some of the passengers were carrying might have contributed to the delay somewhat. Malaysian Airlines allows for two 23 kilo bags in economy per passenger or 32 kilos in business class. You're also allowed one cabin bag up to 7 kilos and a personal handbag or other bag. And ours were checked and tagged. The airport didn't appear that busy and I think we cleared customs, immigration, and security in record time and we headed to the nearest airport lounge, the Aspire Lounge. The old lounge on the mezzanine level is under reconstruction. So, we headed to a temporary lounge on the ground floor, which was somewhat hard to find given its temporary nature and lack of adequate signage. Access to this lounge was courtesy of American Express and my Priority Pass membership. Unlike the other lounge that was under reconstruction, this didn't offer a view of the airport tarmac or of the outside world for that matter. There was a limited selection of drinks and spirits available and the food selection was somewhat meager. And unlike other lounges, it didn't offer barista coffee. There was a machine there instead. And whilst the selection was quite limited, the standard of food was quite good. There was something that I was able to eat that was gluten-free and Joe was able to choose one or two things that were vegetarian as well. The original Aspire Lounge will reopen sometime in 2027. And until that time, I think you're better off going to the American Express Lounge if you've got access to that. Or if you're a Priority Pass member, the Marhaba Lounge at Melbourne Airport International Terminal. As you can see, I didn't have that much on my plate, but it was enough to tide me over until lunch was served on our Malaysian Airlines flight in a couple of hours time. The lounge had a couple of shower cubicles, which I couldn't access because they were locked. The men's toilet was clean, functional, but quite small, which was just as well because the lounge wasn't very busy at all. Given the temporary nature of the lounge, there was no Wi-Fi, so I couldn't do a speed test on it. We spent a couple of hours in there and then slowly made our way to the departure gate. Boarding was orderly and relaxed, and it was called in groups. The airline runs up to three daily services between Melbourne and Kuala Lumpur on its new fleet of A330-900 neos. You can tell these are new aircraft from the moment that you step through the door. This newer, small, spacious, and more comfortable aircraft is another one of the reasons why we chose Malaysian Airlines for this particular route. And I was really hoping this aircraft would be much more comfortable than the Airbus A330-200 and 300s that this airline used in the past, as well as the 737-800 that Qantas uses for some of its Southeast Asian long-haul routes between, say, Melbourne and Indonesia, Bali. The interior of the cabin was modern, clean, and somewhat funky. Malaysia Airlines offers 24 extra legroom seats in economy. We were in seats 10H and 10K, and the extra legroom didn't let us down. There was an extra 4 in or 10 cm of legroom, and it made the whole cabin feel quite spacious. They were new Recaro seats and they were quite functional with plenty of storage and offered a tray table that slid out to meet you, as well as a drink cup holder, but I found that I didn't use this. The plane was equipped with Wi-Fi and the entertainment system was pretty good. It offered a 13.3-in high definition 4K screen. It was fast, bright, and offered a fairly decent selection of movies. The touch screen was quite responsive and it didn't take long for movies and TV shows to start loading. Oh, and by the way, if you're planning to visit Malaysia, you need to pre-enter your details in the digital arrival card prior to your departure. It only takes a few minutes via a phone app. The interior seating is configured in a 2-4-2 configuration, which means I got the window seat and Joe avoided the dreaded middle seat. It was quite a comfortable interior. >> [music] >> Staying connected online is a must when traveling. I needed for navigation, messages, emails, travel and airline flight updates, and my social media. With Holafly, you can have unlimited data in over 200 destinations. It's always on and you can choose from an individual destination SIM, 15 plus regional eSIMs, or even a global eSIM customized for daily, weekly, or monthly durations. I was provided with a global monthly plan for 3 months and used it extensively in Asia and Europe. One easy setup that took less than 2 minutes and it instantly and seamlessly connected to a local mobile network wherever I traveled. You get to keep your regular SIM, WhatsApp number, contacts, and access to all your other apps. My HolaFly Global eSIM provided me with great, fast, and reliable service up to 5G in all the destinations I visited. From Kuala Lumpur and Penang in Malaysia, Helsinki in Finland, Istanbul's bazaars and mosques, German castles and beer halls, the Grand Place or main square in Brussels, museums and historic homes in London, castles and distilleries in the Scottish Highlands, the volcanic wilderness in Iceland, or the Palace of Versailles in France. Whether I was exploring ancient sites, walking through markets, or hiking in a wilderness area, I was always connected where a mobile phone signal existed and I never ran out of data. It provided me with peace of mind and no hidden costs. A HolaFly eSIM keeps you connected when you travel without swapping or purchasing multiple eSIMs. So, grab a HolaFly eSIM for your next adventure. Scan the QR code on the screen or click on the link in the description and use my code MAXIMUS TRAVELS for 5% off your next HolaFly eSIM and 10% off HolaFly plans for the first 12 months. Thank you so much for supporting my channel, All A Flight. On on time departure. Even though we departed the gate on time, it did take us around 15 minutes to taxi and prepare for take off. Our flight time was 8 hours and 45 minutes and I'd call that a long haul flight, which is generally considered to be over 6 hours in duration. The take off from Melbourne Airport was smooth and we settled into our 8-hour 45-minute flight. Not only did we appreciate the extra leg room, but the seats were nice, well padded, and quite comfortable. They were wide and supportive of your back and thighs. It was quite a comfortable trip. The cabin layout and decor, with its ambient lining, made the whole experience fresh, modern, and comfortable. The ambience and comfort levels on the A330-900 Neo was quite a step above the economy class experience of some of Malaysian Airlines' nearest competitors, especially out of Australia. The noise levels in the cabin was also a fair bit quieter than the 787-800, for example. The cabin was kept reasonably cool, and unfortunately, there weren't individual air vents where you could control the temperature in your seat. Unlimited, complimentary Wi-Fi was offered on this flight. Unfortunately, it was so slow that you couldn't really use it for very much at all. As you can see from this speed test, it was pretty slow. Although you could check emails and social media accounts, you couldn't stream any movies or YouTube, for instance. I think a standout of the flight was a 13-in 4K entertainment system and the moving map. As I mentioned before, the touchscreen was very good and very sensitive. And you had a number of different views of the moving map and even had the ability to look cameras on all the different corners of the plane, as well as see the map of where you're actually flying over, as well as the total route. In terms of a loo review, there were 269 economy seats and five toilets, giving a ratio of 54 to 1. And that meant that there was some waiting most of the times I wanted to use them. and look at the plane bottle but I don't think the cabin crew are going to clean this toilet up for me first. The menu was available on the flight entertainment screen. But Joe and I ordered a vegetarian lacto-ovo and gluten-free meal respectively. Our special meals were served around about 1 hour after take-off and the rest of the cabin was served 30 minutes after that. >> [crying] >> For economy passengers, drinks weren't served till nearly 2 hours after take-off, but we did receive water with our meals. My rice and lamb dish was very tasty and flavorful and the beetroot and bean salad was great, too. I particularly enjoyed the summer cheesecake. Very nice. Joe received her vegetarian meal sometime after I did and I was too busy eating to film what she got, but she did say it was quite tasty, as well. You could connect your own headphones to the entertainment system, but I didn't bother as the ones that they supplied in economy were quite good. And you can also use the entertainment system to call the crew and order additional drinks or snacks if you wanted to. And the screen controlled everything, including the lights above you. The rest of the flight was rather uneventful, but comfortable and reasonably quiet. Snacks and a drink were served about 2 and 1/2 hours before we landed. Each of us received a pasty, a gluten-free and vegetarian one, respectively. Both were nicely heated and quite tasty. I think Malaysian Airlines really excelled in the food department on this flight. By about 6 hours in, I was quite cold in the cabin, as you can tell by our hoodies and blankets. But, the pastries certainly hit the spot. They were absolutely delicious. If a bit crumbly. They were served in boxes, but I think if they were served in plates, it would have been a little bit more civilized and we would have contained the crumbs a little bit more than we actually did. I do hope you're enjoying this video. If so, please hit that like and subscribe button. And hit that notify bell, so you'll always be notified of my future videos. If you wish to support my channel, please consider buying me a coffee. Use the QR code on the screen or a link in the description. 8 hours and 45 minutes passed very quickly. And it was a daytime flight, so there was no need to sleep. I was kept entertained by a really good selection of movies. We witnessed a beautiful, if moody, sunset as we approached Kuala Lumpur. We made our final approach at dusk and landed while it was quite dark. >> Given the flight time, I thought this flight was nice, easy, comfortable. It cost around $115 per person for the extra legroom seat, and I think it was worth it. The total cost of return flights was around 1,030 Australian dollars, around 730 US dollars. And I'd rate this flight quite highly. I'd give this a maximum rating of 4.5 out of five. >> Both engines, welcome to KL International Airport, Terminal 1. To all our visitors, selamat datang to Malaysia, and to all Malaysians, welcome home. Please remain seated until the visible sign is switched off. >> After taxiing for about 10 minutes or so, we arrived at the gate and headed into Kuala Lumpur's spacious and modern terminal building. Well, to be precise, this was the satellite terminal building. The terminal building was absolutely huge, and it was a fairly long walk to go from our arrival gate to the train that linked the satellite terminal with the main terminal. And we were thankful that the shuttle train between the terminal buildings had reopened just a couple of weeks before we had arrived. It had been closed for more than 3 years due to mechanical breakdowns. The train isn't that big, and it was awfully packed. It was standing room only. We continued walking along the main terminal building and cleared customs and immigration in what appeared to be almost no time. We followed the well-marked signs for the ride-hailing pickup point. And in Malaysia, they use Grab, which is the Uber equivalent. Make sure you download the Grab app to your phone and set up payment via the app. Grab even has a waiting lounge at the airport. It's a very very convenient and cost-effective way of getting around Asia. The 55 km or 38 mile journey that took about an hour from the airport to our hotel in downtown Kuala Lumpur was only 27 Australian dollars, less than 20 US dollars. >> Much, much, much later. >> In fact, just over 12 weeks later, we found ourselves back in Kuala Lumpur at the Movenpick Hotel, which is located just a few kilometers or miles from Kuala Lumpur Airport. This is one of the nicest hotels we stayed at during our trip and I'll do a full review of this hotel in the coming weeks. It was time for our return leg home to Melbourne. We set the alarm for 5:00 a.m., skipped breakfast, and caught the 6:00 a.m. complimentary shuttle bus from the hotel to Kuala Lumpur Airport. It didn't take long to drive to the airport and we arrived at the terminal around about 6:15. We made our way to the departure hall, which was located on the top level of the terminal building, and found the check-in desk for Malaysian Airlines. One of the things I really like about Malaysian Airlines and their check-in area at Kuala Lumpur Airport is it's all-in-one. So, all their economy international flights check in from the same area, which means that you've got oodles and oodles of uh agents working behind the desks. And it only took about 15 to 20 minutes to uh check in, even though it was quite a long line, it did move very very quickly. Although after five flights so far on this trip, I was a little bit tired of seeing and hearing Malaysian hospitality, even though I thought the service was generally pretty good. Once again, we made our way through the terminal building and cleared customs and immigration in almost record time. Once again, we rode on the train between the main terminal building and the satellite building. We both managed to get a seat this time around. It was just before 7:00 a.m. and as the train departed, we witnessed what was the beginning of a very nice dawn. There were a couple of Priority Pass affiliated lounges we could use in the satellite terminal and we decided to use the Travel Club Lounge closest to our departure gate. This is located on the mezzanine level of the terminal. It's quite a large lounge with a quiet, relaxed atmosphere. There's a large bar area where you can get alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, teas, and very nice barista-made coffees. A feature of the lounge that's always welcome is large panoramic windows giving excellent view across the airport and its tarmac. And there was a nice filtered early morning light. It felt such a shame that we were going home. The lounge was very close to our departure gate and we could see our Malaysian Airlines A330-900 neo at the departure gate. The lounge had a pretty good selection of both Western and Asian foods available. Some gluten-free and some vegetarian dishes were also available. There was a somewhat eclectic mix of ingredients and items on offer, especially considering it was breakfast time. I'm more used to the more traditional Western foods, I'm afraid. However, I've got to say some of the Malaysian desserts and fruits look particularly appealing. There was also a selection of different juices and the guava juice was delicious as well as different pastries and breads available. The focus of the lounge was on Malaysian cuisine, but somehow I just couldn't stomach chicken rendang this early in the morning. I did try the baked beans and scrambled eggs, but there was no bacon to be seen as this was a predominantly Muslim country. There were a number of halal dishes available as well. All the food looked and smelled delicious. There was a decent selection of soft drinks, juices, and water available as well as a coffee machine in addition to that barista station. I actually changed my mind on the chicken rendang and with rice it was absolutely delicious. Certainly enough to tide me over until we got fed on the plane. The lounge advertised that Wi-Fi was available, but my phone could never connect to it. So, I wasn't even able to run a speed test. It was a really nice, relaxing, and light-filled place to spend a couple of hours. Sadly, it was time to board our 12th and last trip of our 83-day journey around the world. Our final flight was a return flight to Melbourne on MH 129. The scheduled flight time was 7 hours and 40 minutes, more than an hour less than our initial journey from Melbourne to Kuala Lumpur 12 weeks ago. It was on the same plane type that brought us here, an Airbus A330-900 neo, and we were pretty much sitting in the same position in row 10, just the other side of the aisle in seats 10A and 10C. We had booked the extra legroom seats on our return leg home, so we pretty much knew exactly what we were in for in terms of legroom, the comfort of the seat, and the seat amenity including all the different storage areas the USB A and USB C charging points headphone jack and large entertainment screen. Again, I was really impressed by the legroom and the comfort of the seats. And at 115 Australian dollars per person, I think the extra legroom was worth it. As with the previous flight, the lack of individual air vents is the only criticism I can really make in regards to the cabin. I didn't show you on the previous flight, but the headrest is adjustable up and down and from side to side. And I don't think I saw anyone actually use these cup holders. These Recaro seats were quite comfortable and I would seek out an A330-900 on future medium to long-haul flights, especially across the Pacific. They're certainly much better and more comfortable than Qantas' current fleet to Bali or Japan. The 13.3-in high-definition entertainment screen was just as good as I remembered it from my previous flight. Unfortunately, on this occasion, the choice of movies was somewhat limited and given that I'd caught so many flights in the recent past, most of the ones I wanted to see I had already seen before. Everything about the experience so far was familiar and comfortable. I tried to connect my Bluetooth earbuds to the entertainment system, but unfortunately, no matter how many times I tried, it wouldn't connect. In the end, we pushed away from the gate about 10 minutes behind scheduled, but managed to arrive in Melbourne around 10 minutes before schedule. I can only presume that there was a favorable tailwind. >> Once we were in the air, the noise level was quite moderate. I ordered a gluten-free meal and Joe ordered a vegetarian lacto-ovo meal. They started being served around 55 minutes after take-off and we got our meals around about an hour and a half after take-off. That's quite a long time to be handing out special meals. The food didn't look that appetizing. It tasted okay, but it was lukewarm. The fruit was average and the yogurt was terrible. It was sour and didn't taste real. The gluten-free bread had the consistency of sawdust. I'd rate the meal around about three out of five. Unlike our previous long-haul flight that suffered massive turbulence, we got coffee on this flight. Unfortunately, it was terrible. It wasn't really worth the wait. We got proper plastic cutlery on this flight, but I've got to say that drink holder is actually useless. Complimentary Wi-Fi was advertised on this flight, but unfortunately, it wasn't working. The crew even tried to reboot the entertainment system a couple of times, but it didn't fix the problem and everyone had to restart their movies again. We received snacks around about 2 hours before landing. I received a sandwich made from the same sawdust consistency gluten-free bread. It was actually terrible. Jo received a vegetarian focaccia. She said it tasted okay and the consistency was quite good. But I think on the whole, the food on this flight was a lot more disappointing than our first flight. We received some ice cream after our snacks and they were quite good. We also received some nuts and drinks. I chose a French wine. It was particularly nice. In terms of a loo review, it was the same ratio as the previous flight, which meant often waiting to use the toilet. Although I think the level of cleanliness was a little bit better than our first flight and this bathroom was just as cramped as the one I reviewed on our trip 3 months earlier. >> [crying] >> Now, apart from children screaming and crying for the entirety of the journey, it was an uneventful flight. I would have liked to have filmed landing at Melbourne Airport, but I'm afraid it was just too dark. And I would rate this flight as a four out of five. And overall, the two journeys, MH148 and MH129, is a 4.25. I of five and I would definitely fly with Malaysian Airlines on this type of aircraft and on this route again. This has only been my first video in my new series of around the world in 83 days. It was an actually amazing adventure and Joe and I had such a marvelous time. Make sure you all subscribe so you don't miss a minute of it. So until next time as we start to explore Malaysia and Kuala Lumpur, you take care and bye now.

reviews.transcript_full: Hey everyone and welcome back to my channel! Today, I'm flying Cathay Pacific's economy class from Hong Kong to Taipei Today's aircraft is an A330-300, specifically the 33P configuration It features 293 economy seats with rows extending all the way back to row 76 Walking down the aisle, the layout is mostly a 2-4-2 configuration, tapering off to a 2-3-2 setup towards the very back Today I chose a window seat, seat 62K Let's take a look at the seat Right under the TV screen, there's a handy storage shelf that can hold your phone or small personal items The table is fairly standard, and I particularly love the pop-out cup holder you can use while the table stays closed The headrest is fully adjustable It slides up and down and the sides fold inwards to support your head You'll also find power outlets located under the seat and the headphone jack is right on the armrest In the seatback pocket, you'll find the standard safety card, disposable bag, and the in-flight magazine After a smooth night takeoff with incredible views over Hong Kong, I checked out the entertainment system Headsets were provided for the flight There's a solid library of movies, TV shows, and games I also like the interactive flight map a lot Similar to Starlux, you can zoom in and click on cities to see pictures of points of interest Cathay Pacific also adds some written details for each location, which is a nice touch and a great way to get excited about your trip while in the air Even on this flight under two hours, Cathay Pacific provides meal service Today's meal was chicken, rice, and bok choy The chicken was surprisingly flavorful and delicious I also took a quick look at the bathroom It was pretty standard Please note: the faucet is manual rather than automatic And interestingly, the bathroom featured an air vent inside, which I don't see very often Before long, we were starting our descent into Taipei Here's a quick tip: if you watched my Cathay Pacific business class video, you might remember I also used Qatar Airways Avios Welcome back! Beautiful evening
Here at Bangkok DMK We will be heading to Tokyo
with AirAsia X's A330 tonight AirAsia X has seperate check in row
from regular AirAsia Located at Row 5 at DMK T1 The flight tonight will depart 11:30 PM Ready for check in Check in for NRT Tokyo is showed on display And there's quite a lot of people today สวัสดีครับ Check in ญี่ปุ่นครับ How many person? two person visa in the back na okay your luggage check please only one? After security and immigration The flight will be at Gate 15 Which is located far left of terminal 1 lots of duty free shops on the way DMK has seen lots of improvements
over past few years terminal has been renovated recently and here's the gate and the boarding has been started announcements also made in Japanese Ex Garuda Indonesia plane Boarding has already started Boarding 18K boarding continues boarding completed despite 11 years old, cabin looks quite clean Seat Review Instructions are written both English and Malay A standard tray table without bi-folding now literature surprisingly, the sick bag is without any logo Whats wrong with AirAsia nowadays??? Saftey card, spicifically for A330 Santan food menu book Which we commonly found on normal AirAsia flights Signature bubble tea is also there Along with cup noodles and snacks There's also combo menu As well as blanket rental, for 150 THB There are also Duty Free items The legroom is not so tight but there is no seatrest briefing for passengers seated in emergency exit rows Windows shades are not electronic Welcome announcement And pre-departure check by crew began Flaps are already down, even without engine started Thai language announcement is followed saftey demo has started Captain's delay announcement announcement was made bi-langual pushback started engine startup engines are spooled up and ready for depart started taxi to lineup interior lights are switched off heading towards runway 21L takeoff beautiful view of Don Mueang and Lak Si area Don Mueang tollway Lak Si Intersection Flaps are retracted We are getting close to the sea city lights starts to fade Seatbelt signs are still on Chonburi city lights can be see in the distance Finally, seatbelt signs are off now and the cabin lights are turned on but turbulence hit again Captain: Cabin crew be seated
due to turbulence A few mins later, It was cleared again Then, the crew came to collect orders However, meals will not be served right now Instead, it will be served two and a half hours
before we land time for toilet review lock activated light the area is not too tight basin with trash bin cold/hot water faucet and soap dispenser tissues here and air conditioning above flush test not too loud back to seat for now Upon exiting the toilet
cabin lights are switched off It’s past midnight and
everyone else is asleep Sunrise is about to begin The stars can be seen even in camera As we continue, we started to see a faint morning glow Stars are still visible The glow grew brighter by the minute and the stars slowly faded away Meanwhile, the crew turned on the cabin lights
and began to collect breakfast orders Breakfast carts arrived the crew began to serve prebooked orders first after that they started selling the menu By this time, it was already bright outside Since I can't start my morning without coffee,
I decided to order one for 90 baht Fresh coffee was brewing The rich aroma filled the cabin Americano above 37,000 ft The crew continue collecting breakfast orders
throughout the cabin Bright sunshine glowed along the edge of the wing and beautiful clouds stretched across the bright sky later, the crew began collecting trash handed over my trash cup collecting trash throughout the cabin another bird in the distance no idea what flight that is We are approaching the Japanese archipelago the crew began taking orders for duty-free items finally, engine thrusts start to reduce the crew came to collect trash
once again then there was captain's announcement announcement was also made in Japanese Thank you announcement from the crew seatbelt signs are finally ON spoilers deployed mid-flight final saftey check by the crew clear view of spoilers deployed flaps deployed (out of focus) hold before final approach line up for final approach flaps extended further down geared down spoilers deployed again finally touched down after 6 hours flaps retract back Vietnam Airlines A321 from Da Nang Engine No.2 shutdown Narita Airport Terminal View My thought for this flight Considering AirAsia, you get a widebody,
more legroom with a half of price than full airliners like ANA biggest takeaway is no IFE one thing I want to complain is seat its quite hard, which makes
it harder to sleep

reviews.transcript_full: In today's video I'm in Siem Reap about to fly over to Saigon with Air Cambodia in their brand new ATR 72-600 I'll show you what the experience with this obscure Southeast Asian airline is like and delve a little bit into how Air Cambodia are currently stuck in a battle of geopolitics and tariffs  between two global superpowers and if you're wondering who I am, my name is Freddie and I make videos reviewing airlines and hotels as a hobby So far I've been to over 50 countries and flown over 70 airlines on my travels and all my trips are completely self-funded, unbiased and professional, or at least I like to think so so if any of that sounds interesting to you then subscribe and stick around! For now though, we need to check-in after arriving at the airport 1.5 hours before departure The queue was quite long and only for our flight as the next Air Cambodia flight was a few hours after ours also, they'd just told us the day before the flight time was being changed to two hours earlier so already off to a slightly shaky start Past security the airport is quite impressive for a city of this size It also still feels quite new having only opened in 2023 and during the 1.5 hours or so I spent here I only saw two aircraft operating, one of which was the one I was flying on so they've clearly built it for future capacity, or should I say, China have built it for future capacity because this airport and the much larger Techo Airport in the capital of Phnom Penh which opened last year were both built and financed by Chinese companies aka, the Chinese government this will become more relevant later in the video for now though, I noticed the terminal already seems to have a bit of a pigeon problem and I saw quite a few flying around like this, it was otherwise spotlessly clean despite the pigeons and very quiet though so I would say overall it's a pretty good little airport and these 8 flights were the only ones operating today They even have 2 outdoor terraces which I went out to hoping to see some planes but at the time literally the only plane at the whole airport was this private jet parked in a lonely spot out on the tarmac So without much to do I just headed to the gate, but they do have a foodhall with a Burger King if you're feeling peckish Here's our plane for today's flight, an ATR 72-600 which had been delivered to Air Cambodia just 4 months earlier and I like how the black paint around the cockpit makes it look like it's wearing sunglasses this plane incidentally is also one of my favourites to fly on It's loud and bumpy and cramped, but something about flying on a propeller plane always makes me happy After filming that little bit of the plane arriving I headed to the gate and after a very quick turnaround it was time to board... but before we step on board here are the stats and route map for today's flight where we departed exactly on time and arrived 20 minutes early in Ho Chi Minh City's Tân Sơn Nhất Airport with a total flight time of 1h 15m  Ho Chi Minh City, aka Saigon, aka thành phố Hồ Chí Minh is the biggest city in Vietnam with over 20 million people in the metropolitan area and a focus city for Air Cambodia being the most served city outside of Cambodia in their network Vietnam Airlines actually own a minority stake in Air Cambodia and they have a codeshare agreement Now that we're onboard I can report this cabin is actually pretty nice and almost has that new plane smell Legroom is nothing special and there's this annoying strut right where your feet want to go but it's quite comfy and has everything else you'd expect from a plane seat you can even recline, which actually isn't that common on ATR 72s There's a proper old-school inflight magazine and I was surprised to learn Air Cambodia is actually a Skytrax 3 star airline I didn't know they gave ratings to airlines with barely 6 aircraft Also to clear up any confusion you might have up to this point, Air Cambodia rebranded in January 2026 so most of their planes including the one I'm on look like this But all of their new planes going forward and branding will look like this: in case you end up wanting to book and find the logo looks different... somewhat related, Air Cambodia currently have a fleet of 6 aircraft, 3 being the ATR72-600 we're on today and they're also brand new with one being delivered in May 2025 and the other two in Jan 2026 they also surprisingly for an airline of their size have 10 Boeing 737MAXs on order and a whopping 20 COMAC C909s on order and not to get too bogged down by geopolitics... which is something I often like to do  both of those orders came during the peak tariff chaos last year which makes me think Cambodia copied a lot of other countries (like Vietnam to name just one) and ordered a bunch of Boeing aircraft to strike a better tariff deal because not long after announcing this deal Cambodia's tariff rate went from one of the highest in the world at 49% to a modest 19% and it just so happens that a certain US President is a big shareholder in Boeing and always goes on about how well he wants the company to do but Cambodia still wants to deepen their relationship with China so not to be outdone they ordered twice  as many Chinese-made COMAC C909s, becoming one of the few airlines outside of China to do so but... I digress there's an inflight magazine with some travel articles and most importantly a route map which I love to see but just to note, almost all of these are Codeshare flights, Air Cambodia actually only fly  This significantly smaller network... On the seat back there's also a QR code for "SkyTV" which I assume is some sort of inflight entertainment for your phone but the link didn't work and there's very limited info online about it so I wasn't sure if it actually exists or not This Bangkok Airways plane was literally the only other airline I saw here I also released a video last week of my flight here from Bangkok with them if you're looking for another video to watch Link in the description below and now for the inflight service, literally just a cup of water Now for the loo review... it's cramped after a relatively short bus ride to the terminal it was on to the infamous Saigon passport control queue which amazingly only took 20 minutes today in the past I've queued here for over 1.5 hours so this was a welcome surprise Vietnam recently started making people fill in a digital arrival card so maybe that's actually helped speed things up and that brings me to my final review, and overall I found Air Cambodia to be a pretty decent airline Their website and overall operations are pretty barebones, but the new ATR 72 was good to fly one and they certainly have an interesting future ahead as they go from the 6 planes they currently operate  to the thirty new planes they've ordered in the last year and with the brand new airports they've built in the last few years with the help of China then who knows maybe they'll end up becoming a real player in the world of Southeast Asian Aviation for now though, I'll put them at a 5/10 on my airline tier list as they really are just a middle of the road airline but that's it for this video, like and subscribe if you enjoyed, leave a comment if any questions and if you enjoy the videos I make then you could even become a channel member no real perks but it would be much appreciated and it would help pay for future videos too thanks a lot for watching and good bye!

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome back Travel Bestie. Today we're stepping on board Singapore Airlines Boeing 777 first class. I'll show you the cabin, where it spans the first class dining, [music] and test out that bed. This may be the final part of our Singapore Airlines first class adventure, but the trip is far from over. So, don't forget to subscribe because Hong Kong and our luxury journey home is coming next. Now, let's get on board. I almost missed my flight and I have never missed a flight in my life. So, the problem was I spent the morning relaxing in the private room, having champagnes, [music] and enjoying breakfast. And I completely underestimated how far the gate was. So, while I'm rushing on board, let me give you a few details of [music] the flight. Today we're flying Singapore Airlines SQ892. We're doing Singapore to Hong Kong our destination holiday on a Boeing 777-300. [music] It's a flight just over 4 hours and we are sitting in seat 1C on the airline's tiny [music] four-seat first class cabin. Let's see if the crew noticed that I was late. >> Oh, you're waiting for me. >> We didn't realize it was such a walk. >> [laughter] >> Wait, where am I? 1C? >> It's a seat today. >> Thank you. >> As a hit for this amenity for you. >> Thank you. Nothing humbles you faster than discovering the crew waiting for you. Thankfully, we were all laughing and importantly, we made it. After all that stress, let me give you a proper seat tour and let's take a breath and look at where we're going to spend the next few hours. So, we are in seat 1C, [music] which is one of only four first class seats in this entire Boeing 777. All seats are in one single row at the very front of the aircraft. Even though it's smaller than a 380, it does feel private. [music] Right, let me show you a little seat tour. So, we have our B&O headphones and [music] behind here is our menu. Then we have this big 24-in TV and in here, mirror. Hi. And then down here the storage, I've got my phone in here. There is an eye mask and some socks and slippers. Right here is space for your feet and then underneath is where you can store stuff. And then I'll just show you a little bit more on the armrest. reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm finally ticking off two things from my aviation bucket list. I'm flying Austrian Airlines's very first scheduled flight from Vienna, Austria to Bond Delgada, Portugal and the beautiful islands of the Assaurus. I've always wanted to visit this incredible destination and I've also always wanted to experience an inaugural flight. When Austrian announced this new route, it felt like the perfect opportunity to take both off my list at once. Today's flight is operated by Austrian Airlines on board an Airbus A320 Neo. With a flight time of around 5 hours and a distance of 3,770 km, this is one of Austrian's longest narrow body routes and certainly one of the most interesting ones. Our route today takes us west across Austria, southern Germany, and Switzerland before continuing over France, Spain, and Portugal and finally across the Atlantic Ocean towards the Aource. Since this flight departs early in the morning, I decided to spend the night at an airport hotel located just across the street from Vienna airport, which makes getting to the terminal incredibly convenient. One thing I really like about Vienna airport is how efficiently everything usually works from baggage drop off to security. I've rarely experienced long waiting times here. As a business class passenger or Star Alliance Gold member, you can simply drop off your baggage at a dedicated check-in counters. Economy class passengers can also use the self-service kiosks and print their baggage tags before heading to the baggage drop. Security at Vienna airport has recently been upgraded with new scanners, meaning you no longer have to remove liquids or electronics from your hand luggage. You're even allowed to bring drinking bottles again with a combined liquid volume of up to 2 L in your carry-on baggage. While making my way towards the gate, I noticed that the airport was very busy today, most likely because the European summer holiday season just had begun. Our flight today departs from gate F5. Since this is Austrian Airlines's inaugural flight to the Azour, there are a few small celebrations before boarding. Passengers could have commemorative photos taken with their own phones while the ground staff also took Polaroid pictures that everyone could keep as a souvenir. It was a nice little touch that immediately made the flight feel a bit more special. Boarding followed the usual Lufansa group priority system starting with home circle members and passengers requiring assistance followed by business class and star alliance gold members before econass passengers were invited to board. >> While boarding every passenger received a commemorative inaugural flight card together with an Austrian Airlines luggage tag. Another nice souvenir from today's flight. Since the aircraft was parked on a remote stand, we boarded one of the airborne buses. Interestingly, this was the first time I had seen a dedicated business class section inside one of Vienna airports buses, which was a pleasant surprise. after a short drive across the apron, our aircraft finally came into view. Today's aircraft with the registration Sulo Oscar is an Airbus A320 Neo delivered new to Austrian Airlines in 2022, making it just under 4 years old. It is currently powered by Pratt and Whitney tuban engines. Although Austrian plans to gradually replace this aircraft with new leap powered A320 news over the coming years. Whenever the weather cooperates, I try remote stand boarding. It gives you a much better opportunity to admire the aircraft and capture some nice photos before stepping on board. My seat today is 1A which is usually my preferred seat whenever I fly on the Airbus A320 family. Like most European airlines, Austrians business class uses standard economycl class seats with the middle seat blocked creating additional personal space. The aircraft features modern Ricaro slimline seats. While they certainly look more modern than the seats found on Austrian's older Airbus A320 aircraft, I personally find the older seats slightly more comfortable. The new seats are firmer, which becomes more noticeable on a longer flight like this one. >> They also don't feature adjustable headrests. >> The cabin itself, however, looks great. Thanks to Airbus modern airspace cabin, you get larger overhead bins that easily accommodate roller bags standing upright as well as pleasant LED wood lighting, making the cabin feel much brighter and more spacious than the previous generation. The safety demonstration was conducted in English only, while all other announcements throughout the flight were made in German, English, and some announcements also in Portuguese. Today's inaugural flight to Pontto Deada is completely full. So, it's time to get airborne. One thing you immediately notice after takeoff is just how quiet the Airbus A320 Neo is compared to the older A320. The new engines make a noticeable difference and create a much more pleasant cabin environment, especially on longer flights. Another thing worth mentioning is that there is no Wi-Fi or in-flight entertainment available on today's flight. So if you're planning to watch a movie or series, make sure to download it before departure. Austrian and the Lufansza group have already announced that all the aircraft will gradually receive Starlink internet starting later in 2026, which will be a very welcome upgrade. As always, I prefer sitting in the first row whenever I fly on the Airbus A320 family. It offers the most leg room in the cabin, although you do have the bike head wall directly in front of you, and all your hand luggage must be stored in the overhead bins during taxi takeoff and landing. There is a USBA charging port integrated into the armrest, although unfortunately there are no power outlets available. Some of Austrian's newer A320 Neo aircraft have already been fitted with USBC ports as well. Every seat also comes with an individual reading light and personal air vent. Passengers seated outside the first row will find the USB port underneath the seat in front of them. If you're flying in one of Austrian's older Airbus A320 aircraft, however, you won't find USB charging at all. The tray table is stored inside the armrest and simply folds out when needed. It's sturdy enough for working or enjoying a meal, although it's rather small. Since we're departing in the morning, breakfast is served shortly after takeoff. Breakfast has never really been my favorite airline meal, and today's option didn't change my mind. The main course consisted of an omelette with sausages and cottage cheese, a combination that I personally didn't think worked well together. There was also fresh fruit, a small selection of cold cuts and a braid roll accompanied by tea, coffee, and a wide selection of drinks. Passengers traveling in economy class can purchase food and drinks from the onboard menu. Prices are fairly reasonable, although I certainly wouldn't call them cheap. Let's also have a quick look at the lavatory. The front lavatories normally research for business class passengers while the lavatories at the rear of the aircraft are shared with economy class. Inside you will find everything you would expect including soap, paper towels, toilet paper, toilet seat covers and even a changing table. The only thing I noticed was that the floor felt slightly sticky but apart from that everything appeared clean and wellmaintained. The real highlight of today's flight, however, was without a doubt the cabin crew. Business class passengers were personally greeted by name. And throughout the flight, the crew frequently checked whether anyone wanted another drink or anything else. At one point, we even noticed that I looked a little tired and kindly offered me a pillow without me even asking. Small gestures like that really make a difference and show how attentive the crew was throughout the flight. After around 5 hours over Europe and the Atlantic Ocean, the dream coastline of S Miguel finally appeared. The approach into Pontel Gada is absolutely beautiful and a fantastic way to begin a holiday in the Assaurus. I also had the chance to chat with several of the flight attendants and you could really tell how excited they were to be part of Austrian's very first flight to the Assaurus. They really helped make this inaugural flight feel like something special. A special mention also goes to our captain. Rather than simply making the standard announcements, he spoke enthusiastically about the source, sharing some of his personal recommendations on places to visit and restaurants to try. It was refreshing to hear a captain who clearly enjoyed flying this route and was excited to introduce passengers to the destination. Upon arrival, quite a few photographers were already waiting at the apron to capture Austrian's first ever arrival. I was secretly hoping for a traditional water cannon salute, but unfortunately some hopes have to wait for another time. After leaving the airdrop, every passenger received a small welcome kiss from the airport. The terminal itself is quite compact and within just a minute or two you are already standing in the baggage claim area. Immediately outside back at Reclaim are the desks of the various rental car companies. So collecting my rental car only took a few minutes before I was on my way towards my accommodation. Before heading off, let's have a quick look inside the welcome bag. The bag itself is quite nice and something you could easily reuse afterwards. Inside there was a delicious little cake, some tourist information, a miniature bottle of a soran pineapple liquor, and a small keychain. Quite unusually for a European medium hall flight, Austrian also handed out amenity kits on board. I'm sure these were exclusive to today's inaugural flight. The bag itself was much simpler than the ones used on Austrian's long hole flights, but inside you will find the same amenities, including socks, an eye mask, ear plugs, and a toothbrush kit. A week later, it's already time to leave the Assaurus and head back to Vienna. Honda Delgada airport is a relatively small airport, so during busy departure periods, it can get a little crowded. When I arrived, check in hadn't opened yet, so some waiting was unavoidable. Once the count was open, business class check-in was quick and efficient. There was a small queue at the security, but nothing that caused any real delays. The fast track lane was not available this time. After security, you are already inside the compact departure area. There are a few small shops and cafes, but don't expect a huge selection. One thing that's also missing is an airport launch, so business class passengers don't have lounge access before departure. Boarding started right on schedule, beginning with families traveling with young children, passengers requiring assistance, and business class passengers. One thing I really enjoyed here was boarding on foot. There are no track bridges or buses, so you simply walk across the apron to your aircraft. It's only a short walk, but it gives you fantastic views of the aircraft and the surrounding airport. Today's aircraft with the registration Sudo Lenda is another Airbus Escene delivered to Austrian Airlines in 2022. Once again, I'm seated in 1A. Luckily, the seat next to me remained empty, giving me the entire row to myself. However, there is one disadvantage to sitting in the first row. Since the tray table is stored inside the fixed armrests, they can be folded upwards. In the other rows, the movable armrest allows you to stretch out across all three seats if the row is empty, making it very comfortable for a rest. That's unfortunately not possible in row one. Shortly after boarding, refreshing tissues were handed out. >> We are now ready for takeoff. >> To depart from Potter de Gada, aircraft usually have to backtrack along the runway before turning around for takeoff. After waiting for another departing aircraft, it was finally our turn to leave their source behind. Unlike the outbound flight, today's service included lunch. Passengers could choose between a meat and vegetable strudel or a vegetarian option consisting of breaded mushrooms with cauliflower. I went with the first option and while the presentation could have been better, the important part is always the taste. And this meal was very good. I really enjoyed it and found it considerably better than the breakfast served on the outbomb flight. And Austrian's coffee didn't disappoint either. It remains one of my favorite coffees served by any European airline. Let's quickly check the lavatory here as well. Everything essential was available once again, including soap paper, towels, and toilet paper. The overall cleanliness was good, although there were a few stains on the mirror and a slightly sticky floor. Again, nothing major, but worth mentioning. Before landing, the crew handed out Austrian chocolates on both flights. The small tradition that nicely rounds off the onboard service. So, was Austrian Airlines inaugural flight to the Assaurus worth it? Without a question, the highlight of both flights was the outstanding cabin crew. They were enthusiastic, attentive, and incredibly friendly throughout the journey. Visitor's passengers were addressed by name. Drinks were proactively refilled and even small gestures like offering me a pillow without asking made an amazing experience. Combined with the enjoyable conversations I had with a few crew members, this was easily one of the best mediumhole service experience I've had. For me, the cabin crew deserves a well-earned 10 out of 10 points. The food was a bit more mixed. The breakfast on the outbound flight was acceptable, but the combination of flavors simply wasn't for me. I would give the meal a 6 out of 10. The lunch on the return flight, however, was really good and something I would happily order again. That one deserves a solid 8 out of 10. The seat is probably my biggest criticism. Like on most European airlines, business class is simply a standard economic class seat with the middle seat blocked. While the additional space certainly helps, I personally find Austrian's newer recover slimline seats a little too firm for a flight lasting around 5 hours. For shorter flights, they're fine, but on one of Austrian's longest narrow body routes, I started to notice the firmness after a while. For me, the seat gets 4.5 out of 10. Cabin cleanliness was generally good. Apart from the slightly sticky floor and a few stains inside the laboratory on the return flight, I really didn't have anything to complain about. The rest of the cabin was mostly clean and wellmaintained. So, I'll give clean a 7 out of 10. The only other real downside was the lack of onboard Wi-Fi. For a flight of around 5 hours, internet access would certainly have been appreciated. Fortunately, Austrian aircraft will gradually receive stalling internet beginning in the second half of 2026. So, this should improve considerably over the next few years. Finally, let's talk about value for money. I paid €880 for this roundtrip business class ticket. I think it represents good value considering this was Austrian's inaugural non-stop service to their source combined with launch access in Vienna, priority services, excellent cabin crew, and an overall smooth experience. I'm quite happy with what I received for the price. Would I fly this route again? Absolutely. And I also will fly this route again if Austrian keeps the service. For now, this service is only offered during the summer month. Not only because I really enjoyed the flight, but also because the Assaurus turned out to be an incredible destination that I can highly recommend visiting. If you enjoyed this video or found it helpful, I'd really appreciate if you'd left a like and subscribe. Every week I share new travel content, flight reviews, or better reviews from around the world. Thank you very much for watching and I'll see you in the next one.
