reviews.transcript_full: Welcome back. Today's a big day. We're finally welcoming American Airlines to the channel. Join me as I board Airbus A321neo in first class on a flight from Phoenix to Charlotte where we'll show you the seat and service on this flight. This is one of the newest aircraft in their fleet and it's equipped with their latest first class product, but it's missing a key feature you'll find on Delta and United. This will be a good test of American as we fly out from their hub in Phoenix to Charlotte. Plus, stick around and we'll tell you how much we paid for today's ticket and you can decide if it's worth the upgrade. >> [music] >> Welcome to Arizona. We're starting today at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport. There are two main terminals and they're connected landside via the SkyTrain. Terminal 3 is newer and serves Alaska, Delta, JetBlue, and United. Phoenix Sky Harbor is a hub for American and Southwest. Terminal 4 is their home along with all the international flights. American's checking counters are located on level two of the terminal. First class passengers have access to priority check-in and bag drop. And our ticket includes two free checked bags of the 70 lb each. There was a bit of confusion here this morning as they tried to charge me for my bags. So, know what your ticket includes. Sometimes you have to be your own champion. With that out of the way, let's head up to security. All gates in Terminal 4 are connected so you can go through any of the four security checkpoints. The airport posts wait times so you can pick the best option. While the airport was busy, security was very quick today. As is pretty standard with US domestic first class, lounge access is not included. And today, this lounge is so full they won't take day passes either. So, while you can buy a day pass, don't always count on them working. There are several other lounges in Terminal 4 accessible with Priority Pass or American Express Platinum Card. We recently did a lounge showdown in Phoenix and we'll leave a link to that in the description if you'd like to see more. We didn't make it into the Escape Lounge last time we were here, so let's go check it out. American Express has both a Centurion and Escape Lounge located next to gate B21 in Terminal 4. You do need to choose wisely, though. Once you enter one, you cannot swap to the other on the same day. There was quite a line for the Centurion Lounge this morning, and based on our last visit, I'm not surprised. But, no one was in line for the Escape Lounge, and I walked right in. Access is granted to American Express Platinum, Centurion, and select Delta card holders. This is also Priority Pass Lounge. Alternatively, you can buy a day pass for $45 per person in advance or $60 at the door. This lounge is open from 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. There's a large bar, most of the drinks are free. Premium spirits are available for purchase. The buffet had a good selection. We were visiting during the changeover from breakfast to lunch. The food comes from the same kitchen as the Centurion Lounge, and in our experience, it's largely the same. There's a self-service espresso machine and drip coffee available. This isn't a huge lounge, but there was plenty of open seating. I settled in a high-back chair with views of the final approach path. There are also some dining tables near the buffet. This lounge features two single occupancy restrooms, which are large. However, there are no showers in the Escape Lounge. The seating capitalized on the great views, and I had a bit too much fun watching the planes land. I even managed to catch our plane. I think the views are actually better here than they were in the Centurion Lounge. Wi-Fi is free, and speeds were decent. The password is posted throughout the lounge. When I first came in around 9:30 a.m., it was a little busy, but this lounge was not hard to find a seat. And actually, it emptied out around 10:00 a.m., being very quiet and pleasant the rest of the time. Overall, I was really impressed with the Escape Lounge. This was the first time I've been in one. When we did our lounge showdown in Phoenix, it was around the same time of the day and week. While the airport was busy, the lounge was calm and quiet. Overall, it was comfortable and dare I say I preferred it to the Centurion Lounge. It was less crowded, the food was pretty much the same and the staff were great. >> [music] >> That was a good lounge, is it? But now it's time to board. Sky Harbor is large, so make sure you plan plenty of time to get to your gate. Our 4-hour and 17-minute flight today takes us 1,771 miles from Phoenix, Arizona to Charlotte, North Carolina on board an Airbus A321 neo in first class. Boarding is done in zones with American's premium loyalty program members following after pre-boarding. First class boards in zone one. The first class cabin has 20 seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration. There are also 176 main cabin seats in a 3-3 configuration. 18 of these are main extra. These first class seats are 20 inches wide, have 36.5 inches of pitch and a recline of 5 inches. Overall, the legroom is decent, but similar to other domestic first class products. The headrest is adjustable both up and down and the wings fold in. Each seat has overhead air vents and reading lights. The center armrest flips up to reveal a thin storage compartment. You'll find a universal power outlet in here. Between the seats is a small drink table and an extension table pops out of the front for even more space. There is a USB A port located on the seatback in front along with the device holder. The power output here is low, so if you want to fast charge, use the universal outlet instead. The tray table comes out of the outer armrest and is sturdy. It includes an integrated device holder, which can work in both the half open and fully open modes. >> [music] >> You may have noticed there are no seatback screens. Since there's no IFE, there's plenty of room under the seat in front of you. This is often where some Some the IFE equipment is installed. During the boarding, the flight attendant came by for a pre-departure beverage service. It's a hot one today, so I'm keeping it simple with water, but you can choose other beverages. Boarding wrapped up early and we pushed back. I will admit the red, white, and blue mood lighting was cool. >> [music] [music] >> As we get up to altitude, let's check out the onboard entertainment. As mentioned earlier, there's no IFE system on the plane. American has a BYOD approach and when connected to the onboard Wi-Fi, you can access a library of movies, series, live TV, and audio content. The selection is comparable with other carriers, although they only had partial seasons of TV shows. You do have to watch two long commercials before each video, but the playback was smooth. We had read that they had a moving map feature, but for the life of me, I couldn't find it. I ended up improvising with my phone. Internet is now free for Advantage program members. Download speeds were good, upload was serviceable. Once we leveled off, the flight attendant came by to take drink and meal orders front to back. Service then started with a hot towel, which is always a nice touch in a premium cabin. Drinks and warm nuts came out first, since our baseline drink is a G&T, that's what I got started with. 30 days before your flight, American lets you pre-order your meal online. There were six options to choose from and options for special meals. It's funny that the short rib was on here in two different ways. Options. I ordered the short rib with broccolini and grilled onions. I guess the problem with two similar dishes is I got the other one when I was on board. Not the end of the world, but a mix-up nonetheless. So, my actual meal was the short rib with a twice baked potato. This came with a warm roll, Mediterranean salad of artichoke and stuffed peppers, and a charred romaine salad. In another small mix-up, I did see my neighbor got dressing for the salad and it seems to miss my tray. The meal was a good size, the beef was nice and tender. I was surprised to find two side salads and a roll. The flavors were good, but the presentation wasn't going to win any awards. You may notice something was missing from the tray. Dessert. I was surprised to find out that American actually serves this separately and you get a choice, so that's nice. This is something you typically see in long-haul business class and not in domestic first class. The choices were a fruit and cheese plate or chocolate chip ice cream. I opted for the fruit and cheese plate just to try something different. It was nice to get a choice and for a not sweet option, though the grapes had seen better days. These seats are very similar to the WestJet flight that we reviewed a few weeks ago. We'll put a link in the description if you'd like to check that one out and see how it compares. We're only about halfway through, so let's check out the lavatory. There's one forward lav for the first class cabin. These are a bit small for tall folks like me. I'm 6'4" for reference, but this is a typical narrow-body lav and it was kept clean during our flight. The crew were quick to start service and efficient with the meal, but didn't come through much until we approached Charlotte. I ordered a coffee right after lunch and my empty cup kept me company until our descent. Enjoy the views and I'll see you on the ground to wrap things up. So, that's it. That was our first American Airlines first class flight on this channel on the proper mainline American Airlines. Uh I thought the service was pretty good. Food was better than I expected. The seat was comfortable for a flight of this length. There's plenty of storage and I found the seat was spacious. However, service in the second half of the flight was not proactive. We really didn't see much of the crew after the meal. So, was this premium flight worth the upgrade? Price-wise, American was not the cheapest for this route. My one-way first class ticket connected in Charlotte on my way to Washington, D.C. Delta and United were both about $150 less for this first class ticket from Phoenix to DCA, also with connections. Since Phoenix is an American hub, the other carriers are likely actively undercutting American here. The lack of seatback screens is a unique choice for American. The bring your own device approach is fine and the media selection was decent, but it's not competitive with Delta and United. What do you prefer? Using your own device or having a seatback screen? Let us know in the comments. So, back to our question. Is it worth it? Well, there wasn't anything that made American stand out enough to justify the higher price. Given the choice, we'd probably pick the lower fare on another carrier. The products are just that similar. Thanks for making it to the end. If you enjoyed today's flight, please give us a thumbs up and subscribe to keep up to date with our latest content. You can also check out our channel memberships here and on Patreon, where we post exclusive content that doesn't quite fit the main channel. Thank you for watching. On to the next adventure.

It's cold, so cold!🥶 【✈️Second flight】Singapore to Bali Denpasar is about a 2.5-hour flight.Changi transfers are known to be smooth!However, be careful of the time if you have to move between terminals⚠️ 【🎧In-flight announcement】The cabin crew manager and crew will guide you.The flight time is about 2 hours and 20 minutes...we will be departing shortly 【💤Sleeping soundly on the plane...】It's an early morning flight, so it's finally time to sleep.It 's 7am.Breakfast has been served.This is apple pancakes.Yes, pancakes. 【📍Destination is Bali】One of Indonesia's leading resorts, known as the "Island of the Gods"! Ubud is full of attractions, from rice terraces and beaches to temples. 🌴 The time difference between Bali and Japan is only 1 hour! Being able to enjoy yourself without jet lag is one of the reasons for its popularity. [💱Currency Information] The currency of Indonesia is the Rupiah (IDR)... The digits are large, so a conversion app is essential! [ 🛬Landing Soon] What I can see below is... Bali! Yes, we have arrived! [🌴Finally in Bali] The buildings are interesting! It looks like a fire station! It looks like a fire station (lol) Wow! Amazing✨ [📍Ngurah Rai International Airport] It features a design that incorporates traditional Balinese architecture! From the moment you step off the plane, you are in full tropical mood🌺Flowers on the trees! 🌸In Bali, the cloth and flowers wrapped around trees are a cultural expression of faith that shows respect to the gods. It really feels like the tropics🌴Now , have my luggage arrived safely? Like this picture! [🎨 An artistic airport] The airport is like an art museum, with rows of Balinese Hindu sculptures and paintings inside, so you won't get bored while waiting ✨ There are many traditional items. For immigration, you need e-Arrival and... something about "All Indonesia" 《roughly speaking lol》 All Indonesia is for entry procedures... The visa we got was, well... it's all that, so Visa On... We have a QR code, so this way, this way! Yes, we were able to do it ourselves at that machine over there! [✅ Passing through automatic gates] So easy! We'll be passing through in less than a minute. There's a duty-free shop here. They have champagne and stuff 🍾 Yes, apparently people who flew with Singapore Airlines get this 🎁 《Got one!✌️》 I'll try to get as much water as possible 💧 I'm waiting for my luggage for about 30 minutes now ⏳ Too long! Too long! 【😤 Tired of waiting】 That's why I think they had water and snacks earlier 《Makes sense》 It's so long... Okay, I made it out safely! Oh, there's a Burger King 🍔 Amazing! I'm going to exchange all the money I got from the tax refund earlier into Indonesian Rupiah 💱 So, the All Indonesian QR code I have now... I guess I'll show it after I get my luggage first 【💡 Show at the exit】 Yes, there's a Starbucks and a burger shop called "Johnny Rocket". I'm checking out Starbucks right away (lol). Look, it's from Toy Story... Huh? It 's amazing! Isn't it huge?! 【Boom!】 Wait, isn't this not Toy Story? Isn't that Toy Story? It's just a statue in Bali! The colors are so Toy Story-like, it's a miracle of color combination , but it's cute! I've never seen anything like it! Wow, it's amazing! It seems that everyone who gets picked up by the hotel (transfer) is picked up here, but we're using the ride-hailing app "Grab" 🚗 so we'll just go straight ahead . Yes, we've booked a Grab EV for today! It's an electric car ⚡ [💡 How to order Grab] There's a dedicated "Grab Lounge" at the airport! Follow the signs and it's about a 5-minute walk 📱 Yes, this is my first time in an EV! It's a car brand I've never seen before, but it's so beautiful ✨ That's right! [🚗 Comfortable drive] Grab is super convenient for getting around Bali... The fare is confirmed in advance through the app, so it's safe! We've arrived! [🏨 Hotel arrival] [To be continued in the next Bali episode...!] Yes! So, we're safely on our way to our hotel in Bali, riding in a beautiful Grab EV! 🚗🌴✨This time, I shared my flight report on a late-night flight via Singapore using Singapore Airlines. What did you think? ✈️Honestly, I was a little tired from the long journey (lol), but the in-flight service and entertainment were fantastic, and Changi Airport, where I had my layover, had so many exciting spots that the journey itself was a big entertainment experience! 🎬And above all, this "early morning arrival" schedule! 🌅 I slept on the plane and woke up in Bali, and being able to move around at 100% full power from the first day is the best route for travelers who want to make the most of their limited time! 🔥If you are planning to go to Bali from Japan with Singapore Airlines, please use this video as a reference when planning your schedule! Oh, and don't forget to pre-register for e-VOA (electronic visa of arrival)! As I showed in the video, you can enter the country in just one minute, so I highly recommend it! 📱💨Okay , so the next video will be...the real "Bali Island" series finally begins! 🌺If this video made you think even a little bit, "I want to go to Bali!" or "This was helpful in choosing a flight!", please subscribe to the channel and give it a thumbs up (like button)! 👍I read all of your comments, so please feel free to write anything you're curious about or any thoughts you have! 💬✨See you next time in the Bali Island series! This is Food Joe signing off! Bye-bye! 👋✨Hotel hints👀

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome aboard Emirates’ new Boeing 777 Business Class The video starts with a tour of Emirates' Business Class Lounge  Emirates offers one of the world's best Business Class products  This video covers the full Emirates Business Class experience   This includes Business Class meals, amenities, IFE & flat bed The Emirates Boeing 777 takes us from Dubai to Brussels Keep watching till the end for some stunning drone footage Our journey starts at Atlantis The Royal Hotel in Dubai Emirates Business Class includes free airport transfers  The complimentary limousine service adds extra comfort Emirates operates from Terminal 3 at Dubai International Airport  T3 features a dedicated check-in area for premium passengers  Emirates Business Lounges are located throughout Terminal 3 The airlines' flagship lounge is housed in concourse B I've previously published a full video tour of this lounge The lounge is huge, but still quite crowded during peak hours Emirates’ lounges in Dubai are open 24 hours a day. Our flight to Brussels is departing from Concourse C Emirates also operates a Business Lounge at Concourse C   The lounge features Emirates’ signature Arabian design Large curved windows offer views of the airport apron Comfortable leather chairs fill the spacious seating area The lounge includes a dedicated dining area with buffet The buffet offers a wide selection of hot and cold dishes Guests reviews.transcript_full: Planning a trip to Asia?  Korean Air is one of the leading airlines connecting North America with destinations across  South Korea, Japan, China, Southeast Asia, and beyond.  Korean Air offers non-stop service from several major cities in the United States and Canada,  making travel to Asia convenient and accessible.  Most journeys connect through Seoul, Incheon Airport, known for efficient transfers, clear  signage, and a traveler-friendly layout.  If your itinerary includes more than one destination in Asia, Korean Air's extensive regional  network can make planning easier.  Economy class is known for comfortable seating, adjustable headrest, and generosity legroom  on many long haul aircraft.  Meals and beverages are included, with both Korean and international menu options available  on many flights.  Long haul aircraft feature personal entertainment screens, with movies, TV shows, music, and  games.  USB charging is also available on many aircraft.  Blankets, pillows, and headphones are typically provided to help make long journeys more comfortable.  Korean Air is a strong option for travelers heading to Seoul, Tokyo, Osaka, Bangkok,  Manila, Ho Chi Minh City, and many other destinations throughout Asia.  For more airline reviews and helpful travel tips for economical international flights,  stay tuned with ASAP Tickets.

Each rotation of the jet engines gradually accelerates. The deep majestic roar is not merely mechanical noise, but the rhythm of life awakening. Under the light of a new day, the metallic ship stretches its wings, gliding powerfully along the runway, ready to leave the ground behind and conquer the vast sky. >> [music] >> But the sky is never a path paved only with roses. When darkness suddenly descends, black clouds swirl as if to swallow the space whole. Lightning streaks across the heavens, illuminating heavy raindrops that hammer against the windows, creating a dramatic symphony of nature. Inside the cabin, the atmosphere hangs suspended in anxiety with expectant gazes fixed toward the windows. The intense turbulence challenges the nerves of those aboard, turning every passing second into a slow-motion sequence, a haunting testament to human endurance against the forces of nature. Amidst the heart of the chaos, the cockpit is another world, a place where composure reigns supreme. The glow from the control panel illuminates the faces of the pilots who remain in deep concentration, their hands steady [music] on the controls. Every button pressed and every parameter monitored is the result of tireless training, enabling them to comprehend and steer the ship through the harsh gusting winds. It is the perfect fusion of advanced technology [music] and the iron resolve of those who command the skies.

[music] Today's Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner is whole number VN-A782, which was delivered to Vietnam Airlines almost 7 years ago. Boarding began right on time with business class passengers, SkyTeam Elite members, and passengers requiring special assistance invited to board first. It's certainly different from the darker color schemes used by many airlines and the colors tie in nicely with the airline's lotus branding and Vietnam's natural landscapes. While the color scheme isn't personally my favorite, it does create a calm yet inviting atmosphere and gives the cabin a unique identity that sets it apart from many other airlines. >> [music] >> My seat for today's flight is 5B. The seat controls and IFE remote are conveniently located on the right hand side panel, making them easy to access throughout the flight. While there isn't a lot of dedicated storage, there's enough space to keep smaller personal items such as a phone, passport, or pair of headphones within easy reach. >> [music] [music] >> After settling into my seat, the cabin crew came through the cabin with refreshing cold towels followed by a selection of welcome drinks to begin the journey. >> [music] [music] >> In terms of sleeping comfort, the seat converts into a fully flat bed measuring approximately 75 to 78 inches in length, which should be ample space for most [music] passengers. IFE screen is about 15 inches and the airline provides noise canceling headphones. [music] >> [music] >> There is a wide selection entertainment options including Western movies, >> [music] >> series, music, and games. >> [music] >> As we pushed back and made our way toward the runway, my initial impression of the cabin was [music] very positive. The flight attendants were attentive and professional throughout the boarding process, taking particular care to assist the elderly passengers [music] on board. >> [music] >> Before I dive into meal service, I like to show the amenity kit provided. These days, Vietnam Airlines provide Samsonite branded kits which includes amenities like a toothbrush, lotion, [music] and ear plugs among others. In addition, a blanket, slippers, and small pillow are provided for [music] maximum comfort. Interestingly, the airline provides three lunch [music] choices. The first is Korean followed by Western or Asian. Today, I opted for the Western option. It consisted of smoked salmon, thinly sliced beef tenderloin, and a small salad topped with honeyed pears. >> [music] >> Of the two appetizer courses, I genuinely enjoyed the smoked salmon and beef tenderloin. While the kind of pastes were light and enjoyable, the only one that really stood out to me was the prosciutto with jam as the other flavors were quite subtle. >> [music] [music] >> And finally, the main course came out. It was a small cut of beef steak topped with hollandaise sauce surrounded with grilled vegetables and potatoes. By this time, I was actually quite full. Here we have a standard Boeing 787 lavatory with a small selection [music] of amenities. As the cabin lights dimmed, I turned my seat into a fully flatbed for the rest of the flight. [music] I was definitely feeling quite full after that meal, but hey, that's part of being on vacation, right? >> [music] >> Just when I thought I couldn't eat another bite, the crew came around with a small terrine of peanuts before landing. >> [music] >> Overall, I have very few complaints about this flight. Considering the value for money, I think Vietnam Airlines delivered an excellent business class experience, at times even surpassing [music] some of the five-star airlines I've flown with. If I had to point out one minor criticism, it would be the cabin's color [music] palette. Personally, the many shades of olive aren't really to my taste, although they do give the cabin a calm and distinctive atmosphere. From this point on, can I say my transit through Tan Son Nhat Airport was smooth sailing? Eh, not exactly. But in the end, I made it to [music] Phu Quoc Airport, and that's what matters most. Be sure to join me in the next video as I make my way through Tan Son Nhat Airport's Terminal 3, >> [music] >> where I'll visit three of the airport's four lounges and share what's really like to connect through Ho [music] Chi Minh City. I genuinely think Vietnam Airlines is one of the most underrated airlines in the region, and I hope you have a chance to experience [music] it for yourself one day. Also fast schon ähnlich wie in der wie in der Business Class und der Hintermann davon dann gar nichts mitbekommt, wie ich meinen Sitz verstelle. Also, wenn man einen Nachteil finden möchte, dann ist das hier definitiv der größte Nachteil an diesem Sitz hier. Ansonsten aber bin und bleibe ich sehr zufrieden. Dieser Sitz liefert eine echte Komfortverbesserung. In der Echo dauert es jetzt eine Weile, bis der Service beginnt. Zeit genug, um sich mit dem Inflight Entertainment auseinanderzusetzen. Das ICE System von Emirates ist definitiv nicht das übersichtlichste, aber dafür eines der umfangreichsten Systeme auf den Markt. Hier findet jeder, also wirklich jeder, hundertprozentig irgendwas, um sich den Flug über zu beschäftigen. Das Alter der Kabine ist hier aber am besten zu spüren. Das System ist recht langsam und c, aber wenn dann mal ein Film oder sowas läuft, dann ist alles in Ordnung. Das funktioniert. Gut, finde ich, dass direkt am Sitz eine Universalsteckdose verbaut ist. Das findet man in der Economy Class wirklich selten und ist ein echter Vorteil im Vergleich zu anderen Fluggesellschaften. Was uns zum Thema Internet bringt, kostenloses Messaging, also für WhatsApp und so weiter. Das gibt es bei Eirates. Ich kann mich also einfach hier kurz einloggen und schon funktioniert Nachrichten schreiben ohne Probleme. Größere Internetpakete habe ich auf diesem Flug nicht gebraucht. Die liefern hier aber auch kein wirklich schnelles Internet. Auf meinem Premium Economy Flug sieht das komplett anders aus. Das hier entwickelt sich gerade eher zu einem Vergleich zwischen alter und neuer Kabinausstattung, aber beim Thema Internet ist es wirklich ein ganz deutlicher Unterschied. Es gibt hier schnelles und zuverlässiges Starlink mit absolut ordentlichen Geschwindigkeiten und kostenlos für alle an Bord. Ja, Internet im Flugzeug ist absolut nicht das Wichtigste, aber ich habe hier ganz entspannt mein nächstes YouTube- Video geschnitten und eine 15 GB Datei hochgeladen. Das war dann das Video, was absolut verrückt ist, dass das funktioniert und eine richtig starke Verbesserung im Vergleich zum sonstigen Standard. Das verbaute Entertainment System ist hier deutlich größer und ebenfalls moderner. Die Inhalte bleiben die gleichen, die blöden Kopfhörer auch, aber hier kann ich meine eigenen Bluetooth Kopfhörer, also z.B. die AirPods ganz einfach mit dem System verbinden. Das wollte am Anfang zwar nicht ganz so wie ich das wollte, ging dann aber und lief auch den ganzen Flug problemlos. Doch das ist, finde ich, eine ganz entscheidende Verbesserung. Und so bleibt jetzt natürlich noch das Essen. In der Economy Class kommt alles auf einem Tablett. Bisschen schade, es gibt Fisch oder Fleisch. Keine vegetarische Option, die müsste man vorbestellen. Das ist, finde ich, vor allem deswegen schade, weil ich das Gefühl habe, dass gerade vegetarische Gerichte in der Economy Class oft die besseren sind. Mein Essen sollte Hühnchen mit Kartoffelpüree darstellen, was weder optisch noch geschmacklich toll war. Also das ja macht satt, aber das geht leider wirklich besser. Dazu gibt es ein Getränk nach Wahl. Danach kommt die Besatzung dann noch einmal mit heißen Getränken durch, was am Ende damit ein überschaubarer, aber effizienter Service ist. In der Premium Economy wird ähnlich wie in der Business Class das erste Getränk sowie der Essenswunsch for Service Beginn abgefragt. Wenn es dann soweit ist, kommt auch hier alles auf einem Tablett, aber mit richtigem Geschirr und das Essen ist qualitativ deutlich näher an Business Class Essen als an der Economy Class. Auch hier gibt es wieder nur Fleisch oder Fisch zur Auswahl. Die Qualität ist aber eben ein ganz entscheidendes Stück besser. Danach kommen auch hier heiße Getränke von Hand serviert direkt aus der Gelly. Dazu ein bisschen Schokolade und die Info, dass ich natürlich jederzeit gerne Bescheid sagen kann, falls ich noch irgendwas brauche. Ein Wort noch zur Toilette der Vorständigkeit halber. Hier profitiert man auf beiden Flügen davon, dass die Trip7 schon etwas älter ist. Neuerdings werden Flugzeugtoiletten ja nur noch für Zwerge gebaut. Hier passt immerhin noch ein ganzer Mensch rein. Etwa 90 Minuten vor der Landung kommt in der Economy Class dann noch einmal der Wagen durch. Es gibt einen warmen Snack, etwas zu trinken und einen Keks. In der Premiumie wird daraus gleichzeitig noch mal ein ordentlicher Servicegang mit Tablett, ein paar abgepackten, aber leckeren Sandwichstückchen und danach kommt noch ein Eis und ein letztes Mal heiße Getränke und damit haben wir es. Die Emirates Echo in der alten Trip7 und die neue Premium Economy in der in Anführungszeichen 97. Was soll ich dazu groß sagen? habt ihr gesehen, das war wirklich wirklich gut und ein viel größerer Unterschied als ich dachte. Die Emirates Echo ist solide, nicht mehr und nicht weniger. Ich verstehe das oft grenzenlose Lobter ehrlich gesagt nicht so ganz, denn das hier ist in keinem Punkt herausragend, sondern einfach genau das, was die Economy Class sein soll. günstig, effizient und ohne irgendwelchen komplizierten Schnickschnack und ja, die haben sogar eine Dusche im A380 ist für mich jetzt kein Argument für die Economy Class dieser Fluggesellschaft, aber hier eine Empfehlung auszusprechen oder das halt auch nicht zu tun ist eh nicht sonderlich relevant, weil es in der Economy Class ganz einfach vor allem darauf ankommt, wer auf welcher Route das beste Angebot liefert und da ist Emirates eben doch oft auf vielen Strecken ganz vorne mit dabei. Umsteigen in Dubai, das gehört dann halt mit dazu. Manche mögen das, manche nicht. Ich bin da relativ neutral, solange alles pünktlich ist und auf meinen Flügen bis jetzt mit Emirates war das immer der Fall. In der Premium ist die Frage da schon spannender, denn da ging es ja darum, lohnt sich das statt ca. 550 € für alles Economy Class habe ich knapp 1000 € für die Strecke Singapur Dubai in Economy und Dubai Frankfurt in Premium Economy bezahlt. Lohnt sich das? Ja, absolut. Das hier war nicht nur besser als ich dachte, sondern so stark, dass ich hier heute rausgehe und sage, wenn ich das nächste Mal auf einem Tagflug sehe, dass hier noch was frei ist, dann ist das hier der um welten bessere Deal Business Class. Die hätte hier über 2500 € Aufpreis gekostet. Es kommt natürlich, das muss man fairerweise dazu sagen, auch darauf an, ob ihr alleine reist oder nicht. Hier konnte ich auf beiden Flügen über die App meinen Sitzplatz bis kurz vor der Reise so legen, dass ich keinen direkten Sitznachbarn hatte. Das verbessert die Erfahrung vor allem in der Ökonomie natürlich drastisch, aber zusammen mit meiner Freundin oder sowas in der Premiumie, das wäre für diesen Flug wirklich der mit Abstand beste Deal gewesen. Daher das Fazit auch hier kommt immer natürlich auf die Strecke darauf an und das individuelle Angebot, aber die Premium Economy von Emirates kann was. Hat mir richtig gut gefallen und ist deswegen auch eine große Empfehlung. Das lohnt sich und deswegen kann ich am Ende nur sagen, ich könnte noch so sehr nach irgendwas schlechtem, ich finde nicht wirklich was. Deswegen kann ich das einfach nur weiterempfehlen. Das hat Spaß gemacht. Das war ein guter Flug. Das war eine gute Leistung von Emirates und das ist ein wirklich tolles Produkt und die Ausgabe dafür hat sich gelohnt. In diesem Sinne soll es heute gewesen sein. Vielen lieben Dank fürs Zuschauen. Ich hoffe, das Ganze hat euch gefallen. Hat mir viel Spaß gemacht dieses Mal und dann sehen wir uns hoffentlich ganz bald bei einem neuen Video wieder. Bis dahin lasst es euch gut gehen und tschüss.

reviews.transcript_full: What's EVA Air's long haul economy actually like? After recently flying their excellent premium economy to Taipei, let's take a look at their standard economy. >> [music] >> Hello and welcome back to K S Aviation. Today, we're at Taipei Taoyuan International Airport getting ready to fly home on board EVA Air's flagship Boeing 777-300ER in economy class. We've got a long flight ahead of us, so let's get checked in. Here at TPE, [music] EVA Air exclusively uses Terminal 2. The airline has plenty of check-in counters, and [music] since they open around 2 and 1/2 hours before departure, there weren't any major lines. The entire process was quick, efficient, and friendly. After a quick security check, we are now airside. There's still nearly 2 hours until boarding, so I spent some time exploring TPE's brand new Terminal 3 North Concourse. After a bit of exploring, I made my way over to gate C6 where BR8 was boarding. A quick look at our aircraft for today, Bravo 16716, and it was finally time to head on board. >> Bye-bye. 66 >> If you'd like to see what EVA Air's business class is like, be sure to check out this video. And if you're interested in their premium economy, I've got a review on that as well. But for today, let's check out their economy. Welcome to seat 46 Kilo, a window seat located in the second row of EVA Air's economy cabin. EVA Air's 777 has three configurations. While the premium cabins remain mostly the same across all aircraft, economy varies. Newer 777s feature a 3-4-3 layout, while older aircraft like today's have a more spacious 3-3-3 configuration. This version features 221 Collins Aerospace Pinnacle seats spread across two cabins. Starting at the top, [music] we have a nicely padded four-way adjustable headrest. Moving down, the seat back and cushion are both comfortable, while the seat itself [music] measures 18 in wide. Turning around, the adjustable 10-in IFE screen features both a headphone jack and USB A port. As for the content, we'll take a closer look once we're in the air. [music] Below that is a large and sturdy bi-fold tray table. Underneath sits a spacious literature pocket containing the safety card, inflight magazine, and a small trash bag. Legroom is also very generous, which means I'll be very comfortable throughout the flight. Each seat is also equipped with a universal power outlet, which I found the charging speeds pretty fast. Soon, we were ready for departure. And with EVA Air's new safety video playing, it was time to go. While we taxi, let's talk about today's aircraft. Bravo 16716 is a 16.5-year-old Boeing 777-300ER. It first flew in November 2009 and was delivered to EVA Air the following month. Interestingly, this aircraft was involved in an incident in July of 2024. While operating a flight from Los Angeles to Taipei, the crew encountered an issue with engine number two and returned back [music] to LAX. The aircraft landed safely and later returned to service. Hopefully, we won't be repeating that experience today. Although, we may find out pretty soon as we're now lined up on the runway. >> [music] [music] [music] [music] >> Now that we're the air, let's take a look at the amenities. Waiting at each seat was a nice plush pillow along with a large soft blanket. I especially liked the texture of the blanket, which felt comfortable and cozy. Also provided were a pair of earbuds. While they're fairly standard, I appreciated the soft rubber tips, which made them fit very comfortably. While we wait for the meal service, let's check out the in-flight entertainment system. During takeoff, the glare from the sun actually revealed a fairly large scratch on the screen. Fortunately, it wasn't very noticeable once the display was turned on. The screen itself is actually quite responsive. When it comes to movies, EVA Air offers a large selection, including many new and popular titles. There's also a dedicated TV [music] and music section with many shows featuring full seasons and albums available to enjoy. One of my favorite features is the dedicated kids section, which is great for families traveling with children. Lastly, here's the flight map. It offers several different views and provides plenty of information throughout the flight. Unfortunately, there are no exterior cameras available. Overall, I quite like this in-flight entertainment system. It's responsive, easy to navigate, and does a great job of keeping me entertained throughout the flight. Around 25 minutes after takeoff, the cabin crew came around with a pre-meal snack consisting of mixed nuts, crackers, and a cup of [music] water. For some reason, it took another 30 minutes before the main meal service began. I'm not exactly sure why, but by that point, I was definitely starting to get a little hungry. Thankfully, the wait was worth it as the crew returned with many cards and [music] two meal options to choose from. The choices were Gambay barbecue karubi with steamed rice or spaghetti with seafood in a creamy mushroom sauce. If you don't know, Gambay is a well-known upscale restaurant here in Taiwan. [music] So, my choice was pretty obvious. The presentation of this meal honestly looks really nice. I especially like the individually packaged side dishes as they gave the meal [music] a more premium course-like feel. Along with that, the metal cutlery included [music] in the packet is a nice touch. And even the little tea mug feels surprisingly premium. I then got my drink of choice, an ice-cold Coke. Now, onto the food. Starting with the bread, it's nicely toasted and when paired with butter isn't dry at all. This small appetizer appears to be some noodles with slices of meat. Personally, I found it to be a little salty, but otherwise it was quite good. Next to that is a cup of fruit. For some [music] reason, EVA Air never fails to deliver when it comes to fruit. It's always sweet, juicy, and refreshing. Finally, it's time for the main dish. Starting from left to right, there are several layers of barbecue karubi served over steamed rice. On the right are some vegetables, including broccoli and bell pepper. Sitting on top is a piece of tamagoyaki, a Japanese-style folded omelet. This dish was actually really tasty. The beef was flavorful and remained surprisingly moist. In the corner were some kimchi along with a really [music] tasty green sauce, both of which added even more flavor to the meal. I then devoured the entire meal in no time, and it was finally time for dessert. Today's dessert appeared to be some sort of strawberry pudding topped with a small layer of jelly sauce. It's certainly an interesting choice, but at least EVA Air didn't skip dessert. Honestly, that was one of the best airplane meals I've had in a while. Everything was delicious, and I almost forgot I was eating an economy class meal. As the crew came around to collect my now completely empty tray, they also handed me a bottle of water. Hopefully, that'll keep me hydrated while I get some rest. After the meal, I decided to check out the restroom. Inside, you'll find a large changing table, two full-size mirrors, and a clean spacious layout. As for amenities, there was hand soap, lotion, and even a selection of scented sprays available for passengers to use. Moving over to the sink, it's decently sized and features adjustable water temperature. The water pressure was decent as well. Cups and napkins were also provided on the wall free for passengers to [music] use. The wooden floor was pretty clean, and any water visible on the floor was from me washing my hands, which I cleaned up afterwards. Overall, this is a nice lavatory with plenty of amenities and a surprisingly spacious feel. I then spent some time exploring the aircraft. Near the rear galley, I found an even larger lavatory, which offered noticeably more space than the one I just visited. Also located in the rear galley was a self-serve snack station, where passengers could help themselves to a selection of snacks throughout the flight. After a bit of exploring, I eventually headed back to my seat and noticed a couple of small issues. There was a minor crack near the tray table latch, along with some wear around it. Honestly, it didn't bother me too much, since it was purely [music] cosmetic and didn't affect the functionality of the seat at all. As the sun slowly began to set over the Pacific, [music] it seemed like the perfect time to see just how comfortable this seat would be for the [music] long flight ahead. Holding down the button on the armrest and leaning back, the seat reclines a fair amount. About half a window's worth. Combined with the generous legroom, I found it quite comfortable and had no trouble getting some rest. I actually ended up sleeping for around 4 hours. When I woke up, it was time for a mid-flight snack. Yes, EVA Air actually serves a snack between meals, which is always appreciated on a long-haul flight. Today's offering was a sandwich filled with tuna, lettuce, cheese, and tomato. It certainly looked appetizing and thankfully it tasted just as good. A cup of water was also handed out alongside it. After the snack, I decided to test out the Wi-Fi. During this flight, EVA Air was actually running a promotion that offered complimentary Wi-Fi to all passengers. After connecting, I ran a quick speed test. While the speeds were definitely on the slower side, I couldn't complain too much, considering it was completely free. At the end of the day, it's still better than having no Wi-Fi at all. By this point in the flight, there were only around 4 hours remaining. I spent some time getting a bit of work done, and before I knew it, the pre-arrival meal service was underway. Just like the first meal, there were two options to choose from. This time, the choices were a savory porridge with chicken and corn, or a vegetable frittata with bacon and roasted potatoes. Both sounded quite good, but I ultimately went with a porridge as I was in a mood for a lighter breakfast. A short while later, my tray arrived, and once again, the presentation looks quite nice. Included was the same bread roll as before, while the side containers held an appetizer and a serving of fresh fruit. The appetizer consisted of mushroom, seaweed, egg, and bell peppers. It was surprisingly flavorful and seasoned just right. Moving on to the main dish, it came with a packet of fish floss to mix into the porridge. Combined with the chicken and corn already in the porridge, it made for a very comforting breakfast. After a long flight, I especially appreciated having something warm and easy to eat. The flavors were excellent, and the corn added a nice burst of sweetness in every bite. Overall, I really enjoyed this breakfast. To finish things off, I dug into the fruit. Just like the first meal, it was sweet, juicy, and disappeared in no time. After the meal, I made another trip to the lavatory, and it was just as clean as before. It's great to see how well the cabin crew maintained it throughout the journey. Due to a strong weather system approaching San Francisco, we were set up to land on the 19th instead of the usual 28th, a less common approach into SFO. Eventually, it was time to land. After the announcements and the SFO welcome video played, the seatbelt sign was turned on once again. But before we get there, let's take a moment to rate this flight and talk about pricing. For today's 11-hour journey, I'll be rating this flight in five [music] categories: ground experience, seat, cabin crew, food, and amenities using the KSA Aviation International Economy Score. Starting with the ground experience, check-in was quick, friendly, and efficient, while boarding began right on time. There weren't [music] any long lines or issues throughout the process, earning four out of five stars. Next is the seat. Although there were a few small [music] cosmetic issues, the generous legroom, comfortable padding, and decent recline made this a great seat for a long-haul flight. 4.5 stars here. Moving on to the cabin crew, they were excellent throughout the whole flight. From the warm welcome on board to the efficient meal service and consistently clean lavatories, they did a fantastic job. Five stars here. Following that is the food. While the first meal service was a little slow, the quality of the food made up for it. Both meals were delicious, the fruit was consistently fresh, and the mid-flight snack was a welcome addition. Five stars. Lastly are the amenities. The IFE offered a vast selection of content, while the comfortable pillow, blanket, and scent sprays in the lavatories helped make the flight much more enjoyable, easily earning five stars. This means EVA Air's flight BR8 from Taipei to San Francisco earns a total of 23.5 out of 25 stars. And honestly, it's well deserved. The flight went by surprisingly quickly, and there was very little left to be desired. Lastly, before we touch down, let's talk about pricing. Due to the busy Christmas and New Year's travel season, I paid a total of $2,128 for the standard economy ticket. However, during non-peak travel periods, [music] fares for the same experience can be found for around $900, which makes this an excellent value for a long-haul flight. Anyways, we're now on short final, >> [music] >> so let's enjoy this rare approach into San Francisco. That was a pretty cool landing. After a quick taxi to the gate, it was time to deboard. Following a not-so-quick walk to customs, we finally made it to baggage claim. Baggage claim one. Soon enough, our bags started arriving, but that's when something went wrong. If you can't tell, there's a massive dent in my suitcase. So, let's see how EVA Air handles this situation. It's now been a couple of months since this flight, and I'm happy to say EVA Air repaired my suitcase completely free of charge. That's some excellent customer service. So, it looks like this flight has a happy ending after all. Although there was a small hiccup at the very end, the overall experience was outstanding. I thoroughly enjoyed this flight and would absolutely fly it again. I hope you all enjoyed this review. If you've flown EVA Air's economy before, let me know your experience down in the comments. Thank you so much for watching and I'll see you in the next one. Bye.

reviews.transcript_full: Sweeten, Finding und Service auf höchsten Niveau. Genau das erwartet uns heute auf unserem mehr als zehnstündigen Nachtflug von Los Angeles nach Zürich, der Swiss First Class. Doch wird sie ihrem Ruf als eine der besten [musik] First der Welt wirklich gerecht, finden wir es heraus. Auch die schönste Hawaii Reise neigt sich irgendwann dem Ende zu. Und auch wenn wir das besondere Lebensgefühl der Insel jetzt schon vermissen, gibt es keinen Grund traurig zu sein. Denn für unseren Rückflug nach Deutschland wartet noch einmal ein echtes Highlight auf uns. Es ist unser erster Flug in der Swiss First Class und ich bin wirklich gespannt, ob sie den hohen Erwartungen gerecht werden kann. Swiss ist übrigens die einzige mir bekannte Airline weltweit, die in jedem einzelnen Langstreckenflugzeug eine Firstglass verbaut hat. Und allein das macht das Produkt schon besonders. Einen solchen Flug dann mit Meilen zu buchen ist allerdings fast unmöglich, es sei denn, man besitzt den Senatorstatus. Wie wir trotz den zwei der begehrten Plätze in den vorderen Reihen ohne Status ergattern konnten, erzähle ich dir später im Video. Geflogen wird die Strecke zwischen Los Angeles und Zürich mit einer Boeing 777300 ER. Insgesamt betreibt Swis 12 dieser Flugzeuge, die seit 2016 nach und nach eingeflottet wurden. Unsere Koffer sind schnell abgegeben, doch das Beste kommt erst noch. Ein Mitarbeiter eskortiert uns persönlich bis zur Sicherheitskontrolle und führt uns direkt an den wartenden Passagieren vorbei. Das ist schon wirklich besonders. Nach der Pass und Sicherheitskontrolle erreichen wir den Abflugbereich und ich muss schon sagen, dieses Terminal beeindruckt mich immer wieder. Bis zum Abflug haben wir noch ja so gute 2 Stunden Zeit und die Starlines betreibt hier eine eigene Lounge und bietet sogar an einem separaten Bereich exklusiv für First Class Passagiere einen Platz. Natürlich kommt dieser Bereich nicht an das Firstlass Terminal der Lufthans in Frankfurt heran. Dennoch erwartet ich hier ein angenehm abgeschämmter Sitzbereich mit eigenem Service, eleganten Sesseln, viel Ruhe und genügend Abstand von dem ganzen Trugel des Flughafens. Dazu gibt es hochwertige Snacks, eine gut bestückte Bar, erlesene Weine und auch Champagner, von dem ich uns direkt einmal gleich zwei Gläser zum Anstoßen einschenke. Solltest du Appetit auf etwas warmes haben, kannst du außerdem Gerächte direkt aus der Karte bestellen. Ich war natürlich neugierig, was die Küche zu bieten hat, wollte mir aber dennoch genügend Platz für das Essen noch am Bord lassen. Deshalb haben Katarina und ich uns gemeinsam ein Lachs bestellt und geteilt. Die Firstlass Lounge ist übrigens direkt über eine Schiebetur mit der Business Lounge verbunden. Besonders bekannt ist diese für ihre große Außenterrasse mit dem Blick auf das Vorfeld und die musste ich natürlich einmal anschauen. So, Katharina und ich machen uns gerade auf dem Weg zum Gate und Ja, die Lounge, die war echt schön. Gutes Essen, man sitzt da ganz nett, sehr freundlicher und so vorkommender Service. Also hier kann man ein bisschen Zeit verbringen und ja, jetzt bin ich aber natürlich gespannt, was die Swiss First Class zu bieten hat, gerade im Vergleich zu unserem Flug mit Lufthan auf dem Weg nach San Francisco und ja, ich freue mich auf jeden Fall, dass ich gleich dir das Ganze zeigen kann. Wir sneaken uns an den anderen Passagieren vorbei und steigen durch die erste Tür auf der linken Seite ein, wo wir bereits herzlich von der Crew begrüßt werden. Und der erste Eindruck der Kabine: Ich bin begeistert. Insbesondere im Vergleich zur Lufthan First Class in der Boeing 747, mit der wir auf unserem Hinflug nach San Francisco unterwegs waren. Das Video kannst du dir gerne im Vergleich ansehen. Mein Platz für die Nacht ist 2A. Nachdem ich meine Jacke in der Garderobe verstaut habe, schaue ich mich erst einmal etwas genauer um. Am Sitz warten bereits ein großes Kissen sowie das Amenity Kit auf mich, dass ich dir später noch zeigen werde. Kurz darauf bringt mir die Flugbekleiterin auch schon mein Pyjama für die Nacht. In diesem Sinne erst einmal Cheers auf einen hoffentlich großartigen Flug. Das Ambiente der Kabine und die verwendeten Materialen gefallen mir ausgesprochen gut. Alles wirkt modern, hochwertig und gleichzeitig angenehm wohnlich. Lass mich dir kurz einige Highlights dieses Sitzes zeigen. Unter dieser Abdeckung befindet sich die Fernbedienung für das Inflight Entertainment, die Kopfhörer sowie die Bedienelemente, mit denen sich der Sitz individuell einstellen lässt. Auch die indirekte Beleuchtung der Ablage ist ein schönes Detail, insbesondere auf Dachtflügen. Lediglich eine Möglichkeit zum kabellosen Laden des Smartphones fehlt hier. Das Herzstück des Sitzes ist jedoch der 32 Zoll große Bildschirm, der mit einer sehr guten Bildqualität überzeugt. Der Sitzabstand ist, wie soll es auch anders sein, mehr als üppig. Besonders spannend ist aber der zusätzliche Sitzplatz auf der Automane gegenüber, auf dem deine Begleitung während des Fluges gemeinsam mit dir essen kann. Das zeigen wir dir später. Jacken, Mäntel oder ein Sako lassen sich übrigens auf einem Bügel in der persönlichen Garderobe direkt am Platz verstauen. So, während der Kapitän die Passagiere über die Lautsprecher begrüßt, werfe ich bereits einen neugierigen Blick in die Menü und Getränkekarte, die ich dich hier gerne einmal einblende. information. Schönen guten Abend. Kurz darauf geht es auch schon los. Während die Sicherheitsdemonstration über die Bildschirre läuft, setzen wir uns langsam in Bewegung und rollen hinaus zur Startbahn von Los Angeles. Wenige Minuten später dann heben wir ab und steigen hinauf in den Nachthimmel über Kalifornien. Vor uns liegen nun 10 Stunden und 40 Minuten Flugzeit bis nach Zürich. Zu Beginn des Videos hatte ich dir bereits erwähnt, dass die Swiss First Class mit Meilen nur unter ganz bestimmten Voraussetzungen hochwe ist. Um überhaupt Zugriff auf diese begehrten Sitze zu behalten, benötigst du nämlich den Senatorstatus bei Worn. Unsere Flüg in die USA hatte ich bereits rund ein Jahr im voraus gebucht und der ursprüngliche Plan war eigentlich mit dem Lufthan Airbus A380 zurück nach München zu fliegen, was ebenfalls auch eine großartige Story gewesen wäre, denn Hinflug in der 747, Rückflug im Airbus A380. Doch im vergangenen Sommer paste der Lufthanse dem Flugplan dann an und tauschte den A380 gegen einen Airbus A350 aus, allerdings ohne First Class. Also begann die Suche nach einer Alternative und glücklicherweise konnten wir die Flüge online umbuchen und dabei die Swiss First Class auswählen. Rückblickend war das also ein absoluter Glücksgriff. Mittlerweile haben wir uns Reiseflughöhe erreicht und es wird Zeit in etwas bequemeres zu schlüpfen. Also schnappe ich mir mein Pyjama und mache mich auf dem Weg zum Waschraum. Für die acht Passagiere der First Class stehen im vorderen Bereich der Kabine gleich zwei Waschräume zur Verfügung. Das ist mal ein ziemlich komfortables Verhältnis, wie ich finde. Die Bilder selbst sind zwar nicht außergewöhnlich groß, bieten aber ausreichend Platz zum Umziehen. Darüber hinaus findest du hier feinste Pflegeprodukte von Sisley. Zurück an meinem Platz verstaue ich meine Kleidung ordentlich in der Garderobe und schaue anschließend, was das Inflight Entertainment so zu bieten hat, bevor dann der Service beginnt. Der Bildschirm hat eine angenehme Größe und überzeugt mit einer guten Auflösung. Kein Vergleich zur Lufthansa. Also das gesamte Inflight Entertainment lässt sich bequem über die Fernbedienung steuern. Besonders praktisch, während der Filmläuft, kannst du dir parallel die Flugrute oder andere Informationen anzeigen lassen. Kurz darauf beginnt auch schon der Service. Zum Aperativ bleibe ich meinem Favoriten Treu und stoße mit einem Glas Louise auf den Flug an. Dazu wird ein kleiner Gruß aus der Küche serviert. Ich bin bei solchen Amusgos ehrlich gesagt immer ein bisschen skeptisch. Nicht, dass ich am Ende doch irgendwo wieder einen Pilz versteckt. Ich hatte da nämlich schon mal ein traumatisches Erlebnis. Dann beginnt endlich das Dinner. Der Tisch wird liebevoll eingedeckt und ich denke mir in diesem Moment, wenn das Essen genauso gut schmeckt, wie der Service bisher herzlich und aufmerksam ist, dann wird uns dieser Flug definitiv in Erinnerung bleiben. Schon das Setup gefällt mir ausgesprochen gut. Ein großer Tisch, ein reich gefüllter Brotkorb, Butter, Ausstrich sowie edle Salz und Pfeffermühle. Genauso stelle ich mir ein Firstlass Dinner vor. Die Vorspeisen werden Stelecht direkt am Silvierwagen präsentiert. Das absolute Highlight ist für mich der Baliklachs. Schaut dir allein mal die Farbe und die feine Marmorierung an. Serviert wird er mit Gleinies und Saur Cream. Dazu entscheide ich mich noch für ein Pännchel Orangensalat mit roter Zwiebel und einer gebratenen Jakobsmüchtel. Der Balik Lax ist übrigens eine Schweizer Spezialität und gilt als eine der besten Räucherlachse der Welt. Damit hätte ich ehrlich gesagt nicht gerechnet. Wusstest du das? Als nächstes folgt eine Sellerie Apfelrahmensuppe mit weißen Trüffel und geräucherter Ente. Wunderschön angerichtet und geschmacklich ein Volltreffer. Für den Hauptgang stehen vier Gerichte zur Auswahl. Entweder kurz gebratener Wolfsbusch, Hähnchen mit Barbecussoße, gegrilltes Kräutersitlinge oder eine Rinderfilet. Meine Wahl fällt natürlich auf das Rinderfilet, begleitet von einem kräftigen Rotwein aus Südafrika. Das Fleisch ist perfekt gegart, wunderbar zart und wird zusammen mit einen Krat aus Okinava Süßkartoffeln und Butternskürbis serviert. Auch wenn ich inzwischen wirklich mehr als satt bin, für ein Dessert gibt es bekanntlicher immer einen extra Marken. Und ich teide mich für Babaoorum, einen rum getränkter Naptkuchen mit fruchtiger Orange und einer feinen Konditorcreme. Dazu begleitet von einem kräftigen Espresso mit einer kleinen, aber feinen Pralinenauswei aus dem Hause Sprüngli. Dann genieße ich noch die letzten Minuten meines Films. Mittlerweile sind wir über 3 Stunden unterwegs und die Kabine ist inzwischen komplett abgedunkelt. Die meisten Passagiere schlafen bereits. Damit wird es auch für mich Zeit schlafen zu gehen. Unsere Flugbekleiterin verwandelt meinen Sitz innerhalb weniger Augenblicke in ein richtig gemütliches Bett. Für einen erholsamen Schlaf gibt es eine dicke Matratzenauflage, zwei bequeme Kissen und eine kuschelige Bettdecke. Mit einer Liegefläche von rund 2 m Länge und knapp 60 cm Breite sollte so einer entspannten Nacht über dem Atlantik eigentlich nichts mehr im Wege stehen. In diesem Sinne, gute Nacht. Wir sehen uns morgen früh wieder. Ein neuer Tag beginnt und ich muss sagen, ich habe wirklich gut geschlafen. Zwar war es in der Kabine etwas warm, doch Schlafmaske und Ohrstöpsel haben genauso gute Dienste geleistet wie die bequeme Matratzenauflage und die hochwertige Bettwäsche. Während ich noch langsam wach werde, bringt mir die Flugbegleiterin bereits ein warmes Tuch. Bis zur Landung in Zürich bleiben noch gut zwei Stunden. Genau die richtige Zeit für ein ausgiebiges Frühstück. Doch dieses Mal esse ich allerdings nicht alleine, denn während wir das Abendessen jeweils an unseren eigenen Plätzen genossen haben, möchten wir nun eine der schönsten Funktionen der Swiss First Class ausprobieren. Gemeinsam an einem Tisch frühstücken. Dafür wird der Ottomane gegenüber kurzerhand zweiten Sitzplatz umfunktioniert und wir können den Morgen gemeinsam beginnen. Los geht es mit einem frischen Obstsalat, einer kleinen Auswahl an Aufschnitt und natürlich einem gut gefüllten Brotkorb. Und unsere ätherischen Öle dürfen natürlich ebenfalls nicht fehlen. Wenn du auch wissen möchtest, wie sie dir das Reisen angenehmer machen können, findest du den passenden Link unten in der Videobeschreibung. Für Katharina gibt es einen Cappuccino, für mich eine Tasse Kaffee und dazu einen frisch gepressten Orangensaft. Als Hauptgang entscheiden wir uns für Avocado Toast mit einem Ei und ein paar Würstchen. Das Frühstück ist schön angerichtet und schmeckt hervorragend. Und weil ich bei Süßschweißen einfach nicht widerstehen kann, bestelle ich zusätzlich noch einen Pancake mit Bären. Aber ganz ehrlich, was soll das denn sein? Optisch konnte er mich schon nicht überzeugen und leider hat er auch genauso geschmeckt, wie er aussah. Kurz nachdem unser Tisch abgeräumt wurde, überrascht uns die K noch mit einem kleinen Abschiedsgeschenk. Feinste Pralin von Sprüngli und dazu eine handgeschriebene Karte mit persönlichen Zeilen unserer beiden Flugbekleider. Ich liebe Schokolade und genau solche kleinen Gesten machen einen Flug am Ende wirklich besonders. Jetzt, wo wir uns bereits im Landeanflug befinden, möchte ich dir noch einen kurzen Blick in das Amenity geben. Darin findest du verschiedene Pflegeprodukte von Sisley, einen angenehm dicke Schlafmaske sowie Zahnbürsten und Zahnpasta. Die Verpackung wirkt sehr hochwertig und elegant. Der Inhalt ist gut, haut mich persönlich aber nicht komplett vom Hocker. Während die Kabine für die Landung vorbereitet wird, tausche ich nun den gemütlichen Pyjama wieder gegen meine normale Kleidung. Kurz darauf empfängt uns die Schweiz mit besten Februarbeter. Nach der Landung am Doc werden alle Firstlass Gäste persönlich vom Botenpersonal begrüßt und empfang genommen und im Anschluss mit einem Mercedes Sprinter direkt zum Terminal A gefahren. Ein wirklich angenehmer Service, denn so spart man sich den Weg mit der Flughafenbahn und umgeht gleichzeitig den großen Trubel an einer Passkontrolle. So, weiterflug nach Hamburg bleibt nicht mehr allzu viel Zeit. Für einen kurzen Besuch in der Swiss First Class Lounge hier im Terminal A reicht es aber trotzdem noch. Die Lounge bittet eine stilvolle Bar, einen kleinen Alcatbereich sowie eine gute Auswahl an Exon Getränken. Besonders gut gefallen hat mir das Alpine Desesign mit den vielen kleinen Sitznischen, das eine angenehm ruhige und gemütliche Atmosphäre schafft. Mit einem letzten Glas Champagner und ein paar Oliven lassen wir diese wunderschöne Reise langsam ausklingen. Die Swiss First Class hat unsere Erwartung in vielen Bereichen sogar übertroffen. Vor allem die herzliche Cuh, das hervorragende Catering und das insgesamtstümmige Gesamterlebnis macht diesen Flug zu einem Produkt, das wir jede Zeit wiederbuchen wollten. Ich hoffe, dir hat dieser Flug genauso viel Freude bereitet wie uns. Wenn dir das Video gefallen hat, freue ich mich über einen Daumen nach oben und natürlich über ein Abo, damit du keine unseren nächsten Reisen verpasst. Bis zum nächsten Mal. Mach's gut und bis bald.

reviews.transcript_full: After missing my flight on a 747, it's time to fly on a new airline on the channel, Condor's A330 Neo. >> [music] [music] [music] [music] >> And so our day begins after a forced rebooking by Condor after missing my connection on board one of Lufthansa's 747s. I really did try to fix it, but failed all the same. Today's aircraft is registration D-A-N-R-M. [music] An almost 3-year-old A330-900 Neo delivered to Condor out [music] of Toulouse back in November of 2023. There were not a lot of good angles to see the plane, but it is painted in the green island livery, which contrary to their other liveries, the stripes on this one are green. Hopping on board, Condor offers 216 Heiko economy seats arranged in a 2-4-2 [music] configuration. In recent years, Condor has completely rebranded itself to be the stripes in the sky and with that has also created one of the most recognizable [music] brands in the industry. Their business class in particular is definitely a bucket list product for me, but I'm a bit too poor for that right now. For this flight, I find myself in seat 21K, a window seat on the right side of the plane. Usually at this point, I'd tell you the seat details, but I've saved that for later in the video. As for now though, I'd like to invite you to like and subscribe to the channel. I make videos of airlines, aircraft, products, and experiences and having notifications turned on will ensure that I don't get away with uploading behind your back. We are trying to reach 1 million subscribers by the turn of the century, so I'd really appreciate your support. If you want to support me further, check out the Legits Club, the channel membership you can be a part of for just a few dollars a month. You'll unlock extra content, early access, and have a say in what's going on with the channel. My time in Frankfurt's airport was pretty abysmal. Everything here feels gray and a little depressing and it didn't help that I was screwed out of my original flight booking. This is Condor's home and haven alongside Lufthansa. I've got to say I didn't love being at this airport. Maybe I was in the wrong area, maybe sunlight helps, but for me, this airport is a no-go. Unfortunately, I'll be back here at some point in the future. >> In other news, Condor gives all passengers a nice striped pillow for the flight. Pretty typical economy quality. There was also no blanket provided, a trend that seems to be going up. >> And with that, my time in Europe has come to an end. After spending nearly a week moving around different countries and being caught in a massive snowstorm, I can finally sit down and rest for a solid 10 hours and 29 minutes. I wish I could say this flight was any level of luxury for me, but being considered the budget long-haul carrier from Germany, they definitely slacked in some areas. But before I make this video a place to complain, let's talk about something Condor has done surprisingly well. And that is their IFE. Condor offers a 13-in UHD 4K touchscreen display, which if it wasn't so shiny, would be nearly perfect for economy. The main menu has plenty of organized choices, but the first I went with are the movies. Plenty of good choices here, too. Definitely enough to keep me entertained the whole flight. The music offering also had a decent selection. I'm not much of an airplane music guy, but whatever floats your boat. Moving right along to the large selection of sports, I'm pretty sure these are not live, but still great for fans to check out. The airline has their own information section that has anything from surveys to something I've never seen before, customs forms. If you are hungry, check out the little in-flight menu as well with everything Condor has to offer. And of course, the in-flight map. This one is pretty typical, no surprises besides the slightly higher image quality because of the 4K screen. Still a very popular feature on any flight. Condor also has Wi-Fi on board this flight, charging a steep 7 euros for just text messaging and 20 euros for the full flight internet. Not my cup of tea. The IFE offered other things like Bluetooth and custom settings as well. The seat offers a mere 30 inches of pitch, 18 inches of width, and a nice 8 and 1/2 inches of recline. Using a little button on the seat front, you'll find a device holder so that you can watch a movie on a screen likely half the size as what's provided directly above it. Or if you'd rather have a table, the tray table can be put down using the usual necessary steps. They thoughtfully folded in half for you so that you you immediately see all the dirt and grime hidden on the full-size table underneath. But, that's okay because just off to the side is a coat hook, which is perfect for probably blocking your IFE and tray table. And, of course, some USB ports and a headphone jack for your wired desires. For the drink service, I stuck with apple juice. This was then followed by a meal. I did not film the meal, even though I've done these videos countless times. So, feel free to pause and read the label there if you'd like. All in all, the meal was a solid seven out of 10. Later on in the flight, the crew came around with some water, and I, being fairly reliant on the substance for life and hydration, went ahead and took a cup of my own. It was good, but not nearly as good as the view of the engine outside my window. The lavatory. This place was amazing. I don't know if I happen to get the handicap lav, or if all the lavatories were like this, but this place could fit at least two people. On top of that, it was clean and had an amazing striped accent wall, which is absolutely fantastic. The sink had some interesting signage on it, and the finishing touch was the trash pedal so that you don't feel like you have to wash your hands all over again. I'm sure there was a purpose to filming me do this, but I don't remember what that was. I thought I'd let you all watch anyway. Before the flight, we gave all members of the crew little goody bags. As a show of gratitude, they provided us with a goody bag with a handwritten note and a reusable bag with some stripes. Inside the goody bag was some snacks, which we definitely cracked open after I stopped recording. I guess today I'm feeling the cup shots. Here's yet another clip of a now empty cup against the same window. Later on, the crew came around with some ice cream as dessert. Pretty good size for a single person and pretty good quality, too. There wasn't really a breakfast, but I did get a box pizza as a pre-arrival snack. This was not too greasy and pretty tasty for what it was. I've got to be honest, I got on this flight filled with anger and frustration of how both Lufthansa and Condor treated me and my reservation throughout this trip. A mix of passing the blame and lack of internal communication led to me having to take a flight that no longer worked with my schedule. But by the time this flight reached the point of landing, my hopes for Condor were definitely met and in some ways exceeded. This flight genuinely surprised me for an airline that's supposed to be a more low-cost option versus Lufthansa. It wasn't all perfect, but Condor definitely holds a certain quality to it that at some point will have me flying them again. With all that being said, let's see how it holds up against the legit score. In terms of the seat, it was a modern-day thin seat with some of the worst long-haul legroom I've seen, but good recline and well-maintained. There was no lack of amenities, either. This was super impressive. Entertainment-wise, the IFE was great, but the Wi-Fi options cost money and didn't seem all that worthwhile. For service, the ground staff failed to change my flights to something that worked better, even when I opted to take an extra day of travel in order to better align with my goals. I was forced into taking this flight for a delay that was not my fault. I will say from the agent's perspective, I don't think they could see all the previous cancellations and delays of this trip as I was rebooked to a shorter Condor flight the day prior, which inevitably caused this mess. From their end, I only had a short delay which caused a misconnection. The in-flight service was great. I have no complaints here. For value, I can't say it's a good value because it was not what I paid for and was not what I wanted. Value versus competition, the product was still pretty good and it definitely was not the worst way to fly home. And of course, the cleanliness. The cabin and lavatory were super clean other than the tray table. I ended up awarding the lavatory a bonus point for the sheer size of it. Easily the best lavatory I've seen in a while. Overall, the flight scored 37 out of 50, which amounts to a 74% a solid C tier flight. But had this flight been what I booked or at least what worked for me, the airline's handling of the situation dropped its score by several points. At the end of the day, I would still recommend flying Condor. Just preferably do it by choice and not by force. Welcome to the city where at least seven people call home. It's Seattle, Washington. My flight today was uneventful once on board and I've got to say the in-flight experience was more than what I expected. It's always difficult rebooking with an airline who has limited code share partners or at least partners that fly to the US in any way, shape, or form. Regardless, I walked off this flight with a smile, at least up until I had to deal with more Condor ground staff that didn't seem to have any power to do anything for my reservation. But, that's a much longer story than what I have time for. If you enjoyed today's video, be sure to like and subscribe and follow me on Instagram @legitaviation. Be sure to come back next time where I fly United 737-800 from Portland to Denver. Until then, thanks for watching. >> Thank you. >> Excuse me. >> You know.

Headphones and, as always, a blanket and a small pillow, which in our case, Andrea and I used for our lower backs. Perfect. Listen carefully to what the flight attendant says NOT to do in case of an emergency evacuation: "Locate your nearest exit, which could be behind you." *"In case of evacuation, leave your belongings on board."* Travel Tip: Always carry all your essential documents and money on your person, whether in your pants pockets, shirt pockets, an inside pocket, or a money belt . Do not store them in your backpack or carry-on bag in the overhead compartment, because in case of an emergency evacuation, luggage cannot be taken, and you need to leave the plane as quickly as possible. The legroom is adequate; this is standard in this type of economy class on this airline. Remember that the takeoff phase does not end when the wheels leave the ground, but rather when the plane reaches approximately 10,000 meters (33,000 feet) , and until then, your seat must remain upright. The flight was delayed by 20 minutes, nothing major. I think they make that up during the flight. Mr. José? Huh? Yes, I'll blur your face later, don't worry, I promise. Everything's fine. Yes, everything's fine. Tell me. Good afternoon. My name is Sebastián. I'm here to introduce myself, to say hello as a frequent flyer, and I'll be working in this sector. Whatever you need, I'd be happy to help. Thank you very much.
