reviews.transcript_full: [music] [music] [music] [music] >> Everyone, [music] welcome back to Beirut. Today I'll be leaving the country and heading to Baghdad with Iraqi Airways. After a few unforgettable days in Lebanon and Syria, the journey continues. This time to a country I never thought I'd visit, flying on a national airline I never thought I'd get a chance to try. Located just 5.6 mi from downtown Beirut, Rafic Hariri International Airport has been serving the city since it first opened in 1954. And today it plays host to around 40 to 50 different airlines, including Iraqi Airways. The check-in process was quick and efficient, and Iraqi Airways includes a generous 30 kg checked baggage allowance in economy. I'm in the departures area now. Passport and security was nice and easy. I have about an hour till boarding, and there's actually a couple Priority Pass lounges here, but I'm probably just going to explore the airport before boarding. There are four lounges here that accept Priority Pass, but since it was my first time at this airport, I figured I'd just skip them and explore a bit. And of course, do some plane spotting. Beirut International Airport is Lebanon's main gateway to the world, and for many travelers, it's a surprisingly efficient and straightforward airport to pass through, especially given the region's complex history. Despite the country's relatively small size, this airport offers strong international connectivity, particularly to Europe and the Gulf region, and serves as the primary hub for Middle East Airlines. The terminal itself is easy to navigate thanks to its single terminal layout, which keeps everything centralized and minimizes long walks. Airside there's a nice variety of cafes, restaurants, and shops where you can grab a bite or pick up some last-minute souvenirs. One highlight for me was a small exhibit from the National Museum, which showcased the selection of fascinating artifacts from Lebanon's rich history. After wrapping up my time exploring the airport, I grabbed a coffee, then found a nice window to watch the plane that I'd be flying on today make its way to the gate. I've wanted to fly on Iraqi Airways for a really long time now, and I really had my heart set on flying on one of their 787s, but it was just too difficult to try and book a flight. Iraqi Airways currently has two Boeing 787s in their fleet, which are usually deployed on long routes to places like China and Malaysia, but sadly my schedule and budget didn't quite line up for this kind of trip. But I was still looking forward to today's short flight aboard this 737-800. Iraqi Airways has 14 737-800s in its fleet, and the plane I'll be flying on today was delivered to them back in 2014. >> [singing] >> Boarding was quick and easy. The night before the seat map made the flight look pretty empty, but at the gate it felt like a different story with quite a few passengers waiting to board. This aircraft is configured with 12 recliner-style business class seats at the front, but today I'll be flying back in economy. The economy cabin has 150 seats in a 3-3 layout, and for this flight I'll be in 23A. The economy seats on this aircraft were fairly standard, but overall they got the job done. Leg room was decent for a short regional flight, and the seats themselves reclined, which added a bit of extra comfort. Each seat came equipped with a tray table and a large seatback pocket, which was great for storing personal items. There are also individual IFE screens built into the headrest, which is always a nice feature to have. I was also glad to see overhead reading lights and individual air vents, which always makes a difference in terms of comfort. Storage wasn't an issue either, with plenty of space available in the overhead bins. That said, there were a few drawbacks. The seats didn't have adjustable headrests, which made them feel a bit more basic, and they were showing their age in certain places. In terms of power, there were no universal outlets, but there were USB ports integrated into the IFE screens. Overall, not the most modern product out there, but a perfectly adequate setup for a flight like this. I also noticed that the bulkheads were decorated with images of what I believe was the minaret of the Great Mosque of Samarra, which was a really nice touch and added a bit of Iraqi character to the cabin. The crew got everyone settled in, and we actually managed to push back a few minutes ahead of schedule. Founded back in 1945, Iraqi Airways is one of the oldest airlines in the Middle East. Over the decades, the airline has faced wars, sanctions, and long periods of disruption, but today it continues rebuilding its international network with a surprisingly diverse fleet of narrow and wide-body aircraft. >> [music] >> This afternoon's 1 hour and 30 minute journey will see us fly east across Syria and western Iraq before arriving into Baghdad at around approximately 2:00 p.m. Since this was a fairly short flight, the crew wasted no time getting the in-flight meal service started. Each passenger received a meal box with a sandwich, some peanuts, a bottle of water, a juice box, and a piece of cake for dessert. While the meal itself wasn't anything elaborate, it was still much better than what you'd usually receive on a comparable regional flight in the US. I also loved the Iraqi Airways branding throughout the service. Especially the branded sanitizing wipe, which added a nice touch of personality. After the crew cleared away the meal boxes, I settled in and relaxed for the remainder of the flight. >> [music] >> The in-flight entertainment system was actually pretty solid overall. The screens were very responsive and there was a decent selection of movies along with an audio section for music and other content. I really liked the interactive map, which not only showed our route and flight progress, but also provided information about the cities we were flying over. It even included an indicator showing the direction of Mecca. There's also a kid section built into the map that featured information about different animals, which added a bit of personality to the system. Besides the IFE system, there There also a duty-free magazine in the seatback pocket in case you wanted to do a bit of shopping during the flight. It's also worth noting that there wasn't any Wi-Fi on board. In terms of lavatories, there were two located at the back of the plane for economy passengers. The rest of the flight went by pretty quickly. This ticket ended up costing around $280, which was a bit more expensive than comparable flights with Middle East Airlines. But for me, it was worth paying a little extra for the chance to fly on such an unusual airline. Overall, this was a memorable experience from start to finish. The crew remained professional throughout the flight, and while the aircraft showed its age in a few places, flying with Iraqi Airways was something I'm really glad I got to experience. I'd still really like to fly on one of their 787 Dreamliners in the future. And maybe even check out their 737 Max as well. >> [music] >> All right, made it to Iraq. Thanks for watching and I'll see you again soon. Meet me >> [music] >> Meet me

 While we take a look around the airport and   make our way to the gate, let me share 
a brief history of All Nippon Airways. All Nippon Airways, widely known as ANA, 
was founded on 27th December 1952 as Japan   Helicopter and Aeroplane Transports Company. 
Interestingly, the airline’s IATA code, NH,   originates from its original name, Nippon 
Helicopter. The airline launched helicopter   services in February 1953, before 
expanding into cargo operations,   with its first cargo flight operating 
between Osaka and Tokyo using a de   Havilland Dove aircraft. Passenger services 
on the same route began on 1st Febraury 1954. As the airline expanded across Japan, 
it was renamed All Nippon Airways   Company in December 1957. Just a 
few months later, in March 1958,   it merged with Far East Airlines, creating 
Japan’s largest private airline at the time. ANA continued to grow through the 1960s, 
merging with Fujita Airlines in 1963 and   introducing its first jet aircraft, 
the Boeing 727 trijet, in 1965. For many years, the government-owned Japan 
Airlines had a monopoly on scheduled international   flights. During this period, ANA was allowed 
to operate some international charter flights,   the first of which was from 
Tokyo to Hong Kong in 1971. That changed in 1986 when Japan Airlines’ 
monopoly on international flights came to   an end. ANA immediately launched scheduled 
international services to Guam on 3rd March,   followed by Los Angeles and 
Washington D.C. later that year.   This was followed by the addition of Beijing, 
Dalian, Hong Kong and Sydney in 1987,   Seoul in 1988, London and Saipan in 1989, Paris 
in 1990 and New York and Singapore in 1991. A major milestone came in 1999, when ANA joined 
the Star Alliance. Today, as of June 2026, ANA   operates a fleet of 244 aircraft, with 106 more on 
order, serving around 95 destinations worldwide. Here is our aircraft for today’s flight, a 
Boeing 787-9 registered Juliet Alpha - 936   Alpha, delivered brand-new to All Nippon 
Airways in October 2021. The aircraft is   configured for domestic operations, 
featuring 28 Premium Class seats in   a 2-2-2 configuration and 347 Economy 
Class seats arranged in a 3-3-3 layout. Can we just take a moment to appreciate 
how efficiently ANA handles the boarding   process? Our scheduled departure time 
was 1:55 PM. Boarding began at 1:30 PM,   and by 1:54 PM, the aircraft had already 
pushed back from the gate. That’s just 24   minutes to board a Boeing 787 and be ready 
for departure. It’s genuinely impressive. Another interesting thing is how ANA carries 
out the boarding process. Rather than calling   passengers by row numbers, boarding is 
done according to seat position. Window   seat passengers board first, followed by those in 
middle seats, and finally those in aisle seats. It keeps passengers from constantly 
getting up to let others into the   row, making the entire boarding process 
noticeably smoother and more efficient.   It’s such a simple idea, and I’m genuinely 
surprised why more airlines haven’t adopted it. 32A will be my home for the next hour and a half. Let’s take a closer look at the seat. 
In the front, there’s a crisp 13.3-inch   4K inflight entertainment screen, 
along with a standard tray table.   The legroom is excellent for a domestic flight, 
with ANA marketing a seat pitch of 31 inches.   Unfortunately, individual airvents are not 
available, but every seat comes equipped   with a USB-A port and universal power outlets. 
Inflight Wi-Fi by Panasonic is also available. The inflight entertainment system 
offers a good selection of movies,   tv shows and music, along with a 
dedicated section for children. The inflight map by Panasonic is really 
great, with multiple viewing modes,   such as cockpit view, right and 
left window views and many more. On domestic flights, ANA offers complimentary 
beverages. The options on this flight included   Mineral Water, Cola, Apple Juice, Hot Coffee, Beef 
Consomme and both Hot and Cold Japanese Green Tea. Service throughout the flight was fantastic. 
Although my interactions with the crew were   limited, they were consistently 
warm, courteous and welcoming. Overall, this was a fantastic flight. 
It departed and arrived on-time,   the aircraft was spotlessly clean, the 
inflight entertainment system was excellent,   the beverage service was perfectly adequate for 
a domestic flight, and the crew were outstanding. It was my first time flying with ANA, and after 
this experience, I can certainly understand why   the airline enjoys such a strong reputation. I’m 
already looking forward to trying one of their   international flights to see whether they deliver 
the same level of excellence on a longer journey. I hope you enjoyed this flight review 
today. If you did, please make sure to   like the video and subscribe to my channel for 
a new flight or hotel review every alternate   Saturday. I will see you next time for a hotel 
review.  If you have liked this video so far,   I would be grateful if you like, comment and 
subscribe to my channel. For those of you who   want a perfectly crafted itinerary, designed and 
personalized specifically for your next holiday,   I can actually build it for you. Alongside 
this channel, I run a custom travel advisory   company called Ishara Journeys. We take the 
guesswork out of every trip, tailoring every   single detail to your specific preferences, and 
I can manage the bookings as well. To know more   and get started on your trip planning, scan 
the QR code or visit www.isharajourneys.com.

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Saigon's Tan Son Nhat Airport, or as they say in Vietnamese... Mời mọi người đến Sân Bay Tân Sơn Nhất với Freddie I'm about to take a 2 hour flight from Saigon to Hanoi with Vietnam Airlines in their AIrbus A350 Premium Economy an exciting trip for 2 reasons: Firstly because this is the world's fourth busiest flight route with over 11 million passengers a year and about 70 flights a day flying between the two cities and secondly, because despite being a relatively short domestic route, Vietnam Airlines use their long haul Airbus A350s and Boeing 787s with lie-flat Business Class and Premium Economy on this route so you just need to check the aircraft type when booking, and you can get a very premium experience Also, Vietnam Airlines now use Terminal 3 at Tan Son Nhat Airport for domestic flights It just opened last year and is about a thousand times better than the old domestic terminal as you can see, it's nice and bright and open but this terminal is only used for domestic flights so there's not really much to do past security Now, if you're flying between Saigon and Hanoi then you actually have quite a few choices Vietnam Airlines of course, or Vietjet Air, the country's largest budget airline Then some smaller airlines like Bamboo Airways, Viettravel and Sun Phu Quoc In fact, just look at the ridiculous number of flights available to book in a single day... But my one word of advice as someone who's flown within Vietnam quite a few times, just choose Vietnam Airlines The hassle and delays you might experience with the likes of Vietjet is just not worth saving like $10 Of course Vietnam Airlines get delays too, but at least they'll take care of you Anywho, here's our plane for today, a 9.5 year old Airbus A350-900 painted with what I think is one of the best liveries of any airline... Since we were flying in Premium Economy today we boarded in group 2 out of 3 and it was pretty smooth, no staff checking bag weight or dimensions or anything like you would get on Vietjet Now before we step on board here are the stats and route map for today's flight departing 25 min late and arriving 15 min late, so pretty standard really and after probably 6 or 7 flights on Vietnamese airlines I don't think a single one has been on time So no surprises there Also here's the seat map for this aircraft we're flying today, and I should note This was a group booking for 5 people and I pre-booked these seats circled here but with no explanation they changed us to these seats at the back during check-in so that was annoying, and worst of all it meant I no longer had a window to film out of So I had to go to the gate desk and ask if there were any free windows and eventually got assigned 14A, which you'll see in a moment but first, friendly reminder to like and subscribe if you're enjoying the video so far! and here's my seat at the back of this 36 seat Premium Economy Cabin and you still get good recline despite it being next to a bulkhead The seat is spacious with 38" of seat pitch and has an extra wide middle armrest  and I've found that basically all Vietnam Airlines cabins look pretty dated with the drab colour heavy cushioning and lotus flowers embroidered on the fabric But honestly because the cushions are so thick and plush it makes their seats some of the comfiest of any airline I've flown also a little coat hook but disappointingly, the casing for both armrests seem to have fallen off and they shoddily repaired with duct tape here it was fine for me but unfortunately for my seatmate it made it so his table was pretty much impossible to get out so he ended up eating later in the flight with his tray on his lap There was a very good view of the engine out the window though and of course, a nice plush adjustable headrest You get a little foot rest too, though I've always found these to be pretty impractical to use also cleanliness is just adequate I guess but I do like the Lotus flower pattern on the seat, a nice touch as it's the national flower of Vietnam and also on the logo of Vietnam Airlines They hand a wet wipe out to everyone after boarding is complete and lastly, you get decent over-ear headphones with new ear covers handed out separately slightly annoying to install but good for hygiene at least Before we push back some fun adverts start, this one randomly for a company that makes industrial steel for the construction industry ,and they clearly have a large marketing budget Then as we push back the actual safety video started playing and it's quite entertaining, so here's that and some scenic views as we taxi to the runway... Surprisingly to me at least they do actually give you a meal in Premium Economy, A step up from Economy where it's just water and a snack Here it's a basic but tasty bánh mì, the best sandwich in the world plus some fresh fruit and a yoghurt drink You can also preorder bubble tea and pizza (which I did as I thought we wouldn't get fed) and it's surpsrisingly good value for aircraft food at something like 50k dong for a big bubble tea and 100k for half a pizza and this is the pizza in question, made by Pizza 4Ps, a popular high end pizza chain in Vietnam probably the best pizza I've ever had on a plane, but may that isn't saying much   considering how sad and soggy most airplane pizzas tend to be incidentally, sad and soggy is how I felt when walking for more than 5 minutes outside in  in the 35 degree heat of Vietnam, the bubble tea is good too And finally, a quick tour of the IFE system and if you've noticed I've magically changed to a different seat in Economy,  it's because I filmed this on a later flight, but everything is exactly the same and mainly the movie selection is surprisingly extensive better than many airlines in this region and they have all the standard tv, music and games available too The moving map is very detailed too, but the touch screen just feels a bit laggy There's also these little info cards about every airline in their fleet and some surprisingly good Vietnamese movies, so give them a go if you end up flying Vietnam Airlines some of the movies did have this annoying watermark though, but weirdly not all of them Also fun observation, this infamous sea is labelled as the East Sea, or Biển Đông if you know you know Very last of all, there is WiFi onboard, but the free plan is only 15 minutes But at 5 USD for messaging throughout the flight or 8 USD for full speed (basically half the flight) It is at least priced quite fairly Now on Vietnam Airlines you know it's almost time to land when the adverts start playing... and here we're treated to a standard chilli sauce ad, then slightly more weirdly an ad for another industrial steel company I do feel it slightly cheapens the experience when they play so many ads throughout the flight and definitely shows Vietnam Airlines isn't quite in the realm of premium airlines Like you wouldn't see Qatar Airways or Singapore Airlines advertising some fast food or something... Anyway, the sunset view coming in to land was fantastic so here is that to enjoy instead... So here we are arriving in Hanoi just a few minutes late which meant we got to enjoy a lovely sunset landing They love a bus gate at Hanoi Airport, but a benefit of being in a larger aircraft is that they  reserve jet bridges for them, saving a few minutes on disembarking Domestic arrivals here are pretty smooth so that's it for today's flight... Now on to my final review: and I'll give Vietnam Airlines a pretty solid 75% on this flight today the only thing I can really fault them on is the slightly shoddy condition of the seat and fact they changed our seat selection last minute, but everything else was great and  Premium Economy is something I think is well worth paying for on this route On my airline tierlist they keep their 7/10 rating, the same rank as British Airways Which I think is fair as they're both distinctly average airlines with occasional flairs of brilliance Now if you want something else to watch you can check out my review of Vietnam Airlines long haul Economy Class in their Boeing 787 from Hanoi to London This flight was kind of disappointing, and reinforces my average rating for Vietnam Airlines overall but they do have a few quirks that keep them interesting so thanks a lot for watching be sure to like and subscribe if you enjoyed, and maybe leave a comment too and lastly good bye!

reviews.transcript_full: The airline industry has always been ruthless and a great place to lose your money. Richard Branson said it best, "If you want to become a millionaire, start with a billion dollars and launch a new airline." Suffice it to say, running a successful, money-making airline is no easy feat. Yet, for over 20 consecutive years, Panama's flag carrier, Copa Airlines, has maintained an impressive track record of profitability, all while its closest competitors have faced bankruptcies and restructurings. Today, we'll discuss what has made Copa so successful for over two decades as we fly from Panama City to Bogota, Colombia on its smallest and rarest aircraft, the 737-700. Right from the start, geography has been instrumental in Copa's growth and overall success. Its home nation, the Republic of Panama, is strategically located within 5 to 7 hours flying time of almost every major city in the Americas, making it the perfect place to set up an airline hub. As such, Copa has played a huge role in bringing the world to Panama. It is and will continue to be a major employer in the country and even advertises free stopovers, which I took advantage of. If you're flying between any two cities via Panama City on Copa, you can add a stopover in Panama for up to 15 days for no additional charge. Given that my ticket was between Chicago and Bogota, I elected to take a two-night stopover in Panama. I didn't have that much time, but I was able to visit most of the main attractions of Panama City, including a visit to the Panama Canal. Of course, there is more to Panama than Panama City, and there is a small domestic flight network served by Air Panama from Marcos Gelabert Airport, just a mile west of the city center. I was glad to catch one of these Fokker 50s as Air Panama only has two remaining that are soon to be retired. And soon enough, we were back at Tocumen International Airport, the hub of the Americas, to continue our journey south to Colombia. Given that I was technically on a 2-day layover in Panama, my outbound trip was still ongoing. Thus, I was able to check in online without needing to verify any documents because that had already been done in Chicago. Despite having a mobile boarding pass, I still decided to print a physical copy, which was easy enough. And speaking of easy, security and passport control were extremely efficient with zero lines, and I cleared both within 5 minutes. We're in Terminal 2, which officially opened in 2022 to supplement the existing Terminal 1. As Copa grew its fleet, it needed a larger and more modern facility to better support its growing hub operation. Tocumen itself is a very efficient hub, in part because this is one of the few airports in the world where connecting passengers do not have to clear transit security. The only other airport I've seen this at is Istanbul, but that's only true for passengers arriving from specific countries. Panama City's central location puts it within 5 to 7 hours flying time from nearly every major city in the Americas, as I said before. That means that apart from being the perfect place for a transit hub, all of Copa's routes can be operated on narrow-body aircraft that don't require an absurd amount of range. Thus, Copa has historically stuck with an entirely Boeing 737 fleet with very few exceptions. Having such a simple fleet composition contributes to lower costs because it's easier to coordinate maintenance and spare parts, and you don't need to worry about training crews across multiple aircraft types. Because of this, Copa has been able to keep its costs low while still practicing high aircraft utilization and perfecting efficient hub operations in Panama City. And that's another point. Copa's business model has always been about connecting the Americas and the Caribbean through Panama City, and also promoting Panama as a destination itself rather than a transit hub. Copa has never tried to venture into other markets like long-haul routes that require expensive wide-body aircraft or risk losing money on domestic routes it hasn't flown in 40 years. Copa has simply stuck to the strategy it knows has been successful in helping it make money. I will say though, sometimes I can't help but wonder how different things would have been if Copa had wide-bodies. Take this as an example, Copa operates multiple daily flights to some of South America's biggest cities, namely Santiago, Buenos Aires, and Sao Paulo among others. These three cities specifically are served anywhere from six to seven times daily and some of those flights depart within literal minutes of each other. And that makes me wonder, would it not have made more sense to instead operate two to three daily Boeing 787s on routes like this instead of six or seven 737 MAX 9s? This afternoon, we're flying to Bogota on flight 413 departing just 18 minutes before the next departure, flight 411. Bogota is a short route from Panama and is served up to 10 times daily on Copa and a further four times daily by Avianca. Our flight departs from terminal 1 and given both terminals are connected airside, getting between them is pretty straightforward. You'll notice the rotating soccer jersey of the Panamanian national team as World Cup fever was in full effect. Unfortunately, Panama finished at the bottom of its group despite a well-fought effort and exited this World Cup as the only team that didn't score a goal. Connections between terminals in Panama City do require a decent bit of walking, but luckily there are also airside transfer buses. Terminal 1 is clearly not as nice as its newer counterpart, but there is still an abundance of retail and food options. I did also notice that terminal 1 was kind of more neglected in the cleanliness aspect as it was clearly much dirtier than terminal 2, which was apparent as soon as I sat down at my gate. The plane spotting in Panama City isn't too exciting, but you will see some stuff that's not Copa Airlines fairly often, such as this cargo jet 757, this Uniworld cargo 737-300, and from Venezuela this Rutaca 737-300 heading back to Barquisimeto. Now, onto the theme of profitability, Copa recently posted its financial report for the first quarter of 2026 in which the airline posted a net profit of 212 and 1/2 million dollars. Since becoming publicly traded in 2005, Copa has turned a profit almost every year. Yes, the pandemic hit Copa hard as it did any airline, but after a brief period of losses in 2020, Copa was almost immediately back to turning a profit by 2021 as vaccines began rolling out and countries began reopening their borders. Another ingredient to Copa's continued success is its on-time performance. It has consistently ranked as the most punctual airlines in the Americas and one of the most punctual worldwide. In the first quarter of 2026, its on-time performance was 91.6%, one of the best in the industry. By continuously being on time, Copa avoids unnecessary costs that might result from delays or cancellations like passenger accommodations and potential compensation. Copa continues to use its strengths and simplicity and strategy to grow further. Back in April, it placed a new order for up to 60 new 737 MAX aircraft, a deal valued at 13.5 billion dollars. From this order, Copa has the flexibility to choose between the MAX 8, 9, and 10, which it hasn't yet decided. With the current fleet of 119 aircraft, Copa aims to add more than 100 new planes by 2034, taking it well past 200 aircraft. The Latin American market is growing, but when you look at South America as a continent, international air travel, especially between its countries, remains rather expensive. I wonder if, just like how Copa operates various fifth freedom flights within Central America, also known as milk runs, it could do the same in South America. Just one way to increase connectivity for the continent and maybe even help make flying cheaper there. But something I do want to praise Copa on is its communication. Whether it be delays or gate changes, I was always receiving email updates as soon as they happened, which I appreciated. This flight was booked as a 737-800, but as you might come to find on Copa, aircraft changes to other 737 variants, especially on the shorter flights, are pretty common. I found out the morning of my flight that we'd be on the 737-700, which is not only the smallest plane in the fleet, but also the rarest with only nine active examples. These are also among the oldest planes in the fleet, and with newer MAX aircraft coming in, they will gradually be retired in the coming years. Needless to say, I was happy to fly something other than the 737-800, and boarding soon commenced without issue. This afternoon, I'm seated in 22A, and the seats overall are comfortable with adjustable headrests. Overall, a great short flight on Copa. I will say my seat was definitely broken in some way because it kept reclining back on its own, but for this short flight, it wasn't too big of a deal. reviews.title: Asia's First Starlink Airline — Is the Hype Real? ZIPAIR Flight Review
reviews.transcript_excerpt: to test the free Starlink Wi-Fi onboard.…

captions.text: Today we're flying on a ZIPAIR from Incheon to Narita,
to test the free Starlink Wi-Fi onboard.
It's kind of old, but sill has Starlink Wi-Fi.
We have a USB port and a power outlet here,
Let's try connecting to the Starlink Wi-Fi.

reviews.transcript_full: Have you heard of Starlink Wi-Fi? Today we're flying on a ZIPAIR from Incheon to Narita, trying out the Starlink Wi-Fi above the sky. From this B787, to real Starlink speed tests. Let's find out together. Hello! Good morning from Incheon Airport Terminal 1. Today we're flying on ZIPAIR from Incheon to Tokyo Narita. Not 'Jin Air' of Korea, it's 'ZIPAIR' of Japan. ZIPAIR? Why is the name like this? The airline explains the meaning behind the name like this: It's said to come from the word 'zip', which means 'fast', and also means traveling through various zip codes. Pretty thoughtful branding… but to be honest… Many people would just think of a ZIP file at first. At least we'll never forget the name. ZIPAIR is an airline under Japan Airlines (JAL). A low-cost carrier specializing in medium- and long-haul routes. It operates as a separate LCC brand. Think of the relationship between ANA and Peach Aviation, or Singapore Airlines and Scoot. In the 2025 SKYTRAX rankings, ZIPAIR placed 4th among long-haul low-cost carriers. But honestly, the real reason I booked this flight is to test the free Starlink Wi-Fi onboard. It's SpaceX's satellite internet service. By placing small satellites in low Earth orbit, it provides internet access above the clouds. ZIPAIR already offered free Wi-Fi before, but starting May 8th this year, ZIPAIR installed Starlink on their entire fleet. So, let's get this trip started. ZIPAIR uses the K check-in counters. Today's flight is ZG046, departing at 12:55. The check-in counter opens at 09:55.  ZIPAIR doesn't offer self check-in yet, so if you have checked baggage, you'll need to visit the counter in person. I don't have checked luggage today, just one backpack to carry on. I heard ZIPAIR is pretty strict about the 7kg carry-on limit, so I weighed my bag, and it's 5.1kg. No problem. Heading to security now. Right in front of the K counters is a security check lane for Smart Pass users. Since May 28th, SmartPass-only lanes have expanded. In Terminal 1, they're at the west side of Gate 2 and the east side of Gate 5, which is here. In Terminal 2, they're at gates 1D, 2C, and 2D. I already registered for SmartPass, so let's go right away. It was 11:14 when I got on the move, and I'll see how long it'd take to duty-free area. I came through security check and immigration. and it's 11:26. Only 12 minutes! ZIPAIR is basically a low-cost carrier, which means you even need to buy a bottle of water. A bottle of water on board costs 2,500 KRW($1.63). I picked one up beforehand for 1,000 KRW($0.65) instead. Today's boarding gate is 107 at concourse. To get there, you take the shuttle train, which is basically an underground subway. From the center of Terminal 1, head down to the platform level. There's a platform on the left, and one on the right. Since the last train just left from the left platform, the next one should arrive on the right side. Trains alternate every 3.5 minutes between the two platforms. The display shows the countdown to the next train. Here's a small tip. Most people get crowd into the front doors, but instead, take the 3rd door from the back. Because after 3.5 minutes on the train, you'll be much closer to the exit. making for a faster walk to your gate. It will be helpful when you're running out of boarding time. But it still takes some time, so make sure to leave Terminal 1 at least 20 minutes before boarding. We are here, gate 107. ZIPAIR flights are usually assigned near here, between 107 and 113. and here's our ZIPAIR B787-8. ZIPAIR only operates B787-8, with 8 aircraft total. 6 of these were used ones from parent company JAL, while the other 2 are newly leased ones. Today's aircraft is one from JAL, about 14 years old. It's kind of old, but sill has Starlink Wi-Fi. Whereas most LCCs stick to narrow-body aircraft, packed tight with economy seats, this LCC flies a wide-body, which is pretty unusual. That's actually one of ZIPAIR's key differentiators. This aircraft has 290 seats total. From the 18 full-flat premium seats, to the 272 economy seats behind. ZIPAIR plans to introduce longer aircraft, the B787-9s in 2027. It seems like this airline is on a roll. Starlink is installed here. The layout is 3-3-3 with black leather seats. Even though the aircraft is fairly old, it looks like the seats are well-maintained. That's my seat, 50A. Seat pitch is about 31 inches. The passport just barely fit sideways. There's no IFE screen, on this Recaro CL3710 model. We have a USB port and a power outlet here, so you can plug in your charger. The headrest also adjusts up and down,  as well as side to side. We're pushing back now.  The B787's windows don't have physical shades, They're electronically dimmable. The window is set to the brightest setting, there's a noticeable yellow tint somehow. Let me adjust the color a bit. Please understand the tint is SO yellow that it's still a bit off. We are departing from Runway 33L. Let's go to Tokyo. You can dim the window this way. Press the button to adjust through 5 levels. and it gets dark slowly. Let's try connecting to the Starlink Wi-Fi. After joining the network, you scan the QR code in front to get online. There are many options, but let's check out the flight map first. It's powered by FlightPath 3D from Betria Interactive. Look The display quality is great and it's pretty responsive. You can check altitude, speed, distance, and time remaining, plus a 3D view of the aircraft and points of interest. For food, the options are pretty limited. Instant noodles, water, and a few drinks. The photos didn't load properly, which was a bit disappointing. There's also an entertainment section. You can watch a movie with your phone. As an AvGeek, Top Gun is a must. But subtitles were only in Chinese… with no option to change. I'll rather watch YouTube. Is the Wi-Fi speed actually good enough for YouTube? Let me play my video. Hey, zero buffering. Even when scrubbing forward, it handles it without a hitch. If you can watch YouTube like this at 40,000 feet, A long-haul flight would just fly by. Let's run a speed test on this Wi-Fi, whether it's worth the hype or not. I can see it's provided by SpaceX Starlink. (tesing Wi-Fi speed) For download, I got around 41 Mbps, and for upload, 26 Mbps. That's pretty fast enough for most uses! I even made a video call to my wife with zero lag. Let's take a quick look at the seat. The tray table folds in half. Personally, not my favorite design. Wait... what is this? Looks like something the previous passenger left behind… It's a return leg, so I understand, but it wasn't the cleanest. The seat pocket had a safety card, an electronics restriction notice,  and sick bags. That's about it. Here's the lavatory. Since it's a wide-body aircraft, it's quite spacious. There's a baby changing table, and what I thought was a coat hook, is actually an ashtray. Smoking is of course prohibited, yet by regulation, this has to be here. The toilet flush is sensor-activated, You can just wave your hand near it. Today we have 262 passengers out of 290 seats, a load factor of 90.3%. It's been 2 hours after departure, and we're getting ready to land. We'll be landing on Runway 34L at cloudy Narita shortly. Today we flew on ZIPAIR from ICN to NRT with Starlink on board. You know, there are many airlines flying between ICN–NRT, but very few fly a modern wide-body like B787, and ZIPAIR is the only one offering free Starlink Wi-Fi so far. That said, the cheapest option, Air Premia, includes 15kg of free checked baggage, while ZIPAIR charges around 40,000 KRW($26) extra for up to 23kg, So maybe it's worth factoring in baggage costs when comparing prices. The Starlink Wi-Fi was really fast and smooth. Many airlines are also gradually rolling out free Starlink Wi-Fi. Maybe soon, we won't need to tell our friends and family "taking off now, I'll message you when I land" anymore. If this video helped for your trip, a like and subscribe would be greatly appreciated. See you in the next video!

[music] Japan Airlines operates from Terminal 3 at Haneda Airport, which handles most of the airport's international flights. After check-in, the staff kindly directed me to the priority [music] security line, which I really appreciated, especially since the standard security queue was quite long. Flying Japan Airlines business class gives you access to several lounge options at Tokyo [music] Haneda Airport. Business class passengers can choose between the Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge, the Sakura Sky View Lounge, >> [music] >> and the Cathay Pacific Lounge, giving you plenty of choice before your flight. The Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge is the airline's main business class lounge at [music] Haneda. However, for this flight, I decided to visit the Sakura Sky View Lounge instead, [music] mainly because the main Sakura Lounge was extremely crowded. The Sakura Sky View Lounge >> [music] >> is essentially an overflow lounge for business class passengers, though the overall experience between the two is very similar. Both lounges offer nearly the same [music] selection of food and drinks. The main Sakura Lounge does have the advantage of shower [music] facilities, while the Sky View Lounge is generally quieter and offers even a better view of the airport. >> [music] >> When you enter the lounge and turn right, you first come into the main dining area. Further inside the lounge, it gets noticeably quieter with a more [music] relaxed seating area. There are also a few private phone booth room, as well as the locker room for storing your belongings. Our flight to London was departing from gate 113. As you expect in Japan, boarding started exactly on time. Group one was called first, which includes first class passengers and One World Emerald members. Business class passengers then boarded with group two. >> [music] >> As I stepped on board the A350, [music] you can immediately feel a level of privacy Japan Airlines new business class cabin offers. As I arrived at my seat, I immediately knew this was going to be a great flight. [music] Japan Airlines A350-1000 feature premium heavy business class cabin with a [music] total of 54 seats spread across two cabins in a one-to-one stagger configuration. There's a forward cabin with 20 seats [music] across five rows, and a larger rear cabin with 34 seats across nine rows. For this flight, I'm sitting in 3 Alpha, a bulkhead seat in the forward cabin and a true window seat. Japan Airlines use Safran Unity seats on its A350 business 1000 business class, and they're also the launch customer for this seat. Seat is very impressive, and I really like how they maximize the available space. There's also a surprising amount of storage, and the tech on this flight is truly top-notch. In front of the seat, you find a 24-in 4K IFE screen. >> [music] >> Next to it, it is a translucent sliding panel that's open to reveal a wardrobe, complete with a hanger. The design feels very Japanese and slightly inspired by traditional shoji screens. Beneath the wardrobe, there's also a dedicated shoe storage compartment. >> [music] >> I found this to be a real underrated feature and a clever, innovative storage solution that you don't often see on airlines. And underneath the IFE screen, there's a very spacious footwell. I found this to be one of the most spacious footwells [music] out there, and there's even extra space large enough to store a small bag or backpack underneath the footwell, too. >> [music] >> Business class seats are upholstered in airline's signature dark red fabric with leather detailing around the headrest. Speaking of the headrest, it can be adjusted for extra comfort and also feature built-in speakers, allowing for [music] headphone-free audio. The side console has a lot of useful features. Starting from the top, you find a reading light with three different lighting settings. Along with the small [music] enclosed storage compartment that's large enough for a water bottle or headphones. The IFE screen can be controlled using a remote, but since the screen is touchscreen, there's very little need to use it. Seat controls were just below the side table. Japan Airlines offer an impressive range of amenities in business class on long haul flights. >> [music] >> Waiting at each seat was a pillow and a blanket along with a pair of slippers that even includes a small shoehorn inside. There was also amenity kit, noise canceling headphones, the menu and a drink list for the flight as well as a large bottle of water. Passengers are also offered a set of pajamas to use during the flight. However, these are all the provides on loan. So, they need to be returned before landing and can't be taken home. Toward end of boarding, the crew came around with hot towels followed shortly by pre-departure drinks with a choice of orange juice or champagne. Japan Airlines offers both Japanese [music] and a Western menu and they collaborate with a local chef to decide the dishes. And of course, I went with the Japanese option. The appetizer was served in a beautiful presented [music] bento box featuring a selection of Japanese small dishes. Next up was the main course, which included stewed dishes and a selection of traditional Japanese items. [music] My rating, 10 out of 10. Lastly was dessert, a matcha bavaroise with azuki bean paste and soft [music] mochi. It was a great combination. The matcha and red bean worked really well together and it wasn't overly sweet. >> [music] >> The soft mochi added a nice chewy texture, which made it even better. My rating, >> [music] >> 8 out of 10. Business class passengers have access to three lavatories, all located in the center galley between the two business class cabins. The lavatories were a bit compact but well designed. [music] It featured a fold-down bench and most of the function were touch-free, which felt modern and hygienic. And of course, as you expect on Japanese airline, every lavatory comes equipped with a bidet. I also try out the pajamas and honestly, they felt like a bit like an oversized bath poncho. They may not be the most stylish, but they were comfortable. When converting into bed mode, the seat transforms into a fully flat bed measuring 200 cm in length. I found it to be comfortable wide around both shoulders and feet. Staggered business class seats often struggles from tight footwells, but because I was seated in a bulkhead seats, I had significantly more space. As you can see, the footwell was so large that I almost can't sleep inside it. The mattress cover isn't fitted and tends to slide around a little [music] during the flight, so it doesn't provide much extra padding. I noticed some passenger using mattress pad [music] when leaving the aircraft, so these appear to be available. Unfortunately, I wasn't offered one. And it's something that Japan Airlines could probably advertise a bit better. The amenity kit is provided by Hal Boney and come with a good selection of essentials. And it even comes with a small phone stand. Japan Airlines A350 business class has 24-in 4K screen. The taking interface are great, though unfortunately, the selection of movies and TV shows isn't huge. But it has a lovely map features >> [music] >> plus a tail camera, which is just about my favorite entertainment on any aircraft. Japan Airlines is one of the first airlines to offer three different ways to listen to the entertainment system. You can use the provided headphones, which I found to be decent, connect your own headphones >> [music] >> via Bluetooth, which was my preferred option, or use the built-in speakers >> [music] >> in the headrest. The speakers actually work surprisingly well. They were loud enough to enjoy movies and music [music] comfortably, yet didn't disturb other passengers around you. Japan Airlines also offer free Wi-Fi [music] in business class with no data caps. The airline usually provides all passengers with free [music] 1-hour Wi-Fi pass, while a 24-hour pass cost around 1880. I received a promotional code by email a few days before the flight, and if you [music] happen to miss that mail, you can also generate the code on board. Instead, there's a pamphlet in your seat pocket that's walk you through the setups, [music] and it includes around 12 steps. On polar routes like this one, I often struggle to get Wi-Fi [music] working properly. This flight was no exception. There was a good selection of snacks and light meals available throughout the [music] flight. I decided to start something simple, so I tried Japan Airlines' original [music] fried chicken and a pork cutlet sandwich, a classic combination you often find at a combini in Japan. One feature that I love was that you don't need [music] to press the flight attendant call button to order food. Instead, you can place your order directly from the IFE screen, which [music] I found very convenient. As I expected, the fried chicken wasn't crispy, but I didn't really expect [music] it to be. It was tasty, and the presentation reminded me a lot ordering a famichiki [music] from FamilyMart. My rating, 9 out of 10. The pork cutlet [music] was quite good, but it was dry for my taste. My rating, 7 out of 10. The second inflight meal followed a dine-on-demand concept for the rest [music] of the flight. I think this is a great idea as it allows you to eat whenever you feel like. I went with the Japanese [music] washoku plate, which is served as a single course. It includes a grilled miso-flavored black cod as the main [music] dish along with a Japanese omelet. The side dish is simmered chicken [music] thigh with vegetables. And it also came with steamed rice and miso soup with white leek. Overall, it was a solid meal, [music] well presented, and nicely balanced, but nothing really stood out for me. My rating, 7/10. With this flight, I can finally cross Japan Airlines A350-1000 business class off my bucket list, and it truly lived up to the expectations. Overall, I would rate this experience among the best [music] in the world. There's a lot to like here. The Saffron Unity seat is spacious, well designed, and offers an impressive amount of storage. The take on board is also excellent. And it all comes together with a very strong soft product including great food and drinks, attentive service, [music] and thoughtful amenities. It is easily one of my favorite business class product, but how does it compare to ANA's room? For me, ANA's room still has the edge in terms of hard product. The seats are more spacious, but it lacks some of the tech >> [music] >> and storage solution that Japan Airlines has. On the soft product side, I also slightly give that advantage to ANA, especially in terms of service consistency. However, Japan Airlines does have one major advantage, the aircraft itself. The A350-1000 is a fantastic platform to fly. It's much quieter than the older aircraft, and the improved cabin pressurization makes the long-haul flight experience noticeably more comfortable. That said, both Japan Airlines and ANA are world-class products and you really can't go wrong with either. The best choice often comes down to price, schedule, and convenience. I flew Japan Airlines A350-1000 first class last year and it still stands out one of the best flight I ever taken. If you want to see what that was like, check out this video. We hope you enjoy watching our video and sharing our flight with Japan Airlines in business class on their A350-1000. Consider to like and subscribe to our channel and we look forward to bringing you more amazing content in the future. Until then, take care and see you next time.

reviews.transcript_full: KLM once used to be our favorite airline, but recent experiences have not been great. We haven't tried our economy product in a while, so we are curious to find out if flying standard economy with them is still worth it and if they live up to their own slogan, travel well. So, let's have a look at our full flight experience including an emergency landing and one a very questionable food item. We're flying to Bangkok and our journey starts at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport. We booked an economy standard ticket and that includes one piece of check-in luggage of maximum 23 kg and free seat selection upon check-in. Since we're flying economy, there are no further perks for us, which means we entertained ourselves by walking over this glass floor luggage belt. Last time we flew with KLM, we were in premium economy, which was fine, but not amazing. And especially the breakfast eggs were terrible. So, here's hoping we don't have to deal with those again. All right, let's go and experience economy standard. Time for our flight and here we are boarding the Boeing 777-200, which is set up in a 3-4-3 configuration. It's a full flight and we were seated apart because we wanted to get the full economy standard experience and did not pay for advanced seat selection. Also, because our ticket includes free seat selection during check-in, we figured if we were the first to check-in, we could still select two seats next to each other. We were wrong. Despite the seat map showing lots of availability mere minutes before check-in, the only option to be seated together the second check-in opened were paid seats. A little strange if you ask us, but okay. A very kind solo passenger offered to switch seats, which was a win-win situation since these seats are a lot less wide than we remember and are definitely not made for people with broad shoulders. Remember this solo passenger for later though. So, let's have a look at the seats. When you enter the plane, there's a blanket and basic pillow waiting for you. We have to say the pillow and the blanket feel a bit cheap and especially the pillow is not very comfortable. As for the legroom, it's pretty standard with 79 cm and when the person in front of you reclines, there's still luckily a bit of space left. The seat also comes with a split fold-out table and there's an adjustable headrest. For charging your device, you can either use the USB-A port integrated in the screen or the power outlet below the seat, but it seems that it doesn't get cleaned that often. Now, let's get ready for takeoff and continue our review in disguise. Shortly after takeoff, we received a wet towel and a headset. So, up until that point, you could not watch anything on your screen if you forgot to bring your own. We suspect it's because boarding started later than planned, but we're not sure. Let us know in the comments if you know if this is always the case with KLM. Speaking of the entertainment system, I have to say we were pretty impressed with it and dare I say it, it's one of the better ones we've experienced in economy recently. The home screen nicely shows a timeline of what you can expect during the flight. There's also a pretty good selection of entertainment. You can find the in-flight drinks menu and of course the most important part, a working in-flight map. Yay! To help us celebrate having a good in-flight map, make sure to like this video and subscribe to our channel. Aside from that, there's also free Wi-Fi on board that allows for messaging and emails. If you need more internet capabilities, you do have to pay for it. Before we move on to the food, let's quickly check out the toilets. There's only hand soap available though and no moisturizer creams that other airlines sometimes have. Time for our first meal, which was dinner. And we had the option to choose between the classic chicken or pasta. So, of course, we chose both. As for the sides, there were some peppers stuffed with cream cheese, a mystery dip that was definitely not mayo, some olives and sun-dried tomatoes, and finally, a bread roll. Taste-wise, I'm not sure what to say, except that we recommend the chicken over the pasta. And yeah, don't come to this flight hungry. Right after the meal service, something unexpected happened. Shortly after we were up in the air, a flight attendant noticed that a passenger was feeling unwell, and then someone yelled if there was a doctor on board. And remember that kind solo traveler offering to switch seats? Turns out that person is a doctor and rushed to help immediately. After some time, it was decided that we were going to have to make an emergency medical landing, and that's why we were now heading to Istanbul instead of Bangkok. To be able to do so, the plane started dumping fuel to get ready for landing. We never experienced an emergency landing before, and we really hope that the person in question has made a full recovery in the meantime. We have to say, it made for an impressive sight, though, and Istanbul by night looks very beautiful from above. Once the plane got a whole lot lighter, we made our descent, and once we made it, we awaited the medical staff to do their thing and take away the sick passenger. After refueling, we quickly left again for Bangkok, and the whole situation only took about 1 and 1/2 hours or so, which was very impressive. With the plane safely back in the air and most people trying to sleep, it was time for the dessert portion of the meal, and a brownie. The timing was very unfortunate, because everyone was trying to sleep and these things have the loudest wrappers imaginable. Then finally after some sleep and with only 2 and 1/2 hours of the flight left, it was time for breakfast. We were lucky to not have the dreaded eggs again, but we're not sure if what we got instead is any better. Dear viewer, behold the KLM breakfast. A cup of sour fruit, strawberry yogurt, and what's that? Oh yes, it's a Dutch pastry snack known as a cheese roll or kaasbroodje. Only eaten for breakfast by those who are either under 21 or hungover or both. With the Dutch travelers, you can count on some nostalgia and our love for greasy savory pastries, but to serve this for breakfast to an international audience even is definitely a choice and not a very good one if you ask us. Especially because the cheese roll wasn't executed that well. It was just very fatty and greasy and not something you want to start your morning with. So with a disappointing breakfast done and after 12 plus hours of flying, it was finally time to land >> [music] >> in Bangkok. With us safely arriving at Suvarnabhumi International Airport, it's time to have a look at what we paid for this eventful flight and if we think KLM is still worth it. For a direct flight from Amsterdam to Bangkok, we paid 950 euros per person for a return ticket including one piece of check-in luggage and so-called free seat selection during check-in. Although, I wouldn't attach too much value to that. As for the emergency landing, this was obviously not planned, but was handled very well by the cabin crew who were attentive overall. The in-flight entertainment system was good, too, but the food was honestly very sad, and especially the breakfast is a poor showing. The seats have also become very thin and narrow, and the overall cleanliness is debatable. It seems that KLM is dealing with some sort of identity crisis where its most recent campaign slogan "Travel Well" alludes to flying with a good experience, whilst their pricing and ancillary revenue strategies creams low-cost carrier, but without the fares to match it. So, while the flight was pretty okay and definitely not the worst we've experienced in economy, it's also not worth it to pay a whole lot extra for, since the experience as a whole is just mediocre at best. Oh, well, at least it was a direct flight. Well, sort of. If you want to see what flying premium economy with KLM is like, click here, and otherwise, thank you so much for watching. Bye.

The safety video concludes and the crew goes through the cabin for a final safety check. Once on the runway, we pick up speed and take off into the Singaporean sky. We continued cruising to Bangkok as the sun ever so slowly began to set. The crew then [music] began to make announcements to prepare for arrival into Bangkok, and went through the cabin to make sure all our seats were in the upright position. Then the lights in the cabin were turned off. We began descending, and we touched down into the city of Bangkok. Right on cue, the cabin got up and began preparing to disembark. It was great. Thank you for the service. Thank you. We were off the plane and on the jet bridge. Once past the jet bridge, it came time to look for immigration to be allowed into the country. Since we had no checked bags, we were able to continue straight forward to customs and the arrivals hall. There are public transportation options available from the airport, but for today, we will be taking a Grab. One of the city's most famous sites [music] is the Wat Pho. It is filled with beautiful decorated chedis rising in colorful intricate patterns across the temple grounds and home to the massive reclining Buddha. Wat Pho is so famous that Obama came here during a state visit as well. Nearby is the Grand Palace, one of Bangkok's most recognizable landmarks and one of the most important historical sites in Thailand. For more context on Thai history and culture, the National Museum of Bangkok offers a look at the country's art, artifacts, and royal heritage. But Bangkok is not just temples and museums. The city is also known for its street food, busy roads, tuk-tuks, and the kind of organized chaos that makes it feel alive at almost every hour. And few places capture that energy like Khao San Road, one of Bangkok's most famous streets [music] and a major gathering point for travelers. People were so friendly here and kept offering me massages. From historic temples to street-level energy, Bangkok offers a completely different kind of experience after arriving from Singapore. This flight was not the longest or the most expensive, but sometimes travel doesn't need to be extreme to be memorable. Singapore Airlines delivered a polished and comfortable experience, and Bangkok gave us the perfect reminder of why we travel in the first place. For the food, the history, the chaos, the beauty, and the feeling that somewhere completely different [music] can suddenly feel exciting and familiar all at once. Your temples, your food, your lights, your chaos, and all your beauty came together to make this city unforgettable. I can't wait to see you again. And until then, I'll see you in the next trip.

reviews.transcript_full: Hi there, my name is Earl and welcome back to Bahi Mennez. Cafe Pacific is celebrating its 80th anniversary this year, so what better way to celebrate than by flying with them again. It was also the first airline I featured on this channel, and I'm curious to see how the service has evolved since my last long haul flight with them. In this video, join me on a 9-hour journey from Hong Kong to Sydney in economy class with Cathy Pacific. I had just arrived from Manila and cleared security, which was quite busy and took around 30 minutes. Hong Kong airport is an AV geek's paradise, and I could honestly spend an entire day here just walking around the terminal like I'm in Disneyland. The glass curtain walls not only fill the terminal with natural light, but also offer excellent views of aircraft movements around the tarmac, making it a great spot for plane spotting, and Hong Kong airport takes plane spotting to the next level. So, I headed straight to the sky bridge near gate 24 to check it out for myself. reviews.transcript_full: ഹായ് ഗയ്സ് വെൽക്കം ബാക്ക് ടു കുട്ടി ട്രിപ്പ്സ്. അപ്പൊ ഇന്നത്തെ വ്ലോഗ് നമ്മൾ ഒരു എയർ ഇന്ത്യ റിവ്യൂ ആക്കാം എന്ന് വിചാരിച്ചു. ഞാനിപ്പോൾ കോപ്പൺ വേഗനിൽ നിന്ന് ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് ട്രാവൽ ചെയ്യുകയാണ് എയർ ഇന്ത്യയിൽ. ഫസ്റ്റ് ടൈം ആണ് ഞാൻ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ പോകുന്നത്. ഒരുപാട് കാര്യങ്ങൾ എയർ ഇന്ത്യയെ പറ്റി നമ്മൾ എല്ലാ ദിവസവും കേൾക്കുന്നുണ്ട്. അപ്പൊ എങ്ങനെയാണ് എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ട്രാവൽ [സംഗീതം] അതിന്റെ ഒരു റിവ്യൂ എക്സ്പീരിയൻസ് ആണ് ഞാൻ ഈ ഒരു വ്ലോഗിൽ ഉദ്ദേശിക്കുന്നത്. സോ അപ്പം എന്റെ പെട്ടികളൊക്കെ ഇവിടെ റെഡിയാണ്. സോ നമുക്ക് അപ്പം എയർ ഇന്ത്യ എക്സ്പ്രസ്സിൽ നാട്ടിലോട്ട് പോകാം. സോ ലെറ്റ്സ് ഗെറ്റ് ഇന്റു ദ വീഡിയോ. ഈ രണ്ട് വലിയ പെട്ടികൾ ഞാൻ പൊക്കുന്നത് കണ്ടിട്ട് ഞാൻ ഒരു സംഭവമാണെന്ന് ആരും വിചാരിക്കണ്ട ആ പെട്ടിയിൽ ഒന്നുമില്ല എനിക്ക് ആക്ച്വലി ഇവിടുന്ന് അങ്ങോട്ടല്ല കൊണ്ടുപോകാനുള്ളത് വീട്ടിൽ നിന്ന് ഇങ്ങോട്ടാണ് സാധനങ്ങൾ വേണ്ടത് സോ കാലിപ്പെട്ടിയുമായിട്ട് അങ്ങനെ വീട്ടിൽ എത്തുന്നതും കാത്ത ഉള്ള ഒരു യാത്രയാണിത് അങ്ങനെ ബാഗ് എല്ലാം നമ്മൾ ചെക്കിൻ ചെയ്തിട്ട് ദാ ഇമിഗ്രേഷനിൽ സീലും വെച്ച് ദാ ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് പോവുയാണ് ഇപ്പോഴാണ് ഇത് [സംഗീതം] റിയൽ ഫീലിങ് വരുന്നത് ഞാൻ ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് പോവുയാണ് വീട്ടിൽ പോവുയാണ് എന്നുള്ള ഫീലിങ്് അപ്പൊ ദാ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ജേർണി സ്റ്റാർട്ട് ചെയ്തുഒപന് മറഞ്ഞിരുന്ന ഫ്ലൈറ്റ് ആണ് [സംഗീതം] ഡിലേ ആയിട്ട് ഇപ്പം 10:45നാണ് എടുക്കുന്നത് ഡിലേ ആവാത്തവർ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ഫ്ലൈറ്റ് ഇല്ലഎന്നാണ് എനിക്ക് തോന്നുന്നത് ഈ ഒരു കോപ്പൻ ഡൽഹി അറ്റ്ലീസ്റ്റ് എപ്പോഴും ഡിലേ ആയിക്കൊണ്ടിരിക്കും. സോ ഇതാണ് [സംഗീതം] ഡിലേ ആയതുകൊണ്ട് എന്റെ സെക്കൻഡ് ഫ്ലൈറ്റും ക്യാൻസൽ ചെയ്ത് റീബുക്ക് ചെയ്യേണ്ടി വന്നു. ഫ്രം ഡൽഹി ടു ബാംഗ്ലൂർ ആദ്യമായിട്ട് നമ്മുടെ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ഫ്ലൈറ്റിൽ കയറിയ എന്റെ ഒരു ചെക്കിങ്ങും കാര്യങ്ങളും ഒക്കെ ഉണ്ട്. ഞാൻങ്ങനെ മൊത്തത്തിൽ എല്ലാ സീറ്റും [സംഗീതം] പരിസരവും ഒക്കെ ആകെ ഒന്ന് ചെക്ക് ചെയ്തുകൊണ്ടിരിക്കുയായിരുന്നു. നമുക്ക് യൂഷ്വൽ ഫ്ലൈറ്റ്സിൽ കിട്ടുന്ന പോലെ ഇതിലും കുറച്ച് പുതപ്പും പില്ലോയും കാര്യങ്ങളഒക്കെ കിട്ടിയിട്ടുണ്ടായിരുന്നു. [സംഗീതം] പക്ഷെ മറ്റുള്ള ഫ്ലൈറ്റിലൊക്കെ കിട്ടുന്ന അത്രയും ഐറ്റംസും എന്താ പറയുക ആ ഒരു പ്രീമിയം [സംഗീതം] സംഭവംില്ല. എങ്കിലും ഓക്കെ ഓക്കെ ആണ്. വലിയ ബുദ്ധിമുട്ടൊന്നുമില്ല. സീറ്റ് ഒക്കെ കുഴപ്പമില്ലായിരുന്നു. പിന്നെ ചില [സംഗീതം] സ്വിച്ചുകളും കാര്യങ്ങളും ഒക്കെ എന്താെന്ന് ശരിക്കും എനിക്ക് മനസ്സിലായില്ല. അതൊന്നും വലിയ യൂസ് ഒന്നുമില്ല. ചിലരുടെ ഒന്നും മോണിറ്റർ ഒന്നും വർക്ക് ആവാറില്ല എന്ന് കേട്ടിട്ടുണ്ടായിരുന്നു. താങ്ക് ഗോഡ് എന്റെ മോണിറ്റർ വർക്കിങ് ആയിരുന്നു. അതുകൊണ്ട് വലിയ കുഴപ്പമില്ലായിരുന്നു. സ്റ്റിൽ ഞാൻ ഒരു ഫിലിം കണ്ടു ബാക്കി ഞാൻ എന്റെ ഫോണിലും ടാബിലും ഒക്കെയാണ് [സംഗീതം] ഫിലിം കണ്ടത്. അപ്പൊ ഈ ജേർണി എന്ന് പറയുന്നത് വെരി വെരി ലോങ്ങ് ജേർണി ആണ്. ഇവിടുന്ന് ഡെൻമാർക്കിൽ നിന്ന് ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് ഓൾമോസ്റ്റ് 9 ആൻഡ് ഹാഫ് ഹവേഴ്സ് ഉണ്ട്. ഓൾറെഡി നമ്മുടെ ഫ്ലൈറ്റ് വൺ അവർ മേലെ ഡിലേ ആണ്. ഇത് കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ട് നമുക്ഒരു ലേഓവർ ഉണ്ട് ഡൽഹിയിൽ അവിടുന്ന് നമുക്ക് മൂന്ന് അവർ ഉണ്ട് തിരിച്ച് ബാംഗ്ലൂരിലോട്ട് സോ വെരി വെരി ലോങ്ങ് ജേർണി ആണ് ഇരുന്നിരുന്ന് ഉപ്പാട് വരാൻ പോകുന്ന ഒരു ട്രിപ്പ് ആണിത്. വാ സിറ്റുവേഷൻ ഇപ്പോഴും നിലനിൽക്കുന്നത് കൊണ്ട്തന്നെ റൂട്ട് കുറച്ച് വ്യത്യാസമായിട്ടാണ് എയർ പോകുന്നത് സ ഇപ്പോ കാണുന്നതാണ് ട്ടോ ഈ ഫ്ലൈറ്റിന്റെ റൂട്ട് അങ്ങനെ നമുക്ക് ഫ്ലൈറ്റിൽ നിന്ന് കിട്ടിയ ഈ ഒരു ഇയർഫോൺ ഒക്കെ ഞാൻ സെറ്റ് [സംഗീതം] ചെയ്തിട്ട് ദാ ഈ ഒരു പടം കാണാൻ വേണ്ടി സ്റ്റാർട്ട് ചെയ്തു വേറെ ഒരു പടം എനിക്ക് [സംഗീതം] ഞാൻ കണ്ട ഫിലിംസ് ആണ് പിന്നെ പിന്നെ ബാക്കിയൊന്നും അങ്ങനെ കാണാൻ നമുക്ക് ഇൻട്രസ്റ്റ് തോന്നാത്ത ഫിലിംസ് ആണ് വലിയ കളക്ഷൻസ് ഒന്നുമില്ല ഫിലിംസ് പിന്നെ മോണിറ്റർ ക്വാളിറ്റി ഒക്കെ ഒരു പിക്ചർ ക്വാളിറ്റി ഒക്കെ ഒരു കുറവായിരിക്കും അങ്ങനെ ഞാൻ ഒരു ഫിലിം ഒക്കെ കണ്ടട് ഇരുന്നപ്പോഴേക്കും നമ്മുടെ എയർ ഹോസ്റ്റസ് ഫുഡുമായിട്ട് എത്തിയിട്ടുണ്ട് അങ്ങനെയാണ് ഞാൻ മനപ്പൂർവം ഉറങ്ങാതെ ഫിലിം കണ്ടതാണ് എനിക്കും നല്ല ഉറക്കം വരുന്നുണ്ടായിരുന്നു കാരണം ഓൾമോസ്റ്റ് ടൈം 12ത എല്ലാം ആയിട്ടുണ്ടായിരുന്നു നുക്ക് നല്ല ഉറക്കം വരുന്ന സമയമാണ് ഉറങ്ങിയിട്ടും കാര്യമില്ല ഉറങ്ങി വരുമ്പോഴേക്കും ഒരു ഫുഡ് [സംഗീതം] കൊണ്ടുവരും അതുകൊണ്ട് ഞാൻ മനപ്പൂർവം ഉറങ്ങാതെ അപ്പ ഫുഡ് വന്നിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഞാൻ നോൺവെജ് ഫുഡ് ആണ് ട്ടോ. ചിക്കൻ കറിയും റൈസും ആണ് വന്നിക്കുന്നത്. അതിന്റെ കൂടെ നമുക്കൊരു ബണ്ണ് ഉണ്ട്. പിന്നെ ഒരു കറി ഉണ്ട് ചോക്ലേറ്റ് ഉണ്ട് ബട്ടർ വാട്ടർ ആൻഡ് ഹെരിക ടേസ്റ്റ് എങ്ങനെ ഉണ്ടാന്ന് നോക്കാം ഫുഡ് വലിയ തരക്കേട ഇല്ലായിരുന്നു വലിയ ഒരു പ്രീമിയം സംഭവം ഒന്നുമല്ല നമ്മൾ മറ്റുള്ള ഫ്ലൈറ്റ്സിലൊക്കെ എപ്പോഴും [സംഗീതം] നല്ല പ്രീമിയം ക്വാളിറ്റി ഫുഡ് ആയിരിക്കും ഇതങ്ങനെ വലിയ സംഭവംൊന്നുമില്ല കഴിക്കാം [സംഗീതം] വലിയ തെറ്റൊന്നുമില്ല അങ്ങനെ അത് കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ട് നമ്മൾ ഒരു വാഷ്റൂം ടൂർ ഒക്കെ [സംഗീതം] നടത്തിയിട്ട് ഉറക്കം വരുന്നുണ്ടോ എന്ന് ചോദിച്ചാൽ ഉറക്കം വരുന്നുണ്ട് എന്നാൽ ഉറക്കം വരുന്നില്ല അപ്പോ പിന്നെ വെറുതെ അങ്ങോട്ടും ഇങ്ങോട്ടും [സംഗീതം] ഒക്കെ നടക്കാം ഇരുന്നിരുന്നു അടുത്ത് അപ്പോ ഒന്ന് വാഷ്റൂമിൽ എല്ലാം പോയി അങ്ങനെ ഒന്ന് കറങ്ങി നടന്നു അങ്ങനെ കുറച്ച് ഉറക്കവും ഇരിപ്പും നടപ്പും ഒക്കെ കഴിഞ്ഞ് [സംഗീതം] രാവിലെയായി. രാവിലെ ആയപ്പോഴേക്കും അതാ നമുക്ക് അടുത്ത ഫുഡ് എത്തി. ഇതാണ് ബ്രേക്ക്ഫാസ്റ്റ്. [സംഗീതം] ജസ്റ്റ് ഒരു ബണ്ണും യോഗർട്ടും കട്ട് ഫ്രൂട്സും ടീ പിന്നെ ഒരു ജ്യൂസ് മാത്രമേ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നുള്ളൂ. എനിക്കത് [സംഗീതം] അത്ര വലിയ ഒരു ഒരു ഫുഡ് ആയിട്ട് തോന്നിയില്ല. എന്നാലും ഓക്കേ ഓക്കെ ആക്ച്വലി വിശക്കും നമുക്ക് ഇത് കഴിച്ചാൽ [സംഗീതം] അങ്ങനെ ഇത് കഴിച്ച് നമ്മൾ ഓൾമോസ്റ്റ് എത്താറായി ഞാൻ വീണ്ടും സീരീസ് ഒക്കെ കണ്ട് ഇരുന്ന് [സംഗീതം] നമ്മൾ എങ്ങനെയെങ്കിലും സമയം തള്ളി നിൽക്കികൊണ്ടിരിക്കുകയായിരുന്നു. reviews.transcript_full: Welcome aboard Thai Airways Business Class on the A350  The video includes a tour of the Thai Airways lounge in Bangkok  Thai Airways calls its Business Class product 'Royal Silk' This video shows the full Thai Airways Royal Silk experience This includes the lie flat seat, amenities and amazing food Royal Silk is one of the world's top Business Classes Our journey starts at Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport  Thai Airways has 5 lounges at Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport This is Thai Airways' Royal Orchid Lounge in Concourse E Comfortable seating is available throughout the lounge A self-service buffet is located in the center of the lounge The buffet features both Thai and international dishes The lounge is open daily from 5:00am to 11:30pm Fresh fruit, salads, and desserts are also available Thai Airways' Business Class lounge also features a quite zone It's a 15 min walk from the lounge to our gate This is the Airbus A350 that will fly us from Bangkok to Munich Thai Airways has 23 A350s in its fleet (average age: 8 years) Our stylish Thai airways cabin crew is arriving at the gate I am the first passenger to board tonight's flight The Business Class cabin features 32 seats in a 1-2-1 layout 17K is my window seat for the 12 hour flight to Munich Some window seats are closer to the window, others to the aisle  Some center seats suit couples, while others offer more privacy The 32 Business Class seats are spread across eight rows Each seat is 20 in (51 cm) wide with a pitch of a 44 in (112 cm)  Every passenger enjoys direct aisle access Tamarind tea & chocolates are served as a welcome amenity Thai's amenity kit is designed in partnership with Jim Thompson  The kit contains Erb toiletries and travel essentials Erb is a luxury Thai skincare and aromatherapy brand The bag's print pays tribute to Thailand's national animal White slippers are provided as well Bedding includes a purple pillow and duvet Passengers also get AKG N60NC  noise cancelling headphone  Thai Airways' safety video is shown prior to departure The video is both informative and visually engaging The video blends safety with Thai culture Animated forests and mythical creatures feature throughout We're leaving the gate at 0:50 am (on time departure) Thai Airways' Airbus A350s are equipped with a tail camera We're turning on the runway Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport is equipped with 3 runways Thai Airways' A350s are powered by Rolls-Royce Trent engines  Thai Airways was founded in 1960 The airline began as a joint venture with SAS in 1960 The airline expanded rapidly across Asia and Europe Thai Airways merged with Thai Airways Company in 1988 The merger created a stronger international airline The airline is known for its Thai hospitality and purple branding Thai Airways is a member of Star Alliance Star Alliance is the world’s largest airline alliance Let's have a detailed look at the Business Class seat The seat controls are located along the edge of the side table Below the table is a Panasonic IFE touchscreen remote  Above the table are a magazine holder and a reading light In front of the seat are an ottoman and a 15.5-inch touchscreen chops in red curry with green banana & rice It is served with French beans, grilled corn and soft-boiled egg Dessert: chocolate hazelnut ganache Post-dessert treat: Thai chocolate pralines Business Class passengers have access to three lavatories The lavatories are equipped with Bath & Bloom toiletries Thai Airways' Business Class seat converts into a fully flat bed In bed mode, the seat offers 73.5 in (187 cm) of length Thai Airways' entertainment system is easy to navigate The touchscreen responds quickly to commands Hundreds of movies and TV shows are available A dedicated children's section is available Thai Airways offers complimentary Wi-Fi in Business Class A moving map is available throughout the flight The Bangkok to Munich flight covers 5,490 miles (8,835 km) A few hours later: I'm waking up above Afghanistan Mid-flight meal: cream cheese stuffed chicken with risotto  Breakfast is offered 90 minutes prior to arrival Breakfast service starts with a hot towel to refresh a little Poached tiger prawns with sautéed mushrooms & obster bisque  Breakfast is served with seasonal fruits and Bircher muesli The dish includes an onsen egg in a crisp vol-au-vent We're approaching the Munich airspace We're landing in Munich at 7:00 AM local time Thank you for watching my Thai Airways Business Class video

reviews.transcript_full: Good morning, everyone. We are flying with ITA Airlines today, Italy's official or flagship airline. This is the first time we're flying with them. We are on our way currently on a bus to the Rome airport, where we'll be flying Rome to Athens today for the first time. We've never flown this airline before, we don't know what to expect. We checked in last night online, so we used their web check and were able to get our seats in row 33, I think it was. Got a window and a middle. Didn't cost us any extra to get those seats. There were options to get paid extra to get further up the front or aisle seats. We chose just to take the seats that they're giving us. So, we're now about 10 minutes away from the airport. I will give you some further information on how our check-in experience goes when we arrive. We have arrived at the Rome airport. We're making our way down to terminal one to check in for our flight. reviews.transcript_full:
Sat Morning 9:30am @ Manchester Airport T2 
Not many pax at CI counters, finish bag drop within 10 min Completed security within 10 min and heading to 1903 Lounge There are quite a lot of food & beverage choices There are two lounges at T2 - 1903 & escape Cathay Pacific passengers use 1903 lounge Not a very big lounge, but it offers a great view through the glass window Wide variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks Free flow of Jacques BARDELOT Champagne and Langlois crémant de loire brut réserve Enjoy a nice light breakfast, champagne & glass coke I really appreciate the made-to-order egg & toast Plenty selection of pastries Here comes to what I love the most in this lounge Cheshire Farm Ice Cream!!! One more glass of Champhagne before going to gate Today's flight was operated by this Airbus A350-900 B-LRO Mentioned in last video, I tried extra legroom seat 60K this time My question is: Is this aisle-access seat? There is a missing seat in front but the flight exit door is in front I think I like this extra legroom seat more than the 2 in front,
as I don't have to bother where to look at during take off and landing and this seat got a window unlike the row in front. You can find the remote at the side of the seat The drawbacks are sacrificing a bit of seat width
for the folding table and the IFE screen and cannot use the screen during take off and landing The screen size is ok.  Given the aircraft is about 7 years old,
a little bit of wear and tear is understandable. Greetings in English and Chinese (Cantonese & Putonghua)
Flight time would be 11h47m The space in front looked barely enough to walk
and would probably bother the passenger. Not so aisle-access as I thought Printed menu was distributed by FA Baked chicken fried rice, Braised beef or vegeterian choice
Mushroom and spinach risotto. Shortly after safety demo, we were ready to depart Cloudy morning, very Manchester Here we go A bottled water was distributed shortly after take off Followed by nuts and drink service (12:05pm) I planned to watch three live Premier League games The live streaming is smooth and clear I really enjoyed it becaues the flight departed at 10:30am UK time,
I did not feel sleepy at all. Lunch was served from the front compartment to the back
I chose the baked chicken rice. (1:16pm) It tasted surprisingly good although the serving may be
a little bit small for lunch if I didn't have my breakfast Always love the view from the window Nice sunset near Georgia After the second game, walk to galley to stretch my legs
Snacks in the galley Hot noodle was my choice. I am quite sure it was customised, s
mell not as strong as those purchased from supermarkets. Another concern of these exit row seats are their
proximity to the toilets This seat is ok, but I think row 59 may feel it a bit bothersome. Cannot sleep at all, can only enjoy the night view from sky. 05:50am HKT, breakfast was served
Also from the front compartment to the back Congee with 2 prawns, not bad 06:23 HKT descending to Hong Kong International Airport
Here are some final thoughts CX Airbus A350 economy class is good
at least better than its 777-300er in 3-4-3 seating config The extra legroom seat 60A/K is ok
Can walk from the narrow space in front But if you wish to walk around quite often, aisle seats
or row 59 seats are better choices Because going in and out would inevitably 
bother the passenger in front In terms of the best seat in economy class on CX A350-900, 
I would prefer bulkhead seats in row 40A/C/H/K. I sat at seat 40C on my return flight, and the passengers at 40A/B
did not have to wake me in order to walk out from their seats Lounge 1903 at Manchester Airport T2 is good I like the made-to-order toast and Cheshire Farm ice cream so much There could be more snacks available in the galley
and it would be better if water and juice were ready to take In-flight entertainment system is superb! I enjoy the 3 premier league games on this flight  No free wifi in economy class unless you are CX Diamond member Hope free wifi will become norm in the future You always need some luck to have a cry-free flight, 
but this time, I didn't. Price. About GBP 800 for a MAN-HKG return ticket
Direct flight is more expensive than that with transfer. For comparison, my wife's PEY ticket with AF & KLM also costed her
around GBP 800, but only with 2 carry-on luggages. Find the best deal is better than stick to any specific airlines IMO. Thank you for watching and I will soon post another video
comparing this extra legroom seat and 40A/K bulkhead seats. Stay tuned!
