reviews.transcript_full: In 2025, Ryanair carried just over 200 million passengers. This is more than British Airways, Air France, and KLM combined. By passenger numbers, they are the largest airline in Europe and in the top five globally. But, they also have the reputation of being one of the most irritating airlines on Earth, and it's all being run by a man who's widely regarded as one of the world's most annoying airline CEOs. I guess people will put up with almost anything if the ticket is cheap enough. But, how did a tiny Irish airline frighteningly close to collapse in its early years become one of the largest airlines on Earth? Well, this week we're diving into the Ryanair story and how it was originally not built to be a cutthroat budget airline, but ended up as one anyway. So, we're flying from Manchester to Shannon on Ryanair here, but I was not traveling alone this time. This portion of my trip was a family affair. We've got some special guests. We've got my stepdad, David, my auntie Karen, and of course my mom is back again. Traveling with your mom is fun, right? >> Oh my god. >> Anyway, let's dive into Ryanair. The airline was founded in 1984 by three guys. There was Liam Lonergan, Christopher Christie Ryan, and Tony Ryan. Now, despite the last names, Christie and Tony are not related. And look, I don't want to discount the first two here. They definitely played a big role, but the guy we're really going to focus on is [music] Tony Ryan. He was the money behind this airline, and he also happened to be the founder of a massive aircraft leasing company called Guinness Peat Aviation. Guinness Peat [music] is pretty important to the story, but we'll get back to that in a second. The original pitch for Ryanair was simple enough. They set out to break the high-fare Aer Lingus and British Airways duopoly on routes between Ireland and Britain. But, this was not the Ryanair we know of today. Early Ryanair served food and drinks. [music] It had two distinct classes. It wasn't all economy. It was basically trying to be a cheaper version of the sort of airline passengers already flew. In 1985, they launched their first scheduled service from Waterford to London Gatwick with a single 15-seat Embraer Bandeirante turboprop. In its first year, it carried around 5,000 passengers, and from there they grew. They launched more routes, carried more people, picked fair wars with Aer Lingus and British Airways across the Irish Sea, and by the end of the '80s, they were carrying close to 750,000 passengers [music] a year. Now, this may sound like a small but successful startup airline, but behind the scenes, the economics were not working. They were charging less, but they didn't have a fundamentally lower cost structure to support these prices. They were serving food and drinks, they had a messy fleet, and good customer service [music] was still a priority. So, as they grew and carried more passengers, they would lose more and more money. By 1990, [music] Ryanair had accumulated heavy losses and was in desperate need for a major restructuring. Many inside the airline were even calling for it to be shut down completely. This very easily could have been another case of a failed startup airline, but Tony Ryan refused to let it die. And this is where Michael O'Leary enters the picture [music] and changes everything. But before we get to that, I think it's worth touching a bit more on Tony Ryan and how he was able to finance this little loss-making airline in its early days. Ryanair would eventually define the majority of his legacy and lead to most of his wealth, but back during this period, it was not his main business. It was, if anything, tiny in his empire. Tony Ryan was busy with a completely different part of the aviation world. >> Pathetic. Thank you. That was easy. God, it's chaos. >> Tony Ryan was born in 1936, and in the mid-1950s, at the age of 19, he joined Aer Lingus as a young dispatch clerk at Shannon Airport. That sounds like a pretty standard start to an aviation career, but it really wasn't. Shannon was absolutely massive in shaping not only the current aviation world, but [music] even just the world we know today. I'm going to dive into this in next week's video, so make sure you subscribe for that one, but in short, Tony Ryan is learning all about the airline business from the inside out at one of the global epicenters for aviation. Over the years, he works his way up and ends up taking Aer Lingus postings abroad. He has stints in London, Chicago, and New York all by the late 1960s. And in 1972, he returns to Ireland and is put to work on a problem that he wasn't even originally supposed to deal with. The guy originally assigned to deal with this had a car accident and was out of action for a year. Tony stepped in as the replacement, but what was this problem? Well, Aer Lingus had ordered two 747s in the late 1960s, but by the time the planes finally arrived in 1971, market conditions had deteriorated and demand had weakened. Suddenly, Aer Lingus had more jumbo jet capacity than it could profitably use. Tony had to find a solution, and in 1973, he does just that. He's able to broker a wet lease deal with Air Siam, a small Thai airline, for one of the two 747s. Aer Lingus would provide the aircraft, the crew, the maintenance, and the insurance, and Air Siam would pay one fee for that package. Today, this is simply known as an ACMI wet lease, and it's a term used all the time in the industry, but back then, this was one of the first deals of its kind. And it works out quite well for Aer Lingus. They reportedly make around 3 million USD in profit from that one deal in the first year. But this was the moment that something clicked for Tony. He realizes that placing the right aircraft with the right airline in the right market at the right time could be a business in and of itself. Tony wants to build this sort of brokerage platform inside of Aer Lingus, but [music] they were, at this point, a state carrier. They were interested in developing new revenue sources, but they weren't about to let one guy spin up a speculative aircraft brokerage [music] firm inside of the company. They did, however, come to a bit of a compromise. In 1975, Aer Lingus partners with the London merchant bank Guinness Peat, and together they create Guinness Peat Aviation in Shannon. Tony takes a minority stake, reportedly by remortgaging his family home, and he runs the company as CEO. Quick side note, Guinness Peat, the London merchant bank, does actually have links to Guinness, the delicious drink. It was founded by the great nephew of Arthur Guinness, the man who started the brewing empire. Anyway, in the early years, GPA is essentially an intelligence [music] operation. Tony and his team travel the world working out who has surplus aircraft, who needs capacity, and how to connect [music] the two. They were essentially a matchmaker. But, then Tony realizes something. If you're already the one placing the aircraft with airlines, why not own the aircraft yourself? That becomes the real business. [music] GPA would go on to help pioneer and industrialize the modern operating lease model. Instead of airlines having to buy every aircraft outright and tie up absurd amounts of cash, a leasing company buys the planes instead and then leases them out. That sounds pretty normal now, but at the time it was a major shift. Tony would go on to scale this new leasing model to, quite frankly, ridiculous levels. By the late 1980s, GPA had become the largest commercial [music] aircraft lessor in the world. To put this in perspective, by the end of the decade, it had cumulative orders and options [music] for more than 800 aircraft, giving it more aircraft on order than any other company on earth. But, by the early 1990s, the aviation market was starting to fall apart. There's the Gulf War, a global recession, and collapsing demand. [music] GPA gets caught in the middle of all of this with billions in aircraft commitments it can't finance. There's a failed IPO attempt, and then the whole thing basically implodes. Tony loses his position and most of his personal investment, and GPA eventually gets broken up with all of [music] the pieces still ending up incredibly relevant today. But, we'll get to all of this in a couple videos time. [music] Either way, the main point here is that Tony Ryan was not primarily an airline operator. He was a deal maker, a systems builder, an aviation capitalist. [music] And I think this kind of explains why Ryanair 1.0 had such a confusing beginning. It had the backing of a man with enormous aviation [music] reach, but his real attention was elsewhere. So, how does Ryanair end up as one of the world's biggest airlines [music] today? But he realizes fairly quickly that he hates it. He quits after only a couple of years and ends up buying a newsagent in South Dublin. [music] And this is where O'Leary's worldview starts to make a lot of sense. There's this famous story where he opens the shop on Christmas Day, but he doubles the price of batteries [music] and chocolates because he knows the customers will have nowhere else to go. >> A very happy Christmas from me and my precious. >> He later recalls that by lunchtime the place is completely cleaned out and it's one of the greatest days of his entire life. I think this tells us almost everything we need to know about this guy. He has no sentimentality. There's no business romance, just pure retail logic. If there's margin to be found, he will find it. After a few years of running the news agency business, Tony Ryan comes calling. He already knew Michael O'Leary. O'Leary had gone to school with Tony's sons and had handled Tony's personal tax affairs during his short stint as an accountant. So, in 1986, Tony brings him back in personally this time to manage his finances and his stake in GPA. But by 1988, this role changes. Ryanair is in deep crisis and O'Leary gets sent in as CFO. After looking over all of the books, his first conclusion is basically shut it down. He's not being dramatic. This is not some mythical founder story. O'Leary is not a dreamer. He's an accountant staring at a set of books that made no sense. He actively begs Tony Ryan to close the airline down. But instead, Tony keeps pushing O'Leary, not just to clean up the finances, but to find a way to make Ryanair actually work. Tony still believes there's an opportunity here, even if the current version of the airline plainly isn't it. And he does two very consequential things. First, he sets up a deal where 25% of any profits above 2 million pounds go directly to O'Leary. This made sure that O'Leary was properly motivated. And secondly, he sends O'Leary to Dallas, Texas. >> Let's go get on board this flight and find my family. To be fair, it's uncomfortable, but it's not It's not actually Frontier bad. Frontier was bad, this is >> In 1991, O'Leary heads to Dallas, Texas to study Southwest, one of the earliest and most important low-cost airlines in the world. He's going there to meet with Herb Kelleher, the founder and CEO of Southwest. Kelleher takes him out for this now rather famous dinner. Over the evening, they talk airline economics, operating models, and philosophies, but somehow, [music] rather incredibly given that O'Leary is Irish, Kelleher reportedly drinks him completely under the table. O'Leary later says that he passed out at around midnight, woke up at 3:00 in the morning, and Herb was still there pouring himself another bourbon. The hangover reportedly lasted days, but I guess the real hangover though is not the bourbon. It's what O'Leary sees at Love Field Airport in Dallas. He sees 25-minute turnarounds, aircraft landing, unloading, boarding, and leaving again in what, by European standards at the time, looked almost absurdly fast. He later compares it to a Formula 1 pit stop. He sees a single aircraft type, the 737. He sees point-to-point flying, no connections, no baggage transfers, no unnecessary complexity. And he [music] sees fares low enough not just to steal passengers from competitors, but to create entirely new traffic. That is the revelation, not cheap [music] tickets on their own. Ryanair had already tried cheap tickets. The revelation is that low fares only really work when the whole airline is built around simplicity, efficiency, and low costs. So, O'Leary comes back to Ireland and starts cutting. The business class goes, the free newspapers go, the old mixed-up identity goes. Ryanair starts moving towards a standard [music] 737 fleet. It pushes faster turnarounds. It strips out everything that slows the operation [music] down. But this is also where O'Leary goes even further than Southwest. Southwest had shown the operating logic, but it was still a much softer, more generous version of low cost flying. For decades, it famously gave passengers [music] free checked bags, plus free snacks and drinks on board. And under Herb Kelleher, the whole philosophy was [music] much more employee first than what Ryanair would become. O'Leary takes the operating skeleton and strips it back [music] even further. There's less sentimentality, less excess, less of anything that does not directly keep the fares down. O'Leary truly takes an [music] axe to Tony Ryan's airline. And over the next few years, it becomes increasingly clear whose airline this is turning into. [music] By 1994, O'Leary is formally CEO. Now, this whole Southwest model works in America because America at this point had a deregulated domestic aviation market. Airlines were able to operate whatever routes they wanted, at least domestically. Europe in the early '90s is not like this at all. European airlines were heavily constrained by bilateral agreements, route controls, fare controls, and national protection. You could not just wake up and decide to fly from Dublin to Milan because you fancied it. The system was built around state interests and flag carriers, not around letting whatever airline had the best model loose across the continent. But luckily for O'Leary and Ryanair, the EU starts dismantling this whole structure throughout the mid-1990s. And by April of 1997, any EU airline can operate any route within the EU, including domestic routes in other member states. Hate on the man and the airline as much as you want, but what O'Leary and Co. did is kind of genuinely remarkable. They fundamentally changed air [music] travel in Europe. reviews.transcript_full: Crossing the equator is more than just a flight. It's a commitment. 15 hours, two countries, and the slow shedding of a Canadian winter for the warmth of the south. This time, the journey to Santiago started with a question. Is a business class seat on a shorter widebody plane worth the premium? I'm taking you through the full experience, the lounges, the food, and the honest reality of the longest flight I have taken to South America. Our morning began at the Maple Leaf Lounge in Toronto. It's spacious, dependable, and exactly the kind of stillness you need before a 6:00 a.m. departure. A quick bite of omelette and fresh fruits and we were off. Looking forward to what lay ahead. Stepping onto the first leg. The configuration is a classic 2x two. It feels more like an upgraded lounge chair than a futuristic pod, though. At 5 hours and 42 minutes, it's a bit of a light version of business class. No pillows or amenity kits here. The seats were comfortable, though. I did spot a speck or two of dirt that felt a bit out of place for a premium cabin, but overall it was a fairly clean cabin. The layout is older, so the buttons are manual and need a bit of a wiggle, but they offer great ergonomic control, including a leg rest and footrest that keeps you nicely elevated. I did find one quirk though. The TV pulls out from the armrest, which is a bit nostalgic to the economy exit rows, but at least there's a dedicated plug for charging. Then came the service. We started with orange juice served interestingly in a paper cup. But when it came time for breakfast, we hit a snack. By the time the flight attendant reached us in row 9, they had already run out of the savory egg options. You know what the funny part is? The attendant still asked me what I wanted. I mean, you only have two options, French toast and an egg. If one of them is not available, why even ask the question? It wasn't much of a choice, and unfortunately, the taste didn't make up for the lack of options. The presentation was lovely, though. The soul was missing. It was a quiet disappointment, saved only by a croissant, a posh pear, and a glass of champagne to toast to better things ahead. The crew must have seen it in my eyes because they brought out extra nuts, sensing I was still a little hungry. It was an okay start. But wait, don't make up your mind just yet. As we started our descent into Panama, I realized that travel is rarely a straight line. It's a series of reset. If you're enjoying this honest look at the journey, I'd love for you to join the community here. Hit subscribe because next we are heading deep dive into Chile and Peru and I don't want you to miss a single moment. Touching down in Panama City felt like a reset. We headed straight to the Copa Club. It's a massive bustling space. The food here was a highlight. Tasty hot options like chicken, rice, and potatoes. Big massive machines for coffee and different kinds of sodas. They even have a full stacked bar for you to enjoy. We only had a short stay this time, but I knew I'd be seeing a lot more of this lounge on the way back. If leg one felt like a light experience, leg 2 to Santiago was the full story. As soon as we boarded the 6 and 1/2our flight, the difference was clear. plush pillows, warm blankets, and a proper amenity kit was waiting for us. We were in the first two rows this time, so no running out of menu items here. We got water bottles and a golden frog, dark chocolate, a 60% cacao treat that tells a Panama story. It was the sweetest addition. Even the champagne served in mini flutes this time felt like a step up. Heat. Heat. Heat. Heat. The meal service was a complete 180. We started with a fresh tomato soup and salad that actually had soul. For the mains, I went with the salmon in a rich cream sauce while my partner had the chicken and rice. Both were flavorful, well paced, and followed by a chocolate drizzled ice cream that made the 30,000 ft view even sweeter. This was the business class I was expecting. On the way home, the experience stayed consistent. I finally got my breakfast eggs. But the real highlight was our long layover. On the return trip, we used our layover to actually breathe in Panama City. Thanks to the breezy immigration process for Canadian passports, we stepped out into the heat, found a local cafe, and wash the city pulse before heading back to the Copa Club. The lounge is beautiful. This time we took a hot shower and enjoyed a mimosa by the window while watching the airport bustle. A perfect end cap. After some research, I found the secret to Copa. Under 6 hours, it's a streamline service. Over 6 hours, they pull out all the stops. It's an interesting rule and I'm curious, have you noticed this on other airlines? At just under $3,000 per person, this wasn't just a flight for me. It was the ability to arrive in South America feeling present and rested rather than depleted. If you are looking for luxury that feels accessible and a way to make the long haul to the south feel like part of the vacation, this is a strong contender. 15 hours later, we were finally crossing the southern hemisphere and Chile was waiting for us. Next up, I'll show you what that journey led to from Atakama desert to Patagonia. See you in Chile. Ciao. Hey, hey, hey.

करना है वो कर सकते हैं। तो रिमोट काफी अच्छे से फंक्शन कर रहा है। लुक्स लाइक ये नया सिस्टम है। नई फ्लाइट है तो इसका रिमोट काफी फंक्शनल है। और इससे पहले जब मैंने एयर इंडिया में ट्रेवल किया था तो उसका रिमोट बिल्कुल भी काम नहीं कर रहा था। इनफैक्ट उसकी वायर ही निकली हुई थी। बट यह रिमोट की अभी कंडीशन भी बहुत ही अच्छी है और इसकी वर्किंग भी काफी स्मूथ है। बिल्कुल भी कोई लैग नहीं है। कोई दिक्कत नहीं है इसमें। इसके बाद हमने इसका टच सिस्टम भी टेस्ट किया क्योंकि रिमोट तो ठीक फिर भी मतलब एक्सपेक्टेड है कि ठीक से काम करेगा। टच देखते हैं कि कैसा है। तो टच भी प्रीटी स्मूथ है। आई बिलीव नए सिस्टम्स हैं इस वजह से या इन जनरली भी एना का जो ये टच स्क्रीन का फंक्शनैलिटी होता है काफी स्मूथ काफी इजी टू एक्सेस और अच्छा होता है। आई एम ऑल सेट टू गो। नेक ड्रेस मैंने पहन लिया है। और ये एयर ऑस्ट्रेस मेरे पीछे सारे reviews.transcript_full: This week, our journey in Hong Kong finally comes to an end, and we begin the very long overnight journey back home. From the energy of the city to the quiet of the departure gate, it's time to see how Luanza handles one of its longest routes from Hong Kong to Frankfurt. Well, welcome to this week's video. Some of you might know instantly where I am, some of you might not. This is the iconic Checkerboard Hill in Hong Kong. [music] The visual aid used by pilots landing into the now infamous Kiteac [music] International Airport, which of course closed in 1998. Lots of regeneration going on down there. In fact, we actually nipped down there yesterday. So, I'll show you a bit more of that shortly. But this week, where are we headed? Back home. Pretty much home anyway. We're flying back to Frankfurt, which is close as we could get to London with Lufanza aboard their Airbus A350. Now, there's a bit of a sad tale to this because when I booked this flight, it was supposed to be a queen of the skies Boeing 747. That's now no longer, and instead we're flying on the Airbus A350. It would have been pretty cool to fly back on the 747, especially because Kiteac was renowned for so many jumbo jets landing and of course all aiming for this checkerboard hill approach. And here we are back at Kiteac. And it's so strange to walk around here knowing that not so long ago, wide bodies skimmed the rooftops just meters above where people now live their everyday lives. Where there are benches and cycle tracks today, there were taxiways, holding points, and crews preparing for one of the most demanding landings in commercial aviation. Kiteac has a new life now. Apartment blocks where terminals once stood. Sky gardens tracing the edge of what used to be concrete and [music] tarmac. Joggers following paths that once guided aircraft in on final approach. Kiteac hasn't disappeared. It's simply been absorbed back into the city. Down here at ground level, it feels almost anonymous. Just another stretch of concrete, another forgotten corner. But in 1998, this was a place of movement, noise, precision, and possibility. Thousands of journeys ended and began right here. And with that in mind, it feels only right that we do the same. So, let's get this journey started back to Frankfurt with Lufanza in economy aboard their Airbus A350. [music] So, welcome to Chep Lac Hong Kong's international airport. Husband here proving a point. I mean, come on. He uh has to carry two cases sometimes, but he's more than capable. Bless him. Um if you are departing with Lufansa Airlines from Hong Kong, then you want to go to zone F upon arrival at Hong Kong's international airport. That's where you'll find all the check-in and backdrop areas. If you do get stuck, why not consult Hong [music] Kong airport's new AI ambassador? I'm not sure how I feel about this. I think I much prefer a good old-fashioned human [music] conversation. So, sailed through the airport, found zone F, which is where the Luanza check-in is, and the desks aren't open at the moment. So, I've spoken to a member [music] of staff. There is a couple of staff milling around here representing Lufanza. Um, and they've said the desks will open at 8:00 p.m. So, we depart 23:45. So, you know, it's nice that they're open not just 3 hours before, [music] nearly 4 hours before, 3 hours 45 for backdrop and check-in. So, we're just stood in line at the moment. Um this is the economy line and then behind me business [music] class and first um and then we'll get checked in and head to the lounge and quite a good selection of lounges through priority pass here at Hong Kong. Anyhow, [music] it was time for us to check in and yes I absolutely nailed the packing again. Our economy tickets had a 23 kg checked baggage limit [music] each which is fairly standard and we were checked all the way through to London Heathro. Check out [music] next week's video for the short hall leg. >> [music] >> After heading through security, it was time for us to take the internal transfer train again to gates 40 through 80 in order to visit the lounge. [music] So, on the hunt for tonight's Priority Pass lounge, which is going to be the Chase Sapphire Lounge. And I've heard really good things about this. Now, recently there was some news that this lounge is closing. I still don't know personally whether it's just closing and not going to reopen or if it's closing for refurbishment. I don't know. Haven't really done my research. Quite naughty of me, but um I'm not too sure if that's been announced yet. So, drop me some comments below if you know anything that I don't. But um we're going to go and try and get in this lounge cuz I've heard really positive things. [music] As we waited to enter, the future of the Chase Sapphire Lounge was available to see and it was sadly indeed set to close on the 5th of January, which means for you it's now a thing of [music] the past. After checking in, we took a lounge tour, and it has lots of different seating areas from informal to formal. There's a lovely bar with all-inclusive signature cocktails, non-alcoholic beverages, and spirits, too. And yes, you know me, I couldn't turn down a [music] cocktail or two. There's also a free pour Coca-Cola machine, a variety of fruit juices and milks, teas from Twinings, an automated coffee machine, and still [music] hot and cold filtered water. There was a cold buffet of salads, meats, cheeses, fresh fruit, noodles, and desserts. Yes, quite an amalgamation. alongside [music] more salads, cakes, bar snack items like pretzels and nuts, Belgian waffles, a variety of fresh fruit from apples [music] to pears and oranges, and a help yourself cheeseboard with crackers and nibbles. There were two types of soup on offer and also a variety of hot meals available including a Thai [music] green chicken curry, stir- fried vegetables, and a pennet with cream and mushroom sauce. Finally, there was also mushroom and pork sumai dumplings available. So, not a bad selection to [music] be fair. So, we're on the move. Uh, we've got a gate, gate 27, but we've not announced for boarding yet. We've got about 95 to 100 minutes. Look at me being so precise in airline minutes to go before we board. So, we've seen that uh at gate 23 there's a lounge called Cyra Lounge that's won a couple of awards. So, we get access in there. I'm hoping it's not going to be too busy. and we'll go and give you a sneak preview of that lounge as well before boarding our flight [music] back to Frankfurt. So, if you are flying from Hong Kong, you do have Priority Pass. Um, get yourself down to the Cairo lounge. It's near gate 23. Um, [music] and highly recommend a stop over. There's a really nice floating bar in the middle of the lounge um with alcoholic drinks, cocktails, things like that. All made up on demand and lots of food, both Western and Asian style, too. So, yeah, appreciate this isn't a full comprehensive lounge review like I normally do. Um, but yeah, thought I'd give you a quick brief tour and show you what to expect uh if you come into the car lounge. We then headed to the gate and queued accordingly with us being in group four this evening. After a strict boarding process, much to Lufanza's credit, we were down the airbridge and boarding this A350 back to Frankfurt. We walked through business and [music] premium economy to find our seats on row 16. Took all aboard the Love A350 900 taking us back to Frankfurt on this very long overnight redeye flight. And um sometimes you make a decision, you know, prior to flying or prior to booking your flight or after you've booked it like we did and paid that 100 per seat selection fee that Lutons are charged for the row 16. And um yeah, my goodness me has it paid off. This seat is great for leg room. It is better leg room than premium economy. There's so much glam reflection off them. So, um we're all up in the climb now. um headed out of Cet Black back towards Frankfurt. Um 13 hours is our flight time this evening. But this extra space, this extra leg room really is an absolute winner. Um it's going to make so much difference. I can tell. Um space [music] is the key to comfortable flight. Hence why sometimes you've just got to bite the bullet and pay for it. We received a full 500 mil bottle of still Hawkworld water and a packet of Ritz style Lufansa branded crackers. Now, it doesn't really restrict me to be fair and I'm quite a large guy. So, um I wouldn't say it's anything to consider, but um being the extremely good, hospitable husband that I am, uh I've jumped over to the B seat to give him a bit more space and he's now reclining trying to get a bit of sleep. Um so, yeah, all in all, um no major complaints about Lufanza. Just one thing to mention is it is incredibly hot on board, and it has been since we boarded. reviews.transcript_full: Greetings everyone from Macau international airport. Thank you for joining us! We're taking the Starlux flight from Macau to Taipei today. STARLUX Airlines, one of the youngest airlines in Asia, is already a five-star airline by SKYTRAX. With comfortable seats, great service, and delicious food—I can't wait! The Macau airport is pretty small and not super modern, but it's not too crowded either. After we get through security, let's head to the lounge and grab some dinner! At Macau Airport, other than the Air Macau lounge, Plaza Premium is the one that handles elite passengers from other airlines. If you're using Priority Pass or Dragon Pass, you'll need to go to the Plaza Premium lounge(Business) next door. Siu Mai Fried fish fillet Roast chicken Fried rice Let me dig into my dinner! Yummy! The plane has 8 business class seats and 180 economy seats. The first impression of the cabin is stylish and comfortable. Three Core Cabin Color Schemes  - Earth Gold: Represents the morning, Rose Gold: Represents the dusk, Obsidian Grey: Represents the night. Today, my seat is 1A, accompanying me for a flight time of 1 hour and 20 minutes. Translation: 4K touchscreen Translation: The headphone jack and charging port are on the left rear. Translation: The headphones and menu are on the lower right side of the seat. Translation: One-touch seat straightening button. The headphones feel premium, and I guess the noise cancellation should be pretty good too. How beautiful Macau is at night, all lit up! Even on a short flight, Starlux still give you a full meal with a menu. Great service! Marinated chicken with quinoa. Cake and Fruits. Creamy soup with croutons. This narrow-body aircraft is equipped with lie-flat seats, making the journey more comfortable. Honestly, I don't really care about legroom. For a short flight, just being able to lie flat is enough. The lavatory is clean. And well-stocked with premium toiletries. A fragrance brand from Thailand, The name is Than. The touch screen of the IFE system is very responsive. The content was rich, but the flight was too short to finish anything. We're about to land at Taipei Taoyuan Airport. Let's enjoy the night view of Taipei. Starlux is a stylish boutique airline with top-notch service and hardware — flying with them truly leaves a lasting impression.

In bed mode, the seat impresses again and the bedding, which for the record is being provided here on a flight less than 3 hours long, is excellent, soft and comfortable. Starlux absolutely excels in the air and this is the highest quality flight I've taken in the last year. And we're now approaching Taipei, where I've got a couple of days to rest and relax. >> [music] [music] [music] >> And so, what can I say? Starlux is my favorite airline. It's as simple as that. They are an airline I will make a special diversion to try and fly on for the simple fact they are so good. When I was a kid, a lot of my cheap toys were marked as being from a magical faraway land called Taiwan and it blows my mind that the country of Taiwan's size now has three high-quality airlines in EVA, China Airlines [music] and Starlux. But Starlux is the top of the tree in my opinion. Sure, I traveled from a regional airport here and didn't get their stellar ground service on departure, but this flight seriously impressed me. reviews.transcript_full: Have you ever heard of a first class service where a Porsche takes you right to the aircraft and you can even enjoy a bath before your flight? Today you're coming along for a ride in the fantastic Lufansza first class from Frankfurt in Germany to Tokyo Haneda in Japan. What's up guys? This is DDN. First class passengers can use the dedicated check-in counter at Frankfurt airport terminal 1. You can check in here but should use the separate first class terminal for the full service. I walked about 5 minutes outside the terminal to reach [music] the first class terminal. The first class check-in lounge is located on the second floor. There was no separate drink service as it connects directly to the lounge, but there were spacious sofas and Bang and Olivesson speakers. I had little time to sit because staff quickly handled everything from printing tickets to checking bags. I entered the lounge fast thanks to them. Security screening takes place at the lounge entrance. It is unique that staff take your passport and return it right before boarding. The lounge inside is modestly sized. At first glance, it feels like a welldecorated business lounge. However, the Lufansza firstass lounge has three unique advantages. First, dining service starts before boarding. You might think first class dining is common, but this is special. While waiting for food, you receive the unique Lufansza first class ticket and rubber duck. The ticket comes in a paper case. It is very practical with a hole cut out for the barcode. They also give you a cute rubber duck. The design and color change periodically, [music] and I received a unique one with a white body and blue beak. The [music] lounge dining menu ranges from simple egg dishes to steaks. I ordered tuna tatakei salad and Australian Wagyu. The food was better than expected despite low expectations for German cuisine. I enjoyed it with a glass of lauron perier champagne. Besides the single menu, the buffet offers various cheeses, desserts, hams, and salads. I give the lounge dining service a very high rating. Second, private rooms and bathrooms are available to all lounge guests. The two private rooms operate on a first come, first served basis, so use them when empty. The space is cozy like a hotel room. From [music] the provided water to the German Verther's original caramels, the details are impressive. Private rooms alone are common in other first class lounges, so they might not have a huge impact. At the very back of the Lufansza first class lounge, there is a bathroom with a separate bathtub in addition to the standard shower rooms. Since there are surprisingly many guests in the lounge, you should book quickly if you plan to use the bathtub. Like a hotel bathroom, it provides robes, bath salts, various toiletries, and balain amenities. I wondered if bathing before a flight was necessary, but it felt great. I felt relaxed enough to fall asleep immediately upon boarding. I think the duck souvenir was meant for playing in this bathtub. It was a special service unique to the Lufanza first class lounge. Finally, the strongest point, the Porsche chauffeur service seen in the thumbnail. Each first class passenger has a dedicated staff member who finds you when it is time to board. Following their guidance down the elevator, you receive the Porsche service from the lounge to your plane. I realized I hadn't gone through immigration yet. A separate immigration process for first class passengers takes place here. I also received my passport back, [music] which they had kept earlier when I did check-in. You must wait inside and cannot go out until your vehicle arrives. This area has casual tables and chairs with nice touches like popcorn and ice cream. Finally, my Porsche has arrived. Unbelievable. Riding a Porsche to the plane is such a special experience. Not all chauffeur services use Porsches. [music] Sometimes Mercedes vans are provided. I was lucky to ride a Porsche Cayenne to the aircraft. I thought I would ride alone, but I shared it with another passenger. From then on, it was a sequence of thrilling scenes for any aviation geek. It was an honor to see various Lufansza aircraft parked at the airport up close. I wondered when else in my life I would ever travel to an aircraft in a private vehicle. The B747-8 I am boarding today, registration D- A B YQ has appeared. While other passengers were waiting in line, the Porsche drove up and stopped right next to the aircraft. Uniquely, Lufansza aircraft are nicknamed after German regions or cities. The aircraft I am boarding today is nicknamed after Germany's northernmost state, Schlesvig Holstein. I took a commemorative photo before boarding and headed up the stairs into the plane. The B747-8 I am boarding today is the only double- deck commercial aircraft along with the well-known A380. Unlike the A380, it is not a full double-decker. Only the front half has two levels. It is nicknamed the queen of the skies due to its distinct humped nose shape. Lufanza's B7478 has a total of 364 seats across. [music] First, business, premium, economy, and economy. Like Korean Airs B747-8i, Lufansza's first class is located at the very front of the first floor. The seats are uniquely positioned even further forward than the cockpit. Unlike Korean Air which has six first class seats with three on each side, Lufansza has eight seats by adding two in the back. There is a communal table in front of the center seats. Sometimes newspapers, snacks or chocolates are placed here. The seats are over 2 m long, perhaps designed for tall Germans. Sitting down, it is nearly impossible for your feet to reach the ottoman. With four windows assigned per seat, the space is very generous. The first class seat design fits [music] Germany well. Areas passengers touch like the seat and ottoman are gray while the rest is a yellowish beige. It looks like a gray seat nestled within beige walls. [music] The fabric seats are massive, nearly 80 cm wide. There are antenna-like reading lights at the headrest. Leather is used for the armrests which hide the entertainment and seat controls. The opposite side of the seat uses completely different colors. Beyond the colors, the single red rose by the window stands out. This rose is a symbol of Lufansa first class. KLM also uses fresh flowers in the cabin. [music] The front of the seat has a unique design with a monitor mounted in the middle of a narrow glossy white partition. While most first class seats are very enclosed with high walls, Lufansza's first class feels open at both the sides and the front. This is an unusual design compared to the current trend of adding high walls and doors to business class for privacy. You can raise the sidewall using the controller in the armrest, but most of the seat remains open. Because the seats are densely arranged and the structure is open, the lack of privacy feels like a significant drawback. Below the monitor, the ottoman is layered with different tones of dark gray and beige. It serves as a spacious drawer, [music] perfect for storing shoes during the flight. The window side is decorated with light [music] beige leather. Since the seat is nearly 10 years old, the age is somewhat noticeable, but it feels surprisingly well-maintained and clean. Practical storage spaces are placed throughout, and the windows are covered with soundproofing panels, making it the quietest [music] space in the cabin. The table is incredibly large and sturdy, and it was very convenient that it could move all the way from one end of the seat to the other. The floor uses different materials and colors from the aisle to clearly distinguish between private [music] and public space. While I was looking around the seat, the flight attendant brought a welcome drink along with macadamia. I was also given a voucher containing a code for in-flight Wi-Fi. Around the time I finished checking the aircraft type, [music] the plane began push back and prepared for takeoff. While modern aircraft like the A350 or B787 are the current industry trend, there is a heavy charm unique to superlarge aircraft like the B747 or A380. In fact, many B747-8i models are used as private jets for heads of state or royalty, including in Korea and the US. However, since 4ine aircraft like the B747 and A380 [music] are practically discontinued, they will likely be hard to find in about 10 years. The in-flight meal service began as the aircraft passed over Hungary. [music] An amuse bouch of sea bass topped with carrots was served with an apparatif. Two types of champagne were offered. And since I am not a strong drinker, I ordered the Lauron Perier Alexandra Rosé 2007 vintage because it looked nice. Uniquely, unlike most airlines that take orders early in the flight, Lufansa took meal orders only after serving the amuse bouch. Since it was a flight to Tokyo, I had a choice between Japanese and Western menus. I was craving Japanese food, but I ordered Western since this is a German airline. Both the western and Japanese courses begin with caviar service. I like the detail of serving the lime wrapped in a small cloth to catch the seeds and neutralize any fishy scent. But several elements considered basic to caviar service were missing. To preserve its flavor, caviar, which absorbs metallic smells, is typically served with a mother of pearl spoon. Lufansza is the first airline I've encountered that serves caviar without one. Furthermore, the absence of blinies, Russian pancakes, or biscuits to serve the caviar on left me feeling that the composition was somewhat lacking. On the other hand, I liked how the meals were brought out on a two-tier cart. They paid great attention to the visual details of the cart itself, even including a three tier tray. For appetizers, you can choose from three options served on small plates. Although I usually eat light, I turn into a big eater on planes. So I tried all three. There was venison served with yuzu mayonnaise and asparagus mousse, lobster kung fit with king crab and Italian barata cheese. A salad with Dijon mustard dressing was also served. I didn't have much expectation for the in-flight meals, but everything was surprisingly decent. [music] The Australian Wagyu steak served with bo sauce was tender, juicy, and delicious. They didn't ask for a specific dness when taking the order, but it seemed to be served medium. For dessert, I had cheese. Coffee was served with Belgian noy house chocolates. In fact, there is a separate chocolate menu, and a selection of chocolates is set up on the center table. I was full, of course, but the service felt like the fastest and simplest firstass dining experience I've had. I suppose you could call it a practical Germanstyle meal service. After finishing my meal, I tried to catch up on some work, but I felt cold and requested a blanket. Interestingly, my laptop wouldn't charge because the aircraft voltage was too weak. So, I gave up on editing and decided to sleep. I went to the lavatory to brush my teeth and change into pajamas. Being a firstass lavatory, the toilet lid was covered in leather like a seat, and there was even a window. While not huge, it was stocked with various toiletries, including razors, shaving cream, and facial mist. Most of all, the single red rose in the lavatory was quite romantic. The pajamas were placed on the ottoman when I first boarded, along with slippers and the amenity kit. The dark navy pajamas with a mandarin collar were very soft and comfortable. When I returned after changing, the turndown service was complete. On top of the 180° flat seat, a mattress pad and a thick hotel style duvet were prepared. I used the pillow I received at boarding and got ready to sleep. Breakfast is served as the aircraft enters South Korean airspace. Thinking about the 12-hour layover in Tokyo before catching my flight to Gimpo made me want to grab a parachute and jump out. I woke myself up with some [music] refreshing orange juice. Once again, the food was brought out beautifully on a cart. Bread, cheese, various berries to mix into yogurt and coffee were served. At the time, the Korean Peninsula was experiencing heavy monsoon rains, so the aircraft shook quite a bit, and I failed to get a nice shot of the table setting. The strawberries looked beautiful, but tasted sour. Eggs and bacon were also provided, and the Lufanza specific condiment set was quite pretty as well. While the second meal is usually simple on most airlines, this one felt particularly modest for a first class meal. Let's take a quick look at the in-flight amenities before landing. The first class amenity pouch contains a toothbrush, toothpaste, and skin care products from Augustina Bowder. It also includes socks, an eye mask, a shoe horn, earplugs, a comb, and mints. I wondered what was inside the thin metal tin, and it turned out to be a clever foldable shopping bag. Since there's a lot to carry when disembarking first class, [music] it's great for packing everything up. True to Lufansa's generous reputation with chocolate, each passenger is also given a separate box of chocolates as a gift. As for the headsets, they used to provide bows, [music] but recently they've switched to the AKGN700, the same model used by Korean Air. After looking through the amenities, the final service of hot towels and juice was provided and the 12-hour flight came to an end. When we talk about glamorous first class, we usually think of Middle Eastern, Singaporean, or East Asian airlines. It is true that there are generally fewer expectations for service from Western airlines. However, having actually flown Lufansza first class, the service was excellent and comparable to Middle Eastern carriers. In particular, the ground services provided at the airport, such as check-in, chauffeur service, and lounge service, seem to be top tier compared to any airline in the world. The quality and attention to detail of the cruise service and the provided amenities were also excellent. However, the most crucial elements, the seats and the in-flight meals were quite disappointing. While the seats themselves were spacious and nice, it was very regrettable that they were an open type design with no privacy protection. The dining service, which should be the highlight of the flight, was also lacking compared to first class on other airlines. Fortunately, these drawbacks seem to be well addressed in Allegris. The new first class being installed on Lufansa's A350. The meals were certainly a bit underwhelming, but they weren't entirely bad as there were several nice details throughout the service. Lufansza First Class may not be the best in the world by my standards. However, the premium service, which is rare for a Western airline, and the unique experience of being driven to the aircraft in a Porsche, are truly unrivaled. This was DDN. Thank you.

reviews.transcript_full: Hey everyone and welcome back to my channel! Today, I'm flying Starlux Airlines business class from Taipei to Los Angeles I've flown Starlux in economy a few times before and I thought their economy experience was incredible, so I'm really excited  to try their business class product today The business class experience started with a great first impression at check-in A dedicated staff member on the floor proactively grabbed my luggage to place it on the conveyor belt for me This was a premium touch I've never experienced when checking in for business class before After a smooth check-in, I headed to Starlux's GALACTIC lounge in terminal 2 The welcome was incredible Upon handing my lounge pass to the agent, he personally walked me into the lounge, helped me with my carry-on at the lockers, and gave me a thorough introduction to the layout of the space The lounge is spread across two floors with seating areas and bathrooms on both levels The two shower suites are located downstairs, while the luggage lockers are exclusively upstairs Both floors feature the same buffet spread, but you'll find certain items like some desserts and the hot dogs, only on the upper level If you're looking for a dessert recommendation, there was a pudding from LOOL that was a total standout I'm not usually a pudding fan, but the combination of its incredibly soft texture and rich, deep flavor made it probably the best I've ever had As for the hot dogs, the flavor was actually great, but interestingly there were no buns to eat them with In addition to the buffet, you can access a full made-to-order menu via a QR code at every table I highly recommend the items under the "Star Rated Cuisine" section of the made-to-order menu One thing I really appreciated was the portion sizes They were small enough to give you a full sense of the flavors without being so large that they felt overwhelming to finish  It allowed me to try several different dishes, which is exactly how I like to eat in a lounge I particularly love the Biang Biang Noodles They were wide and chewy with a nice kick of spice that wasn't overwhelming I actually ordered them twice since they were so good The futuristic aesthetic of the lounge continues into the shower suites, which feature the same gray metals and bright yellow accents The setup here is consistent with what you'd expect from a premium lounge The showers are stocked with THANN Eden Breeze shampoo, conditioner, and body wash However, I did notice slippers aren't provided and the towels aren't wrapped in plastic, but these are minor details in an otherwise well-designed space The shower queuing process is quite manual You have to hand your boarding pass to the front desk And they'll ask you where you'll be sitting and tell you they'll come find you when it's your turn Because there are only two shower suites, I'd recommend putting your name in as soon as you arrive In my experience, you may need to be a bit proactive I think a staff shift change happened while I was waiting for the showers and my request seemingly got lost in the shuffle, so I had to follow up myself to get access It's a great space to freshen up, just be sure to check back in with the desk if you've been waiting for a while Soon it was time to head to the gate Since the lounge is located near the D gates and my flight was departing from the B gates, it was a solid 20-minute trek I'm a fast walker, and even I found it to be a pretty long walk, so definitely budget enough time to get there Business class passengers are in Zone 1, so you're among the first to board Today's aircraft is an A350-900 The cabin features 26 business class seats in a 1-2-1 configuration When I was booking my flight, the Starlux website actually flagged that rows 3 and 7 have partially obstructed window views I really appreciated that transparency, and since the other window seats in rows 2 through 5 were already taken, I opted for seat 6K Waiting at my seat was a plush pillow and blanket, along with a pair of slippers and the Starlux amenity kit Once I was settled in, a flight attendant gave me an incredibly detailed seat tour The entertainment screen is impressive I measured it at about three-and-a-half iPhones wide by two-and-a-quarter iPhones tall There is a digital panel for seat and lighting adjustments, as well as physical "quick buttons" for immediate shortcuts into takeoff or sleep positions For storage, there's a deep side cabinet that houses the handheld remote and universal outlets It also features a wireless charging pad, though I couldn't get it to work despite trying several different placements The cabinet comes stocked with a bottle of Acqua Panna, noise-canceling headphones, and a Onelux facial mask Rounding out the space, there's a lamp at the seat， an additional side compartment for smaller items, as well as a coat hanger by the seat entrance The seat also has a sliding door that was easy to operate and made the space feel private Before takeoff, the crew came by to offer pajamas and asked which size I wanted These pajamas are the new 2026 pajamas that are a part of a collaboration with Paul Smith and replace the old version As we begin to prepare for takeoff, I buckled the over-the-shoulder belt that is required for takeoff and landing Dinner service started soon after we were in the air I'll flip through the menu and wine list quickly here, but feel free to pause if you want to see the full selection I pre-ordered my meals online, which is a service available when managing your trip on the Starlux website from 21 days up to 24 hours before departure It's definitely worth checking out the site because they often have online exclusive dishes that aren't on the regular in-flight menu I chose the Taiwanese menu by YuenJi, a Michelin one star restaurant in Taichung, Taiwan The tea smoked pork and the pumpkin flavored stir fried rice noodles were delicious It was a sophisticatedly and balanced, light meal However, the service tempo felt rushed My main course arrived while I was still working on my starters Having both courses on the table at once created this awkward pressure to choose between finishing my starter or eating the main while it was still hot, which took away from the relaxed, paced dining experience you'd expect During the dinner service, I also tried the boba latte While it wasn't the best boba I've had, it was my first time having it on a plane, and I thought it was a fun, unique offering from Starlux After dinner, the crew came by to ask if I wanted the mattress pad put on my seat I checked out the amenity kit It included a small pouch with products by THREE, including a balancing stem moisturizer, a balancing overnight oil serum sq, and a balancing protective lip bar There was also a dental kit, a comb, earplugs, an eye mask, and socks The lavatory is well-designed, featuring a main mirror with a magnifying section and a waist-down side mirror I also like that they automated the experience: the toilet button is sensor-activated, so you never actually have to touch it They also provide toothpicks, mouthwash, and fabric hand towels Even though they were wrapped in plastic, having actual towels in the restroom is a nice premium touch that I just don't see in other business class cabins It's something I've only ever seen before in ANA first class I changed into the new 2026 Starlux pajamas, which are a collaboration with Paul Smith They were comfortable I actually found them to be a bit more comfortable than the pajamas I had in ANA first class I've heard a lot about the legendary reputation of the previous version of Starlux pajamas, so I'm curious if this new version lives up to that standard For those of you who have tried both the old and new sets, which one do you like better? Let me know in the comments what your experience was Returning to my seat, I prepared for bed I'm 183 centimeters, or six feet tall, and in the full lie-flat position, the legroom was ample The armrest is also adjustable with three different settings: the standard position, a higher position for lounging, and a lower setting that levels with the lie-flat seat Putting it in that lowest position gives you a bit of extra width for sleeping I also tried the seat's Zero-G function, which shifts the chair into a dentist-chair like position and is supposed to trigger a relaxing pulsation on your back However, when I first set it to Zero-G mode, I couldn't feel the sensation at all I even set the pulsation intensity to the highest level using the digital control panel, but even then, the movement was barely noticeable so definitely don't expect a full massage feature here I'll be honest, I didn't sleep well on this flight The cabin air was a bit warm, which made my throat feel dry and the blanket, while comfortable, was a bit too warm for the environment Also, if you're a light sleeper, I'd definitely recommend using the earplugs from the amenity kit or the noise-canceling headphones From row 6, the operational noise and talking from the galley between business class and premium economy were quite noticeable Since I couldn't sleep, I spent some time exploring the in-flight entertainment The library is massive, with a wide range of English-language films, TV shows, and music alongside plenty of Mandarin, Korean, and Japanese content They even had Angry Birds in the game section It's been a long time since I've played that so it was a fun throwback A feature I really like is the heart icon, which lets you favorite movies, TV shows, and music and quickly access them from the menu bar The flight map is also fantastic If you zoom into a city, it displays points of interest complete with pictures They also have a new "live discovery" feed at the  bottom-left hand side of the screen that suggest landmarks and locations related to your destination, which is a great way to get excited about the journey The remote is actually quite unique It has a clean design without too many buttons and features a trackpad area to control a cursor on the screen I love that the remote displays the remaining flight time and has dedicated buttons for quick volume adjustments However, while the trackpad is an interesting innovation, it felt less efficient for navigating the interface than traditional directional left, right, up, down buttons would have been Since the screen was easily within arm's reach and very responsive, I found it much faster to just touch the screen directly I also tested the free business class WiFi To get connected, you just enter your email, last name, and birthday Unlike economy, which is usually limited to texting, the Starlux business class experience included full web browsing While it was a nice option to have, the speeds were very slow If you get hungry in the middle of the night, the crew comes around with snack baskets filled with items like cereal sticks, dried mangoes, chocolate, and rice crackers There is also a snacks menu you can order from I decided to try the Lion's Mane Filet Burger One thing to keep in mind is that even though this is on the "snacks" menu, the burger is actually quite large, so plan your appetite accordingly I feel like there was just too much bun for the size of the patty, but the plant-based patty itself was actually quite interesting I also ordered the peach sparkling drink which was a refreshing and great non-alcoholic option About 90 minutes before landing, the breakfast service began Being a big fan of wagyu, I had pre ordered the wagyu burger for breakfast While the flavors were great, it was a heavy choice for a morning meal In the future I'd likely opt for the lighter congee set that was offered for breakfast from the Asian menu The real highlight, however, was the bread basket which featured a fresh croissant, almond oatmeal honey bread, and a yogurt banana scone They felt like they came straight out of the oven and had this soft, almost cloud-like texture Even the scone, which I thought would be hard, was surprisingly soft and light We finished the service with fresh fruit, and I also ordered the hojicha latte Since I already had the boba latte earlier, I was glad I got to try the other signature drink now I really appreciated the nutty aroma of the hojicha latte, though both the boba and the hojicha lattes were a bit watery Soon, we were preparing for descent and the cabin crew came by with a tray of various candies I appreciated this thoughtful touch and grabbed one of each flavor So, what's the final verdict on Starlux's business class First, in terms of the hard product, there is no denying that this business class cabin can easily compete with some of the best in the industry Everything feels brand new and sleek, and you can tell that they put a lot of thought into the aesthetic However, I did find some of the tech choices to be a bit superfluous For example, the seat's Zero-G has a pulsation function that was barely noticeable even at its strongest setting It didn't really contribute to or detract from my comfort Similarly, the trackpad remote was less functional than traditional directional left, right, up, down buttons would have been, especially since it was often easier to just use the responsive screen within reach While these features were certainly novel, they felt more like bells and whistles As for the soft product, my first impressions were incredible From the seamless check-in to the lounge experience and the initial welcome on board,  the level of proactive, attentive service made this feel like a first class experience on a business class ticket However, during the flight I noticed a consistency gap I interacted with 6 or 7 different crew members, which felt high for a cabin that wasn't even half full I wonder if they were using this mid-week flight for crew training With so many hands involved, this service lost a sense of consistency Onboard, the flight attendants I interacted with most were truly exceptional: attentive and personable in a way that felt very premium But when you receive  such a world-class level of warmth from one person, the transition to a colleague following a more standard, functional service flow becomes very apparent It wasn't that the other staff were lacking, but rather that the  elevated standard wasn't a consistent thread across the entire team Starlux already has a world-class hard product, but I think they're still polishing the gold to reach that final layer of seamless, end-to-end consistency found on legends like ANA or Cathay Pacific Once they do, Starlux clearly has the ceiling to be the best in the sky For those interested, this flight cost 75,000 Alaska Airlines points and $46.63 USD in taxes and fees If you enjoyed the video today, please hit the like button and the subscribe button I really appreciate your support as it really helps the channel and I'll see you in the next video

reviews.transcript_full: Sometimes you book a small plane for the convenience and end up on something much much bigger. I was expecting Stallux's Airbus A321 Neo with short boarding, fast disembark, and hopefully my luggage lands before me. But apparently the universe had other plans and I found myself on their flagship Airbus A350 instead. Economy, yes, but a lot more real estate than I bargained for. So, can that luxury and attention to detail found at the front of the plane find its way all the way back here in the cheap seats? From seat comfort and service to those signature little touches, [music] I'm about to find out if economy can still feel considered on a big plane. As the hottest new airline in Taipei, is it any good? Before we even get to the seat, the service, or the meals, let's set the expectations. I'm going to show you what it's like to fly this aircraft in economy. not from a marketing brochure, but from the perspective of someone who's flown a lot of planes and knows what's worth paying attention to, the details, the quirks, the little things that actually make a flight enjoyable or not. So, stick around because there's a few surprises along the way. For the start of today's video, I've come to the Starux 7-Eleven in Taipei. reviews.transcript_full: Greetings. On behalf of YTM, welcome aboard. Enjoy your flight. Join us today as we fly on Arrow Mexico, the flagship carrier of Mexico, on their Boeing 737 Max 8. Now, we've flown Aerexico many times over the years, and we've also spent plenty of that time on their Max 8. On this trip, we're heading from Mexico City to New York's JFK in economy class, and we're going to take a look at the seats, service, and overall experience to see if Arrow Mexico's 737 Max 8 might be a good fit for you on your next trip through Mexico. If you love to travel and want to stay in the loop with all the latest tips, reviews, and updates, be sure to hit that subscribe button. And don't forget to like and share. We do appreciate the support. Now, let's take a look at Arrow Mexico by the numbers. Most of the information is on their website, but we're going to highlight some of the details that might really matter to you. So, just be aware. So, if carryons and personal items just won't cut it for this trip, you need a checked bag. And with Arrow Mexico, it all depends on your fair class. Basic economy does not include a free checked bag. Most of the other classes do. So, check ahead before you book your flight. Check bag size is also pretty standard at 62 linear in. And here's a couple of YTM pro tips for you. Buying baggage ahead of time is almost always cheaper. And keep an eye on those overweight fees. They do add up fast. Now, Arrow Mexico typically opens up check-in 48 hours before domestic flights and 24 hours before international flights. You can check in at the airport, online, or through the mobile app. And honestly, the app is usually the easiest. Now, some people have asked us, "How easy is the process once you get to the airport?" Simple. Check in online, find a self-service kiosk, scan your boarding pass, drop off your luggage, and just head to security. Pretty simple. And since we're traveling with our pup, Boo on this trip, he deserves a vacation, too. Here's Arrow Mexico's pet policy, just in case you're bringing your little companion along for the ride. Now, before we head to the gate, we're making a quick stop at a few of Arrow Mexico's lounges. We have full lounge reviews coming soon, so just consider this a little taste. So, now we arrive at our gate and ready to board. Today, we're at gate 53. Our flight's on time and our plane is already here. All good signs. So, we grab a seat and wait for our zone to be called. Arrow Mexico typically uses a four or five zone boarding system. Ours was a five zoner today with Sky Priority usually in the first couple of groups. Now, here's a quick look at Arrow Mexico's boarding order, which is pretty standard in the industry. And like most flights, everyone calmly stays seated and waits for their zones to be called. Okay, not exactly. Pretty much everyone stood up at once. But no worries. Boarding moved along and we were on the aircraft right on schedule. Before we look inside the aircraft, let's take a quick look at the seat map for our 737 Max 8. First up is class premier business with wider seats and a lot more legroom at a higher price of course. Then we have AM Plus. A little more legroom and closer to the front. Then you have your exit rows. Usually more space, but some of those seats don't recline, so keep that in mind. Lastly, we have the main cabin economy where you'll find us today. Now, in our version of Arrow Mexico 737 Max 8, there was 166 seats. Two bathrooms in the back, one in the front. That means just two bathrooms serving the entire economy cabin. Not the best ratio, but we made it work. For today's flight, we were located right over the wing in seats 18E and 18F, which were perfectly fine for me, Lily, and our pup Boo. And here are some standard amenities offered on our flight today. In addition, you usually get a hot meal and drinks, including alcohol. Not too bad for a flight under 5 hours. Now, let's take a look at our seats on this Aero Mexico 737 Max 8. They're in a standard 3x3 configuration. Now, I wouldn't say these are the most comfortable seats in the industry, but they were definitely decent. There's a nice amount of cushion on the bottom, and you do have this adjustable headrest. And for a little over 4-hour flight, these seats worked just fine for us. Now, let's take a look at what's in front of us. I'm about average height and I had roughly 2 to 3 in of space before my knees hit the seat in front of me. I'll call that acceptable. And under the seat, I had just enough space to store my 25 L backpack. First up, you have your 10-in personal screen, which we'll talk about in the next section. Then, we have the tray table. And of course, with the tray table comes the tray table demo. I'd say this tray table is a little on the smaller side, but it functioned well for meal time and getting a little work in. You also get a mesh seat back pocket for smaller items. And inside ours was the 7378 Max safety card along with an Aero Mexico vacation pamphlet, I believe. Now, if you take a look down in between the seats, you'll find this universal power outlet and USBA port. I always appreciate having an actual power outlet, not just a USB port. And the fact that it lights up is a nice touch. It makes finding it in the dark a whole lot easier. Overhead, you've got your individual reading lights and personal air vents. Always appreciated. And you have plenty of overhead bin space on this 737 Max 8. And in row 18, we had one full window and part of another. So, I'll count that as two. Now, let's take a look at the if system on this 737 Max 8. They had it in multiple languages, of course. Underneath the screen, you'll find a 3.5 mm headphone jack and a USB port. Both very convenient. Now, this is a 10-in personal screen, which is actually pretty good for economy, especially compared to some of the other flights we've been on recently. Now, as for content, Arrow Mexico selection is really solid. Now, for films, they have a nice mix of new releases, older movies, and classics. And lastly, we have the about section, just in case you want to learn a little more about Arrow Mexico's destinations, fleet, or how to connect. Then you have this seat chat feature. Although we've never really used it, I can see how it can be useful. Now, let's take a look at the Wi-Fi on Arrow Mexico's 737 Max 8. Full disclosure, we did not use the paid Wi-Fi on this trip, but we did use the free messaging through WhatsApp. It was pretty useful. And here's some important information to know in case you do plan on connecting. And once we reached altitude, it was time to dine. A hot meal on such a short flight is a rare thing these days, so it's much appreciated. We were actually pretty optimistic going in because Arrow Mexico has been fairly consistent with their meals and from our past flights, they're usually more good than bad. Let's take a look at what we got. Now, since this was a shorter flight, they also included the small peanut snack with the meal, which was totally fine. We had a fresh salad, and I really like that they don't put the dressing on it. All airlines should do that, but they did provide a packet of Italian dressing if that's your thing. For the main, it was a kind of like vegetable stromboli dish. Hot, flavorful, and we both actually really enjoyed it. And for the chocolate dessert, it was light, not too sweet, and a good way to wrap up the meal. Overall, a solid meal. And once again, Arrow Mexico economy catering comes through better than most. Nice job, Arrow Mexico. After the meal, they dim the cabin lights, giving everyone a chance to sit back and relax for a bit before arrival. And before we knew it, we were landing at JFK in New York City. Now, arriving at JFK can feel a little overwhelming, so if interested, check out our video for a step-by-step guide on how to get from JFK to Manhattan. Now, for some final thoughts, I'd have to say our overall experience with Arrow Mexico was pretty solid. Service was friendly and attentive, and the meal was actually impressive for economy. Connecting through Mexico City can feel a bit chaotic at times, but we didn't run into any real issues. And the seats themselves were comfortable enough for our 4 plus hour flight, and the if selection was better than a lot of airlines we've flown. Plenty of overhead storage, universal outlets, and personal air vents all make the experience a little better. Just keep an eye on those baggage fees. They can add up quickly. So, when flying with Arrow Mexico, you generally get a solid economy experience with meals, drinks, and good entertainment. So, if you're planning a trip through Mexico, we feel they're one of the better options to consider. Safe travels. If you enjoy traveling and like our videos, please subscribe, share, and like. We really do appreciate it as it does help support the channel.

reviews.transcript_full: We're at Warsaw Chopin Airport. Ahead of us is an Airbus A330-300 in Qatar Airways livery. The aircraft that will take us to Doha, Qatar, today. This model is a wide-body, long-haul aircraft used on intercontinental routes. In this configuration, there are nearly 300 seats divided into two classes: business and economy. The A330-300 has two aisles, so even when fully booked, moving around the cabin isn't particularly troublesome. Qatar Airways uses these aircraft primarily on medium- and long-haul routes, such as the one from Warsaw to Doha, which takes about 5.5 hours. In this episode, we'll focus on Economy Class. We'll show you exactly what awaits you on board, the service, the entertainment system, and, of course, the flight itself. We start with a classic: boarding, a quick glance at the interior, and we find our seat. The seats are arranged in a 2-4-2 configuration with a standard pitch. Before the plane takes off, crew hands out wet wipes. Hands can be sanitized. Each seat has a hanger, a paper safety manual, an in-flight entertainment screen, a headset, headphones, a blanket, a pillow, and a drink holder. There's also a fold-out table, which we'll use for a meal in a moment. The Oryx One in-flight entertainment system awaits us on the screen. Qatar Airways offers a wide selection of movies, TV series, music, and games. A special feature is the section dedicated to our destination, Doha. Here, you can read about local attractions, history, culture, and what's worth seeing after landing. Before takeoff, you can watch a Qatar Airways safety video, as usual . It's quite creatively presented. Let's see what else you can watch in the movies section. There are new releases, as well as classics and productions from various countries. There are also games ranging from simple puzzles to classic arcade games. For the little ones, there's a separate section with animated films. Time for lunch. The flight attendant hands out a tray with a meal. We're served chicken with rice and vegetables. A small bottle of water, dessert, and, unusually in economy class, metal cutlery. The whole thing looks aesthetically pleasing and, considering the on-board conditions, quite tasty. The restrooms are also clean. There are air freshener sprays, running water, and paper towels. It's all the usual fare, but it's really well-maintained, and the restrooms are indeed spotless. A promotional video for Qatar plays on the screens before landing. A few shots of museums, the desert, stadiums, and seaside bars. A mini-guide that might inspire you to plan your sightseeing. After landing and taxiing, it's time to disembark. Standard procedure: first business class, then economy. A final glance at the cabin, and we're off to the terminals in Doha. This is what our flight from Warsaw to Doha with Qatar Airways looked like on an Airbass A330-300. If you have any questions about the flight or the route itself, let me know in the comments. If you'd like more flight and travel vlogs, subscribe and give me a thumbs up. See you in the next episode.
