Today we're flying on one of the most anticipated 
new cabins, the Aria business class suites from   what many would consider to be one of the most 
highly regarded airlines, Cathay Pacific. Over the   past few years, Cathay has definitely had a bit of a 
rough go of it amongst political tensions in Hong   Kong, being shut down for an extended period of 
time due to 2020, and the struggles with employee   morale. Not to mention that competition with other 
airlines has only grown fiercer over the years.   But with the release of their brand 
new Aria business class suites,   is this Cathy's signal that they are back to take 
their place as the crown jewel of the skies? Let's   find out on today's 11 hour and 35 minute 
flight from Hong Kong to Vancouver, Canada. But first, our trip starts off here at the Hong 
Kong airport terminal 1 at the Cathay Pacific   the Pier Business Class Lounge. Hi. So, let's 
talk about Cathay's lounges a little bit. So,   as a business class customer, you 
do have access to three of Cathay's   lounges here in Hong Kong airport. There is 
The Wing Business, The Bridge, and The Pier   Business where I am right now. For those of 
you who are looking for shower facilities,   keep in mind that only the Pier Business and the 
Bridge have shower facilities. The Wing does not,   and the Wing is also the smallest 
out of the three. So, like I said,   you can access all three if you want. If you 
have the time and you want to lounge hop,   you can definitely do that. Or you could just 
go to the one that's closest to your gate. For   those of you who are interested in seeing 
what the Bridge and the Wing look like, I   did cover them as part of my other video on Cathay 
Pacific when I covered their older business class,   which I will link in the description box below 
for those of you that want to see that. But in   the meantime, let's check out the Pier Business. 
Cathay Pacific's The Pier Business Class Lounge is   located in Terminal 1 by gate 65. It's the 
largest of Cathy's business class lounges   and spans over 3,300 square meters or 35,500 ft. There is a 
buffet with both Western and Asian food options,   a full service bar, and of course, their famous 
noodle bar, which serves an assortment of dim   sum and multiple noodle options. I of course had 
to get a bowl of my favorite, the dan dan noodles. In the meantime, let's check out the shower 
rooms. The shower rooms are stocked with Bamford   soaps and lotions, as well as other amenities 
like dental kits and cotton pads. Although,   you can request additional amenities like 
deodorant and slippers at the front desk as well. And even though the shower rooms are quite small,   I always find them to be clean and 
well-maintained. So, no complaints here. All right, that's it for the lounge. Now,   let's get going to the gate so 
that we can board our flight. Today, we'll be boarding out of gate 23. And 
since our aircraft today doesn't have first class,   we'll get to board in group one as business class 
passengers. Our flight does depart slightly late   today, but eventually we get boarding. I'm just 
thankful that the flight wasn't cancelled. And as   I make my way towards the seat, I didn't notice it 
at the time, but looking back at this footage now,   you'll notice that the guy in front 
of me is stealing random pillows.   Here he is taking one pillow. And then here 
he is taking a second pillow. Not sure what   he plans on doing with these, but I feel bad 
for whoever seats those are. All right, that's   enough about the pillow thief. Our 777-300er 
today has a 1-2-1 configuration in business class.   And we will be seated in seat 16K today. And here 
they finally are, the long awaited Aria suites.   These new seats have a 21 inch or 53 cm width in 
between armrests, although the width does extend   to 25 inches or 63.5 cm at the shoulder area. As 
for row pitch, you'll get 43 inches or 109 cm. Hidden   inside the side table, there's a small storage 
compartment where you can store some small items.   There's also a storage locker where you'll find 
the headphones, a bottle of water, and a mirror   that flips out. And just down below, you'll also 
find another small storage compartment. In terms of   charging outlets, you'll get a USB A port, 
two USB C ports, and a universal power port.   Side table also has wireless charging, although 
it is hard to miss if you don't look closely.   And finally, we have every introvert's favorite 
part, which is the privacy door, making this a   fully enclosed suite. Before takeoff, the crew 
stops by and gives us hot towels for our hands. They also come by with some welcome 
drinks. There was a choice between   orange juice, champagne, and Cathay's 
signature drink, the Cathay Delight,   which is a mint kiwi drink. It's very 
refreshing, and I highly recommend it. Now that we're in the air, let's check out the 
food and beverage menus. We'll start with the   beverage menus first. This was the wine and 
champagne list. And then here's the beer,   spirits, cocktails, and non-alcoholic beverages.

there were Bamford soaps and lotions. And tucked   away in the drawers, there were some antiseptic

which we always love to see, of course. Lastly,   there's also a full-length mirror along 
the back wall. Now, before we head out,   let's take a moment of appreciation for these 
custom door locks on the lavatory doors. This   is my first time seeing custom locks like this in 
a lavatory door on an airplane, and they really   give it a premium feel. And just one more thing, 
on your way back from the lavatory, make sure you   check out the small art gallery that they have 
on board, which features art from local artists. All right, now let's finally head back to our 
seats so that we can get it into full liat mode.   Back at our seats, let's get everything set up. 
I slip on the mattress cover and there are seat   controls at the edge of the side table to get 
it into lie flat mode. In fully lie flat mode,   the bed is 79 inches or approximately 200 cm. The bed 
sheets are also by Bamford and they're quite nice.   I did find them to be thick enough to keep me warm 
throughout the flight. Most importantly though,   this is what the footwell space looks like in lie 
flat mode. I do think it's more narrow compared   to their older cabins, but I personally didn't 
have any issues with foot space. I am quite short   though at 5"3' or 160 cm, so taller people, you

yt_comments.author: @markjones2781
yt_comments.text: Hmm, The showers at the CX Pier Lounge are dark and tiny (I'm 190cm tall and fairly lean at 90kg). Moving about or even taking off your shoes is a challenge. The clammy humid air is suffocating. The showers at Changi are much better! As for the Aria Suite itself, despite its Instagram wow factor, it has many down sides. The IFE screen is just too damn big. It's like sitting in the front row of a cinema. The leg space/cubby hole is cramped and you can't swing the IFE screen out of the way like in the old cabin. Just what is the point of storages spaces so small you can't drop a handbag or whatever into? The wireless charging spot doesn't work in the real world of a moving/vibrating plane. There is no reading light! For those of us who still read books this is a tragedy. Finally, the door offers little privacy from people or crew walking up and down the isle and yet takes the claustrophobia level to an extreme. In summary, the Aria suite is a step backwards not forwards. Thankfully, the CX crews are simply fantastic and go some way to making up for the deficiencies of the new hard product.

The inflight entertainment system really is the only area for improvement that I was able to identify on my flight. We're just exiting this Airbus A350-1000 that brought us in from Auckland. It's 10:43 at night right now which gives us an easy 4 hours to make our 2:45 a.m. flight to Vienna. My main goal during this transit is to get something to eat and have a shower. Not just did we get a super convenient stand at the terminal which meant very little walking to security, the check there was also super quick. It's 10:54 p.m. and we're done with security and ready to head out again. That's very impressive. At least Doha Airport is an efficient airport. I'm saying at least because as a whole, I am not a fan of this airport. I've mentioned in a previous video my disdain for closed-off gate areas which trap you there before boarding. Doha has plenty of those. But the airport is also generally very uncomfortable as food and shopping outlets are even more expensive than what you might be used to from other airports. And since Qatar Airways flights arrive in waves, if you transit there like I am, you'll be inside the terminal during its busiest hours. Unfortunately, the airport's facilities do not seem to be designed to handle this number of guests which reduces the comfort for everyone. Let me show you this at the example of a pay-to-use lounge. Doha has a bunch of these lounges which people like me can access using programs like Priority Pass or certain credit cards. Nowadays, there are a lot of people like me though which means the lounge gets unbearably crowded. Just got myself an espresso and there is nowhere to sit. Look at this. There's not a single available seat anywhere. To the airport's credit though, they're keeping the lounge spotlessly clean. Usually, lounges like this look horrendous when they're so busy but the staff is working super hard and are doing their best. Here's an observation I find amusing. See those dishes? What What do they remind you of? Hummus, salad and so on on one side, sweet dishes on the other, cold savory items, appetizers and desserts basically. But not just any. Those appear to be the exact ones Qatar Airways serves alongside their economy class dishes in flight down to the plastic cups they're in. This is not a complaint as Qatar Airways economy class catering is very good but it does take away from the elegance of a lounge if you serve deconstructed economy class meals there. But there really isn't much elegance in this anyway. This was the Al Maha South Lounge. There's a fairly new Al Maha North Lounge that was way less crowded during my stay at the airport. So while still not great, the airport is doing its best to improve things. As for the shower, there are a few outlets called Sleep Over available where you can make use of private nap pods and rooms to take naps in and use their shower facilities. I opted for the latter which was included in my Priority Pass membership too but you may also opt to pay and boy was I happy to clean off the sweat and stench of a 17-hour economy flight. As part of the airport's latest extension, they added what they called the orchard, an indoor green space to add tranquility to your travel experience. I am a huge fan of real plants in airports. They just calm me down so much. Often airports resort to plastic plants which well, cheaper but easier to handle. But these are actual trees and bushes inside the building and I love it so much. I can't help but think of Singapore Changi Airport's Jewel though and I can just picture some airport executive in Doha being like, "I want that, too." Overall though, the airport is architecturally stunning and lately has also become more bearable from a passenger perspective. Still, the world's second best? Come on, Skytrax. We're finally ready for boarding. Like many flights in Doha, ours has a remote stand, too which means we'll have to take a bus. Thank you. The triple 7 over there is about to depart to Paris Charles de Gaulle as QR41. Usually, I don't mind bus rides too much but Hamad International Airport is so big that bus rides can become uncomfortably long. According to the timestamps of my video clips, this bus ride took over 10 minutes. I know, it doesn't sound too bad but it's 2:00 in the morning, it's 30° hot outside and I just came off of a 17-hour flight. Believe me, it felt longer than 10 minutes. Taking us to Vienna tonight is Alpha 7 Alpha Hotel Yankee, a 2012 built Airbus A320. It's one of 27 A320s in Qatar Airways fleet which operate on the carrier's dense short-haul network as well as selected mid-haul routes such as to Kigali, Zanzibar, Budapest and Vienna. Up front, the cabin is fitted with three rows of Collins Aerospace parallel diamond seats. This means that business class passengers get the comfort of a lie-flat seat even on a plane this old. It is important to note though that not all of Qatar Airways A320s feature lie-flat seats in business class. The other version which we have showcased on a flight from Doha to Erbil back in 2019 is fitted with Recaro CL4400 seats in business class and standard Recaro BL3530 slimline seats in economy class without an entertainment system. In rare circumstances, operational issues can lead to these A320s being used on mid-haul red-eye flights like this one which I would say is unacceptable for an airline like Qatar Airways. Economy class on our plane consists of 120 of these older Recaro CL3620 seats in the A320's standard 3-3 layout. I'll spend the next 6 hours in 18F, a starboard side window seat. The headrest covers are made from a single-use fabric and the entire headrest can be adjusted vertically with fixed ears adding to its comfort. Being 180 cm tall, the legroom is disappointingly small. While my knees have enough room, the seat is so low that stretching my legs is barely possible. And this plane is fitted with very large, clunky hardware boxes. Older entertainment systems used to require these and I've encountered them before aboard Qatar Airways Airbus A330 where they were equally bothersome. Luckily, the CEO has announced the A330s are due to be retired in 2022 and the A320s in 2024. Uh hold on. It's 2026 and they're both still here? Ugh. Beneath these seats, you will find universal power ports, which I highly appreciate. Another useful feature is the little extra compartment at the front of the seatback pocket. The seats also come with bi-fold tray tables and an adjustable entertainment touchscreen, to the sides of which are a coat hook and a USB A port to charge smaller electronic devices. In the ceiling above, reading lights are installed, and you got your own adjustable air vent. The audio port for the entertainment system is located on the inside of the armrest, ensuring it pokes your leg the entire time. Plus, it makes them break quite easily. The age of the screen really shows when compared to an iPhone 15 Pro Max. Not much bigger anymore. A blanket and pillow are provided, too. Once again, with a fairly scratchy single-use cover. Compare that to Etihad, for example, where you'll find much softer, reusable fabric covers. Sounds like a small thing to whine about, but when trying to sleep in economy class, this can honestly make a big difference. And beside me here, little toiletries are handed out before departure. 2:25 a.m., and we are almost ready to go. A Holzkern watch like this one joins me on most of my trips because I really like how well their natural aesthetics fit with my style of brown and beige tones. But, they don't just offer things that fit me, but rather have a wide variety of watches, jewelry, and other accessories made from materials like sustainably sourced wood, stone, or even things like leaves and peacock feathers. And that's what makes their products fantastic Valentine's Day presents because each piece is unique, just like that special someone. Holzkern has been a long-term supporter of our channel and I've visited their headquarters before, meeting all of the amazing people that make the company work. And they are superb to deal with, too. With 24-month warranties on all watches, free worldwide express shipping with products arriving in 3 to 5 business days, and if you're based in the United States, customs fees are fully covered. On top of that, for a short time only, you'll get 15% off your entire order when using the link holzkern.com/simply and coupon code aviation at checkout, plus a free red gift bag for your loved one's present when ordered until February 14th. Now, we're finally getting ready to depart, our final flight of the trip. Shortly after takeoff, the crew started their service, offering us a beverage and a sandwich. Our choice was between a vegetarian sandwich or one with chicken, where I went with the latter. Q Zine is a cute play on words. Along with it, I once again went for the airline's signature mango Bellini, which is mango juice with club soda and optionally some other things. For a sandwich, the quality is all right. I had way worse on a plane. But, for an airline like Qatar on a flight of this length, I honestly would have expected a hot meal service. Afterwards, little bottles of water were handed out, too. As we're cozying up for the night, let's have a look at what the in-flight entertainment system has to offer. The interface looks the same compared to the one we encountered aboard the Airbus A350-1000 just now. You can tell the touchscreen isn't the newest anymore. Content-wise, the selection is all right for the length of flights this aircraft operates. Obviously, it's a notably slimmer variety compared to the one aboard the A350. There are a bunch of movies, an audio library, TV shows, a dedicated kid section, and an old 2D in-flight mapping application. Compared to their A350, it's night and day, no question about it. But, that's almost an unfair comparison. For an Airbus A320 to even have an in-flight entertainment system installed is fantastic. You won't find that on most European airlines, so I'm certainly grateful for it being available at all. Cruising through the night with gas flaring across Iraq and Iran, illuminating the night sky. This happens when you drill for oil because there's always some gas that comes with it, and for safety and a lack of infrastructure to capture it, it's often just burned off. Speaking of releasing dangerous gases, the lavatories of this plane are small, but have got everything you need, including a changing table, some paper cups for when you brush your teeth, face and hand towels, hand soap, and eau de toilette. Around halfway into the flight over northern Turkey, the cabin lights came on and the crew started another round of service. This time, a hot breakfast. I honestly did not expect this after the sandwich they handed out in the beginning. I was sure that was going to be it. A snack service and a full meal service on a 5 and 1/2 hour flight that departs in the middle of the night is incredibly impressive. But, I can't help myself but be annoyed by the timing. It's less than 6 hours from Doha to Vienna. Do they have to serve the meal in the middle of the flight? Couldn't they have done so after takeoff or an hour from landing? Why now? Everybody was sleeping. Nobody would have minded if they waited another hour. Anyway, the meal service itself was just superb. Qatar Airways once again offers three options, either a frittata with chicken sausage, which is what we've got, an omelet with sweet potato, or some sweetish I didn't really understand. But, I prefer savory breakfast anyway, so here we are with our frittata, served with creamy spinach, a rösti, and a chicken sausage. Alongside our breakfast dish, we received a warm croissant and some strawberry jam, as well as a bottle of water, a cup of raspberry yogurt, and some fresh fruit. And come on, these are the same plastic cups we saw in the lounge, aren't they? To drink, my morning combo of coffee and orange juice, and once again, some metal cutlery. The beverage selection is extensive and includes complimentary alcoholic drinks, too. They even offer real French sparkling wine in economy class, with their brand of choice currently seeming to be Veuve Clicquot. It's basically champagne, but just from a different region of France. Quality-wise, this is a 10 out of 10, an all-around phenomenal breakfast service with a diverse and tasty main course, sensible additions like a warm croissant, yogurt, and fruit, and presented nicely alongside bottled water, beverages of choice, and metal cutlery. There really is nothing they could have done better in this regard. What continues to puzzle me is the timing. So, let me get this straight. We departed Doha shortly before 3:00 in the morning, got a sandwich after takeoff, lights off, and everyone went to sleep. Then, 2 hours after that, lights back on, a full hot breakfast is served, but we're not at the end of the flight. We still have another 2 hours to go. So, now lights are off again, and we go back to sleep? What the intention here is continues to elude me. After another 2-hour-long nap, we have begun our descent and are nearing the end of our day-long journey back home from New Zealand. Qatar Airways continues to laud itself with its many accolades. The world's best airline is what it loves to call itself. Undoubtedly, Qatar Airways is an excellent choice, regardless of what aircraft or class you choose to travel with them. Flawless meal services, cabins that almost always come with entertainment screens, generous legroom, and elegant design features. However, from overcrowded Doha Airport to its extended bus rides, the old A320s and A330s that continue to grace Qatar Airways fleet with its uncomfortable, tight cabins and poor entertainment quality, it has room for improvement. I think even the world's best is allowed to not be perfect, but this level of imperfection just makes their marketing seem disingenuous. Should you choose Qatar Airways when you come across a good deal? Absolutely. They're not a bad airline by any means. But, are they better than every other airline on the planet? Of course not. I wouldn't even go as far as to say they are definitively the best one in the Middle East. Etihad offers more comfortable pillows, Emirates more substantial meals. There are aspects in which their competition is better. At the end of the day, the differences between the three are too small to justify spending more on one over the other. So, picking whichever one's the cheapest or offers the best flight times is the way to go. But, I will gladly be back on Qatar when the opportunity arises. With that, welcome back to Vienna. I hope you have enjoyed this exhaustingly long journey and I was able to give you a good impression of what it was like. As always, please feel free to let us know where we can do better and if you have any airlines or routes you want us to try in this new year. And whether for you or a loved one, Holzkern has something for everyone. But, whether you are a channel member, a subscriber, or are simply stopping by for this one video, thank you very much for watching and coming along. I'll see you again for a new video next week and until then, safe travels.

reviews.transcript_full: Does BA Club Suites live up to the hype? After three incredible weeks in Maitius and Kenya, it was time to head home. And what better way than in British Airways flagship A350 featuring the club suites. Can BA compete with the world's best business class? Stick around and let us find out. Nairobi airport is relatively small and gets busy during peak hours, so the fun begins outside. Before you even reach check-in, there's a queue just to get into the terminal. Now, I'd originally picked seat 1K, but I switched to 10K last minute. Why? To avoid the galley noise, and honestly, the engine views on takeoff from row 10 are absolutely spectacular. After check-in, they thankfully have fasttrack security here, which is handy given the crowds. British Airways doesn't have its own lounge in Nairobi, so eligible passengers are sent to the Plaza Premium Lounge, also used by several airlines, including Emirates. It's small, but surprisingly pleasant with warm decor and comfortable seating. There is also a second room at the back which is much quieter. The food here was genuinely good. article_quotes.text: Executives at seatback IFE specialist RAVE Aerospace have for many years talked to airlines about bringing more content, higher resolutions and larger screens to the aircraft cabin.

The Brea, California-based firm’s portfolio certainly reflects that evolution; its 4K miniLED HDR 10+ Liquid Crystal Displays can now be sized up to 32 inches, and its latest embedded IFE systems feature massive cloud networked storage and powerful processing.

We think they can transport them someplace virtually,” Louis Poupard, RAVE’s staff product manager said at the Aircraft Interiors Expo in Hamburg, where, together with seatmaker Safran Seats, RAVE introduced the premium suite demonstrator Origin.

Made of micro-LED bendable panels, the Immersive Display Concept from RAVE that is at the core of Origin is complemented by advanced seating technology and Euphony headset-free audio from Safran Seats.

RAVE and Safran Seats are not alone in exploring how a deeply immersive IFE and engagement experience — as achieved with vast screen real estate and compelling content in a premium suite — can transform the passenger experience.

Origin’s reveal comes two years after Collins Aerospace and Panasonic Avionics at AIX 2024 unveiled MAYA , their next-gen business class seat concept featuring a 45” curved ultra-wide OLED screen from Panasonic.

In terms of screen footprint, RAVE used the equivalent of 17.5ft in the semi-enclosed Safran Seats suite — including real estate above the passenger’s head — to transport attendees to another time or place.

By enabling passengers to escape from reality beyond the aircraft, airlines can create “sticky, really cohesive experiences,” said the RAVE executive, confirming to RGN that the firm has “already filed a few patents” around this IFE/seat integration project.

reviews.transcript_full: Well, good day and welcome back to the Flying Doctor channel. On today's one minute flight review, we'll fly with Starlocks on their inaugural flight from Taipei to Ontario, California. Nothing special in the check-in hall that distinguished today's historic flight. So, I quickly got airside and checked out the Oriental Lounge. This lounge is one of Priority Passes 2025 lounges of the year. [Applause] [Music] A party at the gate is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. So, let's head down and check out what's in store. There was an executive from Starbucks, a former MLB pitcher, games and giveaways. Just before boarding time, the crew passed through the waiting area. Tonight's captain is none other than the Starlux founder. I made the journey down the jet bridge and onwards to the last row of the aircraft, where I'll be seated for the 12-hour journey. The cabin was very clean, modern, and the colors were warm. At the seat was a pillow with a soft case, blanket, slippers, and headphones. We were pushed back from the gate and quickly airborne. Dinner service was a little uncoordinated, but the meal tasted decent and was a good size. Not everyone was able to get their first meal choice, and the FA is in charge of my section almost forgot the dessert. The I system is very responsive, has a good mapping system, games, and movies, but the TV show catalog is hit or miss. After a few hours of broken sleep, the cabin crew announced the second meal service would begin shortly. I was able to pre-select both meals on tonight's flight. The main lacked flavor, but the croissant was the best I've had in the air to date. Knowing we were overland, I became irritated by my inability to adjust the window darkness. Roughly 20 minutes prior to landing, light began to shine through and I could once again see the outside world. A water can salute welcomed us to Ontario. How much did this flight cost? I paid $655 for the one-way ticket and seat selection, which equates to 9.6 cents per mile. As always, thanks for watching. See you.

reviews.transcript_full:
Today we're flying on Asia's 
most hyped up airline,   Starlux in premium economy from Los 
Angeles to Taipei on their A350-900. We'll check out their seats, the food, and of 
course, the service to see if it's worth the   cost to upgrade to Starlux's premium economy from 
economy class. Or maybe we'll discover that it's   just a huge waste of everyone's hard-earned 
money and more importantly a waste of time.   But let's find out together which one it is on 
today's flight. As a premium economy passenger,   you get two pieces of luggage weighing 23 kg 
or 50 pounds each. Unfortunately though, there's no   priority check-in or security, so you'll have to 
use the same check-in counters as economy class. Okay, so I just finished clearing security 
and unfortunately Starlux does not provide   premium economy passengers with lounge 
access. That is okay though. I am still   super excited to finally try out their premium 
economy. So, let's get to boarding. Today,   we'll be boarding out of gate 206. As a premium 
economy passenger, you'll get to board with one   personal item and one carry-on item with a 
max weight of 7 kg or 15 pounds. And they   will actually weigh your carry-on bag to make 
sure it's below the max weight limit. Here is   my bag getting weighed. This is actually only the 
second time in all my years of traveling that an   airline has weighed my carry-on bag. The other 
time was with EVA Air. Thankfully, my carry-on   luggage just met the exact weight limit. But 
let me know if you've ever had your carry-on   weighed at the gate before boarding as well. As 
a premium economy passenger, you'll also get   priority boarding. You'll board in group two after 
first and business class, but before economy. All right, it's now time for us 
to get our boarding pass scanned   and our passport verified and get on the plane. Our A350-900 today has 36 seats laid out in a 2-4-2 configuration in premium economy. The seats are   fabric with an 18.7 inch or 47.5 cm width. 
The pitch is 40 inches or 101.6 cm. In terms of   legroom space, this is what it looks like and what 
we'll have to work with for this 15 hour flight.   And this is what it looks like under the space 
in front of you for your personal items or if   you want to try and stretch out your legs. Also, 
below the seat, you'll find both a calf rest as   well as a footrest that pulls out. In between the 
seats, there's a double wide armrest, so you won't   have to fight your neighbor. And at the end of the 
armrest is also a small cocktail tray for drinks.   At the side of the center armrest, each 
person gets a three-prong headphone jack,    a USBA port, a universal power port, and 
a USBC port. And finally, for the recline,   you'll get 8 inches or 20.3 cm. You can see what the 
recline looks like here, as the person in front   of my seatmate is fully reclined, whereas the 
person in front of me is not reclined at all.   And here's just another angle of the recline. You 
can see the person in the aisle is fully reclined   onto the seat behind them as well. Before takeoff, 
we're given small bottles of water as well as some   moist towelettes for our hands. There wasn't any 
real towels, just the moist towelettes. And before   we know it, it's now time for the safety video 
and take off. Because this flight departed at   12:30 in the morning, the crew gets started 
on meal service immediately after takeoff.   This is what the menu looks like. There were 
no paper menus, but you could pre-order online,   which is what I did. The menus for both the 
food and beverage could also be found on the IFE. The food options were the same regardless if you 
pre-ordered or ordered on board. As for beverages,   they had two signature cocktails available, 
as well as wine, spirits, beers, liqueurs,   and non-alcoholic beverages. And all of these 
beverage options are complimentary, of course. My meal arrives and everything is served on 
one tray with real ceramic dishes as well   as metal cutlery. Whereas in economy, you'd get 
disposable food containers and disposable cutlery. The appetizer was a smoked duck with 
a pearl barley salad. I loved the   smokiness of the duck and it was quite tender. The   pearl barley salad had great texture 
and it was also really tasty as well. For my main, I ordered the Thai seafood 
curry served with ginger jasmine rice and   roasted vegetables. It came with some 
really nice sized scallops and shrimp,   and the flavors were really incredible. The 
roasted vegetables and the jasmine ginger   rice were also cooked really well 
and made for a nice accompaniment. There was also a side of fruit and a dinner roll 
with some butter. Lastly, for dessert, it was a   guava cheesecake. This was just all right. It 
wasn't terrible, but it wasn't anything special   either. Now that dinner is done, let's take a look 
at the amenities, and then we'll go check out the   lavatories. For the amenities, you'll get a pair 
of slippers. You also get a more elevated amenity   bag by the brand Smiley. Inside the amenity bag, 
there's a pair of Smiley socks, a Smiley branded   dental kit, Smiley lotion and lip balm, some 
Smiley earplugs, and of course, a Smiley eye mask.   They do also give economy an amenity 
kit, but it's a Starlux branded one   and much more basic containing a 
dental kit, eye mask, and socks. This is what the blanket looks like. 
It's quite nice. It feels like a velvet   material and it's a decent thickness 
considering this is premium economy.   You also get a standard sized pillow 
and I found it to be pretty fluffy. All right, now let's go check out the 
lavatories. There is one dedicated lavatory   for premium economy located on the right 
side or starboard side of the plane when   facing the nose of the plane. This means that 
if you're sitting on the left side of the plane,   you'll have to cross over to 
the galley to get over to it.   In terms of lavatory amenities, there are 
soaps and lotions from Swedish brand IDUN. There's also a container of other amenities that 
contain things like moist towelettes as well as   dental floss picks. They also had some plants in 
here that added a really nice pop of color, even   if they were fake. And of course, we can't forget 
Starlux's signature space themed toilet paper. All right, let's head back to our seats now to 
check out the IFE and then we'll talk about the   cost of the flight. Back at our seats, let's take 
a look at the IFE and headphones. This is what the   headphones look like. The headphones are noise 
cancelling and I actually found these to be pretty   good. If you prefer to use your own headphones 
though, the IFE does have Bluetooth capability. As   for the IFE itself, it's a 15.6 inches or 39.6 cm HD 
touchscreen display, although there is a remote   tucked into the side of the center armrest if 
you prefer. For entertainment options, I found   there was a good selection of Western, Asian, 
and European movies and TV shows. There was 97   TV shows and 109 movies, if you want to be exact. 
I have to say that one of the best parts though   is that Starlux gives premium economy passengers 
complimentary Wi-Fi for the entire flight. Economy   passengers get free messaging only though. And 
if you get hungry in between meals, the crew does   walk by periodically offering snacks, although you 
can also head on over to the galley where there is   a basket of snacks available as well. There was 
also some sandwiches in the galley if you wanted   something a little more substantial. I did try 
one of the sandwiches and the sandwich had bacon,   lettuce, and tomato inside. This wasn't very good. 
It was very soggy. There were also many Snickers   bars and rice cracker snacks, and these were quite 
good. Okay, now before we do a cost comparison,   let's check out the pre-arrival meal, which was 
served about an hour and a half before landing. Here's what the menu options were for the 
pre-rival meal. There was a choice between   pumpkin congee, omelette with bacon, or shakshuka 
with poached egg. I went for the pumpkin congee   with chicken, scallions, and goji berries. 
It was warm, delicious, and very comforting. There was also a side of potato salad,   a bowl of fruit, and a container of 
vanilla Greek yogurt, and a croissant. Okay, now before we land, let's talk about how 
I paid for this and then we'll also do a cash   cost comparison as well. I did use points for 
this and one way between LAX and Taipei was   50,000 Alaska Miles plus $18.10 USD in taxes and 
fees. And even though I did use points for this,   let's compare what the price would have been 
in cash to see how much more premium economy   costs compared to economy. Keep in mind prices are 
dynamic, but at the time that I booked a roundtrip   airfare in cash between LAX and Taipei in economy would have 
cost around $750 USD. Premium economy would have cost   approximately $1,800 USD. And just for reference, 
business class would have been just under   $5,600 USD and first class around $15,500 USD. So, premium 
economy would have been approximately two and a   half times the cost of economy, which is on the 
slightly pricier side since most airlines premium   economy normally tops out at double the cost of 
economy class. But let me know what you think   about these prices. Do you think Starlux's 
premium economy is worth 2 and a half times the   cost of economy? And how do you think Starlux 
compares to the other major Taiwanese carriers   EVA and China Airlines? As always though, 
thanks for joining me on board today and   please do like and subscribe if you've enjoyed 
the video so that we can fly together again

Why this Aviation YouTuber Is Surprisingly Controversial
reviews.transcript_excerpt: Over the past few…
reviews.transcript_full: Over the past few years, aviation YouTuber Sam Chui has slowly earned a reputation that many find increasingly questionable. The groundwork for this downfall was laid the moment people began to wonder whether the personality shown on camera truly matched reality. In his highly polished videos, Sam Chui comes across as friendly, passionate, and deeply invested in aviation. Everything appears carefully crafted to make him likable. Yet an increasing number of signs suggest a very different picture behind the scenes. And those warning signs did not appear recently. They began showing up years ago. You see, Sam Chui began making videos at the very dawn of YouTube, uploading his first content as far back as 2007. As the platform grew, he grew with it. Over time, he became widely viewed as one of the OG’s in aviation YouTube. But according to some, as his audience expanded and his influence turned him into one of the biggest names in the niche, his ego grew alongside it. Or as this reddit post states “Sam Chui’s ego is massive now and he’s at the point where he thinks he’s untouchable.” With other viewers noticing the same shift in his content. “Used to love his videos… “, “Stopped watching and unsubscribed almost two years ago” Meanwhile Traveler MSY says that “He started as a hobbyist because he liked aviation, but now he’s a publisher/presenter.” Things however took an even darker turn after a flight on Kazahkstans national airline, Air Astana, with his then-friend Josh Cahill. In a video released later, Josh alleged that during this flight, Sam Chui assaultetd members of the cabin crew. In his podcast with Aviation Youtuber Swiss he stated that this is a recurring theme. To be fair, Sam Chui was not always the primary cause of controversy. The 2022 incident involving Nepal Airlines is a good example of that. In a video filmed on a Nepal Airlines flight, Chui appeared in the cockpit together with the airline’s chief pilot, Vijaya Lama. Several media outlets described this as a violation of aviation safety regulations. Later, on a Nepalese podcast, Lama himself referred to the incident as one of the biggest mistakes of his career and claimed that Sam Chui had been paid by airlines in general. In situations like this however, responsibility lies primarily with the flight crew. Access to the cockpit is strictly controlled, and only the pilot in command has the authority to grant or deny entry. Chui did not enter the cockpit on his own initiative; he was invited in by the chief pilot. For that reason, placing the main blame on Chui feels misplaced. The regulatory and safety responsibility rests with the pilot, not with a guest who was allowed into the cockpit by someone in a position of authority. But this is not the only time when chief pilots got in trouble for Chui entering the cockpit. In May 2023 for example, Chui was suspected of violating Taiwan’s Aircraft Flight Operation Regulations after entering the cockpit without the required authorization. As a result Taiwan’s civil aviation authority opened its investigation against Chang Kuo-wei, who was flying the aircraft at the time and is also the founder of STARLUX Airlines. Chang was summoned for questioning, and authorities concluded that this incident constituted a regulatory breach. With the relevant regulation stating that: “No person may be admitted into the flight crew compartment of an aircraft except for the authorized personnel and Flight Dispatchers of the operator.” However it is undeniable that there is a broader pattern of Sam Chui frequently appearing on camera chatting with pilots or filming inside cockpits during active flights. These moments give viewers access that most other aviation YouTubers simply never get. However this level of exclusivity not only fuels curiosity, but also skepticism by his viewers. Many viewers ask how this level of access is even possible. Others openly question whether Chui cooperates with airlines behind the scenes, or whether his videos function as promotion rather than independent documentation. Chui himself repeatedly insists that his content is authentic and not sponsored. According to him, airlines do not pay for coverage and he retains editorial control. Yet a quick look at comment sections tells a different story. A large share of viewers clearly doubts this narrative. According to some viewers, the lack of authenticity in his videos is obvious, with one critic even calling him a paid cheerleader without integrity. The combination of privileged access, unusually friendly cockpit interactions, and consistently positive portrayals makes many people unconvinced that these videos exist without some form of financial support by the airlines. That gap between Chui’s claims and audience perception therefore remains one of the most persistent points of tension surrounding his work. In general, Sam Chui’s videos are highly polished and rarely focus on negatives. That alone is not a flaw. This style clearly resonates with a large audience and has helped make his content some of the most popular in the aviation space. Chui himself repeatedly emphasizes that he is not a reviewer. His work reflects that position. There is also clear demand for this approach. Many viewers prefer watching unique and impressive insights into aviation rather than constant conflict or outrage. For them, Chui’s videos offer escapism, access, and spectacle. And that appeal explains his sustained success. At the same time, it is difficult for many to ignore that his videos often carry a promotional tone. Even without explicit advertising, the consistent positivity, exceptional access, and cinematic presentation create the impression of marketing. This does not automatically mean the content is sponsored, but it does blur the line between documentation and promotion. That ambiguity sits at the core of the debate around Chui. His content satisfies a real audience need, yet for a significant portion of viewers, it still feels closer to brand-friendly storytelling than to neutral aviation coverage. When you look at Chui’s videos, they are usually not labeled as sponsored. On the surface, they appear independent. However, occasionally the content contains hints that suggest otherwise. For example, some videos include links in the description pointing directly to the airline or organization featured. A clear case comes from his coverage of the EBACE Airshow. At first glance, it seems like regular reporting, but a closer look reveals a connection: the video description contains links to EBACE itself. A little research confirms this was indeed a cooperation, as the organizers explicitly state in a press release. Now don’t get me wrong here: promotion in itself is not inherently problematic. Sponsored content provides creators with additional revenue streams, reducing reliance on YouTube ad revenue and giving them more financial freedom to produce high-quality content. The issue arises when sponsorships are not clearly disclosed. Failing to label paid content can be seen as disrespectful to viewers, as it misleads them about the independence of the content. But non-disclosure may also violate YouTube guidelines, which explicitly require creators to label sponsored content. Beyond platform rules, undisclosed sponsorships can also conflict with media and trade laws in many countries. In the United States, where Chui’s channel is based, the Federal Trade Commission Act requires that any material connection between an endorser and marketer must be clearly and conspicuously disclosed. This is meant to guarantee transparency so viewers understand when content carries a promotional element. In Chui’s videos, you usually won’t find any explicit sponsorship labels. I’m not a lawyer, but it’s easy to see why people make these allegations. In Chui’s early days, to many his content felt more authentic. His passion seemed genuinely focused on aviation, and that authenticity attracted a loyal audience. Over time, however, perceptions shifted. Many now view the channel as primarily a money-making machine. Despite Chui’s claims that his content is unsponsored, he maintains a dedicated page on his website for sponsorships, highlighting how attractive his channel is for potential partners. This contradiction between public statements and the promotion of sponsorship opportunities fuels skepticism and raises questions about transparency. Cases like these certainly eroded trust among his audience and explain why some viewers gradually turned away. Claims that he was paid by the subjects of his videos certainly contributed, but there’s more to the story. Because another notable incident started to take shape in 2023, involving a dispute with fellow YouTuber Josh Cahill. I’ve made a dedicated video covering that case, so I won’t go into full detail here, but you’re welcome to watch it after this one. To be honest, I was a bit biased in that video and, in retrospect, I’m not particularly proud of it. But anyway here’s a quick summary of why the conflict erupted between the two: Now, there had already been minor disputes between the two, including a Twitter argument where they exchanged jabs. After that, they seemed to get along and even met in person. But the feud escalated when Josh Cahill claimed that Sam Chui had been paid by the Indian airline Vistara. Chui viewed this as defamation and, in a now-deleted YouTube comment, accused Cahill of blackmailing the airline. In response, Cahill released a video detailing the whole situation. This triggered a huge backlash against Chui, forcing him to apparently temporarily block comments on Instagram. The incident clearly damaged his public image, splitting the community, with those critical of Chui forming the seemingly larger group. After some time, Chui posted a statement video, apologizing to Cahill while also defending his own positions. However, as of December 2025, that video appears to have been removed from his channel. but in December 2025, Josh Cahill posted a video titled: “Still BANNED by QATAR AIRWAYS? Let’s fly them and see what HAPPENS!” In that video, Cahill explained why he had been banned from Qatar Airways and alleged that the airline had engaged in bribery to secure sponsored content. He further claimed that Qatar Airways later collaborated with Chui, suggesting that these efforts aimed to improve the airline’s public image. The video reinforced the perception among some viewers that Chui’s access and coverage could involve covert partnerships with airlines, fueling skepticism about the independence of his content. Now, you can think whatever you want about Josh —he has his own reputation for drama—but it’s clear he is not the only one raising concerns about Chui. Well, the aim of this video is not to gossip or to defame anyone. Disagreement in my comments is not only allowed but welcome, as long as it remains civil and respectful. But all in all being fair to viewers matters. When someone buys a product, books a flight, or engages with content, they expect unbiased information. Transparency and honesty are the key, and that’s what this video aims to highlight. Shortly after Cahill’s December 2025 Qatar Airways video went live, he discussed the situation on his Josh Cahill & Swiss Show. In their latest episode, Chaill claimed that Sam Chui’s damage-control videos were not a single incident but a pattern: every time he posted a negative video about an airline, it was soon followed by a positive one from Sam Chui. He further alleged that people from Qatar Airways told him that the airline provides Chui with unique access, accommodates his requests, and essentially lets him operate freely. He also claimed to have emails and screenshots supporting that Sam Chui had been asked to “fix the mess” created by prior coverage. Clearly we’re dealing with two major creators accusing each other, so where the truth actually lies isn’t for me to decide. That said, it is true that Chui sometimes portrays airlines with a negative reputation in a positive light. There is, however, one airline with a particularly bad reputation that he can’t cover anymore because its license has just been revoked. How this “corrupt mafia airline” fell—you’ll see in this video. Thanks for watching, and see you soon.

reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm flying from Bangkok to Hong Kong on a Cathay Pacific Airbus A330 This plane is definitely on the more dated side and features the oldest cabin in Cathay's fleet but hopefully in this video you'll see why even when you're not in their most modern cabin Cathay Pacific still offer a very solid experience... I started off my journey by taking the airport train from the centre of Bangkok to Suvarnabhumi Airport which is quick and only cost me 15 Thai Baht, or about 35 British Pence In the airport itself it's huge and somewhat overcrowded, and this is actually my first time flying out of this airport so I can't say I'm that familiar with it but my overall review of it is that it's just fine The Cathay Check-in area is in the S Zone and 2 hours before departure there was barely any queue and check-in was very quick Impressive as Cathay operate about 7 flights a day from here, mostly on massive aircraft like the Boeing 777  or Airbus A330 I was on today Airport security was pretty slow as they seemed to be doing a secondary inspection on almost everyone me included, but I'm pretty sure that was because I had a big cake and some fruit in my bag so it was probably my own fault once through to the departure zone there are loads of shops and restaurants and these cute little cleaning robots but the whole place is laid out in a few long thin corridors absolutely crammed with people and it's a big building so walking anywhere takes a while  One cool thing I noticed though which I haven't seen at other airports is the departure board which says how long it takes to reach each gate, and the direction you need to go to get there anyway, I made it to our gate and whilst watching this Myanmar Airways plane our plane for today just happened to appear out of nowhere, what are the chances hey? and some more perfect timing, that's another Cathay Pacific plane taking off in the background as ours parks at the gate Today we're flying on an 18 year old Airbus A330-300 with 262 seats in total 223 of which are in Economy class, and the Airbus A330 is really the workhorse of Cathay's short haul fleet, with them operating 43 in total making them the largest operator of he type in the world and as these old planes age out, they'll eventually be replaced with the much newer Airbus A330neo It was soon my turn to board, and whilst walking down the jetbridge another Cathay A330 was pulling up alongside showing just how many flights they do to bangkok Now, before we step on board, here are the stats and route map for today's flight, where a 40 minute late departure would see us land 20 minutes late in Hong Kong and all the pilots said about the delay is it was due to Chinese airspace restrictions which I'm slightly dubious of as I feel every flight I've ever taken in or around China has said the same thing but in anycase, here is the plane's cabin, and as someone who always sits by the window the A330 is probably my favourite plane to fly thanks to its 2-4-2 layout I chose seat 61A here which was free to select and the thing I like about this plane is I only have to climb over one person to reach the aisle so it feels much less claustrophobic if you're in one of the window aisles like I was today Now looking at the seat itself, legroom is good with 32" of seat pitch, much better than the 29 or 30" you'll see on most narrowbody aircraft It has a nifty folding tray table which folds out like this Then a small storage shelf just above that... and a little drink holder so you can have a drink without needing the table down The screen is pretty small at 9", maybe one of the most noticeable flaw of this slightly dated cabin and as you'll see shortly, the touchscreen is pretty laggy, but it's still perfectly usable another noticeable thing is the seatback is actually quite short I'm only 5'6" and you can see my head pokes above the headrest, so taller people might need to crank the headrest all he way up to be comfortable The headphones meanwhile are some of the best I've used in Economy, also, the crew went through the cabin offering blankets, I didn't bother get one though and the seat back pocket has plenty of little storage pouches so very convenient Now for the TV, it has Cathay Pacific's award-winning IFE system with a really good selection of movies, tv and games in fact, it was rated the best entertainment system in the world by Skytrax in 2025 However, on the A330 the tv is a bit too old to run it properly, so you can see here it's just a bit slow and laggy not an issue on their newer planes but it is noticeable here, especially coupled with the small-ish screen we started pushing back about 30 minutes behind schedule and the safety video started playing so here's that... one of the better safety videos I've seen actually and shows a nice bit of Hong Kong culture Now getting ready for takeoff the sun was just about to set which made for some very scenic views,  so stay tuned for that coming up in a second... Despite being a short 2.5 hour flight, this is Asia we're flying in so of course we had a full meal service I can't remember exactly but I'm pretty sure this was pork noodles with warm bread,  a fruit bowl and their signature Haagen Dazs ice cream on the side Everything was good and it's just a solid service for a short haul flight plus you get actual metal cutlery and Haagen Dazs is a premium touch There's also an inflight magazine with some interesting articles in both Chinese and English, especially this one about the cats of Hong Kong and speaking of cats, here's mine, he wants you to like and subscribe to support the channel and help fund his ice cream addiction back to the magazine though, it has a cool route map which I always love to see and they have a bit about their fleet, which I amusingly noticed already includes the 777X even though it's been delayed for years with no end in sight last of all as we approach Hong Kong for landing, they do have inflight WiFi but you have to pay for it so I didn't bother Worth noting that Business, First and Diamond status passengers get it for free though anyway, here's the landing in a dark but somewhat light-polluted Hong Kong also I noticed as we were landing a big gap in the fencing and lighting around the runway and that was actually due the the Air ACT Boeing 747 which had crashed into the sea 2 weeks before this flight and I guess they hadn't rebuilt the fence at that point so you could still see the big gap So as we disembark the plane it's time for my final thoughts... Cathay Pacific just offer a very solid shorthaul experience on their Airbus A330 It might not be as snazzy and modern as their A321neo or A350  but it's comfortable and the inflight service is top notch the price was very competitive too, being about 20% cheaper than a similar time with Thai Airways and similar to budget airlines like Hong Kong Express when you factor in things like food, seat selection and baggage costs... So I'll just give them a solid 80% score accross the board and on my airline tier list they keep their spot as a 10/10 airline in my opinion,  mainly because in the past I've had some really good experiences with them and even though this flight wasn't perfect, it was still very solid for a short haul trip now if you want to see something that was a 10/10 experience then check out the flight I took after this one a 14 hour flight from Hong Kong to London in their Airbus A350-1000 Economy Class which was just an exceptional flight in every way I'll also have reviews of Oman Air, Jet2, Air Europa and Air France to name a few coming in the next few weeks so subscribe to keep up to date with that like and leave a comment if you enjoyed this video thanks a lot for watching and good bye

reviews.transcript_full: In today's video, I take a gruelling 14 hour flight from Hong Kong to London in Cathay Pacific's brilliant Airbus A350-1000 Economy on what would actually end up being one of the best flights of my life so you'll find out why after flying over 60 airlines Cathay Pacific are one of my favourites and also I'll show you a useful trick which helped me get one of the best seats on the plane completely for free so buckle up and enjoy this Cathay Pacific Trip Report! and we start at an eye-wateringly early 5am in the morning in the impressive departure hall of Hong Kong Airport This is actually my first time flying Cathay Pacific Economy long haul, though back in 2018  I actually flew their Business Class from London to Tokyo via Hong Kong and remember those being some of the best flights of my life Just things like the cabin crew greeting me by name as I boarded and being able to order burgers in the middle of the flight not to mention that was my first time on an Airbus A350 too and the seat is really good plus their Business Class lounges in Hong Kong are probably the best in the world and up until that point in my life I'd only ever flown Business with British Airways and Virgin Atlantic which I don't think are bad airlines per se, but flying Cathay was just such an eye opener to what  a real world-class airline is like anyway, all that to say, I was exciting to be flying Cathay Pacific today, even if just in Economy... Hong Kong Airport is pretty good too, and I think is best summed up with the word efficiency though I feel like for an airport of this size there's actually not many shops or food and worryingly, the shopping area was filled with Labubu statues here I was thinking that trend had died down by now but clearly not in Hong Kong as you can see here, the airport is also pretty big, my gate happened to be all the way over here, literally the furthest you can get from the entrance so there was a lot of walking involved and I was lugging about fifteen kilograms of luggage so reaching the gate took a while and yes, that much carryon is vastly over their seven kilogram allowance... but they don't weigh bags at the gate, and I wanted to bring home a lot of souvenirs and snacks... anyway, now that the sun has started rising I have to say Hong Kong Airport is amazing for planespotting there are so many widebody aircraft here including a whole fleet of 747 cargo planes making it a feast for the eyes and the backdrop of skyscrapers and mountains makes for a lovely view in terms of seating though,  there isn't that much by each gate actually and I think if our plane was full then there wouldn't have been nearly enough seats for everyone Now here's our plane for today, a 7 year old Airbus A350-1000 registered B-LXI which had just arrived a few hours earlier from Boston it has 334 seats in total, 256 of which are Economy Class also this was the only one I caught on film but I got a great view of many cool takeoffs whilst I waited around for boarding to start and start it did, about 45 minutes before scheduled departure One way that Hong Kong Airport is living in the future is that they have these cool biometric gates so you don't even need to show your passport and boarding pass it just scans your face and lets you through after a few seconds hugely efficient and really speeds up boarding, not that that was necessary today as the flight probably wasn't even half full Now before we step on board here are the stats and route map for today's flight where we would actually take a pretty indirect route over North China around the Himalayas whilst avoiding Russia to land slightly early with a flight time of 13.5 hours, but about 15 hours actually sat on the plane due to a slightly delayed departure and as I alluded to in the intro, there's a good trick you can do with many airlines to find the best seat for free Cathay Pacific let you view the seat map online right up until departure I saw the best exit row seat 60K was actually still available, but cost £156 extra so I ignored it and thought I would be happy with the seat I'd been allocated 46K, this locked-in window seat but then the thought of spending 15 hours trapped by the window reminded me of this scene from White Lotus... So I went up to the gate agent, showed them the seat map and asked if I could have that exit row seat and to my surprise they did it for free very quickly so that was great you'll see how good this new seat was in a moment, but moral of the story is, just keep an eye on the online seat map and even if it's not an exit row you should be able to ask them to change you to the best seat available and even better, the two seats next to me ended up being empty too making this literally the best seating setup you can ask for in Economy Class obviously all this was largely due to the luck of having an empty flight,  but hey, I'm just reviewing my experience and this is just how it turned out now obviously legroom is fantastic and in this seat you get direct aisle access too and actually, the non-exit seats are also pretty good with 32" of seat pitch and 6" of recline the tv is a decent sized 11.1" too so overall it's a very competitive seat You get quite a nice soft pillow, no scratchy disposable cover here... and what is probably one of the better Economy Class blankets out there, soft and very large, plus I had 3 of them since my row was empty... a well padded adjustable headrest and a very nice wing view also something pretty rare to see in Economy Class these days, they actually give you a printed menu which first of all, just feels a bit more premium, but it's also nice being able to read it and decide what you want well ahead of time, rather than making an on the spot decision when the food cart comes round also the entire drinks menu is here, so you don't have to guess at what they have or don't have also they give everyone a water bottle after boarding, vital on a long flight like this and the headphones are actually pretty decent for Economy Class... though I've recently started using this Bluetooth transmitter instead which lets me connect my wireless headphones instead and makes for an infinitely better audio experience Amazon affiliate link in the description if you want one for yourself This is the new Naked Gun movie by the way, extremely stupid but I enjoyed it a lot and that brings me to the IFE System, which is actually really good so good in fact that Skytrax ranked them as having the best inflight entertainment of any airline in the world this year and they basically have everything you could want, loads of movies in many different languages a nice slick interface, tv shows, music, games quality of life things like airport guides and connecting gate info two external cameras in very high definition which I always enjoy watching... plus the inflight map is pretty good too they also have the full inflight menu here in addition to the paper menu handed out during boarding and the full Cathay Pacific Shop, which has a satisfying range of quality-looking branded merch Boarding finished very quickly due to how empty the flight was but of course, the pilot announced a 40 minute delay due to of course, air traffic restrictions over China which seems incredibly common due to how restricted China's airspace is and was mildly annoying, but we still ended up arriving 20 minutes early in London so it wasn't the end of the world and now here's the safety video, which I liked a lot,  makes me want to visit Hong Kong again and eat some claypot rice with a side of egg tart and milk tea After a bit of taxiing and some more waiting we were finally ready for takeoff and I definitely made the right seat choice as the view of Hong Kong on takeoff was jaw-dropping so get ready for that, coming up now... and here's something weird you can see here so genuinely curious if any pilots watching could explain... after fully raising the flaps the pilots lowered them again, only to raise them a few seconds later here they are going down after being fully raised... and here they are going up again... please leave a comment if you have any idea why? anyway, apart from that the views of Hong Kong taking off were incredible The contrast of the skyscrapers and mountains with the bay make for one of the coolest takeoff views in the world and hear you can see Guanzhou, which is just an absurdly big city and it has one of the busiest airports in the world which you can see here Pretty soon after takeoff breakfast was served, and the service was rapid due to how empty the plane was and I can report that this was easily the best airplane breakfast I've ever had mainly because they had proper dim sum and it was actually pretty good, which I've never seen on a plane before also metal cutlery make it feel fancy There was a prawn dumpling, a meatball thing and this yellow dumpling, all very tasty Then a well-seasoned congee which I mixed the meatball into They also give you a towelette, butter, jam and a bread roll which was actually warmed up then lastly a strawberry yoghurt, fresh fruit and orange juice to drink Then on top of all that I got a Hong Kong milk tea to drink which is pretty big in Hong Kong and also a unique thing offered by Cathay Pacific Another cool feature of the seat is they have a device holder built in not so useful on the exit row seat, but it's well placed here on the regular seats I got up to stretch my legs, and you can see here just how empty the plane was, back here I would say it was maybe only 20% full, with a lot of people just laying down on a full row and I'm aware Cathay took a very big hit after Covid, but I'm surprised they still seem to be struggling to fill planes Now for a loo review, toothbrush kits are available but I had to ask the crew for one and the toilets were kept clean throughout, with crew constantly going in to clean them Also, this is by far the biggest sink I can remember seeing in a plane toilet even when compared to most Business Class loos Another nice quality of life feature is they show you the flight timeline letting you know when to expect food and drinks services throughout the flight Halfway through the flight it was time for meal number two, and I got  sweet and sour pork with pineapple, rice and vegetables then for the starter a chicken and jicama salad, which I had to look up, apparently a jicama is a vegetable from Mexico then fruit, Haagen Dazs ice cream, and warm bread and butter to round things off and ginger ale to drink The cabin then stayed dark for the rest of the flight prety much, and I ended up watching Mulan If you get hungry or thirsty there's a drink and snack stand in the galley, plus you can just ask the crew to get you either cup noodles or a Hong Kong egg tart and I got an egg tart which was a nice mid-flight snack and all I needed as the two main meals were tasty and filling enough then right before landing the crew came round and handed out these Palmier biscuits which were also very nice so overall a fantastic flight when it came to food and Cathay Pacific clearly know how to  keep you well fed throughout a super long flight We then began our descent into a very overcast London which brings me to the very last feature of this review, the WiFi all I can really say is that it exists, and it was too expensive for me to bother trying it would be nice to see them catch up to many competitors who offer free WiFi Like Qatar Airways or British Airways but that's pretty much the only criticism I have for Cathay today... and now the landing... it was raining when we landed so the window instantly fogged up but to summarise, if you couldn't tell already, I just really like Cathay Pacific and they're probably my favourite airline and this super long haul flight confirmed that for me and as someone who mainly flies Oneworld Airlines, Cathay are my airline of choice when flying to Asia if the price is right also this was a personal record for me, it took maybe 4 minutes from stepping off the plane to passing through customs and there was no queue at all for immigration so that was very satisfying, and I just made a quick stop at M&S to buy these cookies,  which are the best in the world by the way, before heading home I used miles to pay for this flight and it cost a very reasonable 31,000 Avios plus £81 and sure, not everyone will be as lucky as me and get an almost empty flight to relax on but I'm just judging based on my experience on this flight so I'm giving Cathay an 82.5% and putting them up to a 10/10 on my airline tier list, the same rank as Singapore Airlines, who are maybe a bit better if I'm being completely objective but either way, I think Cathay have earned their place at the top of my list Now if you're looking for something else to watch then check out my recent review of Oman Air's Business Class a super underrated airline with one of the best Business seats out there and some fantastic food as well as part of this trip I also flew Oman Air's 787 Economy, and Cathay Pacific's short haul A330 and I have many more videos in the pipeline so don't forget to like and subscribe to stay up to date with all that! thanks a lot for watching and good bye!

reviews.transcript_full: As one of the top Asian carriers, Japan Airlines has won a few awards for the best economy seats in industry. So, come experience this flight with us as we fly from Seattle to Tokyo. What's up you guys? Welcome back to our channel. Currently, we are at the SeaTac airport and we are about to board the flight from Seattle to Tokyo on Japan Airlines. We actually flew with them on premium economy back in March, but today we are flying on the regular economy and we're so excited to take you guys along and share this experience with you guys. It is currently 10:05 p.m. right now, which is about 30 minutes before the actual departure time and they just started boarding process. We are in group 4 and because we were sitting after row 30, so we get to go on first, which to me is a very efficient way to board because you start at the back and then you would not hold up anyone else behind you. The boarding process is really efficient. It is 1 p.m. right now and we're already walking in the jet bridge to get on the airplane. [music] All right guys, so it has been about 15 minutes since we took off. So I would like to take this time to give you some quick info about this flight. So we are flying on Japan Airlines flight JL67. For this flight in the economy cabin, it has a 242 seat configuration. And we are sitting at the very last row in row 59 at seat 59D and E. And my first impression is that it is actually quite nice because there is no one sitting behind us. So I can just lean back without feeling bad about knocking into the the person behind us. And when it come to the first impression, the seat is very spacious. The padding is really thick and also it is pretty wide. Now that we are situated, let me give you a quick tour of our seats. When we first arrived, the first thing that stood out to us is the seats upholstery which follow the red and black color branding of Japan Airlines. This give it a nice and modern feel. The fault leather headrest cover also adds a nice touch as well. On each seat, there's a blanket and a small pillow. As we sit down, at the back of the seat in front of us is the inflight entertainment system on a 10.6 in screen. [music] The screen is quite responsive, and you can choose between movies, music, video games, and other options. One downfall was that the movies collection was a bit dated with not a lot of new release. Right underneath the screen is the USB port to charge their device. Japan Airlines add a nice touch to each seat with the row number and the seat letter which helps [music] passenger to find their seats easier. The thicker than normal seat cushions provide extra comfort on a long haul flight. Moving along, below the screen is the literature pockets with the magazine, inflight shopping catalog, air sickness bag, an instruction to access 1 hour free Wi-Fi, and the headphone for the in-flight entertainment. What we like the most about this seat is how spacious it is. As you can see, I can even cross my leg comfortably in my seat. Lastly, the dining traits folds out like this, halfway for your drinks and [music] fully extended during meal service. >> A few minutes later, >> we are about 30 minutes into the flight now and the flight attendant just came around and provide everyone with a wet towel with the business class branding, which is quite interesting. But I'll take it since it will help us stay refreshed as we wait for our meal. It is about an hour into the flight and they just serve us with our first snack which is this um rice cracker pouch. And of course we have to get the iconic peach and grape juice from Japan Airlines. It's really refreshing. Not too sweet. Now let's try the snack. This is the first piece. It's like toasted rice. reviews.title: Starlux Airlines' A350: Is this the BEST Transpacific Economy Flight? (LAX-TPE) ⚾🧢 DODGERS Theme!
reviews.transcript_excerpt: Right below the seat, you have a standard charging port…
