in-flight entertainment, but even so,

reviews.transcript_full: Hey everyone and welcome back! Today I'm flying Starlux Airlines' economy class from Los Angeles to Taipei I've flown this route a few times and it is my preferred way to cross the Pacific so I'm excited to share the details with you today From my experience, Starlux always seems to operate out of the west gates of the Tom Bradley International Terminal so I made sure to arrive at least two hours before departure, which I felt was plenty of time Check in was easy. A quick FYI: if you have a carry on, I noticed they are diligently weighing and tagging all carry-on luggage at the counter the official limit is 7 kg or 15 pounds for economy so please keep that in mind After clearing security it's a long walk my gate, 221, is located at the West Gates of the international terminal Everytime I've flown Starlux from LAX, my gates have been located in this West Gates section This requires going downstairs to use the long passenger tunnel with moving walkways. It's a significant distance so I would recommend travelers budgeting at least 10 to 15 minutes, especially if you are a slower walker Prior to boarding, staff members walk around the gate before the boarding call, checking your passport and stamping your printed boarding pass They said the stamp is enough to board and they won't need to check your passport again Please note that they required a printed boarding pass to apply the stamp. No mobile passes were accepted This pre-check really streamlines the process Prior to boarding, they have designated stands for each boarding group, allowing everyone to line up neatly with their group prior to their group number being called Once boarding started, all you needed was your stamped boarding pass Stepping onto the Starlux A350, I'll show you the seat map There are two economy sections The first is rows 30 to 41 And the second is rows 50 to 69 I chose an aisle seat, 59C, as I always prefer easy aisle access for long-haul flights Starlux's economy seat offers excellent comfort The headrest is fully adjustable, moving up and down, and the sides fold inwards There's a pull out panel underneath the in-flight entertainment screen with a slot for a drink and a space to place your phone Below that is the standard slide-out tray table, which is fully adjustable Right below the seat, you have a standard charging port and a USB-C port for charging Waiting at your seat, you're provided a pillow with a futuristic brown design, slippers, blanket, and an amenity kit There's also a small Crystal Geyser water bottle and Starlux-branded headset in a sterilized bag in the seat pocket Inside the amenity kit, you'll find a dental pouch that contains a toothbrush and toothpaste, socks, earplugs, and a comfortable eye mask Everything you need to settle in Soon, we were beginning to prepare for takeoff The safety video has a cool, futuristic, space aesthetic that reminded me of Buzz Lightyear And with that, we were taking off and beginning our journey across the Pacific The in-flight entertainment screen is very wide It's the largest I've seen for an economy flight I measured it at about two iPhones wide and one and a quarter iPhones tall The UI is sleek, clean, and intuitive I was happily surprised by a significant improvement in the entertainment library When I flown Starlux in the past, I thought the selection was limited, but now they have a much larger and more diverse selection of movies and TV shows Great job on the upgrade, Starlux! Two features I love: first, you can hit the heart icon to favorite movies, shows, and music, and quickly access your favorited items from the menu bar at the top Second, the flight map is fantastic If you zoom into a city, it even displays points of interest, complete with pictures, which is a cool way to start getting excited about your destination Starlux provides free Wi-Fi for all economy passengers, specifically for texting and image sending It was fast for sending messages on iMessage and Line Receiving pictures was quick, though audio messages did take a little longer to load The dinner service arrived shortly after takeoff There were two options: Tex Mex beef stew with mashed potato or chicken minced meat rice bowl I chose the chicken option The egg that came with the rice had a nice, soft texture The meal also came with a bread roll, Mexican corn salad, cheese and crackers, plus some fresh fruit This flight features a partnership with the Los Angeles Dodgers, which you can see with the Dodgers themed napkin For drinks, I ordered the Apple Sparkling Mocktail Please note that the mocktails are prepared after the main meals are delivered to all passengers so be patient. Once the drinks arrived, I noticed that the drink stirrer is also Dodgers-themed, which is a nice touch if you're a Dodgers' fan! Now, let's talk about comfort This is probably the most comfortable economy seat I've ever taken over the Pacific The recline is quite deep You can see here how far the seat in front of me is reclined But the real star of the seat is the headrest It truly holds your head ergonomically, allowing you to settle in without any neck strain As someone who is rarely able to sleep on long-haul flights, I was able to get a comfortable five to six hours of sleep Mid-flight, I checked out the lavatories I'm showing you the one in the very back of the plane It was surprisingly spacious and large compared to the ones in the middle of the economy cabin The toilet paper had this cool galactic space design, and the sink had an automatic water dispenser Just put your hands below and water comes out You can use the red and blue buttons to control the temperature They've also added some other nice touches, like a little succulent for color and facial mist and lotion About an hour and a half to two hours before landing, it was time for breakfast The options were a ham and cheese frittata with pesto cream, or fish and celery congee Now, I remember the congee being incredible on previous Starlux flights that I've taken In fact, I remember the congee I had with Starlux being some of the best congee I've ever had So I selected the congee I was a little disappointed by the congee this time It was very light on flavor and the texture was very watery I remember Starlux congee being incredible on previous flights so this one was a little bit of a letdown For drinks, I tried the green tea special mocktail option It was good, but I personally preferred the apple sparkling from dinner During breakfast, I noticed another Dodgers detail When you clear the main tray items, you can see the custom Dodgers-themed placement on the tray It really shows the thought that they put into this collaboration And speaking of Dodgers' touches, during the dimmed cabin period prior to breakfast, the crew handed out rice crackers in this Dodgers jersey design packaging Also, if you're a Dodgers' fan, make sure you ask for a pack of the special Dodgers and Starlux collaboration playing cards I went to the back galley about three-quarters of the way through the flight, and the crew was happy to hand me a pack at no extra cost Soon after breakfast, we were on our final descent into Taipei and then shortly welcomed into Taiwan So, what are my final thoughts on Starlux Airlines' economy experience from Los Angeles to Taipei In short, this is my preferred way to fly over the Pacific Ocean The seating comfort, thanks to that headrest, is unmatched in economy The plane feels new, the amenities are great, and I was highly impressed by the massive improvement in their in flight entertainment library A major plus since the last time I flew with them My one small critique, and I am being very very nitpicky here, is that the food quality wasn't quite as high as it was on my very first Starlux flight on the same exact route. Although I'm not usually very attentive to meal quality on flights, I remembered Starlux economy dining being some of the best airline food I've ever eaten I suspect they've maybe shifted some budget towards their improved in-flight entertainment, but even so, the meals were certainly still edible and good compared to many other carriers Overall, this is a premium experience in an economy cabin packed with great touches like the Dodgers' memorabilia The comfort, the technology, and the sleek design makes Starlux my top choice for an economy flight across the Pacific Thank you so much for watching and please let me know in the comments below if you flown Starlux before And don't forget to please hit the like button and subscribe button as it'll really help the channel and I'll see you in the next one

reviews.transcript_full: Hey everyone and welcome to Hong Kong International Airport Terminal 1. We are just in transit and making our way down to the trains that will take us to our gates. Cathay Pacific currently have two flights to Perth on most days, which are CX171 departing at 3:00 p.m. and CX143 departing at midnight. Unfortunately, it is blocked by the aerobridge, but anyways, it is registered as Bravo-Lima-Romeo-Foxtrot and is 9 years old. After a quick walk into the premium economy section, I arrive at my seat 31A by the left side of the aircraft. Altogether, there are 28 seats in premium economy made by Collins Aerospace arranged in a 2-4-2 configuration. These seats have a pitch of 40 in and a width of 20 in, a pretty impressive increase from economy. In front, there is a 12.1 in in-flight entertainment system with the Studio CX software. Be sure to stick around and we will take a closer look throughout the flights. Under the screen is a personal device holder that doubles up to also adjust the screen above. Below this is a little pouch area to store any belongings. Each passenger will also receive pillows and blankets to maximize comfort. The extra seat adjustment controls are located under the armrest and next to this is the retractable controller. Personally, I never use these much and prefer to use the touch screen instead. Between the seats are double USB A charging ports as well as double universal power points, which is very handy. As passengers settle in, welcome drinks were served by the Cathay cabin crew and today I chose the orange juice. Hot towels were also handed out and other things provided are water and an amenities pouch. We will open this up later. With a slight delay, we departed out of gate 48 and during this time the Cathay Pacific safety video was played. >> Yes. >> So, after a very scenic takeoff from Hong Kong, I opened the flight's map, which has pretty good features and information. Whether you care about the finer details or just how long left of the flights remains, the unit will satisfy both. Digging deeper into the movies, there is an excellent range including Western and Asian cinema. For TV shows, they are organized into genres and also include news channels and HBO Max. For drinks, I chose cola. Metal Starlux cutlery is provided, which is fantastic, and the only thing in the peanuts theme is the wet wipes. Digging deeper into the main meal, we have the beef donbur laid out with vegetables and egg. Tastewise, it was pretty good. However, I would say it is a little bit too salty. Opening the fruit bowl, we have some very fresh slices of fruits, including guava and dragon fruits. Inside the seat pockets, there is the Starlux Inflights magazine, as well as the A330 Neo safety card. One more thing to mention are the Starlux playing cards, which you can request for free. These Snoopy edition ones are unfortunately out of stock, but I love these default Galactic Space ones Starlux has. The Starlux A330 Neo seat pitch of 31 in is nothing special, however, with other airlines offering 32 to 34 in in economy. Considering all this, I'm giving this category a 9 out of 10. This is an early arrival of 20 minutes. So for this category, it's a perfect 10 out of 10. Finalizing everything, we get a strong score of 9.31 out of 10. yt_comments.text: I flew the WTP cabin on their 777 and it has the newer IFE and seats. VERY comfortable and a very responsive IFE with some neat games included. Amenity kit was the same. Enjoyable flights and a good return on investment. I've flown the Club World cabin too and it is nice, but the WTP cabin gives you an almost as comfortable experience without shelling out nearly as much as you would for Club. Food was super tasty too. And the snack cart setup in the galley was a nice touch. (They don't announced when they do this, to avoid stampedes of freebie hunters)

reviews.transcript_full:
While some call Aeroméxico North America’s
most underrated airline, others see it as a nefarious corporation
unworthy of Mexico’s flag. Today I’m not only finding out
whether Aeroméxico is amazing or awful, but also experiencing the uniqueness
of flying domestically in Mexico for the first time. We start our journey in Mexico City,
a small town that casually holds the title of second largest city,
in the entire western hemisphere. Approaching
the massive Terminal 2 of Benito Juárez Airport, it’s easy to see how this is
the country’s largest airport. With its enormous terminal,
bright departure hall, and translucent roof, Terminal 2, which is dedicated
entirely to SkyTeam partners, feels more like a convention center
than an airport. Here you have the option to check in
at the counter for free, which, in Mexico too, is not something you can take for
granted anymore. However if you happen to own
one of those new technological miracles they call a “cell phone”,
you can simply check in online and head straight through security with nothing
more than a mobile boarding pass. While checked luggage
isn’t included with Aeroméxico, you are allowed to bring 10 kilos of hand
luggage plus a personal item on board. These amenities, however, come at a price. On this route for example,
Aeroméxico is about two to three times more expensive than its competitors. But with only around
90 USD per person for today’s trip, at least domestic flights are still
priced rather reasonably. Before heading to the gate we try the Aeroméxico Lounge…
Or at least we try.. to try it. Because despite being listed
on the Priority Pass app, for some reason
they don’t accept priority passes. This leads to the uniquely
pleasurable experience of being rejected at the door in front of everybody else,
so we move on to another lounge… if you can call it that. Because lounges in North
and Central America keep proving my point. Which is that they’re not that great. I mean, the only food they have at the lounge
are nachos and melon which is fine
if you hold an unlimited Priority Pass. But if you paid the 25 dollar entry fee
it makes no sense. For the three of us, my brother,
my wife and me, that would be 75 dollars basically for nachos, melon and water. At least the view is nice. But when I look a little closer, my
confidence in the airline starts to fade. But this is Aeroméxico Connect,
which is a very different story from Aeroméxico itself. Or at least I hope so. The mainline carrier seems to be well established, serving around
a hundred destinations on four continents. To my knowledge, it’s also the only Latin
American airline flying directly to Asia. But I also always forget
just how huge Mexico is. It’s the 13th biggest country in the world
by landmass. So it’s no wonder there are more than 40
domestic destinations too. Today, we’re
headed to one of them: Puerto Escondido. Like most planes in Aeroméxico’s
all-Boeing fleet, today’s ride is a 737,
a MAX 8 to be exact. With the history of this aircraft it’s
not really my favorite, so for me the fleet it’s
not a big plus of Aeroméxico. Unfortunately we couldn't book seats together, which was a bit annoying,
but it is what it is. At least the crew seems welcoming
and the cabin itself feels comfortable, so overall the flight
still starts on a pretty good note. I'm also quite impressed with the onboard product
but let me give you a short tour. The seats recline
and come with an adjustable headrest that feels more comfortable than what an economy
class flight should be allowed to offer. There’s also a universal power outlet,
and my personal highlight is the massive inflight
entertainment screen right in front of me. With 79 centimeters, that’s about 31 inches, Aeroméxico
gives you roughly 11 percent more legroom than its local competitors
Viva and Volaris on the same route. So all in all with this kind of interior,
Aeroméxico easily has one of the best onboard products
I’ve ever had on a domestic economy class flight. As the plane lifts off from Mexico City, the first thing that hits me
is just how endless this place is. It’s just concrete, stretching out
in every direction as far as you can see. And then suddenly it just stops. Out of nowhere there’s this massive empty
patch cutting through a sea of houses, like somebody forgot to hit copy-paste
on that part of the city. Even though you may believe
that the empty patch down there is the pickleball court
of some very ambitious local sports club, it’s actually what remains of Mexico City
Texcoco Airport. What's Mexico City Texcoco Airport
you may ask? Well it’s a project where Mexican
taxpayers had the honor of burying about 3.5 billion US dollars
before the project was finally abandoned. I don’t know anything about politics
in Mexico, but burning billions on an unfinished project
sounds like peak government efficiency. Anyway, for a country the size of Mexico,
3.5 billion is probably just peanuts. Which brings
us neatly to the topic of catering. Since today’s flight is only about an hour
and a half, I wasn’t expecting a full Mexican feast
with a bottle of tequila. Not that it wouldn’t be nice. Instead, a cup of water
and a tiny bag of salted poison for anyone with a peanut allergy
feels just about right for the occasion. Anyway it’s time to relax. To my bitter disappointment, today’s
flight is just a few minutes too short to watch the My Little Pony movie. Still, it’s
nice to know that the multilingual IFE has enough content to circle the globe
a couple of times. You can even connect your AirPods directly
to the IFE, log into the free Wi-Fi, and chat with your homies
who ended up a few rows away. Little touches
like that really make a difference. And I know I can be hard to please
sometimes, but I am impressed. When it comes to the onboard product, Aeroméxico
actually delivers something impressive. The airline is twenty percent
owned by Delta, and even though I have never flown
with a U.S. carrier myself,
I have heard plenty of good things. And experiencing that level of quality
here feels quite refreshing. Another highlight comes with the view
on approach to Puerto Escondido. It may not be as famous as the beach towns
along the Riviera Maya or in Baja California, but this laid-back surf town
is steadily gaining attention. Once a small fishing village, Puerto
Escondido on the Pacific coast of Oaxaca has grown into a destination
that attracts visitors from many places with its relaxed atmosphere
and surf culture. If you ever plan to visit, Aeroméxico
might actually be a good option. We arrive on time, and the whole
experience turned out far better than I expected. The onboard product feels refined,
almost premium, and while prices are higher than with the low-cost
carriers, they remain reasonable. Of course, there are cheaper alternatives
such as Volaris, which you can check out in my video
from Oaxaca de Juárez to Cancún. Thanks a lot for
watching, and see you soon.

reviews.transcript_full: [Music] Hey guys, this time we won't be sipping on champagne in business class. Today we're in economy with Asia's most awarded carrier, Singapore Airlines. Let's see if it really lives up to that hype. >> If you're new here, in our last video, we had just 12 hours in Singapore and tried to eat our way through as many Michelin Guide street food stalls as possible. If you missed that one, definitely check it out after this. And as always, hit that subscribe button to follow our adventures. [Music] >> In this episode, we're taking you along from our journey from Adelaide airport to Singapore and onwards to Taiwan. A rough flight time of 12 hours, plus however long you want to be in Singapore. Our first flight was on a Boeing 78710 in a 333 layout. much better than the dreaded 343 squeeze, but leg room was only the standard 32 inch pitch. Fine for me at an average height, though the seats definitely felt on the narrow side. Cushioning was decent for economy, and the cabin itself was clean and well presented. There's a crisp and bright 11.6 in touchscreen, which I found responsive, a USB charging port and headphone socket, and a call attendant buttons, a nook to store your phone, and a cup holder. Just below there was plenty of seat back storage which expanded enough to fit my water bottle. Always important. Soon after boarding we were handed steaming hot towels. And I mean steaming. A nice touch often admitted in economy class these days. The flight was reasonably quick to board. With little traffic in Adelaide, we departed on time. With Singapore being a gateway to Europe and the rest of Asia, the flight was full. So, it did take a while for the service to reach us for our first meal, lunch. A bread roll kicked things off, followed by two choices for the main. The first being Kungpow chicken with rice and greens. A Chinese classic. Surprisingly, they even included peanuts and chili for an authentic take. Surprisingly tasty, too. The bread roll was also warm and fresh. On the side was a creamy pasta salad with smoked salmon and also for after dinner, a snack of cheese and crackers. A bit of an Aussie take there. The alternative meal was a pepperc corn beef with spring onion mash and steamed veggies. The veggies here look very much like frozen ones, and I paired the meal with a tiger beer, Singapore's local brew included in the service. The beef and mash were mild and comforting enough, but honestly a bit forgettable. The Kungpow chicken though had a much better flavor, a little kick, and a lot more character. Definitely the winner between the two. To finish it off, a little tub of chocolate gelato was served. Creamy, rich, and surprisingly good for an airplane dessert. A sweet way to round out the meal. Later came a snack with a bit of an Aussie touch, a pumpkin and chickpea parcel and a chicken and veggie pasti. The pasta was a bit reminiscent of an empanada. Both of these were served volcanic lava hot. And let's be honest, they were both fairly forgettable. If you're not hungry, maybe save the calories for a Changi airport treat instead. The pastries were thick and the fillings were bland. One bite was more than enough for one of us. And before long, we arrived at Changi Airport, Singapore. [Music] And speaking of Changi, in our last episode, we toured some of its highlights and showed why the airport itself just might be the best part of any Singapore layover with some tasty, affordable food. Definitely worth checking it out if you missed it. Links are in the description. Before long, it was time for our second flight to Taipei on an identical 78710. The same layout with those blue gray seats. A smooth takeoff above the iconic Singapore shipping lanes is always impressive. [Music] A snack of peas and rice crackers was served with a drink, apple juice, for me as an early refreshment. For dinner, our first selection was the soya brazed pork with steamed rice. The pork was quite fatty and is a similar dish to Taiwanese lurafan braised pork. Not bad, but not great. It didn't quite hit the mark for me. That fatty pork was balanced though with a healthy portion of rice and a mix of vegetables. [Music] I did appreciate the garlic bok choy and mini corn as opposed to just the peas and carrot mix from the last flight. I may have also been slightly harsher on this meal since I had eaten my fill at the airport prior to this flight. On the side was a cold puff wheat barley salad mix with shrimp and had a very pickled flavor. It was a bit strange. We were split on the reviews of this one. One of us liked it, the other one didn't. What was unanimous though was our opinion of the second optioned dish. A chicken pasta bake with a tomato base. A healthy amount of cheese, but there was definitely no cheese pull here. And chicken, well, it was ground up. Very average. You can also pre-order your food, which opens up to a few other options. It might be worth checking out prior to your flight. Otherwise, you might be still searching through your pasta for that said chicken. There it is. Apparently, dessert was a Magnum Mini. And yes, emphasis is on the mini. It honestly took me longer to unwrap the thing than I did to eat it. Despite its size, it was sweet, creamy, and surprisingly satisfying. A tiny treat that punches above its weight, and a funny reminder that sometimes the best things in life come in small packages. [Music] I also gave the Wi-Fi a quick test and unlike Lethan's, it actually worked. Smooth connection and free for Chris Flyer members. A nice touch. So, our final thoughts. Overall, Singapore Airlines economy delivers a solid experience. Pros: The seats were comfortable, the cabin was clean, the entertainment screen was bright and responsive. Wi-Fi was free and easy to use, and the food had some highlights. Cons: The seats were a bit narrow, some of the meals, like the pasta bacon, the mid-flight snacks, were underwhelming, and the surface could be a little slow at times. All up, it's a comfortable, reliable economy experience. We'd give it four stars. What do you guys think? Have you flown Singapore Airlines in economy before? And did it live up to the hype? Drop us your thoughts in the comments below. We'd love to hear from you and we'll see you again in the next

reviews.transcript_full: Hey CI ye? Taiwan's skies are beautiful right? Ye So many Sun Yat-sens  (New Taiwan Dollars) too Let's share? Let's share. Fk...it's your fault. Hello everyone, I'm Ben Today I'm unboxing Starlux Airlines. Yes, can you imagine that tiny Taiwan actually has room for a third full-service airline? A special thank you to EVA Air. They thought dominating Taiwan's aviation industry was too easy (???) and were willing to increase the difficulty. But even so, they managed to stand out from two of the world's top airlines, China Airlines and EVA Air and even survived the pandemic Today, Starlux is even making money. Starlux Airlines, what are you? Let's unbox it today. 321 Let's go! Today's flight is the super popular Taiwan-Hong Kong route . I've actually unboxed EVA Air's Taiwan-Hong Kong route before , so I'm really looking forward to it this time. How does Starlux differentiate itself from its traditional big brother, EVA Air? The outbound flight was Starlux's signature A350-900, and the return flight was Starlux's A330-900neo. Are there any significant differences between the two aircraft types? Is Starlux worth the higher fares? Let's quickly jump to our starting point, Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport (TPE). Like EVA Air and China Airlines, Starlux operates from both terminals at Taoyuan Airport . Your check-in terminal is determined by your destination, so be sure to check to avoid ending up in the wrong terminal . Today, I was flying to Hong Kong, so I went to Terminal 1. The Starlux check-in counter at Terminal 1 has three check-in lanes: self-service check-in, bag drop check-in , and general check-in. I didn't see a business class lane, so I'm guessing it's in another row. As for first class, you use the very exclusive Universal Business Center . I'd love to go there, too. But I don't have any money. Would Starlux sponsor me? :D I'd like to take this opportunity to talk about Starlux's unique branding, which is about exquisite space travel. You can see this in so many details, including the graphic design, Starlux's colors, the staff uniforms, the safety video , the name Starlux itself , and so on. Even Starlux's VIP lounge is called The Galactic Lounge , and the mileage program tiers are called Traveler, Adventurer, Explorer , and Insighter. Every detail embodies Starlux's unique brand image. Besides, Starlux is still a Taiwanese airline , and Taiwanese airlines love to collaborate with cartoons. China Airlines has collaborated with Pokémon and Chiikawa, and EVA Air has Hello. Kitty Starry Sky is collaborating with Snoopy. Starry Sky is incredibly attentive to Snoopy's collaboration , from the boarding passes and baggage tags at the check-in counter to the in-flight entertainment system and meals. Snoopy's presence can be seen everywhere, so if you're a Snoopy fan, you'll probably be delighted. I wouldn't be surprised if Starry Sky suddenly sported a Snoopy livery someday . Let's look forward to it. Okay, after getting our boarding passes and going through security and customs , I wanted to talk about the VIP lounges at Terminal 1. One floor above customs, you'll find a whole row of VIP lounges. Both China Airlines and Cathay Pacific have them set up here. But did you know there's actually a free rest area here? Taoyuan Airport calls it the Airport Experience Area, but I personally think calling it the Airport Sleeping Area is more appropriate since everyone sleeps here . What's special about this place is that there are two free showers for everyone to use . The only thing to note is that everyone needs to bring their own towels and queue up . It's free, which is reasonable. They provide things like a hairdryer, shampoo, and shower gel, so you don't need to bring everything. Okay, let's take a look at the plane. Today's boarding gate is A4 , and it has a blue and white porcelain butterfly theme. I think flights from here should be smooth, because... BUTTER fly, Okay, today I'm on Starlux Airlines ' JX235 A350-900. Starlux currently has a total of 10 A350-900s, with an average age of only 1.5 years, which is super young. The B-58505 I took today is also only one year old , basically a plane that just jumped out of the belly of empty air. The A350 is also Starlux's flagship model, which can be seen from their cabin configuration. There are a total of 4 cabin classes with 4 seats: First Class, 26 seats in Business Class , 36 seats in Premium Economy Class , and 240 seats in Economy Class . The seating layouts are 1-2-1, 1-2-1, 2-4-2 , and 3-3-3, respectively . I think many people have already known this, but the 1-2-1 First Class cabin at the front is also the only First Class cabin in Taiwan. It's one of Starlux's selling points . Okay, let's take a look at my seat today, 64K. The chair is made of the very popular RECARO. The CL3710, the economy class seats on the EVA Air 787 and Delta A350 I've previously unboxed, both use this model. But I have to say that the Starlight 's design is superior to the other two. The chairs are painted in brown and gray , a calming and understated color scheme with a touch of luxury . Compared to EVA Air's checkered pattern, which I don't quite understand, it 's truly much better looking . Starlight's website also lists the concepts each color represents, so if you're interested, you can check it out for yourself. Before you sit down, a pillow is already placed on the chair . The pillow uses a very comfortable pillowcase, not the disposable ones many airlines use. Let me take a quick peek here. The China Airlines headrest is made of leather, and the chair itself feels like a fine fabric. It's truly one of the few times I've sat on it. The seats are so soft and comfortable for my butt . For me, the legroom is just right, with an extra fist and a half. With an 18-inch width, the chairs are really comfortable to sit on. I'd like to mention that after Airbus's optimization of the A350, it can actually fit 10 seats per row, but Xingyu still chose a 9-seat per row layout, which is why the width feels relatively comfortable . The headrests can be adjusted up and down , bent left and right , and even the bottom can be concave, making it a true hexagonal warrior. There are charging heads under the chairs, not only universal sockets but also Type-C chargers , two for every three seats. Then there are the electronic windows, which are also worth mentioning because Xingyu is the first airline in the world to launch these electronic windows on the Airbus A350 . Regardless of whether you like electronic windows or not , you have to admit that they are indeed very technological and in line with Xingyu's brand positioning. The adjustment speed is also much faster than the 787 I've ridden, so I think this is still a good choice. Finally , each chair has a coat hook, and the one with it only has a personal reading light but no personal air vent . Great! Let's move forward and take a look at the seatbacks. There's a large pocket underneath and a small pocket in the front. The large pocket contains a safety information barf bag and Otani's flight magazine. The small pocket holds Xingyu's headphones. The headphones are certainly cool, but what's even cooler is the plastic bag that holds them. Even that has a Snoopy theme. I'm really impressed. Looking up, there's a folding dining table and a tablet and cup holder, which I really like. Most CL3710 seats don't have these, so I think this is Xingyu's attempt to differentiate itself from other airlines . Then there's the entertainment system at the top. This system is probably the same one used on China Airlines' A321neo. It's highly sensitive , has narrow bezels, is large in size, and is adjustable. There are also USB and headphone jacks underneath. In terms of hardware , this is definitely one of the best on the market. Xingyu has also put a lot of thought into the software. Each destination has its own exclusive Snoopy Home. The page is incredibly cute , and the entertainment is all there— movies, TV shows, games, music , and even mind-reading! Since I don't have any friends , I found this perfect children's book for me. Speaking of children's books, children certainly have their own dedicated children's page, and foodies can also find today's flight menu. Personally, I was most excited to find a state-of-the-art flight map and the ability to connect my Bluetooth headphones. Otherwise, I really don't have any complaints. This entertainment system is perfect for me. After unboxing and settling into my seat , I'm off to perform my mission today: act naive and ask the flight attendant for playing cards. I don't know. I've always felt a bit embarrassed asking for playing cards since I'm not a child. But these Xingyu playing cards are really beautiful . They have a lot of slogans that fit the Xingyu brand image, like " The Journey of Exploration" and " Navigate to the Shiniest Star." How could I not grab such cool playing cards ? Then the safety section played. The demonstration also continued to echo the theme of Starry Sky space travel. The characters were all so cute and adorable, it felt like a Pixar movie. I particularly liked that if you carefully read the safety instructions, you'll find they're all part of the same plot. This continuity really makes you feel like you're on a fun journey. These details are really great. Soon after, the plane started pushback. Let's take a look at the takeoff sequence. After reaching altitude, the crew quickly began serving food. But before the food arrives, I want to quickly explain in-flight internet. All Starry Sky aircraft offer internet access . Passengers in Premium Economy, Business Class, and First Class can use it free and unlimited. As for Economy Class, although internet access is also free , it's limited to messaging. Even so, it's excellent. I give Starry Sky a thumbs up here . Let 's go back to the in-flight meal. This time, Starry Sky's meal was fried rice noodles with pumpkin and pork, just like the one I saw on my previous EVA flight. Airplane meals are all about fried rice noodles. Wow, is that so intense? A head-on confrontation . This in-flight meal includes a main course, a bowl of fresh fruit , a small snack , and apple juice . The main course rice noodles are topped with pumpkin and vegetables. Just looking at it is enough to whet your appetite. For those who don't like pumpkin, this might be hell , but I'm a pumpkin guardian. Pumpkin is my Nanber 1. The rice noodles themselves are very moist and not dry (what nonsense). They are very flavorful. I can only say that I think this beats EVA Air's fried rice noodles. It's over. And forget about the main course. Xingyu provided the fruit, EVA Air directly gave it to them. I've never had bad fruit on flights departing from Taiwan , so there's really nothing much to say about that. The most important thing is the snacks and apple juice. Actually, they didn't taste anything special. They were just egg rolls and apple juice , but I thought the egg roll packaging was cute and made them perfect for taking off the plane or giving as gifts. I think it's important to note that because the Taiwan-Hong Kong route is so short , cupped drinks aren't provided. Even the entertainment system says they 're not available, but if you ask the flight attendants, they'll give them to you. I ordered an extra Calpis. As for the famous Xingyu Special, unfortunately, it's not available on this route either . So... I'll wait for another longer flight to unpack it. Overall, this is truly an excellent in-flight meal service. Not only is the food delicious, but the tableware is also made of iron . The packaging for the wet wipes, toilet paper, salt, pepper, and toothpicks has all been designed by Xingyu. They really don't miss any detail. For Taiwan-Hong Kong routes, this is definitely the best (I think I said the same thing last time I flew EVA Air, haha). I give Xingyu a thumbs up . After eating, let's take a look at the restroom. There's a huge mirror, two coat hooks, an air vent , a toilet seat , a faucet with adjustable water temperature, a cup, Xingyu-branded hand soap , and a moisturizing lotion and spray from a collaboration with IDUN . If you ask me if I know this brand, I'll tell you. IDUN know :D The above are things that many other airlines also provide, but the following are what make Star Universe different. First of all, there are green plants in the toilet . It's amazing. I can't even keep plants alive on land, but Star Universe can do it on the plane. Then the toilet paper for wiping butts is designed like the runway. Star Universe, you are really good. How can I bear to wipe my butt like this? I can only say that this is a very impressive toilet. Star Universe always finds ways to make some improvements on some seemingly insignificant points , which makes this trip particularly memorable. I think this is why so many people have such high opinions of Star Universe. Then we are about to land at Hong Kong International Airport. Let's jump to the return trip. Oh~ Let's go back and forth to Taipei~ Star Universe uses Row D at Hong Kong Airport, which is divided into three check-in lanes: general check-in, bag drop check-in, and premium check-in. You can also find cute luggage tags at the check-in counter. The boarding passes are also Snoopy-themed. It seems that I will be bombarded by Snoopy for another hour and a half. After passing through customs, our flight today is still on the way, so I just wandered around Hong Kong Airport to check out the planes. The weather today is great. I happened to see this Cathay Pacific A350-900 flying to Shanghai Pudong. I have actually unboxed this aircraft for this route before , so if you are interested, you can click on the upper right corner to see it. At this time, I happened to see China Airlines and Air China in the same frame. I was so PTSD. Old fans who follow my channel You might know that I actually filmed a video about Air China vs. China Airlines. My original intention for making that video was simply to make it a fun topic. However, I didn't expect the comments section to spark a lot of disagreements, which I didn't want to see. It even affected my own mood. So, after reflection, I decided to take the video down. But don't worry if you still want to see it! The content will still be up, just in a different form . I'd appreciate your continued support then. Okay, let's take a look at the flight that just arrived from Taipei. My return flight was Starlux JX234. Starlux currently has five A330neos, with an average age of about three years. Today's aircraft, B-58304, is also about three years old , so it's quite new. Upon boarding, we saw that its seat layout is quite different from the A350 . There are only two cabin classes: Business Class with 28 seats and Economy Class with 269 seats, both featuring the A330's standard 1-2-1 and 2-4-2 seating arrangements, respectively. My seat today was 52A . Let's see how the A330 and A350 seats differ. Actually, they're practically identical, with the same RECARO CL3710 seats and the same entertainment system as the A350 . So, the overall experience shouldn't be significantly different, though... There are a few minor differences, so I'll quickly touch on them. First, due to the width of the fuselage, the A330's seats are only 17.1 inches wide , slightly smaller than the A350's 18 inches. So, consider this for yourself : do you prefer slightly larger seats, or a 2-4-2 layout? Feel free to leave a comment below to share your thoughts. Next, there's an entertainment system box under the window seats this time , so there's a little extra space, but thankfully, it's not overly large , so it's still acceptable. Also, on my return trip, I asked the flight attendant for an extra blanket. It was so fluffy and comfortable to the touch , one of the best blankets I've ever used in economy class. If I had to compare, I'd say it's more comfortable than EVA Air's and about the same as China Airlines'. Those are the differences from the outbound flight (I forgot to mention the windows). Everything else remains at a very high standard, so I don't think the flight experience will be significantly affected by the aircraft change (only in economy class). But if I had to choose, I still think the A350 has a slight edge. What do you think? Okay, let's take a look at the meal on the return flight. It was the same as the outbound flight. It came with a main course, a bowl of fruit juice , and biscuits . That's it for the fruit and juice . I'll focus on the main courses and biscuits, which were a bit different. Today's main course was Hong Kong-style barbecue pork fried rice noodles . The presentation alone was way better than the pathetic fried rice on EVA Air. There were four large pieces of barbecue pork , very Hong Kong vegetables, and noodles. The only thing missing from this dish was the word "Hong Kong" written directly on it. Not only was it beautiful, it was also quite delicious. Although the barbecue pork was not the best barbecue pork I've ever had , it was really good for an airplane meal. Next was the egg rolls, the same as the outbound flight , but this time they were Ruby Black Tea flavored. I'm going to mention it again because I think the flavor is super delicious. The light tea aroma offsets the sweetness of the egg rolls, creating a beautiful taste that makes me want to go to Dawushan Ranch to buy a box. Overall, it was another excellent meal. My impression after trying the meals on these two Xingyu flights is this. Starlux really values ​​aesthetics and creativity. While other airlines offer classic dishes, Starlux always strives to be a little different with its in-flight meals . For example, EVA Air fed us classic Taiwanese fried rice noodles, which I found delicious . However, Starlux seems a bit boring. They insisted on adding a pumpkin to the fried rice noodles , making the meal colorful and beautiful. I think this is why so many people look forward to trying Starlux's in-flight meals. Not long after, I landed back at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport. This brief Starlux trip has already made me look forward to my next Starlux flight. From the basics like the boarding pass and security video to the thoughtfully designed in-flight meals and restrooms, every aspect clearly shows that Starlux is different from other airlines. You may not like everything Starlux does , but I think these innovative breakthroughs will only be good things for Taiwan's aviation industry. I believe EVA Air and China Airlines won't sit idly by when they see Starlux doing this. I hope that Taiwan's three major airlines can grow and become better airlines through this healthy competition . The above is all about the Starlux Airlines unboxing. Finally, I want to share a very interesting thing with everyone . After landing in Taiwan this time, I was actually recognized and asked for a photo? It really scared me. Who is this person to be so honored to be asked for a photo ? I am very grateful to this friend who approached me. For the next episode, I'm thinking about whether to do Thai Airways or Singapore Airlines. Many people have said they want to see both, so I welcome everyone to leave a comment below to let me know. See you in the next video.

reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm reviewing Qatar Airways Economy Class on a 6 hour flight from London to Doha and since they've been rated the best airline in the world for the last 5 out of 6 years by Skytrax I thought it time to put them to the test and see if Qatar Airways are really as good as people say... and spoiler alert, this was an excellent flight with only a few conceivable issues so sit back and enjoy the ride... and Starting off at London Heathrow Terminal 4 we actually encounter pretty much the only bad thing about the whole experience The check-in queue was long, taking just over 30 minutes to clear to be fair, this was probably our fault as we only arrived 1.5 hours before departure But just bear in mind the queues can be long and plan to arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure and you should be fine anyway, we dropped off our bags just 5 minutes before check-in closed and security was much quicker plus they have those new scanners that don't require removing laptops and liquids So we basically walked right through Our gate today was gate 2 right here, a 2 min walk from security whilst in the past I've had gate 25 over here, which is a 10 or 15 min walk and boarding started pretty much as soon as we arrived, so besides the slow check-in everything else was very smooth I couldn't get a good view of the plane from the gate, so in its stead, here's a great view of another random 777-300ER I saw after landing in Doha same aircraft type but different registration whilst waiting for our boarding group I also got a bit of plane spotting in Here's a Qatar A380 also heading to Doha just half an hour before our flight they do up to 10 flights a day between Heathrow & Doha so you'll pretty much always see at least one of their planes here Also there was a Malaysia Airlines A350 about to head to Kuala Lumpur I flew that 2 years ago and it became my most viewed video ever, so shameless plug for people to watch that too... and I think they're a severely underrated airline btw with some of the best food I've had (in Economy at least) Now before we step on board here are the stats and route map for today's flight where we would fly over Europe, Turkey and Iraq before landing into Doha almost 20 minutes early on what would be a very smooth and uneventful flight also random fact, the day we flew the temperature in Doha was 43 degrees, so I was glad we didn't have a bus gate stepping on board we were greeted by some smiley cabin crew and headed to our seats, 21A & B and we paid £50 each for  what QR call "Preferred Seats" near the front of the cabin Only reason I did that is because we had a 2 hour transfer and I wanted to ensure we got off the plane quickly in case of any delays, as you can see from the seat map they have 3 separate Economy cabins but as it happened we were early anyway so it didn't matter Now looking at the seat, it's really good with excellent legroom and it's very well cushioned making it perfect for long haul flights The seatback pocket has 3 separate pouches to that's handy and I also found the seats are very tall which gives quite good privacy for Economy Class also part of the reason I chose this seat was for the great engine view... Back to the seat, you get a folding tray table and USB port, and for some reason an ethernet port... so leave a comment if you have any idea what that could be used for There's a power socket under the seat  Then your bog standard fleece blanket and relatively well sized pillow and I guess I appreciate they provide both on a 6 hour daytime flight as I've flown some airlines who wouldn't on a flight this length and the last feature of the seat is this adjustable headrest Headphones are decent for Economy Class, and I find them better than the in ear headphones many airlines provide and they even give you a little hand wipe, something many airlines don't bother with these days... Then last thing about the seat is the entertainment system and this plane is actually one of Qatar Airways' older cabin so the screen looks a bit dated But the screen itself was fine and has the same slick interface you see on all their aircraft It was also a decent size at 10.6" Which isn't as good as the 13" screens you get in Emirates Economy for example but it is comparable to most major airlines The movie and tv selection was extensive so no complaints there the only thing that confused me is the map seemed to be stuck in Arabic and I couldn't find a way to change it and this only affected the map, everything else was in English... Also they have this slightly dated tv remote which I personally never use but I guess it's there if you want it And lastly before the safety video, it has this good picture in picture function So you can watch a movie whilst having the map in a smaller window, or vice versa Now here is the Muslim travel prayer and safety video, featuring Kevin Hart... and just on the safety video, they say they don't want it to be "no nonsense that is a direct call out to Emirates who say at the start of their safety video how no nonsense it is... so Qatar's video is definitely a bit more interesting than Emirates, but still not the world's greatest like they say Also spotted this weird wingless and tail-less plane, so leave a comment if you know that it is... Now it's time for the takeoff, where we got a great view of all the planes parked at London Heathrow... even if the weather was a little grey Service started with a drink and a bag of crunchy corn snacks I got a ginger ale to drink and then I also asked for coffee and they made me some actually impressive as most airlines would just tell you they only serve coffee after the main meal so props to Qatar Airways for being very accomodating there Then for the main meal it was a choice of beef or vegetarian pasta and I got the beef Now presentation and portion-wise this was great However, taste-wise it was one of the blandest meals I can remember having on a plane... not bad... just bland so a bit more flavour or maybe some salt and pepper would pouches would be nice you do get metal cutlery though, which is a plus and also a first for me on a plane, foccacia bread, though it was a bit stodgy This was Spätzle by the way (German pasta) Then after the main meal hot drinks and Biscoff were served And now for the loo review, it was kept clean... but that's about it just a normal airplane toilet otherwise though it did have a lot of mirrors... Another very strong point for this flight was the free superfast Starlink Wifi It worked flawlessly, was super fast and they also let you watch live sport if you use a QR code on the screen It was fast enough to watch Youtube videos in 1080p with no issue and so far they've just rolled out Starlink to almost all of their Boeing 777s and some Airbus A350s  but eventually it will come to all Qatar Airways Aircraft, though the wait might be long... and very lastly before landing we were served a light snack with a choice of chicken or vegetarian pastry And I have to say, this Harissa Chicken roll was better than a Greggs sausage roll as sacriligeous as that may be to say to my UK viewers Coming in to land we got a view of these crazy private mansions, each one on its own private island though I have to say, if I paid that much money for a private island I might get a bit annoyed by the sound of planes constantly flying over So here we are in Doha, where the outside temperature was 43 degrees at the time of arrival and I'm happy to report it was a very good flight Only just over 6 hours so you could barely class it as long haul but they did get 2 meal services in and the crew were really good throughout so I would happily book Qatar Airways on a proper long haul flight in the future and between today's flight and the connecting flight I took with them in Business Class I think Qatar Airways are probably now my favourite Middle Eastern Airline, Just slightly beating Emirates and Etihad Though I'm flying Etihad next month from London to Singapore and back so we'll see if they can get some redemption there... and I've made a bid to upgrade to Business on one of those flights so hopefully it comes through and very lastly, I was connecting onwards to Ho Chi Minh City after this and the last time I transferred at Doha we had to go through a security check so I was pleasantly surprised when we walked off the plane straight into the terminal anyway, that meant our 2 hour layover was more than enough time and we had a good chance to explore the airport especially this cool rainforest area... now without further ado, here is my final score for Qatar Airways Economy Really my only gripe with the entire experience was how bland the main meal was but literally everything else was well above average so I can forgive them for that  definitely earning their rank as one of the world's best airlines... So after all that Qatar Airways will keep their ranking of 9/10 on my airline tierlist Just below Singapore Airlines which I must admit I still prefer but that's probably just down to personal preference and just ahead of Emirates and Etihad by the skin of their teeth Now here's a quick preview of my next flight in Qatar's 787 Business Class on a flight to Ho Chi Minh City which I've already released so click the link in the description or top right corner to see that it was also a fantastic flight despite not being in the QSuite seat Coming soon I'll have reviews of Vietnam Airlines, China Eastern, and a cool hotel on the island of Phu Quoc so stay tuned for all that and more! Thanks for watching, please like and subscribe if you enjoyed and good bye!

reviews.transcript_full: The 2026Qar Airways Airbus A380 is more than just an aircraft. It is an experience that combines scale, comfort, and elegance in a way that only the largest passenger jet in the world can deliver. For years, the Airbus A380 has symbolized longhaul luxury. And Qatar Airways has embraced it fully by refining every detail to create a journey that feels closer to a five-star hotel in the sky than conventional air travel. From the moment you step inside the aircraft, the first thing you notice is the sense of space. The double-deck design means high ceilings, wide aisles, and cabins that feel open and welcoming. Qatar Airways has redesigned the interiors for 2026 with modern lighting, upgraded climate controls, and materials chosen to create a calm atmosphere. Even on flights lasting over 14 hours, passengers feel comfortable and refreshed. Economy class has been enhanced with better seat ergonomics, improved leg room, and larger personal entertainment screens. Each seat now includes charging ports, USBC connectivity, and Bluetooth pairing, so passengers can use their own headphones. The entertainment system is faster, more intuitive, and offers thousands of hours of movies, TV shows, music, and games. Even on the longest routes, there is more than enough to keep everyone entertained. Premium economy is now available on the Qatar Airways A380. Positioned as a perfect middle ground. The seats are wider, recline deeper, and offer extra personal space. Passengers in this cabin also enjoy upgraded dining with menus designed specifically for longer flights along with larger entertainment screens and amenities that make the experience feel much more premium without the price tag of business class. Business class remains one of the highlights of flying Qatar Airways. The A380 features the airlines award-winning Quit redesigned for the spacious cabin. Each seat converts into a fully flat bed and is equipped with privacy doors. Couples and families can create private areas by opening partitions, making the cabin flexible for different types of travelers. Dining is on demand with restaurant style service, fine ingredients, and presentation designed to feel like a luxury restaurant above the clouds. Wi-Fi is fast and reliable, allowing passengers to work, stream, or stay connected throughout the journey. First class is where the aircraft truly shines. The 2026 update includes larger private suites, enhanced finishes, and luxury bedding. Each suite offers a flat bed, large highdefinition screen, direct aisle access, and personal storage. The menus feature gourmet dishes designed by top chefs paired with premium wines and champagnes carefully selected for altitude. Exclusive amenity kits, designer sleepwware, and refined service make first class feel like a private retreat in the sky. One of the most unique features of the Qar Airways A380 is the onboard lounge. Located on the upper deck, it serves as a social hub for first and business class passengers. With comfortable seating, a bar offering premium beverages, and a selection of light snacks, the lounge is designed for both relaxation and conversation. The 2026 upgrade introduced softer lighting, quieter surroundings, and improved seating arrangements that encourage interaction or peaceful downtime depending on passenger preferences. Technology also plays a central role in the passenger experience. The Orex 1 entertainment platform now features 4K resolution screens in premium cabins and an interface that responds instantly. Passengers can create playlists that carry over to future flights if they are frequent travelers. Wi-Fi has been upgraded to high-speed satellite systems, making it possible to stream, video call, and work without interruptions. This connectivity transforms the A380 into both a leisure and business environment. Qatar Airways has also made strides in sustainability with its A380 operations. The updated engines have been tuned for better fuel efficiency. Cabin refurbishments use lighter materials, and the airline invests heavily in sustainable aviation fuels and carbon offset programs. For passengers who are conscious about the environment, this commitment adds reassurance that luxury and responsibility can exist together. Cabin crew continued to play a vital role in shaping the journey. Qatar Airways is known for its attentive service, and on the A380, this reputation is enhanced by the generous space and carefully designed service routines. Crew members anticipate passenger needs, assist with dietary requests, and maintain a calm, professional presence that makes every traveler feel valued. Another detail that passengers notice is how quiet the cabin is. Despite the size of the aircraft, sound insulation and engine design make the flight environment peaceful. This is especially important on overnight routes where rest is a priority. The improved air quality systems also reduce fatigue, making longhaul travel less exhausting than on smaller aircraft. Families are well cared for on board. Qatar Airways provides children's entertainment content, kid-friendly meals, and practical support like bassinets and early boarding. The spacious cabins make traveling with children more manageable, and parents appreciate the extra consideration that helps keep younger passengers comfortable and entertained. The A380 is deployed on some of Qar Airways most important routes. Cities like London, Paris, Sydney, and Bangkok see the aircraft regularly, reflecting demand for both capacity and premium service. These are high-profile routes where the airline showcases its flagship product, ensuring that passengers experience the very best the brand has to offer. For aviation enthusiasts, the A380 is still an incredible sight with its massive wingspan and double-deck design that towers over most other aircraft at the airport. Boarding this aircraft always feels like a special occasion. And Qatar Airways has leaned into that sense of wonder by making the onboard experience as memorable as possible. Every detail from the seats and dining to the entertainment and service is designed to make passengers feel that they are part of something extraordinary. The 2026Qar Airways Airbus A380 is more than just a means of travel. It is a statement about what air travel can be. It blends tradition with modernity, combining the scale of the world's largest passenger aircraft with the elegance and service that have made Qar Airways one of the most respected airlines in the world. Whether flying in economy, business, or first, the journey offers comfort, technology, and hospitality that elevate longhaul travel into a truly remarkable experience. Thanks for watching.

yt_comments.text: I did some research on Emirates registrations and what cabins you can roughly expect for all of them. The # will resemble [insert letter] For the A380s, registrations with “A6-ED#,” you will see the oldest cabins, which come with the most dated cabins and features the oldest and smallest IFE system within the A380s. For A380s registered “A6-EE#,” you will mostly see the cabin that was featured in the flight from Brisbane to Dubai: The “middle class” cabin which comes with the 10” black bezel IFE screen based on the eX3 (or maybe eX1?) platform. yt_comments.text: some more facts about pegasus for those who wonder: - planes are named after daughters of the employees. - most of 321neos are based in Istanbul SAW, 320neos and 737 are based in secondary cities (Antalya, Izmir, Ankara and others.) - PGSUS is the code for its stock in Istanbul Stock Exchange. a couple of years ago, it joined to BIST30 index (top 30 stock in istanbul exchange). never pays dividends. - seats don't recline. - there is no screen in seats but in many planes there is in flight entertainment used via wifi. no internet, tv shows and movies etc. (paid or premium packages) but you can check your location in map, and other flight info in real time (this is free) - bolbol points are useful especially to buy upgrades. one return flight would give enough points for your next flights meal or seat selection.

reviews.transcript_full: Good day and welcome back to the Flying Doctor channel.  On today's one minute flight review, we'll go from Belan, Brazil to São Paulo on a Latam A320 in  premium economy. I use the self-service kiosk to check in and print my boarding pass before  heading airside to catch a few special livery's.  Premium economy with Latam is similar to your business where all seats are economy but the  middle seat is blocked. The FA created each passenger by name and handed them a bottle of water  before we were pushed back and sky-borne. About 45 minutes after takeoff, I was offered the choice  of a frittata or sandwich. I opted for the beef and cheese sandwich which came with a bag of chips  and granola bar. Lager room was comfortable and power options were available if I needed.  No IFE on the seatback but a catalog of movies and TV shows are available after connecting to  the inflate Wi-Fi. The ability to message and serve the web costs a few extra bucks.  I paid $154 for the premium economy seat which was only about $30 on top of basic economy.  Considering you get a light meal, early boarding and additional baggage allowance,  I think it's definitely worth the extra money. reviews.transcript_full:
Today, we're flying ITA Airways Business Class aboard a 
brand-new Airbus A330neo from the Maldives to Rome The video features the full Business Class experience on
ITA Airways (seat, meals, service, entertainment, amenities) Welcome to the International Airport of the Maldives We're taken to the main terminal by a Four Seasons luxury car Check-in is smooth, with dedicated Business Class counters We’re taken by bus to the remote aircraft stand The new international terminal at Velana International Airport 
in the Maldives is officially set to open this summer The Maldives’ old terminal was built for 1.5 million passengers
but now serves over 2 million, causing major congestion The new Maldives airport expansion will ease congestion 
and handle the growing number of travelers This is the Airbus A330neo that will fly us to the Maldives
(aircraft registration: EI-TYC; named Stefano Baldini)  ITA Airways operates a total of 23 long-haul aircraft in its fleet:
11 Airbus A330-900neo, 6 Airbus A350, and 6 Airbus A330-200 ITA Airways' fleet has an average age of 5.7 years Have you ever flown with ITA Airways?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment ITA Airways' A330neo Business Class cabin is arranged in a 
1-2-1 configuration, giving each passenger direct aisle access 6L is my Business Class seat for the flight to the Rome The seat model is the Thompson Vantage XL,  
an excellent seat type used by several leading airlines What makes ITA’s version unique is the bespoke Italian styling Window seats alternate between true window seats (set closer
to the fuselage) and aisle-adjacent seats (set closer to the aisle) In the center section, seats are arranged in a paired layout, 
designed with couples or traveling companions in mind ITA Airways' A330neo Business Class cabin features a
stylish decor, reflecting Italy’s legendary design sensibility A hot towel and welcome drink are offered upon boarding Nineteen athletes, including Olympic and Paralympic
medalists, demonstrate the procedures in the safety video We're leaving the gate at 1 pm local time (on-time departure) We pass a Dreamliner of Neos, an Italian airline specializing 
in leisure travel and a competitor of ITA Airways Male Airport has 2 runways measuring 45 × 3,200 m
(148 × 10,499 ft) and 60 × 3,400 m (200 × 11,150 ft) ITA Airways' Airbus A330neo aircraft
are powered by Rolls-Royce Trent 7000 engines The Trent 7000 engine delivers a thrust of 72,000 pounds
(one engine has the push of 100 Ferraris racing flat out) This enables the A330neo to achieve a non-stop range
of up to 7,200 nautical miles (approximately 13,334 kilometers) We get some terrific views of the Maldives after takeoff The Maldives' islands and atolls
are the visible tips of an oceanic volcanic mountain range The Maldives has 1192 coral islands & sandbanks: 200
islands are inhabited & 140 islands are home to resorts Let's have a closer look at the
ITA Airways Airbus A330neo Business Class seat The seat features a 17-inch high-definition TV screen A spacious footwell is located under the TV Passengers can hang their jackets with a built-in hanger The seat's side cabinet keeps belongings handy
and also holds a modern, elegant light and the power ports The side table under the cabinet holds the entertainment 
handset and seat controls for easy comfort adjustments The seat's tray table is smoothly released via a simple latch Let's explore ITA Airways' Business Class amenities The kit is an elegant clutch in sustainable and reusable canvas,
and contains a dental kit, eye mask, socks, and earplugs Business Class passengers also receive a second kit: a soft 
cosmetics bag by international wellness company QC Terme The kit includes shower gel, shampoo, 
sanitizer, face cream, body cream, and hand butter Bedding includes a pillow, duvet and slippers Noise-cancelling headphones are also provided Let’s explore today's inflight dinner menu ITA Airways’ Business Class wine list features 
a curated selection of fine Italian and international wines Aperitif, served with mixed nuts Starter: pumpkin and parmesan cheese flan
with mushrooms and toasted pumpkin seeds Turnip greens Orecchiette pasta: Italian pasta dressed
with anchovies of Cetara, tomatoes and bread crumble Main course: braised beef cheek, 
accompanied by roasted cubed pumpkin and sautéed chard Fresh sliced seasonal fruit plate Dessert: tiramisu with coffee glaze and dark cocoa crumble ITA Airways' A330neo Business Class has 3 lavatories: one 
at the front, and two shared with Premium Economy at the rear With the push of a button, the Business Class 
seat reclines into a fully flat bed The bed measures 80 inches (203 centimeters) in length Let's explore ITA Airways' inflight entertainment The program offers the latest Italian movies, Hollywood 
blockbusters, TV shows and immersive music playlists ITA Airways offers Wi-Fi on its Airbus A330neo fleet The flight path takes us over Abu Dhabi We encounter some turbulence in the Iraqi airspace It's time for a midflight snack: assorted Italian cheese board
served with pear mustard, dried apricot and pistachios A light dinner is served 90 minutes prior to arrival: 
a slice of gourmet Napolitan stone baked pizza The pizza is served with a walnut brownie as dessert We're approaching the Italian airspace ITA Airways is Italy’s national airline,
founded in 2020 as the successor to Alitalia With its striking blue livery and Italian flair,  ITA Airways 
represents a new chapter in Italy’s aviation story ITA’s fleet features modern Airbus aircraft, including the A220, 
A320neo, and the sleek A330neo & A350 for long-haul routes Despite a challenging start in a competitive market, ITA
is expanding its network across Europe, the U.S., and beyond Thank you for watching my video about 
ITA Airways' Airbus A330neo Business Class
