reviews.transcript_full:
As soon as I sat down in my very nicely 
equipped all aisle access flat bed business   class seat- like when I really sat down to 
settle in, the first question that came to   mind was: Wait a minute, is this seat 
actually better than their old 2-2-2?  Everyone always wants a modern all aisle access 
flatbed, for the record, myself included. But,   this was the first time that I’ve ever sat 
in those traditional lie flat seats followed   by a tight squeeze of a staggered seat just 2 
hours later and well, I have opinions to share.  By the way, the price that I paid for this and 
every flight I take is always in the description.  Let me welcome any of you who may be new to the 
channel, my name is Kevin. I’m here to give you   a self-funded and honest look at some of the 
best- and some of the not so best- airlines and   hotels in the world, which I’ve been bringing 
to you full time for the past four years.   Check out my hundreds of videos, scan 
the QR code or click the link in the   description to learn more about how I do 
things. Let’s get into the trip report.  I just arrived here in Santiago from Sao Paulo 
and when I say “just” I mean seconds ago and now   I need to high tail it through what honestly felt 
like a never ending maze from the new additions   here at Santiago’s international airport. 
Editions that Google Earth hasn’t even added yet.  I was meant to have around a 2 hour layover. 
Short, but relaxed and was really looking   forward to visiting the LATAM lounge since I 
love their lounge in Sao Paulo and this one   is meant to be even better. But, the winds 
over the Andes today were extreme and so   we had to take a very out of the way route to 
get here, adding an hour to that first flight   and meaning that I needed to walk directly to 
my next gate after passing through security.  As I arrived they were already pre-boarding 
so I was glad I decided to come straight here.  Tonight we’d be hitching a ride on a 7 
year old 787-9 of which Latam group has   27 of with 19 more on the way- along with 
10 787-8s. This flight was originally sold   showing the older configuration 2-2-2 
seating as you saw in my last video,   but around a week prior to the flight, the 
seating was updated to the newer layout.  I should mention though, while today’s layout is a 
very modern seat, LATAM has also revealed a third   layout featuring seats with doors which they 
begun installing, I believe to eventually   replace both of these existing layouts.
Like I said, multi national airlines with   fleets spread out over five countries 
can get a bit complicated at times.  Stepping on board I was warmly greeted and 
quickly found one of my favorite cabin designs   flying these days. I had previously reviewed 
this product- and I use air quotes around this   product because on the 777s, especially in the 
bulkheads, the layout is wildly more spacious.  On board our 787 tonight, all of the finishes 
that I loved from that 777 are the same here,   from the really satisfying squishy interior of 
the shell, to the red leather accents and even   what I swear is real stone on the side tables. 
It’s one of the classiest cabins you can find.  If you’re enjoying the video and would like to 
support the channel there are many ways you can   do so. A quick like on the video and subscribe 
helps videos with the algorithm. You could join   my Youtube Memberships to get early access to some 
videos and access to all of my Community Posts or   you could check out my Patreon where I post the 
most and can help out if you have travel related   questions. Whatever you do, thanks for doing it.
Next to you you have an open storage area with a   small integrated closed area what is built 
like a tank and really satisfying to click   close. The build quality of it makes me wonder 
if it was originally meant to have a lock,   which would have been pretty cool.
Controls, remotes and outlets are   thoughtfully laid out and easy to use and access.
The seat itself though is quite narrow, as is the   aisle to access the window side seats. Generally- 
tight as it may be- I can fit my size 12 foot in   this space, but that wasn’t happening today.
Same as my previous flight, no pre departure   drinks were served but there were 
bottles of water at each seat.  The foot cubby is quite shallow but tall and 
doesn’t have space under it to stow anything.  To get fully situated you’re going 
to need to macgyver it in this seat.  So about what I was saying. Of course, it 
is wonderful to have your own private space   and I have sat in these staggered lie 
flat seats more times than I can count,   some of those times on other airlines on 787s but 
here they were clearly trying to pack these seats   in as tightly as possible. I’m 6’ tall or 181cm 
and while I was seated it was one of those cases   where both of my knees were touching parts of the 
seat and the monitor just felt needlessly close.  I checked the seatmaps of ANA and EVA air who both 
use similar seats on their 787s- both of which,   especially EVA felt extremely roomy 
and they all look to be fitting the   same amount of seats in the same space- 
so, I’m not sure what was going on here.  Anyway, it’s less a complaint and more just 
an open question about the pros and cons of   certain 2-2-2 seats vs certain all aisle access 
seats. The safety video began and we pushed back.  The first drink service started 
promptly after take off, but first   let’s take a look at the comfort items on board.
First up, love a really good quality and cushy   pair of slippers- that along with a great pillow 
are investments I wish more airlines would make,   they can really make a good flight great.
Luckily, LATAM got the message and the pillow   was fantastic in size and fluff- nearly 
as good as Iberia’s but not quite there.  There’s a duvet style blanket in 
the bag as well, one that is soft   and cozy and a good weight as well.
Finally there’s also a mattress pad   which I’ll show you in action in a bit, but 
for now, another creative storage solution.  The drink cart came down the aisle and 
I had a glass of Sauvignon Blanc along   with a sad bowl of cold and somewhat stale nuts.
Here’s a look at the full menu. Prior to take off   orders were taken and I went for the special dish 
of the day, part of their Sabores que Transportan   or flavors that transport a series of local 
inspired dishes created by locally renowned   chefs- a type of program I love to see on board 
any airline, I’ll blindly order whatever they   recommend. Unfortunately when I did order it, it 
had already sold out, so I went with the beef.  Luckily, shortly after take off my 
very friendly member of crew came   by and let me know she found one for me and 
it turned into the highlight of the flight.  The full meal is served all at once which 
is standard for Latam. For the starter   there was thinly sliced Chilean Abalone with 
lemon and potato salad and a green salad.  The main dish, which to their credit looked 
incredibly similar to the photo in the menu   was Smoked pork tenderloin with smashed Chancado 
potatoes with paprika oil, caramelized apples and   plums. Give me pork and apples together and I’m 
there for it all day and this was no exception.   Overall I’d say the dish was lighter in flavor 
than I was expecting but was still a delight to   eat. I can’t tell you how refreshing it is to try 
something truly new on an airplane of all places.  That was finished off with a Dulce de Lech Mousse 
with Chocolate Ganache and brownie chunks which   was perfectly indulgent and a great finish to 
the meal. Overall, the full meal gets a 9/10.  I know some don’t like full tray services 
but for a late departure like this,   I thought it was a good way to go. My tray 
in the last row was cleared just an hour and   25 minutes after take off, leaving plenty 
of time for sleep on this 10 hour flight.  The entertainment on board was decent with 
over 200 movies on offer from all types   of genres as well as a great newest 
generation moving map. Quality noise   canceling headphone were available as well.
Here’s the bed in full flat mode. It is a bit   of a tight squeeze around the knees 
but it gets the job done. At least   that food cubby is tall enough to not also 
restrict you in that direction. That said,   this is not a seat I can comfortably 
sleep in as a flat bed as I’m not   part of the mummy sleeping crowd.
The sleeping pad was thin but very   nice and squishy foam which even while sitting 
up made for a much more comfortable surface.  I enjoyed a few hours of wine assisted half 
reclined sleep and came to as we were approaching   Florida, just before the sun began to come up.
Let’s take a look at the amenity kit and   get ready for the breakfast service.
I loved the kit. These and the smaller   kits offered on my previous flight are both from 
the same artist collection of kits that they   had rotating through different designs. While I 
don’t need socks or ear plugs or stuff like that,   the number one thing I look for in a good 
kit is whether it’s practical to use again   and this surely, for something, is.
Bathrooms on board were sparse but   kept mostly clean throughout the flight.  The cabin was woken up around 80 minutes prior 
to landing and I was served around 15 minutes   later. A much appreciated efficient service again. 
LATAM really understands what important on these   overnight flights that often stay in the same time 
zone. There’s no need for jetlag if you can get a   decent sleep and LATAM’s service allows for that.
For breakfast there was a choice of scrambled   eggs, a ham and cheese selection or crepes with 
dulce de leche and strawberries. Now, crepes   or pancakes are something I never order unless 
necessary for breakfast on a flight- but also,   I have a rule which requires me to order anything 
that ever has dulce de leche- a rule I adopted   many years ago during my time in Argentina.
Well, today it was a mistake. The dulce de leche,   it can do no harm, was good, even the 
overheated nearly burnt part. But,   the crepes turned into a globbual of sticky hot 
dough as the individual layers fused together.  I also had some yogurt, a small fruit plate 
and… ⅓ of a muffin? Are we rationing muffins   now? Overall, the breakfast gets a 6/10.
Service on board was exactly what I want on   an overnight flight. Friendly and efficient 
during meal services and hiding in between   them for all I care. I also appreciate that 
they never locked the dimmers on the windows.  This flight on it’s own I’d say is 
a 7, but averaged out with my other   LATAM flights I think keeping them at a 6 is fair.  A gorgeous morning approach over 
Sandy Hook and into JFK is coming up.  So, LATAM is a solid airline and I wouldn’t 
hesitate for a moment on flying them again-   though I would be on the lookout 
for their new seats or at least   their 777s which was vastly more comfortable.  So I really do hope you enjoyed this wonderful 
flight with me today. If you did, please be sure   to click that like button and subscribe with 
notifications on so you don’t miss my weekly   flight and resort reviews. I’ll see you next time 
for my final installment from Punta Cana for a   video that I honestly didn’t want to 
make which sounded really tempting to   watch. You’ll understand when you see. As 
always, thanks for watching until the end.

reviews.transcript_full: [Music] Welcome back. In this video, we're stepping on board LAM Airlines in their new business class seat on a Boeing 767300 ER on our way from Lima, Peru to Atlanta in the USA. How does LATAM and this business class product stack up against other options? And is it worth flying? Stick with us and find out. Join us as we get on board one of the last 767s ever built in LATAM's newest business class product and embark from the brand new terminal at Jorge Chavez International Airport. [Music] Welcome to Travel at Random. We're Trevor and Ryan. This channel started out of a love of travel. We're here to share unbiased and self-funded trip reports, hotel and flight reviews, and travel advice. We hope we inspire your next getaway. Check out our playlist in the description and browse the channel. If you enjoy this video, please hit that like button and subscribe to keep up with our latest content. Thank you for watching. Now, let's fly. [Music] We're starting off today at Jorge Chavez International Airport in Lima, Peru. Serving about 23 million passengers annually. The airport recently completed construction of a brand new terminal which opened on the 1st of June 2025. While the new terminal is open, it's not exactly finished yet. If you've never been to Lima, one thing to know is that the traffic is terrible. This city of more than 11 million people has very limited mass transit and lacks major highways. The new airport terminal is not currently connected to public transit and traffic is routed over two temporary bridges. Traffic can be slow and congested, particularly at peak times. We had given ourselves plenty of time, but it still took about 90 minutes from our hotel in Mirror Flores to get to the terminal at 9:00 a.m. on a weekday. In fact, we were sitting for so long that Uber sent us a message to make sure we were okay. Once we made it to the terminal, things improved. Check-in is located on the upper level with LATAM on the far right side of the terminal. LAM Airlines has a premium check-in area at counters A11 through A15. There is a separate check-in room just past the counters for top tier status holders, including Delta Diamond, Platinum, and LATAM Platinum members. There are check-in lanes for Delta Silver, Gold, LATAM Gold, Gold Plus, and a separate queue for business class passengers. There are four concourses at the airport. the domestic B concourse on the lower level and three international concourses A, C, and D on the third level with check-in. Since this terminal is brand new, currently the only airside lounge is the club Lima. LOM is opening its own club in August of 2025, so we missed it by just a few weeks. The lounges are accessible to international passengers only. Priority Pass is accepted at the club or you can purchase a pass at reception for $55. This is the newest and largest The Club location at almost 20,000 square ft. It has the capacity for more than 450 guests and is designed to provide options for travelers of all kinds. It features relaxation areas, private meeting rooms, and an enclosed player area for children. The club is decorated with local Peruvian artwork and greenery. There are two small buffets on either side of the central bar. There are also drink stations at each buffet. We were in the club for breakfast and the options were basic. The buffet closer to check-in had more options available. There are showers in this lounge and you can reserve them with QR codes on each table. Wi-Fi was available. The speeds were pretty good. The club was comfortable and had plenty of space. It felt open and spacious, and we didn't have any trouble finding a seat. One note, our LATAM business class ticket did not get us entry, and the LATAM check-in agents did not even mention a lounge when we dropped off our bags. Our 7-hour flight today takes us a little over 3,000 m from Lima, Peru to Atlanta, Georgia in LAM Airlines premium business class cabin. LAM is in the process of refitting their planes with new interiors. The 767s, trip 7s, and some 787900s have these new business class seats. They are currently also deploying a new business class suite on their 787800s that feature a door. Lat's boarding process was a bit chaotic, and we started an hour before departure. Boarding for premium cabins is zone one and includes both business and premium economy passengers. There are only three zones in total. Everyone had to have their carry-on items searched prior to boarding, and they held us on the jet bridge for another 5 minutes before we were allowed to board. Boarding for all passengers was at the front of the plane, leading to a lot of foot traffic and liloos in the business class cabin. We saw several economy passengers stowing their bags in the business class overhead bins, and the flight attendants didn't seem to care. This is a Boeing 767300 ER with 20 business class seats and 213 economy seats. This aircraft also features 39 LATAM plus seats which feature additional legroom. The business class seats are arranged in a 1 121 staggered layout and all seats have direct aisle access. We are in seats 3A and 5A today which are the window seats closest to the windows. Even rows are closer to the aisle. Each seat has a 16-in touchscreen, USBA, and universal power plugs. The universal power plugs didn't get turned on on our flight, or they weren't working, unfortunately. The seat has a decent amount of storage space. There's a small closing compartment below an open area to the side of the seat. A goodiz counter with a real stone surface. [Music] The seat surface uses three-dimensional textiles to help improve air flow and temperature. The seat was a bit narrow, and I found that I often hit the seat controls with my elbow, causing my seat to move unintentionally. The seat has a pitch of 45 in and a width of 19 1/2 in and recines to a fully lay flat. As a bed, the seat was comfortable. I think more comfortable than as a seat where it was a little too flat and didn't have much lumbar support. The footwell was a bit tight, but as long as you lay on your back, Trevor found it comfortable, and it was long enough for him to lay completely down, even at 6'4 in. When in bed mode, it is a little difficult getting in and out of the seat. That's one of the problems with the 767. The cabin is narrower than newer aircraft models, so the seats tend to be a little tighter. There were accent lights above the literature holder and storage area and you can control their light level. There's also a reading light which you can adjust the brightness on. Waiting at our seats was a mattress topper, duvet and pillow. The linens were good quality, the pillow a decent size and the duvet was quite large also welcome. The amenity kits are eco-friendly and focus on sustainable materials throughout. The bags feature designs from South American artists. Inside the kit features a bamboo toothbrush, eye mask, socks, earplugs, a refreshening towel, lip balm, and hand cream. Push back was prompt, but the taxi and wait to depart took about 20 minutes. We took off to the south and quickly escaped the cloud cover. [Music] On board, the in-flight entertainment system is called LATAM Play. With over 300 movies and a thousand TV episodes, there's a decent selection available, and the system was responsive. There were also music and games available and a flight tracker. This aircraft did not have Wi-Fi. Some LATAM 767s have it installed and they're working to install Wi-Fi across the fleet. No pre-eparture drinks were offered, but they did take our meal orders on the ground. On this flight, there was a lunch service and a hot snack service just before landing. Just after takeoff, mixed nuts and sparkling wine were served. LATM has refocused their onboard dining experience recently and now provides Latin American focused meals with a focus on the local flavors of the departure point. For lunch, we both ordered the Amazonian shufa, which is a fried rice dish, and Luca mimoose for dessert. The starter was a take on a kowsa, a traditional Peruvian potato dish, although a bit deconstructed. The shrimp were fine, a little tough, but fine. Overall, this dish lacked flavor. The salad was literally three leaves of lettuce and a basic vinegarette. I guess it counts as a salad, but it could have just been a garnish at that point. The starter was fine, not great, not bad. The main dish was their signature dish from a local chef, Ilia Garcia, and it was great. It was flavorful, and anything with plantains is always a plus to us. The Luca Mimoose was light with some tart mango fruit bits on top and then cookie crumbles on the bottom. It was good, but the mango on top was what made this. Overall, the lunch was good. We're glad to see local flavors on board. And while the starter wasn't anything special, we did enjoy the rice dish. About 70 minutes before arrival, a snack service was served. It was a sandwich and a dessert. Trevor ordered the lentil burger and dol de leche pudding and a Coke Zero. I skipped the snack. Trevor said the sandwich was pretty good and had mozzarella, lettuce, and tomato on top of a lentil patty. It was served with potato chips and an ioli. The pudding was very light with a few cookie bits on top and fresh blueberries. Overall, the dish was decent and more than some carriers will offer on a flight of this length. For comparison, we flew Delta down to Peru and there was no second meal or snack service offered in business class. We arrived into Atlanta around 8:00 p.m. This was a completely daytime flight. [Music] Evenings are a bit busy at ATL, but we got a good sunset view as we taxi to our gate in the F concourse. [Music] We found this flight to be comfortable. I slept a good chunk of this flight since I wasn't feeling great. I found the bed to be long enough and the footwell decent, although I found it more comfortable to sleep on my side than my back due to the contours of the seat. Trevor felt like he could have slept, but it wouldn't have been the best sleep due to the space restrictions around his shoulders and legs. The service was good, the food was enjoyable, and had a unique flare to it. The flight attendants were present throughout the flight and were personable and friendly during service. I think this product is fine for a mediumh hall flight. We got a great fair for our trip and had a good experience. Would we fly LAM again? I'd say absolutely for a mediumh hall flight like this one. Our biggest complaint about service was the fairly indifferent LATAM ground staff in Lima. Once on board, the flight attendants were friendly. One important thing to note is that we booked this trip through Delta. Latam has a joint venture with Delta. And while LATAM is not part of the Sky Team Alliance, Delta medallions get many perks and benefits with LATAM. This includes priority boarding, check-in, etc. We also earn Delta miles and elite MQDs on this flight. Have you flown Latam? Let us know in the comments what you think of this airline. And don't forget to hit that like button and subscribe to keep up with our latest travels. Thank you for watching. We'll see you on the next adventure. [Music]

reviews.transcript_full: We flew from Miami to Lima, Peru on the Tom Premium Economy, also called the Tom Plus on a Boeing 767-300.  So was it worth it?  Yes, it was worth paying extra compared to regular economy.  We appreciated the additional legroom, priority boarding, and being able to sit towards the front to get off the plane earlier.  Because the sooner you get on the airport immigration line in Lima, the better.  We'll show you the food, legroom, your reserved overhead bin space, entertainment options, and more.  We'll also reveal the secret to booking these seats at a lower price.  We're Scott and Metty. We slow travel the world while making money online.  Coming up, we'll also show you which rows are stinky because of the bathrooms and what I didn't like about the seats.  La Tom Premium Economy, Check-in, and Security.  We packed light for our two-week trip to Peru, so we didn't have to check a bag.  And here's how we got the cheapest price for our La Tom Premium Economy seats.  We booked the light fair option round trip.  It's the cheapest and doesn't include checked bags.  When it gave us the option to choose our seats, that's when we selected La Tom Plus seats, which are located in premium economy.  These seats cost extra and that's how we got the benefits of the extended legroom,  exclusive overhead bin space, premium boarding, a better meal, and getting off the plane faster.  As for security, we didn't get any special treatment in Miami,  but we already have TSA pre-check so that helped.  Boarding.  La Tom split boarding into two main sections,  general boarding and premium.  With your premium economy ticket, you can get on the plane before most other passengers.  We were assigned group three.  I hate waiting in lines, so this was a relief.  Personally, I'd rather board last, so I don't have to sit on the plane any longer than I have to.  But the issue is storing our carry on bags.  This is where premium economy might be worth it for you.  You get an exclusive overhead storage bin that's only for you.  La Tom did not wear carry on bags or make us put them in the size.  But coming up, we'll explain why you might not want to bring an oversized carry on.  Seating layout.  The seating layout on this Boeing 767-300 was the same in both premium economy and economy.  It was three seats in the middle of the plane and two seats together nearest the windows.  We sat in seats 14J and 14L.  We were in premium economy, but if you're flying regular economy, we strongly recommend against  sitting in rows 1920 or 21.  It smelled like fart.  Yes, the bathrooms are at row 20 on either side.  Seat and legroom.  This is the main reason we upgraded to La Tom premium economy.  Regular economy is listed as having 31-32 inches of pitch.  I'm 6'2", and I find this pitch a bit tight for my legs, especially on longer flights.  La Tom premium economy is listed as 35 inches of pitch.  This was plenty of room to keep my legs stretched out,  but there is something I found a bit annoying with the legroom that Maddie actually liked.  There's a metal footrest that you can swing up or down.  I'm 5'8", and for me, keeping my feet on it was comfortable.  But I found that when I folded the footrest up, it pushed against my legs a bit.  Not a deal breaker at all, but not great for taller people.  Another thing about the legroom.  If you sit in the outside rows, there's no divider on the floor between the seats.  This was totally fine for us as a couple, but you might not like that if you're seated next to a  stranger. The seat is listed as 18 inches wide, which is the same as regular economy.  The seats looked a bit dated, but they were comfortable enough for our 5.5 hour flight to Peru.  You can adjust the headrest up and down to match the length of your neck.  The seats were climbed pretty far back. It's almost like laying down,  so that's good if you want to nap.  Or you can stay upright and awake and complain how the person in front of you is cramping all your  space. To prevent that, we recommend row 11 in the middle seats or row 12 on the outer rows to  get the premium economy bulkhead where no one can recline into your lap.  You also get a pillow and blanket.  We put these behind our backs to use as lumbar support, and it worked great.  Eventually, I used the blanket to cover up because it got pretty gold on the flight.  One unusual thing is there is no air nozzle above, but we didn't need it anyhow.  Storage space.  With your Latum premium economy ticket, you get access to exclusive overhead storage.  In our exclusive bin, we were able to keep our two carry-on suitcases and one backpack.  Yeah, the overhead bins are kind of tight, so stick to the baggage size restrictions or your bag  may not fit. In-flight entertainment and Wi-Fi.  The in-flight entertainment included over 300 movies, 1000 TV series episodes, and video games.  And you got to watch Bridget Jones' Marries Dr. McTremey.  You mean Bridget Jones' baby?  We do recommend bringing your own wired headphones.  Latum's headphones look like they're from the 1980s and sound like they're from the 1880s.  There's also a USB port. This was helpful for keeping our phones charged,  but the port was loose so it didn't work all the time.  We didn't use the Wi-Fi.  Streaming cost about $12 for the length of the flight.  However, Latum says that it's only available on flights within Brazil,  Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.  Food, meals, drinks.  Latum served complimentary wine, soda, juice, and water.  My Savian Blanc white wine was just okay.  My Coke Zero presented a deep obsidian hue with a vivacious cascade of carbonation.  The bouquet opened with a sharp effervescence, releasing caramelized sweetness,  and charred vanilla bean, forming a bold, mid-palad experience that ultimately made me have to pee.  We had two food options, chicken or pasta.  Both featured cheese, which I didn't want, so I chose the only non-cheese option which was to scrape it off.  I thought that food was all right, not amazing, but good enough.  Online, Latum said regular economy class would get sandwiches instead of this hot meal.  We were given wooden utensils, which is fantastic if you want to save the oceans,  but kill the trees, all while risking a splinter to the tongue.  The drinking food carts only came around once, and that was about an hour and a half  into a flight that left at 5 pm.  A couple of hours later, the flight attendants did come by offering only water.  Yeah, so I'm glad we brought bottled water and snacks with us on the plane.  Latum Premium Economy isn't worth it.  It was definitely worth it for us for the leg room because we were sitting on the plane for over six hours.  Plus, getting off the plane earlier meant we got in Peru's immigration line sooner.  Yeah, we stood in line for border control for about an hour.  It might not always be that slow, but that was our experience, so I'm glad we didn't have to wait even longer  because of getting off the plane later. reviews.transcript_full:
Welcome on this Air France Business Class
flight in an Airbus A330 from Paris to St Martin (Caribbean) The video features the full Air France Business Class
experience, from seating & meals to amenities & bedding This Air France Business Class video also includes
the A330’s landing at St Martin’s iconic Princess Juliana Airport Our journey starts at Charles de Gaulle Airport in Paris,
Europe's third busiest airport (after Istanbul and Heathrow)  Unfortunately, my Air France Business Class 'light' ticket does
not include access to the lounge for some pre-flight relaxation We’re taken by bus to the remote aircraft stand This is the Air France Airbus A330-200 that will
fly us to St Martin (aircraft registration number F-GZCN) Air France has 11 Airbus A330s in its
long-haul fleet with an average age of 22 years The Air France Business Class on the Airbus A330
features 36 seats spread over six rows in a 2-2-2 layout There are two Business Class cabins: a front cabin
with 24 seats (4 rows) and a rear cabin with 12 seats (2 rows) The Air France A330 Business Class cabin has a sleek look 4A is my seat for the 9 hour flight to St Martin Air France installed Equinox 2D Business Class
seats by Stelia Aerospace on its Airbus A330 fleet The Air France Business Class seat on the A330
has a pitch of 78 inch (198 cm) and a width of 22 inch (56 cm) A retractable screen provides privacy between seats I’ll take a detailed tour of the 
Air France Business Class seat after takeoff A hot towel is provided to refresh a little Air France’s safety video is an elegant and stylish movie We’re leaving the aircraft stand at 10 am (on-time departure) Air France’s A330s are powered by General Electric engines  Air France’s A330-200s are being replaced
by the next-generation and larger Airbus A350-900s Let’s have a look at the Air France A330 Business Class seat Each Business Class seat features a large TV screen,
with a storage cabinet and footrest underneath  Directly next to to the seat’s head rest is a small
cubby for storing headphones, water and small items The power plug and passenger service unit
(remote control for IFE) are within easy reach The arm rest houses a large tray table Let's have a look at the Air France Business Class amenities The Air France Business Class kit contains the following items:
a dental kit, earplugs, eye mask, socks, and Clarins cosmetics A soft microfiber pillow and a warm blanket
are offered to all Business Class passengers All Air France's Business Class passengers get slippers Air France branded noise-cancelling headphones are provided  One hour into the flight, we're leaving Europe behind us
and will now fly over the Atlantic Ocean for the next 8 hours  I am a very nervous flyer, especially over the ocean Are you also scared of flying over the ocean? Leave a comment As we start the Atlantic crossing, the Air France crew
hands out the Business Class menus for the inflight meals Appetizer: cream of smoked sweetcorn soup,
girolle mushrooms and toasted buckwheat Air France also serves its Business Class passengers
crepes fourrées (stuffed pancakes) during the aperitif Starter: Camargue red rice, sweet potato,
and rainbow trout salad with raspberry vinaigrette Main course: beef chuck, peanut sauce, celery, Taggiasca olives Mustard in grains from the prestigious moutardier 
Edmond Fallot in Dijon is served with the beef  Cantal, Fourme d’Ambert, & Chabichou du Poitou cheeses Dessert: crispy hazelnut and caramel cake Air France's Airbus A330 is equipped with
two lavatories for the 36 Business Class passengers The Air France Business Class seat on the A330 can be
reclined into a fully flat bed with a lenght of 197 cm (77 inches)   Have you ever flown in Air France Business Class?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment Air France’s inflight entertainment system
offers a wide variety of movies, shows, music and games Snacks & drinks are available in the galley during the flight A light meal is served 90 minutes prior to landing Smoked salmon, tangy creamy sauce, 
pearl pasta with vegetables, and orange & pink grapefruit The Air France A330 pilot addresses
the passengers as we are approaching St Martin’s airspace There's a lot of traffic at St Martin airport, and we
have to circle for 30 minutes before starting our descend  We get some great views of the Caribbean during the descent St Martin has one of the world’s most scenic airport landings Maho Beach on St Martin is famous for being
next to the international airport, right at the end of the runway Thanks for flying with me in Air France Business Class Don't forget to like, comment,
and subscribe for more flight reviews!

reviews.transcript_full:
This video features a spectacular seaplane flight in the Maldives Enjoy the Maldives seaplane flight and the magnificent views! The destination of the flight is Soneva Secret,
the Maldives' newest ultra-luxury resort Welcome to Male International Airport in the Maldives, where
Soneva hosts meet guests who arrive by international flight The Soneva hosts also assist guests with the check-in
at the airport counters to secure seaplane boarding passes The Maldives has two seaplane operators: 
Manta Air and TMA (Trans Maldivian AIrways) Next, guest are transferred to the seaplane terminal by a Tesla The drive to the seaplane terminal takes only 5 minutes The new seaplane terminal was inaugurated in October 2022 At the seaplane terminal, Soneva operates its own
lounge, where guests can wait for their flight to the resort The lounge’s interior reflects Soneva's signature eco-design Snacks (cheese, chocolates & ice-cream) and beverages
are served, and complimentary WiFi is provided The lounge also features a play room for children The lounge features a large outdoor terrace, with views of the
seaplane docks, which is the world's largest seaplane terminal Prior to boarding, passengers are escorted 
to a small room, where a safety video is played Soneva has its own fleet of luxurious seaplanes Maintained and operated by Manta Air,
the Soneva seaplanes offer a superior travel experience The Soneva seaplanes have only has 8 seats
(for comparison, a regular seaplane features 16 seats) Aboard the plane, leather interiors welcome passengers Twin Otter seaplanes have short take-off and landing abilities They have a range of 886 mi (1425 km)
and a cruise speed of 173 mi (270 km) per hour Have you ever flown onboard a seaplane in the Maldives?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment Flight time from Male to Soneva Secret is 75 minutes
(a stop-over is made at Soneva Fushi along the way) All pilots in the Maldives are commercially trained and
they fly the plane with bare feet or flipflops (so cool!) A seaplane flight in the Maldives is a breathtaking journey
as it offers some of the most incredible views in the world The first part of the flight crosses the North Male Atoll - home to
the airport and capital city Male - which consists of 50 islands The first hotel in the Maldives opened
in the North Male Atoll in 1972 and had only 30 rooms The seaplane is flying over the famous One&Only Reethi Rah
Resort, located on the outer edge of the North Male Atoll We're making a stop-over at Soneva Fushi to drop some guests Soneva Fushi is regarded as the first luxury hotel in the
Maldives, setting of the trend of luxury holidays in the nation Opened in 1995, Soneva Fushi is still one of the Maldives' best 
resorts, blending ultra-luxury with environmental responsibility Welcome to Soneva Fushi International Airport,
probably the tiniest airport in the world The stop-over at Soneva Fushi takes only 5 minutes The plane takes off at short distance from the resort
as not to disturb the guests on the island Here we go again ... We get a spectacular view of Soneva Fushi after takeoff Soneva Fushi is located in the Baa Atoll,
a designated UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve The Baa Atoll is home to 1200 fish species, including manta
rays, sharks, and an abundance of sea turtles and dolphins The Baa Atoll consists of 75 islands of which
13 are inhabited with a population of over 11,000 people Two luxury resorts can be seen in the distance:
Anantara Kihavah Villas and Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru As the seaplane leaves the Baa Atoll, the Maldives' 
next atoll - the Raa Atoll - comes into view Surfers and sailors flock to Raa Atoll
for its excellent surf spots and idyllic sailing routes We get a nice view of Joali Being Resort from the air This is Joali Maldives, the sister resort of Joali Being We're leaving the Raa Atoll and now head towards the
Haa Dhaalu Atoll, the most remote atoll in the Maldives We get our first glimpse of Soneva Secret,
the Maldives' most exclusive resort Soneva Secret is located in the bluest lagoon I've ever seen The only resort in the Haa Dhaalu Atoll, Soneva Secret is set on
Dhipparufushi Island at the westernmost tip of the Maldives Soneva Secret features only 14 water & island villas; each villa
comes with a dedicated team of three (including a butler & chef) This is how the landing looks like from the cockpit ... From the landing site, it's 5 min by speedboat to the resort The resort staff is waiting for us on the beach 
(it feels like a scene from the White Lotus, only the real version)

reviews.transcript_full: Over the years, few airlines have fascinated me as much as China's Junyao Air.  It's not a widely known airline, but I think it should be, especially when you're  into aviation because there are so many interesting things about them.  For example, they are currently the only so-called Star Alliance connecting partner, meaning  they are not a full member of the alliance but work closely with them by offering connecting  at Tineraries and let Star Alliance frequent flyer status holders enjoy their benefits on  Junyao Air flights as well.  And the airline isn't even that small.  Despite only commencing operation in 2006, the airline has already grown to more than 100  planes, including a fleet of 9 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners sporting one of five unique colorful  liverys.  These are some of the most stunning paint jobs you'll find on any Dreamliner if you  ask me.  And with their three digit number of aircraft, Junyao is amongst the largest airlines in the  world to have started operation in this century.  They mostly focus on domestic routes, primarily from airports in the Yangtze Delta region,  from which they also operate a small number of long-haul routes.  As of March 2025, they connect Shanghai Pudong with Helsinki, Manchester, Brussels, Athens,  Melbourne and Sydney, as well as fly from Henan Province's capital Changzhou to Helsinki  and Milan, Malpenser.  Today I'm very excited to bring you along a flight aboard Junyao Air and share more  of the airline's unique intricacies as well as dive into the intriguing contrasts of  domestic air travel within China on our journey from Shanghai Hong Xiaotang to Shenzhen.  I'm glad you're joining me on this trip, so without further ado, let's get going.  Ibeation geeks and frequent flyers welcome to this new episode of our Flight Review series  Brutally Honest.  I'm just about to leave my hotel here in Shanghai and make my way over to Hong Xiaotang  International Airport.  The city of Shanghai is served by two airports, the older original one being Hong Xiaotang  in the city's west, and right before the turn of the millennium, Pudong International Airport  was inaugurated, which now serves as the main international gateway to the region and has  surpassed Hong Xiaotang's size.  Due to its proximity to the city center, Hong Xiaotang Airport mainly caters to domestic  flights these days, as well as a handful of cross-border short-haul flights to other inner  city airports like Taipei Songshan, Seoul Gimpo, and Tokyo Haneda.  This early in the morning, taking a cab from the Bund takes only half an hour and costs  around 80 yuan or roughly 10 euros.  Usually, I would take the subway, which also wouldn't be an issue for a 730AM domestic  departure, but when booking this flight, there was no way to reserve a seat.  I appreciate my 150 USD ticket, including a 20kg checked bag, but I would have also been  willing to pay a few bucks to ensure I would be getting a window seat.  Even emailing their customer service to no avail as their inbox was full.  So my last resort is going to the airport as early as possible in the hope I'm able  to snag one of the remaining window seats at check-in.  There might be a possibility to do it online and Mandarin, but even with translation apps,  I wasn't able to figure it out, and neither in their own app nor on platforms like WeChat,  which sometimes are the key to getting what you want in journeys in China.  First, we're passing a brief security check followed by us being allowed into the check-in  area.  Junyao staff gave all of us waiting in line already about and then opened the check-in  desks perfectly on time.  And we got our window seat.  Personally, there are many things I love about Chinese airports.  They are usually pretty efficient and reliable, despite the masses of people.  I also appreciate how well connected to public transit they are.  Junyao is a particularly great example as it is not only connected to three different  metro lines, which also connect to Pudong Airport directly, but also one of the main high-speed  railway stations of Shanghai.  Although saying it's connected is somewhat incorrect, as the train station and terminal  two were built as one super-sized intermodal transportation hub which opened in 2010.  Naturally being a nerd for air travel and transportation in general also means I take  a deep interest in urban planning, and this is a text book implementation of intermodality.  And the Chinese are, rightfully so, proud of that, displaying this super-fascinating 3D  model of the terminal complex at the Shanghai Urban Planning Exhibition Center, an interesting  museum about how Shanghai is designed and works.  Connecting high-speed intercity rail lines with major airports is something that needs  a bigger focus in the future.  There are many examples of where this makes travel easier already, such as in Amsterdam  and Frankfurt.  Both airports that arguably wouldn't have gotten as big as they are had they not been that  well connected within their respective countries.  Another aspect that Chinese airports generally do well in is the plentiful availability of  lounges, which are often accessible with lounge access programs such as priority pass or  with premium credit cards.  Just look at how many different ones there are.  Thanks to my credit card I was allowed into the Juniao Air Lounge, despite traveling in  an economy class.  It's a chic space with elegant, French-inspired interior in the airlines' distinct color scheme.  The lounge offers a self-service buffet with a variety of hot and cold beverages and a scrumptious  food selection with local staples like T-eggs, Malai Gal, Golden Fried Rice and Yo-Tiao.  Let's inhale this gorgeous breakfast and then make our way to the gate.  Cross Hong-Tiao Airport you'll find a large variety of western brands, which I didn't  expect as it mainly serves domestic routes.  There's a Starbucks now, which is a local iteration of Starbucks exclusively offering  products to go mainly through mobile ordering so the brand can compete more effectively against  local rivals such as Lucan Coffee.  There's also a Shake Shack, a Hardies and a Lulu Lemon, as well as a Japanese Ramen  chain, and a relay, a type of convenience store you really only see across European train  stations, which for me as a European seems amusingly out of place at a Chinese airport.  The Dreamliner down there will take us to Shenzhen today.  Registered Bravo 20 Delta Tango, this Boeing 787-9 is the 100th Boeing 787 to operate in China,  which is commemorated by a decal at the front of the aircraft.  It was delivered to Jun-Yao Air in 2019 and wears a delivering featuring Chinese Pienese,  which is known as the King of Flowers in China.  What's unique about the boarding passes on some Chinese airlines is that they tear on  both sides.  That's so the staff can confirm your presence at the check-in counter and again at the  plane which is usually only done when buses and remote stands are involved.  You can see my ticket having been torn on this side, but I still have another terrible  slip on the other side remaining.  Entering the plane through door 2, the business class cabin is to our left, which consists  of 29 121 configured Thompson Vantage XL seats.  We're back here in Economy Class though, where 295 Recaro CL3710 seats are fitted in  the Dreamliner's Classic 3333 configuration.  Waiting for us on the seat already is a pillow with a soft reusable cover.  The headrests of each seat are adjustable in three ways on the sides, vertically, as  well as down here for some extra next one.  With my height of 180 cm, the legroom is phenomenal, also for a long-haul flight, but  especially so for a 2 hour domestic flight like this one.  Above a standard seat back pocket is a bifold tray table and a high literature pocket  a signature element of many Recaro seats.  Universal power ports are not installed, but you will find a USB-A port at the bottom  of the entertainment screen.  The port hooks are offered too.  There is a notable amount of advertising around the cabin, including the C-through stickers  at the bottom of the windows promoting their new road from Chunchaw to Milan, as well as  large stickers on the over-at-binds. reviews.title: Flying on a WWII-Era DC-3! A Historic Day Trip from Melbourne to King Island
reviews.transcript_excerpt: The one-hour flight passed quickly, this was certainly a unique, once-in-a-lifetime experience.…

captions.text: The one-hour flight passed quickly, this was certainly a unique, once-in-a-lifetime experience.

chapters.title: Currie Boathouse (The Restaurant with No Food)

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Melbourne! Today, I'm taking a flight like no other, I'll be flying on an 81-year-old DC-3 to King Island. Built in 1945 during World War II, this aircraft is truly a piece of living history. I can't wait to get on board and learn about its story. Let's go! My DC-3 flight departs from Essendon Fields Airport. From 1921 to 1970, Essendon was Melbourne's main airport and played a key role during the 1956 Olympic Games. Suburban expansion prevented the airport from expanding, so Tullamarine was constructed and has since become Melbourne's main international gateway. Today, Sharp Airlines is the only airline that operates scheduled passenger flights from Essendon Airport. The DC-3 is owned by Shortstop Jet Charter, one of many charter operators based at Essendon. This flight isn't a scheduled commuter service but is sold as part of a day tour to King Island. Check-in took place at their hangar 30 minutes before departure. We received our seat assignments and were then invited to relax with a cup of tea in the lounge or enjoy a glass of champagne or orange juice in the hangar. Here, you can see the company's Falcon 900C business jet and, in the distance, our legendary DC-3. The Douglas DC-3 was developed in 1935, just 32 years after Orville Wright made the world's first powered flight. Before World War II, it revolutionised air travel by establishing longer routes previously unreachable by its predecessors and became one of the first airliners capable of operating profitably without mail subsidies. It was affectionately nicknamed the "Gooney Bird" due to its resemblance to the albatross, a large seabird known for its long wings and effortless gliding ability. This particular aircraft was among the last ones produced. Delivered as a C-47, the military version of the DC-3, to the Royal Australian Air Force in 1945, it was purchased by Shortstop Jet Charter in the late 1980s. While the airframe is quite old, the interior has been refurbished. There are 28 passenger seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration. I was allocated a window seat in row 3. As the DC-3 has a small tail wheel at the back, boarding requires a short uphill walk to the front. The seats, sourced from a former Airbus A300, are quite comfortable and have plenty of legroom. This aircraft is powered by two Pratt & Whitney twin-row Wasp piston engines, each with fourteen cylinders and generating 1,200 horsepower. The DC-3 can take off and land on dirt runways and has a low stall speed of around 125 km/h. It felt like we lifted off the ground in just a few seconds. The flight to King Island takes about one hour. We will fly past the Westgate Bridge, over Port Phillip Bay, and across the Bass Strait. This flight operates on selected Sundays throughout the year, and as of January 2025, the cost is $697 per person. The price includes return flights on the DC-3, lunch, and a tour of King Island. For an additional $75, you can ride in the jump seat with the pilots during either takeoff or landing. Apart from trips to King Island, this aircraft is also used for day excursions to wine regions, 45-minute joy flights over Melbourne, and evening cocktail flights. The back section of the plane has been converted into a lounge area, where passengers can relax, chat, and take in the views through the large rectangular windows. I was pleasantly surprised to find a toilet onboard, and it's very spacious. Back at my seat, I was offered a snack pack and a drink. The DC-3 does not have a pressurised cabin or air-conditioning, it flies much lower than modern jets. As such, for passenger comfort, flights are often cancelled, typically when the temperature exceeds 25 degrees Celsius or the wind surpasses 25 km/h. In the event of a cancellation, you can request a refund or be rebooked for a future date. The one-hour flight passed quickly, this was certainly a unique, once-in-a-lifetime experience. About 20 minutes before landing, I was escorted to the cockpit for my pre-booked jump seat into King Island Airport. Watching the pilots land an aircraft from inside the cockpit had always been a dream of mine, and sitting in the legendary DC-3 made it even more special. I was given a headset, which allowed me to hear the pilots' communications with Air Traffic Control. King Island Airport is regularly served by Rex Airlines, King Island Airlines, and Sharp Airlines, connecting the island with Melbourne and a few other Tasmanian destinations. A bus was already waiting outside the terminal to take us to lunch and the attractions. During the ride, the driver provided a brief yet informative commentary about this Island and its largest settlement: Currie. For lunch, we were taken to the King Island Hotel. The meal was included in our tour, and we were given several options for entrées, mains, and desserts. The hotel had set aside a dedicated area for our group, with each family assigned their own table. Since I was travelling alone, I had a table to myself. To start, I ordered the chilli plum prawns served with steamed rice. The sweet and sour plum sauce complemented the rice beautifully, creating a delightful contrast of flavours. For the main course, I chose the steak with gravy. The portion was generous, and the steak, cooked to a perfect medium as requested, was exactly to my liking. To finish, I chose the panna cotta of the day, which had a rich and creamy texture with a refreshing strawberry flavour. Overall, I was thoroughly impressed with the quality of the meal. Each dish was prepared with care, and everything was absolutely delicious. The lunch took up half of our time on the island. Now, we are taking a scenic route to Currie Harbour, where we enjoyed a short walk along the beach and came across a beautifully decorated boathouse. This small building, overlooking the harbour, is dubbed 'the restaurant with no food.' The place is furnished with an assortment of colourful dining tables and chairs. The only thing missing is the food. You can bring your own, and enjoy the company of friends and family.  Furthermore, the paintings on the walls, books on the tables, and nearly every collectible in the house are for sale. Just leave the money in the honest box or pay ID the owner, and you can take an artwork or two as souvenirs. The harbour at Currie is small, but it holds significant importance as the only safe haven for boats on the storm-battered west coast. Currie Wharf was King Island's major port for over 100 years until Grassy Harbour was constructed in 1972. Before heading back to the airport, we made one final stop - the highlight of the day and a key reason for many people to book this tour: the King Island Dairy. Established in 1923, this dairy has earned an international reputation for producing exceptional specialty cheeses, including award-winning varieties of blue, cheddar, brie, and camembert. Upon arrival, we were welcomed into their tasting room, where a tasting plate featuring six of their most iconic cheeses awaited us. Each cheese was a masterpiece, and I can confidently say they were some of the finest I've ever tasted. Sadly, the future of this iconic dairy is uncertain. Saputo, a Canadian multinational company that acquired the diary in 2019, announced in September 2024 its decision to close it by mid-2025 after failing to find a buyer. The closure will mark the end of an era for King Island, taking with it over a century of cheese-making excellence. It would be a heartbreaking loss for the local community, the dairy industry, and cheese lovers around Australia. And just like that, our enjoyable time on King Island has come to an end. One of the greatest perks of a charter flight is the convenience—once everyone is onboard, we're ready for takeoff! An hour later, we're already over Melbourne. Essendon Airport's proximity to the city means passengers on the right side of the plane are treated to stunning views of the CBD during landing. To conclude, what an incredible day out!  I think $697 for two flights and a guided tour of King Island is excellent value. Everything was well-organised, the flights were smooth, and the staff were exceptionally friendly. Considering the cost of maintaining this historic aircraft and its age, it's hard to say how much longer the DC-3 will continue flying. If you're an aviation enthusiast, this experience should definitely be on your bucket list. Thank you so much for watching. If you find this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews. See you all in my next video!

yt_comments.text: We flew Chicago to Frankfort and back route in Jan 2024. Both legs were on the 747-800 and we were upstairs in business for both flights. I found both flights to be enjoyable. The planes were clean, the staff was some of the best I've encountered and every meal and drink onboard was great. With all that said, I'm really looking forward to trying out the new cabin on the 800's once it is in place. If these flights were daytime flights I'd give them 9 out of 10 but, because they were at night, both my wife and I tried to get a little sleep. I'm 6ft tall and have broad shoulders. My wife is 5'9. We both felt the shoulder area of the seats when in the bed configuration was too narrow. She is a side sleeper and she found it very difficult to get comfortable. I tried to get comfortable but eventually gave up and put the seat back in the upright but reclined position and was able to get an hour or so of sleep. I found the IFE to be pretty good but the screens were dim even when adjusted to their max brightness and showing their age. I still watched several good movies during my flights but did wish for a better screen. Can't wait until they update the 800's cabin.

employs Safran's RAVE system, which you will also find
aboard their A330s and A340s, as well as on older twin-aisle airliners of their
subsidiaries Austrian, Brussels and Discover. Despite it's age, it offers a solid
selection of movies and TV shows, including multiple episodes of popular ones as well as games, the Kids section,
as well as music, audio books and podcasts. An in flight mapping application
is installed too. The headphones handed out in the beginning
are simple earbuds that get the job done. After a little nap, we're already
above North America, and before we start our descent into
Chicago, it's time for another snack. On this flight, Lufthansa offers
a vegetarian hot pocket, a simple yet tasty tomato-and-cheese calzone. Before landing they even handed out
hot towels, which is a nice gesture. And we've got another little piece of chocolate,
which shows a small change as well. This is still some of the old chocolate they've
been serving for a while, made by coppeneur, while the new ones, which are equal in weight, are made by Lindt and also come in a paper packaging. Over the years, Lufthansa was widely criticized
for an array of issues, and rightfully so. However, I personally believe it is time to
acknowledge just how much things have improved In the grand scheme of things, today's journey was superb! An on-time connecting flight, a fast
and efficient transit at Frankfurt, good legroom on the long haul flight,
high-quality amenities with a focus on reducing plastic waste, an overall good meal offering, a pleasant crew, and, considering how little I actually paid,
including a checked bag and a seat reservation for what essentially was a main season ticket,
a fantastic value for money! With the arrival of more modern aircraft, which will come with a new and improved in-flight entertainment system
and a bunch of new seat features, Lufthansa is slated to become one of
the better choices to cross the Atlantic with. And I'm here for it! WHEELS TOUCH DOWN With that, welcome to Chicago's
O'Hare International Airport! We're about to arrive at O'Hare's
Terminal 5, like all international flights, but it's important to note that
Lufthansa is one of three airlines whose international flights depart from Terminal 1, alongside United and ANA. Thank you again to Holzkern for sponsoring this video and check out their selection of watches, jewelery and accessories,
as Valentine's Day is coming up and Holzkern offers the perfect gifts,
plus free worldwide express shipping. Once again, also a very special thank you
to our channel members for supporting our work, through monthly financial contributions,
but whether you are a channel member, a subscriber or are simply stopping by for this
one video, thank you very much for watching! I'll see you again for a new video soon
and until then, safe travels!

yt_comments.text: You have to love the Japanese ground crew waving and bowing on push back etc....how Japanese...can you imagine that happening at Melbourne Airport...they would more than likely give you a 2 finger salute! Great to see Milkshake has a proper Business Class seat as well ! I agree with you Stef...the BEST in flight entertainment on any day light flight is out the window!! I have over the years never seen a bad review of Finnair....and often they have some great ROW fares as part of their Alliance ( I think with QF) in Australia.Some friends booked one of their ROW fares in Business and flew to Singapore with Qantas and then Finnair to Helsinki and onward to London and they said the Finnair flights were fantastic and this is prior to the A350 going into service! You have travelled at the right time of the year "welcome to sunny Helsinki"....probably would avoid the place in the winter months!!! Rain coming into Melbourne over the weekend apparently....hopefully will get some up here in Mansfield!! Fantastic stuff again Stef and I hope the delightful J and Milkshake enjoyed it as well!! Looking forward to the next episode!

yt_comments.author: @epapa737
yt_comments.text: I absolutely hate when airlines tell you to use your phone to watch movies, I'm not gonna drain my battery and rely on a ran through USB port

yt_comments.author: @jeffreyperkins9985
yt_comments.text: Removing seatback screens on domestic flights will also remove me from ever flying American again. I don't want to bring a laptop on a trip. Will stick with Delta going forward.

yt_comments.author: @Chris-st9mm
yt_comments.text: The issue, especially when I fly with American, is that half the time they either don't offer wifi or their wifi service isn't working. And I won't be holding my breath that this measure will result in cheaper airfare. And I've tried those device holders, they are awful they dont hold tablets and they snap down so hard it can hurt you. Ideally I'd still like some form of setback infotainment. Maybe a hybrid approach with a smaller screen to view your flight info, maybe food and snack options, and airport info while still emphasizing customers stream their own entertainment. But I can't remember the last time airlines have done anything for the good of the customer.

yt_comments.author: @christopherzy
yt_comments.text: Taking the American A319 soon here and yeah don’t care for IFE on it what so ever, but this definitely won’t bring airfare down one bit.

yt_comments.author: @CM73878
yt_comments.text: United is changing course. Since 2019, under CEO Scott Kirby, the airline announced its “United Next” program: all new narrowbody aircraft (like the 737 MAX and Airbus A321neo) will come with seat-back screens. • The reasoning: • Competing with Delta and JetBlue, which advertise seat-back screens as a premium experience.

yt_comments.author: @VinniChannel
yt_comments.text: US Airways management had some influence on this decision. The old AA plans were to have IFE on smaller aircraft like 737/A320 family. They have even received some aircraft on this configuration.

reviews.transcript_full:
While other US legacy carriers have sought 
to ensure inflight entertainment is present   on ALL their mainline aircraft, American 
Airlines has moved forward with more of an   austerity approach. Indeed, we’ve seen 
a reduction of seatback entertainment   across much of the fleet operating 
domestic services. Most recently,   the carrier opted to remove seatback screens from 
its A319s in its latest retrofit program. These   jets were the carrier's final short-to-medium 
haul aircraft equipped with the systems. It should go without saying that this 
move has been implemented to save costs. As you can guess, when compared to NO 
screens at all, inflight entertainment   systems cost money to install and upkeep, and 
licensing for the films and TV is not free. Furthermore, screens add additional weight,   thus contributing to greater fuel 
burn. From an operational perspective,   there’s a lot to lose by having the systems, 
and a lot to gain from removing them. American has begun retrofitting the 
cabins of over 30 legacy Airbus A319s.   This move is important because the 
legacy A319s were the last of the   carrier's short-to-medium-haul aircraft that 
were fitted with seatback entertainment. Thus, it won’t be long before American Airlines 
short and medium-haul passengers will lose all   hope of seatback entertainment. Of course, 
a notable exception occurs when widebody,   intercontinental jets are deployed domestically as 
a way to reposition for another long haul flight. There were 32 A319s received from 
2013 to 2015, with the airline's   other A319s having been inherited from 
US Airways and America West Airlines. The group of 32 are noteworthy as 
the only Sharklet-equipped A319s   that operate in the US. These will 
be American Airlines' first batch   of aircraft to be overhauled as part 
of its fleet retrofitting efforts. When it comes to the passenger experience, it will 
set American Airlines back from the competition,   as it will become the only US legacy carrier that   has no seatback entertainment on its 
short-to-medium-haul mainline aircraft.   Carriers like Delta and United have opted to 
continue seatback entertainment. These carrier   retrofits have focused on improving 
and installing seatback screens. It won't be a case of bringing a 
book or getting bored, however. As is a trend with some airlines, 
seatback entertainment will be   replaced by seatback device holders and 
passengers are able to stream content. This is available on smartphones,   tablets and laptops, although it may not 
work until the aircraft reaches 10,000 ft. There is also free Wi-Fi for T-Mobile customers   on certain plans, while connectivity 
can be accessed by others for a fee. To bring things full circle, American has 
taken a bet that customers won’t mind the   lack of seatback entertainment because they’ll 
choose the airline for other reasons - such as   connectivity to certain airports, or comfortable 
flight scheduling. IF this bet pays off,   then American will save money on acquiring, 
installing, and maintaining those screens.   And again, as mentioned, it will 
save on fuel with lighter aircraft. But what do YOU think of this 
decision by American? Is it a   move that will pay off? Or backfire? 
Let us know by leaving a comment.
