reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm taking you on one of the longest flights I've done recently, flying Qantas from Sydney to Dallas on the Airbus A380. This was a long haul economy flight, and a lot of people ask me about it, and I took notes the entire way, so I can give you guys an honest review. Okay, before we get started, this flight came right after a cruise around New Zealand. So, I boarded the flight well rested and really curious to see if Qantas actually lives up to its reputation. Qantas gets a lot of hype, at least that's what I'm seeing, especially when it comes to their A380. And by the end of this video, I'm going to share whether I think it is deserved, plus three important watch outs you're going to want to know before you book this exact flight. So, I want to know if you've ever flown Qantas before. Drop your experience down in the comments. I'd love to see if your Qantas flight lived up to the hype, too. This was a Qantas Airbus A380 800 flying nonstop from Sydney, Australia, to Dallas/Fort Worth. The flight time was 15 hours and 25 minutes, and we departed about 20 minutes late, around 2:30 in the afternoon. So, you guys, this aircraft is massive. It is a full two-level plane, and it was not at capacity, which definitely impacted the experience. So, before boarding, I stopped off quickly at the Qantas First Lounge. I have One World Emerald status through American Airlines Executive Platinum, and the lounge was outstanding. And I don't always get access to the first lounges, so this was a real treat for me. I had a lovely lunch there, and I even got a complimentary 20-minute foot massage, which felt like a total luxury before such a long flight. So, I want to know if you're kind of a lounge person. Do you hit the lounge before a long flight? Which one do you like to go to, or are you kind of a person that just goes straight to the gate? I'm curious which approach that you prefer. So, boarding took place at gate eight in Sydney and it was very organized and well staffed. So, Qantas boards by number and the lower level of the aircraft actually boarded first, which made the boarding process really smooth and efficient and I was in that first group cuz I was on the bottom floor of the aircraft. My seat was actually 52H. It's an aisle seat at the front of the economy cabin on the lower level one row behind the bulkhead and right behind first class and kind of the galley. So, I had this entire row to myself, which meant I could enjoy the window for takeoff and if I wanted to to stretch out to nap throughout the flight. You guys, so good. I thought about choosing the bulkhead, which is like the front row in economy, but ultimately I didn't do that because the armrest don't lift up and the seats feel kind of tight and if you get really lucky and there's nobody else there, you can't lay across at all. I'm going to come back to that later when we talk about some of the watch outs here, but I just wanted to mention that. So, what do you prefer on long haul flights? Are you front of economy? Are you bulkhead, back of the plane? Are you first class, business class? Let me know your go-to spot. I'm usually an economy girl, but I love to try to get as close to the front of that cabin if I can. So, I was seated just in front of the wing near the engines, but the takeoff and landing were so smooth. We had zero turbulence at all and you guys, honestly, the seat belt sign, I think, was off for almost the entire 15-hour flight and the cabin on this aircraft is extremely quiet, which I had read was the case. It was so nice not to hear that constant, really loud, reverberating engine noise. And like I mentioned, I had those two windows I could kind of see halfway out each one of them, which was really nice. The cabin temperature was a little bit warm while we were on the ground in Sydney, but about an hour into the flight it kind of cooled down a little bit and stayed more comfortable throughout. As I would walk back to the restrooms, I did know that the uh noticed that the cabin got a little bit cooler. So, as you were going towards the back of the temperature came down a little bit. Now, the cabin noise level was really low, like I said, exactly what you'd expect on an A380 out of the aircraft itself. And one of the biggest positives on this aircraft was the seat recline. You guys, look at this. I mean, this is excellent. It makes a huge difference on a long-haul flight. You can really get that seat back. Now, charging in the seats was a little bit tricky. My US plug actually worked to charge, and I was really glad I brought a long cable because the charger's kind of down low between the seats close to the floor. Now, I didn't even find the USB port in the armrest until the very end of the flight, but the USB charging did not work on my seat, and I heard a lot of people saying that it did not work in their seat. So, it is best to pack a traditional charging setup with like a cable and actual, you know, little hub thingy just in case. Let's talk about entertainment. The in-flight entertainment system was okay, but nothing really special. It's controlled with a remote and the touchscreen option is available, but it worked really inconsistently and with a noticeable delay. In fact, I noticed people banging on their touchscreens to get them to work, and that is really unpleasant for the person in front of you. It feels like a thumping banging sound. So, I think this aircraft needs a little bit of repair. And compared to my recent Japan Airlines flight, the screen quality felt really small and pretty poor. With that said, though, there was actually a good selection of content, including movies from HBO, Paramount. They had Australian films, music, and lots more. I watched a full two movies and appreciated the first-run selection. I saw a lot of people watching a lot of movies on this particular flight. There was also a moving map that showed airspeed, altitude, like time to destination, and even a sky cam view from above the aircraft, which was really, really cool. And the system also very clearly displayed meal and drink options with detailed choices, which was great. So, how do you entertain yourself when you're flying? Are you like a a movie person? Do you listen to music on your own device? Do you use the seatback, or do you just try to conk out? I'm kind of trying to see what's most popular here. Now, the restrooms were a little larger than average, especially compared to like American Airlines, but smaller, I'd say, than Japan Airlines, but they were not cleaned a single time during the 15-hour flight. Yeah, they replaced the toilet paper, but trash overflowed, the floor became literally sticky, like your feet would stick and unstick when you walked in there, and the overall cleanliness really declined throughout the flight. I just couldn't believe it. The service overall was professional, but it was kind of, I guess you could say, minimal. The crew did their jobs, but there was no explanation of like restroom locations if you're in this cabin or that. There was really no overview of how the self-serve snacks worked. The captain said something about it for like 1 second, and there just wasn't a lot of proactive communication. And if I'm being honest, some of the interactions came off as a little bit snobby. >> [gasps] >> But then some of the crew were warm and friendly, so it was kind of a mixed bag. People are people, it's just the way it is. Now, let's talk about the food. I had high expectations for this. On the way to New Zealand, I flew American Airlines from Dallas to Auckland, and the snack that they gave me at mid-flight, you guys, it was like a raw stromboli, like they'd forgot to bake it. It was like raw dough. So, my expectations for Qantas were kind of high because I thought, well, I mean, it's got to be better than this, right? So, here's how everything worked. About 30 minutes into the flight, we were handed a bottle of water, which was great. A lot of times you're thirsty and you don't want to wait forever, followed immediately by a snack and beverage service. A very early dinner was served around 3:45. I mean, that's early if you're thinking the flight just took off. The main options were pumpkin tortellini, a beef with mustard gravy, or cold chicken salad along with a selection of Australian wines. I chose the beef. It was served hot, but it was fatty, it was kind of bland, and the gravy tasted like cheap brown gravy, not like a mustard gravy. The meal came with bread and cheese and crackers, but there was no salad or fruit. They gave us a dessert of an ice cream bar, which was really delicious, but I don't know, I just wasn't in the mood for it. In hindsight, I probably would have selected the salad main cuz I saw it and it looked really nice and tasty and fresh. Had like edamame in there, looked really good. There were also some self-serve snacks and drinks toward the back of the plane, but it was really easy to miss that because they didn't talk much about it, and the drinks were like put away. If you didn't know, you wouldn't be able to grab them. Later in the flight, there was a snack walk-through around 8:00 p.m. It was a little chicken toasty. Oh, I'm sorry. The snack walk-through was just like little packaged snacks and some waters. And then around 10:00 p.m., we got a chicken toasty, which tasted great. It was served hot and not raw like my weird American Airlines strong bully. Then they had a full breakfast before landing at 3:30 in the morning with a choice of your main could be frittata or fruit. Everybody then also got a muffin, coffee, and a yogurt pod on the little plate. That was great. I'm sorry, the coffee would have been on request, but the the yogurt and the muffin were included. The breakfast was decent and hearty, and the yogurt was really, really good. I'd say the coffee, though, was really bad. It was watery, lukewarm, so I ended up having to grab a coffee when I landed in the airport to trick my body into thinking, "Okay, it's like morning time." So, for those of you out there who fly a lot, I want to know what is the best or worst economy meal that you have ever had on a flight. Share it below. I really love to read the flight food stories. Now, for those watch-outs about this flight specifically from Sydney to Dallas. First, I would not recommend boarding the flight super hungry. The food is fine, but it's not especially filling or exciting, and timing kind of matters on a flight this long, so I would bring some snacks. Second, be very, very cautious when you're booking bulkhead seats, the ones up at the very front of the economy cabin. The seats are narrower, remember those armrests don't lift, and there is a lot of foot traffic and galley noise cuz you're right by the galley a lot of times. Also, if you see baby icons on the seat map, book those nearby rows carefully. They have these pull-down bassinets and a lot of times toddlers, babies, families are traditionally seated here. And in my experience, because these families sometimes will congregate here and sit here, the extra space in front of them means the kids are going to roam about, run about, and that can happen. On the flip side, if you are traveling with kids or as a family, this can be a great place for you to sit as long as you understand the front row armrests don't move, and your little ones cannot nap. I saw a family with a baby moving from the bulkhead to an empty row behind them because they couldn't let their baby nap. So, just something for you to be aware of. And this again has happened multiple times on my flights where the little ones are up front. So, if you want to sleep, I would not recommend booking at the front of the aircraft. I'm going to change my strategy on this. Now, the back of the lower deck of this aircraft actually tends to be really quiet, and you're not really sacrificing space. So, move yourself back there if you're going for quiet. Third, Qantas does not allow power banks, you guys. They mention it several times in their overhead announcements. So, you're supposed to rely on that in-seat power. You need to bring long charging cables or charging your phones and your devices might be really frustrating due to the location of the charging spots close to the floor, and your USB charging in your armrest may not work. All right, my overall thoughts on this, you guys, on the flight. I got to tell you, that seat recline alone makes this a good aircraft for long-haul flights. The flight was quiet. It was smooth. It was comfortable. But, beyond that, nothing truly wowed me about Qantas in this case. It's a solid experience, but it's not one that completely lives up to the hype. Now, if you want a comparison, be sure to check out my Japan Airlines flight review. That one is from Dallas to Haneda Airport, which is Tokyo. And also, for my adventures before this flight, be sure to watch my New Zealand cruise content, which I'm going to link to down below. Now, I want to hear from you. Would you fly Qantas again based on what you've heard? Comment yes or no, and tell me why. I'll be reading all your thoughts. And until next time, we'll see you on the high seas or in the friendly skies. Bye-bye.

reviews.transcript_full: Does Emirates really have one of the best economycl class products in the world? Buckle up because you're about to find out. Let's get started. [Music] Welcome to London Heathro Terminal 3. I'm very excited to fly the iconic Emirates A380 economy class to Dubai today and share this journey with you guys. Our journey today begins at the Emirates check-in area. Most passengers are asked to use these selfservice kiosks where you can print your own boarding pass and back tags. This area is super crowded and feels extremely chaotic. The infrastructure of Terminal 3 is pretty bad. Old, small, and with low ceilings. So, you can't fully blame Emirates for the check-in experience. Now, straight to security. Follow me. Security at Heathrow can be a test of patience, and today was no exception. Okay guys, time to head to the gate to board our Emirates flight EK32. Let's go. And here we have it. No introduction needed. The iconic Emirates A380 800. Have you ever flown on an A380? Let me know in the comments. Something I noticed is that everything is ready to guarantee an ontime departure. The cargo door is open. The tug is in position for push back. And there you have the crew getting to the aircraft from that back door. The Emirates lounge is conveniently located right next to the A380 gates, so you can maximize the time you spend at the lounge. Pre-boarding started around 80 minutes before departure. There are no boarding groups, so you can proceed as soon as the gate opens. Guys, look at that beautiful aircraft, isn't it? Did you know that Emirates has over 100 Airbus A380s in their fleet? It's by far the world's largest A380 operator. Very punctual boarding starting 50 minutes before departure. All passengers are called to board at the same time. Time to board this A380. Follow me. Today we have a lovely window seat in the front section of the lower deck. First impressions, amazing. It's easily the most luxurious and spacious economy seat in the skies. And here we have some goodies waiting for us. We have a small pillow, a blanket, and the if headphones. The Emirates economy class seat is very comfy and elegant. The texture of the seat is very soft and pleasant. The headrest is super plush and comfortable, and you can adjust the position and height like this. Speaking of comfort, this seat offers plenty of space for a long flight with a width of 18 in and a very generous pitch of 32 in. One more inch than most airlines. The armrest has the seat number over here, which is very handy. And here's the button to recline your seat to a maximum of 4 in. Economy seats are equipped with a 13 in HD touchscreen. There is also this remote with a touchcreen to control your IFB. You have a USB port over here to charge your devices and the port for your headphones. You will also find a power socket by the screen, which is a much better place than underneath your seat. Now, let's see what's inside the seat pocket. a 380 safety card, a guide to the entertainment and shopping on board, and a waste bag. Before push back, the crew came to deliver some special goodies for the kids on board. Okay, guys, it's time to fasten our seat belts and get ready for push back. Guys, if you enjoyed this video, drop a like now, share with your friends, and subscribe for more great content. Ready for takeoff. You might be surprised to hear that the A380 has the quietest cabin environment of any modern jet. It's even quieter than newer generation aircraft. The pillow provided is comfortable but relatively small and thin in line with what other airlines offer. The Emirates blanket is quite soft and warm and seems relatively new. Always great when you don't get a super worn out blanket, isn't it? And here we have the economy class headphones. These are the most comfortable headphones I've ever used in economy class. They are lightweight and the ear pads are very soft and comfortable. Now, let's explore the if Emirates is well known for having the most extensive entertainment catalog on board. The ice if is easy to navigate. It has an intuitive layout and the screen is very responsive. The selection of movies is endless, featuring hundreds of movies from all over the world, including recent releases. You can also enjoy loads of content from HBO, Paramount, Discovery, and more. But let me tell you, the coolest feature is live TV. You can watch live news and even live sports. Guys, I can already smell the food, so it's now time to pick a good movie for tonight. You can use this remote to control your screen and even watch content directly on it. In economy, the seats are very close to the screen, so I find this remote a bit redundant. Before dinner, the crew pop by to offer complimentary instant photos for families. Let's now take a look at the tray table. It's a classic economy class by folding table. Clean, stable, and adjustable. Oh, and here's a cup holder for your drinks. The dinner service was a bit slow. It took the crew over 2 hours to start serving dinner. Here we have it. I went for the chicken biryani and it looks pretty good, right? The tray is loaded with different things, but it's well presented and all fits nicely within the tray. As a starter, we have this potato salad, a bread roll, some cheddar cheese, crackers, and for dessert, we have this huge cookie with Belgian chocolate, a nice small chocolate, and a chocolate brownie topped with salted caramel. Emirates provides stainless steel cutlery in all travel classes which is lovely and a wet wipe is also provided. This biryani is excellent. The chicken is succulent, the rice is perfectly cooked and the spice level hits the mark perfectly. The potato salad is not my thing. Too much sauce. Dessert. Check this out, guys. The texture of the brownie is superb. Super fluffy and the caramel goes so well with it. I couldn't finish the cookie, but it's also of very high quality. I'm so full. Tea and coffee service started shortly after clearing out the trays. The flight time between London and Dubai is just over 6 hours and I didn't get any sleep despite the cabin being fairly quiet. I spent most of the journey enjoying the great selection of movies on board. The crew popped by multiple times to offer water and juice. Always much appreciated. Breakfast was served very early, two hours before arrival. I wasn't particularly hungry, and to be honest, the breakfast didn't look very appealing. You get this muffin, and you can choose a vegan or a cheese hot sandwich. I wonder why airlines don't serve more healthy options like some fruits and yogurt. That would make me so happy. So, how was my Emirates economy class flight? Overall, I'm super impressed with the experience. The airport experience wasn't the best, but not much you can do if you fly from Heath Terminal 3. The seat is excellent from the comfort and dimensions to the design. Small details like having a power socket right under the screen make a difference. Entertainment on board is amazing. Emirates clearly has the best I in disguise. I have mixed feelings about the food. The main meal was delicious and the quality and quantity of the food were spoton. Breakfast was very underwhelming though. The cabin environment was perfect. The aircraft was very clean and the crew were extremely welcoming and attentive. What do you guys think? Have you ever flown with Emirates? Leave a comment and let me know. And that's all for today, guys. I hope you enjoyed today's video. And if you did, check out the videos on screen. See you in the next one.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome back to the channel. Today we're flying Qatar Airways economy from Doha to Cape Town. We'll be trying their special meal options, Hindu and vegan. Are these meals worth choosing or is the regular menu the better option? Let's find out if the world's best economy class really lives up to the hype. As you arrive at Doha airport, you'll notice there are two entrances, one for premium class and one for economy. Hopefully, we'll get to review that business class experience sometime soon. But today, let's dive into the economy class journey and see what it has to [Music] offer. Doha airport is one of my favorite airports. second only to Singapore. As you enter, you're greeted by an enormous yellow teddy bear lounging under a giant lamp, an iconic sculpture here. It was actually created by Swiss artist Bers Fischer and was bought by a member of the Qatari royal family. The bear brings a playful touch to the airport's sleek design, making it memorable and unique for travelers. [Music] Dova airport is massive with huge open corridors leading right to the jet bridge. The boarding process was smooth and organized and before we knew it, we were on board and ready for the journey ahead. here's a quick peek at the business class as we head to our seat. This flight doesn't have Q suites, but the business class layout still looks comfortable, even if it's not quite as private. [Music] Heat. Heat. [Music] We chose the first row of the com which has just two seats. Perfect for traveling with family. No need to share an armrest with a stranger here. Let's take a quick look around the seat as we get settled in. [Music] We pulled back right on time and everything is running smoothly as we taxi to the runway. With the engines powering up, we're now ready for takeoff and on our way to Cape [Music] Town. The takeoff was smooth and we said goodbye to the brightly lit city of Doha below. If you ever have a layover of at least 6 hours, I highly recommend taking a transit tour of the city. It's a great way to get a quick taste of Doha, even if you don't have much time to explore. [Music] The Orex1 entertainment system on Qar Airways really stands out in the cabin. With over 4,000 options, there's no shortage of movies, TV shows, music, and games to choose from. The large, highresolution screens offer a sharp, vibrant display, making movie watching or gaming a pleasure. Navigating through the system is straightforward thanks to the intuitive interface, and I found the built-in controller easy to use. Whether you're in the mood for a blockbuster film or just some relaxing music, Orex 1 delivers a seamless entertainment experience that certainly helps pass the [Music] time. Please like, share, and subscribe the channel for more content. [Music] Dinner was served shortly after takeoff and I decided to go with the Hindu meal option which is a non-vegetarian Indian selection. The meal included a salad, the main course, dessert and bread. The bread unfortunately didn't impress me much. It lacked flavor. On the other hand, the salad was decent while the dessert was just okay. Nothing to write home about. The main course, however, was a pleasant surprise. It consisted of rice, dal, and chicken curry. The curry had a nice depth of flavor and was packed with surprisingly rich Indian spices, giving it an authentic touch that I didn't expect from an in-flight meal. Overall, while the bread and dessert didn't stand out, the main course certainly made up for it with its bold and flavorful taste. My wife tried the vegan meal, and that left a lot to be desired. While I appreciate the effort to cater to different dietary needs, the actual meal was underwhelming. The main course lacked variety with a somewhat repetitive flavor profile that leaned heavily on tomatobased dishes. The noodles were bland. The sides, like salad and fruit, were fresh, but overall, the meal didn't feel as satisfying as I'd hoped for a long haul flight. All right, here's a quick look at the restroom in Qatar Airways economy class. It's a pretty standard design, but it's kept clean and functional. You've got your basics: soap, lotion, even a light fragrance. Sometimes they actually do a good job keeping it stocked and fresh during the flight, which is definitely appreciated on a longer route like this one. And I'd say it's roomy enough to move around without feeling too cramped, which is a nice touch for economy class. A snack was served before landing, and I went with the Hindu meal option again. The taste was definitely on point, full of rich flavors and spices that I appreciated. However, the presentation left a lot to be desired. The meal was a bit messy to eat, and it wasn't as neatly arranged as I would have liked, which made it harder to enjoy without making a bit of a mess. While the taste was great, a cleaner presentation could have made the whole experience better. [Music] My wife went with the vegan option again, and this time it came with tofu and some other ingredients that we honestly couldn't identify. It definitely fell short of our expectations, but maybe that's because we're not true vegans. I imagine people who are more accustomed to vegan meals might appreciate it more, but for us, it just didn't hit the mark. My recommendation, unless you're a dedicated vegan, I'd say skip it. As we wrap up the flight, here's a quick recap of my experience with Qatar Airways economy class on this DOA to Cape Town journey. From the moment we boarded, the service was attentive, and the seat was surprisingly comfortable for longhaul travel. The entertainment system with its wide selection of movies, TV shows, and music helped pass the time effortlessly. The meals were a mixed bag. The Hindu meal was flavorful, though a bit messy in presentation, while the vegan option didn't quite meet expectations, especially for those not strictly vegan. Overall, Qatar Airways offers a solid economycl class product with excellent service and comfort. The food could use a bit of refinement, especially for special meal options, but the overall experience was good. I definitely recommend this airline if you're flying long haul, especially if you're looking for great in-flight entertainment and solid customer service. [Music]

reviews.transcript_full: Cathay Pacific is well regarded for its comfortable and high-quality economy class service, offering a solid experience for both short and long-haul flights. Seat comfort and legroom. Cathay Pacific offers a seat pitch of 31 to 32 inches and a seat width of 17.5 to 18 inches with seating arrangements in 3 to 4 to 3 or 2 to 4 to 2 configurations, depending on the aircraft. While legroom is adequate for most, taller passengers may feel a bit cramped. The seats feature moderate recline, adjustable headrests, and are equipped with pillows and blankets on long flights for added comfort. In-flight entertainment (IFE), the personalized screens, 10 to 12 inches, offer a wide selection of movies, TV shows, games, and music. Wi-Fi is available on many long-haul flights, though it's often pricey. Passengers also have access to USB charging ports and power outlets, ensuring devices stay charged throughout the flight. Food and beverage meals in economy class include a mix of Asian, Western, and vegetarian options with complimentary soft drinks, wine, and beer. Special meals, e.g., gluten-free, halal, can be requested 24 hours in advance. Overall, food quality is above average for economy class, and service is efficient. Service. Cathay Pacific's cabin crew is known for being friendly, attentive, and professional, making sure passengers are comfortable throughout the flight. Boarding is well organized with priority boarding for premium passengers. Cabin ambiance. The cabin is modern and clean with calming lighting and good air quality. Restrooms are regularly cleaned, and the overall atmosphere is conducive to relaxation, especially on long-haul flights. Baggage allowance. Economy class passengers are typically allowed one checked bag, up to 23 kg, and one carry-on bag, up to 7 kg. A small personal item is also permitted, offering enough space for most travelers' belongings. Final verdict. Cathay Pacific offers a comfortable and reliable economy class experience with solid service, ample entertainment, and good meal options. It's a great choice for travelers looking for a pleasant flight experience. Pros: comfortable seats with adequate legroom, extensive in-flight entertainment options, friendly and professional service. Cons: limited legroom for taller passengers, Wi-Fi can be expensive. Overall, Cathay Pacific is a strong contender for those seeking comfort and reliability in economy class.

reviews.transcript_full: Flying with ANA, All Nippon Airways in premium economy, offers a refined experience that bridges the gap between standard economy and business class. Noise cancelling headphones are provided ensuring a great audio visual experience. Three, cabin experience. The premium economy cabin is separated from economy, providing a more private and quiet space. The cabin lighting is soothing and the service feels more personalized with a better crew to passenger ratio. Flyfi app highlight realtime flight tracker during your ANA premium economy journey. Enhance your experience with the FlyFi apps realtime flight tracker. You can monitor your flight's route, altitude, and speed in real time along with weather updates and estimated arrival time. Meals are elegantly presented with fresh ingredients and flavorful choices. Premium beverages, including wine, sake, and spirits are also available. Additional perks, premium economy passengers enjoy priority boarding, extra baggage allowance, and access to ANA's lounges at select airports, making the travel experience smoother and more luxurious.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to Plane Stuff! Today’s flight review will take us aboard Delta Air Lines newest fleet member, the A321neo, from Los Angeles to Minneapolis. In the next video I'll cover the onward flight on an almost 31 year old A320. Make sure to subscribe so you don't miss it! This is my first narrated video, or even video of this type in general, so it will probably be a little rough. Please do let me know what you think in the comments below so I can improve! Flight details can be found in the description, and I hope you enjoy! Welcome to LAX. It's very early in the morning and I've just been dropped off in front of Delta’s Terminal 3. LAX has 9 terminals in total, Delta occupies Terminal 2 and 3, although all check-ins for Delta now go through 3. I’m not checking bags on today's flight and already have my boarding pass, so I’m able to head straight to TSA, which is really quick at this time in the morning. It looks like we'll be going out of Gate 37B, so time to get walking! LAX is in the middle of a massive overhaul and work on terminal 3 was just completed shortly before filming. It feels very clean and roomy, although it has no moving walkways and some pretty long distances, which may be annoying to some. The food options here are a little limited, however all LAX terminals are now interconnected thanks to the ongoing overhaul... ...so you can always make the hike to other terminals for plenty more options. I decided to grab some snacks at this Hudson Nonstop, which uses cameras to track what you pick up and automatically charge you without the need for a cash register. Here is our aircraft today! N512DE. This aircraft was delivered to Delta in December 2022, making it just 8 months old at the time of filming. The A321neo is the newest member of Delta's ongoing fleet renewal... ...alongside the A220, A330neo, A350, newer 737-900s, and the upcoming 737 MAX, which are replacing or already have replaced many of Delta's older fleet members. One thing I didn't mention earlier about Terminal 3 is the music. The music here is pretty overwhelming, especially near the windows where I tend to sit. I think I can safely say this music just doesn't work at 7am, and even less so at 5am as I’ve previously experienced. Well after about an hour of enduring the music, it’s time to board. Delta boards in 10 groups. As with most full service carriers, Delta starts by boarding premium cabins and elite status holders... ...and after that they’ll move into the Main Cabin, which is split between status holders in Main 1, this will be our group, then Main 2 and 3, and finally Basic Economy. Gate Agent: In the general boarding lane I'd like to continue the boarding process by inviting Main 1, Main 1 welcome aboard. It looks like this aircraft has Delta's new free WIFI! We’ll check that out after takeoff. Delta A321neos currently have one seat layout, with a total of 194 seats. The front of the cabin has 20 of Delta's newest first class product, these are hard-shell recliners that are supposed to be a step up above their traditional counterparts. These seats do look really cool and I'd love to review them one day, but for now I'll have to direct you to this great review by Jeb Brooks! Behind first class, there are 42 Comfort+ seats, Delta's premium economy offering with more legroom, extra snacks, and dedicated overhead bin space. Finally in the back is the main cabin, with 132 seats. And here is our seat 30F... without a window. Well it looks like I got unlucky, and booked a windowless window seat. I normally check third party seat maps while booking, and this is the one time I slipped. This is exactly why I recommend you check out websites like seatmaps.com while selecting your seats to help avoid reclineless seats or windowless seats like this. I really wish airlines would just warn you if a seat lacks a window, I'm sure plenty of people out there wouldn’t shy away from such a seat... ...given how many I never even see open their window shades anyway. If Ryanair can get this right, I'd expect Delta to. Anyway, time to check out the seat! Overhead you will find the standard personal air vent, reading light, and flight attendant call button. The seatback features one of Delta's wonderful screens, which we will explore in a few minutes. Just below the screen you will find your headphone jack as well as a USB port. The seat also comes with a single piece full sized tray table. The Legroom is perfectly fine, for reference I am 6ft/1.8m tall. In between the seats in front of you, you will find universal power outlets, meaning there are two for every row of three seats. The seat also has a moderate amount of recline and an adjusting headrest. The seatback pocket is pretty big, and another safety card pocket is hidden inside. Speaking of the safety card, here is a quick look! After getting complementary earbuds, which are alright, it's time to take a look through the in flight entertainment system. First off, Delta seatback screens have a very clean flight tracker installed, which offer tons of viewing options, including the heads up display, which is my personal favorite. Next up, the screen has this nice list of all the aircraft types in Delta’s fleet. As well as an airport directory featuring terminal maps of major Delta hubs and their partner hubs. You will also find a link to the menu for today's flight on a QR code, as well as a WFI guide. Now for the main feature of the in-flight entertainment, the entertainment. Delta offers a massive selection of movies and tv shows, too big to scroll through in reasonable time.  I doubt most people will have a problem finding something to watch here. You can also find live news, music, games, and a kids section. If you prefer to use your personal device instead of the seatback screen, inflight entertainment can also be streamed to your device for free. Safety Video: …make sure your seatbelt is fastened, to fasten, insert the metal tip into the buckle and adjust the strap so it's low and tight across your lap. Safety Video: To release the belt, just lift the top of the buckle. Please remain seated with your seatbelt securely fastened... Time to push back! Thankfully the person sitting behind me said they didn't mind me filming out of the window just behind my seat, so I still got some cool views for you. If you’d like to skip the takeoff and head straight to the narrated part of this video, chapters are available below. Now that we are in the air, it’s time to check out the WIFI. Delta is in the process of rolling out free WIFI for SkyMiles members on domestic flights. You can tell if your aircraft has their new WIFI system by looking for that blue sticker next to the door we saw earlier as we entered. Getting access to that free WIFI is as simple as just logging into your SkyMiles account, and watching a quick ad. I'd say that's a pretty good deal! About 40 minutes after takeoff, a snack and beverage service arrived.  For snacks you have the choice between a small bag of Sunchips, a bag of salted almonds, a white chocolate granola bar, and the famous Biscoff cookies. I always ask for two items, and have yet to be disappointed! And here is the bathroom, this one is the rear right. There isn't anything special about it, being a little tight, and a little dirty just an hour into the flight. Well, without a window there isn't really much else for me to show you, as I didn't want to disturb the passengers behind me mid flight... ...so I'll check back in as we get closer to Minneapolis. About an hour before landing, the crew did a second quick service! I decided to just get another cookie. I really hope this screen isn't correct! And thankfully it wasn't, so time to get ready for landing! Flight Attendant: It's been our pleasure to have you on board with us today. Flight Attendant: To prepare for landing please ensure your seatbelt is fastened, your seatback and tray table are in their upright and locked... Flight Attendant: It's our pleasure to welcome you to Minneapolis-Saint Paul where the local time is 11:34, there has been a two hour time change. Flight Attendant: Please stay seated with your seatbelts fastened...  I really enjoyed my first time on a Delta A321neo, despite the lack of a window, which is partly on me anyway. Overall Delta offers a great service, and they have equipped their A321neos with very nice and comfortable seats... …and good quality in-flight entertainment systems that should hold up for years to come. Anyway welcome to Minneapolis-Saint Paul! I hope I'll see you in the second part of our journey, where, instead of a brand new aircraft, we'll be taking a nearly 31 year old A320! Please let me know what you thought of my first flight review in the comments! I know I have a lot to learn, but I still hope you could enjoy it, and will stick around for the next one!

reviews.transcript_full:
Tonight it's American Airlines turn 
to show us what they got for one of   their transpacific flights! We'll be flying 
from Tokyo to Dallas in Main Cabin Extra,   American's step-up economy product. We'll 
also see how the largest airline in the   world stacks up to some of the other 
transpacific flights we've seen on this   channel. Is Main Cabin Extra worth the extra 
cost? Come along and let's find out together! Good afternoon and welcome back to another video and welcome back to Haneda Airport terminal 3. Well,   we're getting close to the end of the year but
we still have time for a few more flights and   to start us off we'll be flying with American 
Airlines on a flight from Tokyo to Dallas. And   this is actually going to be my first time 
flying American on an international flight   outside North America so we'll see how their 
trans-pacific product is and compare to some   of the other airlines which we've experienced on 
the channel. We'll be flying in economy class on   one of their Dreamliners and the flight is set 
to depart at 6 p.m. So come along let's enjoy   American Airlines as we go from A to to A!  All right well arriving to the airport I headed to   the kiosks at the I check-in area which was 
being used by American. Earlier I checked in   online through the AA app so by the time I arrived at the airport I just had to drop off my bags and   the bag drop off lane took no more than a few 
moments. I should point out that I was headed   to Toronto so at baggage drop off I received an 
'international to International' sticker on my   passport which signified that I didn't have to collect and recheck my bag after US Passport control. With   the formalities out of the way I figure it was 
a good idea to step outside for a few moments   before heading through passport control on a 
pleasant early winter day. We even catch a Finnair Dreamliner! They have quite the interesting 
route due to the closed Russian airspace and   I recently found out that they were the first 
European airline to fly non-stop between Europe   and Japan. Did their non-stop flight to Japan 
begin in 1979,  '81, or '83? Leave your guess in the comments. EE: Terminal 3 used to be called the "Intl Terminal"
until T2 started accepting intl flights! Today we'll be departing from gate 145.   It's one of these lower level gates 
which exist only on the east side of   the terminal. Already waiting for us is 
our Dreamliner which will take us to DFW! We still had some time to kill and the good 
news is that gate 145 is not too far from the   food court so I figured I might as well. I went 
to the noodle outlet at the end and picked up   a tsukemen dish - one of my favorite noodle 
dishes in Japan! It's very similar to Ramen   with the main difference being the noodles and 
soup are separate and you dip one in the other.   There's a healthy serving of cold noodles 
alongside a warm broth with pork, nori and   green onions. A solid call and I can't believe 
it took me all these years to try this place out! By the time I returned to the gate boarding 
was well underway and look who's beside US! Air   Canada has since returned to using the B777
for their Toronto - Haneda route. That plane will beat   me to my final destination by about 6 hours. So is a detour through America worth it? Stay tuned and   find out! The only upgrade I purchased for this 
trip was Main Cabin Extra which gave me group   five boarding. It appears that Americans value 
higher boarding zones a little bit more than we do   north of the border. I really don't know why nine 
boarding zones are necessary but I digress. today   Today we'll be in seat 20J, an aisle seat on the emergency row which is dedicated to Main Cabin Extra passengers.   Passengers in this row can take advantage 
of the dedicated overhead storage bins as well. EE: Winter is a good time for aisle seats. Easy access to the aisle, and there's not too many sights due do darkness. Tonight we're on an almost 4-year-old 787 7-8 Dreamliner. American   has one configuration of this aircraft with 
234 seats across three cabins. Main Cabin Extra   and main cabin seats are in the same cabin but 
marketed as different products. There are seven   lavatories on board and it's important to 
note that there are none at the rear of the aircraft. It'll take about 10 
and 1/2 hours to reach Dallas.   and we'll be staying well south 
of Alaska as we cross the Pacific. EE: Footage of cabin is combination of AA176 and AA169 (LAX-HND) The economy cabin is laid out in a 3-3-3 seating 
configuration. Bulkhead monitors provide flight   information and messages throughout the flight. 
The cabin had a healthy blue glow during the   start of the flight and warm orange and reds 
towards the end. Main Cabin Extra are rows 10,   11, and 20 along with the centre seats of rows 12 through 18 so if you are after a window seat and   Main Cabin Extra you are limited to six possible 
options on the dash eight Dreamliner. The seats were   quite comfortable with an adjustable headrest. 
A pillow and blanket were provided for guests   which was advantageous as I thought they kept 
the cabin on the very chilly (read: freezing!) side. Of course one   benefit of the emergency row is the unlimited leg room at your disposal and you don't have to worry   about others in your row passing you when they 
want to get out. On the other hand no luggage can   be stored on the floor during taxi takeoff and 
landing so the dedicated bins come in especially   handy for the emergency row passengers. With no lavatories at the rear of the plane this area   was highly trafficked perhaps more than other 
Dreamliners particularly after the meal service   so I wouldn't recommend the aisle seat of the 
emergency row. The seats are slightly different   than the rest of the cabin housing a control 
panel on the one side. The IFE system pulls out   from under the armrest and you have to to press 
the tab to release it which took a few moments to   spot in the dim cabin. On my return trip I was in 
17D which I think is a better illustration of what   you get with Main Cabin Extra. The seatback has 
a large adjustable display. The lit pocket which   contained the safety card was just below with 
a table and pocket under that. You'll find the   power outlet at the base and the seat pitch is 35 
to 36 inches, about 5 in more than main cabin seats and   the extra bit of space is quite welcomed on these Long Haul flights. With the table extended you can   really get a sense of the extra space. To compare you can see how the table meets the armrest in the   regular main cabin seats over there overall. I was 
pleased with this seat more than the emergency exit   row and I thought the extra space was worth the 
added cost for Main Cabin Extra on these Long Haul flight. Wi-Fi is offered on the Dreamliners and is 
available for purchase at $23, about $30 Canadian   for the full flight it's in line with what I've 
seen on other airlines. With the AA app you can   also stream videos to your device which is useful if you have your own Bluetooth headphones. The app   is pretty extensive and worth downloading for 
your trip. It even has a track your bag feature   which provides peace of mind especially if 
you have connections. And as always I take a   moment to welcome new viewers to subscribe 
for continued travel and aviation related content:) About an hour after takeoff the dinner 
service commenced. The service started with a warm   oshibori... nice touch! The options were pork 
and rice or a shrimp pasta and I went with   the pork and rice which was a solid call. It came 
with a salad, a spinach side, and a lemon cake and   bonus points for providing a warm bun!
Everything was delicious and it was no chore   finishing every last bite. To accompany the meal 
I enjoyed a Goose Island IPA so cheers to another flight! ooo fresh! The IFE system on American is 
smooth and easy to operate. They have a   very extensive library in which to choose 
something to watch. One difference compared   to domestic flights is that there is no live 
TV available even when the plane is over the   US. Also one thing I think missing from the I 
system is a menu tab for the onboard service   many other airlines have this feature and 
I think it greatly benefits the guest!  And here's a look inside the lavatory closest to 
my seat considering there are no laboratories in   the rear the plane they were kept quite clean 
throughout the flight despite being heavily used. Don't let the darkness fool you it's early 
afternoon outside and plenty bright perfect time   for breakfast which was served with the last hour to go. The options were French toast toast or udon.   The hot meal was accompanied by some fresh fruit I wasn't particularly fond of the French toast   I thought it was on the dry side and no amount 
of syrup was going to save it but I did manage   to have a coffee with my breakfast ...or lunch ...or whatever you want to call this early afternoon meal. Overall this was a pleasant way to cross 
the Pacific the staff were kind and friendly   there was good entertainment and an abundance of food, snacks, and drinks. The flight was one   of five on a roundtrip ticket from Tokyo to 
Toronto and the price came out to C$1,368 which   includes the C$230 upgrade to main cabin extra. I thought the added of cost of main cabin extra was   worth it considering it was spread out over five 
flights. We also offset 613 tons (kg) of carbon for this flight. Landing in Dallas the passport control 
was much faster and better organized than when   I flew through Chicago a year ago. There's a 
dedicated line for US and Canadian [and PR] passport   holders which sped things up a bit. The ITI 
sticker on my passport did its job and my   bag was checked onto my next flight without 
me having to collect it at the carousel. So   as a Canadian would I fly them again well it 
depends! There is added time to your trip when   transferring through the states and another set 
of passport control but the flight was about 400   bucks cheaper compared to Air Canada. American is the largest airline in the world and they   simply have the size to provide a competitive 
price and times so if the price is right I'd   fly them again though I'd Try to snag a codeshare
flight with JAL through the American   website like I did last year. Anyways thanks 
for watching let me know what you thought   about the American Airlines transpacific 
product and I'll catch you in the next episode :)

reviews.transcript_full:
Hi there and welcome to a bit of a gloomy day 
in Taipei. This was actually filmed the day   before my Starlux flight. I was hungry and as one 
does in Taipei when you’re hungry during the day,   you goto 7-Eleven. Of course at 
night, you would goto a night market.  I could say that I’m here because my flight 
to Saigon is Starlux 711, which is true,   but that’s not trueeee. Why I really came 
to this side of town, is because of this.  How often do you get to see an airline and 
a convenience store collaboration? I sure as   hell never have. Now, you’ll forgive me, filming 
inside 7-Eleven’s is not quite my forte, but I did   think visiting this 7-Eleven would be a good way 
to really show you how ingrained the three major   airlines are in daily life in Taiwan. I’m going 
to buy my very cool seat belt key chain and then-  Ah here we are, it’s tomorrow. I 
suppose gloomy is going to be a theme.  Taipei has two airports, the much smaller 
Shongshan airport in the city center which   serves some regional and domestic flights and 
then the much larger Taoyuan airport to the   southwest of the city. Taoyuan is the primary hub 
for Starlux along with China Airlines and EVA Air.   Quite the trio of airlines, literally three of the 
best in the world, just casually chilling here in   Taipei. I guess that tips my hat on this review.
So, before we head inside and get checked in with   Spiderman, let me introduce myself to those of you 
that are new to the channel. My name is Kevin and   I am the Flip Flop Traveller. I’m here to give you 
two honest videos each week about unique flights,   hotels and trains. This flight today was 
self funded, the price I paid is in the   description and Starlux has no idea who I am. 
So without further ado, let’s get into episode   316 and see what Starlux is really all about.
Here we are at Terminal 1. The airport has a   bit of a unique setup in that terminal one is over 
here on the right side and everything on the left   is terminal two, but they are all connected 
in what is in theory a continuous loop. Plus,   there’s a new terminal three being built as well- 
the concourses of which should be open by mid next   year with the full terminal opening in 2027.
Today is a pretty easy day here but I’ve seen   this place packed before, so they certainly need 
the breathing room with Starlux now added to the   mix. Last year Taoyuan saw around 35 million 
passengers, putting it in the same league as   the like of Tokyo Narita and Hanoi Noi Bai.
Here in terminal 1, Starlux has a single row   of check in desks- and there’s spiderman. 
They seem to be very much into the branding   collaborations. On their LAX flights, 
they even have LA Clippers branding.  I should mention that Starlux has a 
split operation now between the two   terminals and since my flight, Saigon and 
Da Nang’s flights have moved to Terminal 2,   while Hanoi and Phu Quoc stays here.
Let’s get through security and immigration   and head to the lounge, on the way, I can tell you 
about the level 9 drama that morphed into Starlux.  The current CEO of Starlux- Chang Kuo-Wei- used to 
work at EVA Airlines. He was a mechanic and then a   pilot and eventually made his way to be chairman, 
since you know, his father was the founder of   Evergreen Group. Chang became chairman of EVA in 
2013. Three years later, his father died and named   Chang as his successor as Chairman of Evergreen 
Group. This is when things got spicy. Problem was,   Chang was the youngest of his father’s sons, from 
his second marriage to boot. There was more a less   a coup that ensued at Evergreen and Chang was 
booted from the company. Within a few months,   he had the idea to create Starlux.
The name Starlux comes from the Chinese   character for Star, in honor of his father 
who navigated via the stars before GPS and   the Character for Universe, framing Chang’s 
own ambitions. In English, it became Starlux.  Let me pause that for a moment as we take a look 
at the lounge here in Terminal 1. It is small and   this is probably the weakest link of the entire 
Starlux network. That said, all of the longer   or more premium routes are now operating 
from Terminal 2 which has a larger lounge.  There was a small buffet selection on offer 
as well as a few a la cart items, from which   I chose the scallion bun and soy milk which was 
actually quite a stand out, all things considered.  I also loved the attention to small 
details- such as the ice on offer.  The only other big negative for this lounge 
is that the restrooms are a solid 100 meters   down the corridor outside of the lounge.
I know this isn’t ideal, but if the lounge   is ever too crowded, there’s a public lounge of 
sorts named the Airport Experience Zone which   looked surprisingly calm and comfortable.
I can never leave this airport   without mango tarts in hand.
So, obviously, Starlux is competing with China   Airlines, but much more so, with EVA. Their first 
flights were in late 2020, delayed due to COVID,   with the first three destinations being Da Nang, 
Penang and Macau. They’ve quickly expanded to   their current 26 destinations with 2 more on the 
way by the end of the year, with an impressive   operation to Japan and a stated goal of being a 
major player connecting southeast asia to the US.  One unique thing is that on their A350s,   which they have five of at the moment to fly to 
the US, they actually have a true first class,   something you won’t find at their competitors, 
as Starlux says they, “promise to commit to   luxury that Taiwan’s dominant carriers have 
lost sight of in recent years.” Still ironic,   they're talking about two great airlines. Also 
kinda cool that Chang flew the first A350 from   Toulous himself for the delivery flight.
They currently have 23 aircraft on   hand with 30 on order.
I got to the gate on time   but our aircraft didn’t. While the signs were 
updated in time, I was surprised there were   no announcements for the flight’s delay.
Here’s our 2 year old bird pulling in now.  Around 30 minutes behind schedule, boarding 
began with Business Class passengers- they’re   not part of any alliance yet, so it was a very 
small group one. That said, there’s quite a bit   of speculation that Starlux may end up joining 
Oneworld alliance- especially since there’s also   speculation that Cathay may leave it. Then Taipei 
would be one of the only cities on earth serving   as a hub for all three alliances.
Ok, as we head down the jetbridge,   let’s take a look at today’s flight stats.
I stepped on board and there is one thing   that is like the finest crystal clear as soon 
as you step on board. This is an airline that   is here to impress- and I mean that both 
for the hard product and soft product.  The staff were enthusiastic, thoughtful and 
knowledgeable and that cabin was gorgeous.   The business class on these A321neos has just 
8 lie flat seats in a 2 x 2 configuration.  As I’ve said before, I’ve always liked 
these seats since in the seated position,   I think they’re pretty comfortable, even 
if they’re a bit narrow when lie flat.  But it’s all of the finishing details 
that make the difference here though.  From the leather trim, to the contrast stitching, 
and even things like the quality of the seatbelt-   it’s a very well designed product.
There’s a fully adjustable headrest   as well as a storage space over your 
shoulder with a universal outlet.  So we all know what happens if you click 
like on this video and subscribe to the   channel, but do you know what happens if you 
don’t? You may never see me again. So if you enjoy   this style of content, be sure to click all of 
the buttons. If you’re interested in a peak of the   inner workings of the channel or just need some 
travel advice- be sure to check out my Patreon.   Whatever you do, thanks for being here right now.  I was served a hot towel along with a 
really good cold pressed pineapple and   guava juice. I love creative- but not too 
creative- signature pre departure drinks.  Across, there’s a nice high resolution in 
flight monitor along with a good side foot   rest. The storage space under the foot rest 
is limited though. Also keep in mind the foot   rests for the bulkheads in this type of seat 
are around double the size of the other rows.  We pushed back and a very- shall 
we say different- safety video   began to play. Perhaps, not to Emirates taste.  We had an excruciatingly long taxi and wait in 
line for take off- at one point we were next in   line and it honestly felt like they just forgot 
about us. 72 minutes from push back to take off.  But it’s coming up now, 
along with the airport stats.  So before the meal begins, let’s take a look 
at the comforts and amenities on offer today.  The pillow is a decent size and 
quality- and freshly laundered.  Then there’s a fantastic blanket. At 
first glance it may look like a towel,   but it’s actually a super soft and fluffy blanket 
which thankfully doesn’t leave lint everywhere.  As for the headphones, they were noise canceling 
and quite good actually, but I think I actually   like the case even more than the headphones.
The tray table could be used fully   extended or folded in half.
Ok, let’s get into this really good   meal service. First, we will start off with an 
insanely comprehensive menu for a 3 hour flight.  Note that the prices in red are my addition 
to the graphic just to give you an idea of   the current retail price for each bottle.
As I said before, I love drinking wine   but my knowledge is limited, so I always 
appreciate wine lists that go into detail   about region, pairings and tasting notes.
Of course, I chose the Contemporary Asian   and Longtail Menu for my meal which 
honestly, even if I didn’t like it,   I would have loved it- and I’ll tell you why.
It’s clear, even for a single tray service,   they are trying to elevate the 
experience from the ground up.  For our meal today, we start with a Pineapple 
Pura Longtail and sparkling water. The starter is   Milkfish toast, Avocado, Daikon and Dill. Reading 
that, I had precisely zero idea what to expect,   but I think this is quite clever. 
It’s so elevated for in flight food,   but not at all fussy or difficult to serve.
For the main, we had USDA ANgus Beef Tenderloin,   Pineapple Rice, peanut and pickled kohlrabi.
So, when it comes to beef, let me tell you   how I know when a dish is really good. 
When I start taking little tiny bites.   I think I cut each of those slices into 2 or 
3 pieces. The pineapple rice was great too.  In East Asia, we are spoiled with the food 
offerings in business class on these regional   routes, but it’s worth pointing out that Starlux 
is the only airline in the region right now that   doesn’t follow the same exact format for 
meals. Small salad or cold meat appetizer,   plus hot preplated main and dessert. 
Cathay, ANA, JAL, EVA, China Airlines,   Korean Air, Asiana- it’s all the same 
format- and it’s generally all good,   but this is just another level. I’d be 
really curious to try Starlux’s catering   on long haul services- more on that in a bit.
Earlier I’d asked for a glass of the Reisling,   but the crew insisted that I allow them to chill 
it for a bit more time since it wasn’t properly   prepared- attention that I appreciated- so that 
came along with my dessert which was a Chocolate   Magao cake along with seasonal fresh fruit.
Entertainment on board- it’s just okay. I   have little doubt that it’ll improve 
overtime, but at the time there were   just around 150 movies on offer- along with 
a handful of TV shows with random episodes.  Loved the detailed map and in 
flight magazine though. There   was also in flight wifi which 
was free for Business Class.  And here we have the seat in full 
flat mode- definitely not needed on   this short day flight, but nice to have for sure.
So, how I ended up on this short Starlux flight.   Last year, Starlux announced a partnership with 
Alaska Airlines and then Alaska announced they’d   be selling Starlux tickets for points. Alaska 
communicated that there would be promotional   fares available for the first few months. The 
aviation world collectively freaked out and   everyone started trying to book. At that time, I 
had 43000 Alaska points. The had a promo to buy   more points and so I topped that up to 60000 
miles which would be enough for the Taipei   to LAX flight. I knew the points would take 2 
days to appear in my account, but it was fine,   Alaska advertised these fares would be 
available I believe from April until August.  Well wouldn’t you know they forgot to mention that 
each flight only had four seats available at that   price. By the time I went to book, everything 
was more than double the price. So in the end,   with my 60k alaska points, I got this 
flight, plus a longhaul LATAM flight,   decided to dump Alaska all together before 
they continued to devalue their program.  So yeah, I wanted a long 
haul flight- and I still do,   perhaps now even more so- and will 
keep my eyes open for them. That said,   this was a really nice first taste of what will 
clearly be a new major player in the market. Oh,   did I mention they even already began 
turning a profit last year? Yeah.  Ok, I’ll let you enjoy the rest of the approach 
into Saigon. The airport stats are coming up.  And so, that is that. We were late, the 
airport was mobbed but I was still on   cloud 9 so I didn’t even care. Starlux, 
I will be back- if you join Oneworld,   or any alliance frankly, I’ll be back often.
So I really hope you enjoyed this trip report   today. If you did, be sure to click the like 
button and subscribe with notifications on so   you don’t miss out on my twice weekly videos. 
I’ll see you next time from a surprise out of   order flight on an airline that needs to do a 
hell of a lot better protecting their passanger’s   data. You don’t want to miss that one. Oh and 
as always, thanks for watching until the end.

reviews.transcript_full:
Hello everyone, I’m Edin~ Today, I’m taking you from Taipei to Singapore~ This time, I’m flying on Starlux A330-900 in economy class I’m seated in 32K, near the No. 2 engine~ Engine View (Aviation enthusiasts’ favourite!!) A blanket and pillow are already prepared at the seat. The headrest has multi-angle adjustments. There’s a TV in front, with space below for small items. Under the TV, there’s a USB port and headphone jack. Meal tray~ Legroom when sitting upright (I’m 177cm tall)~ Underneath, there are headphones and a stack of documents (the black bag on the right is mine). In the middle, there’s a shared Type-C/international charging port with the adjacent seat. In-flight magazine, Wi-Fi access card, safety card, and airsickness bag. The in-flight entertainment system offers a variety of movies, TV shows, music, and games from different countries. There’s a decent selection, and most are fairly recent. You can also check the menu on the screen. There were two meal options that day (I chose beef pasta). Meals can be pre-selected online. Starlux offers signature drinks in collaboration with local bars (not available on the short Taipei-Hong Kong route).
This flight offered the Sci-Fi Cosmos signature drink. Of course, standard drinks are also available~ Now for the aviation enthusiast’s favorite section – the flight map!! It can be viewed from multiple angles! For convenience, you can connect wireless Bluetooth headphones to the TV. It’s meal time! This time, it’s beef in tomato sauce with long pasta~ Overall, I found the taste to be very high quality.
The beef had a great balance of fat and lean meat, with excellent texture! If I had to nitpick, I’d wish they offered ice cream. Sci-Fi Cosmos drink paired with a movie! Drinks in blue plus blue skies and white clouds outside ^^ Snapping a photo for the memories~ All Starlux flights offer free Wi-Fi for text messaging.
Just connect to the plane’s Wi-Fi, enter your email, and agree to the terms. Lavatory Visit There’s a green plant~ Moisturizing spray/lotion. Overall, it’s clean and tidy! About an hour before landing, they offered snacks and drinks (peach juice). In summary, I found this flight experience very comfortable and enjoyable. The hardware was nearly flawless.The only minor issue is that the window could be cleaner... On the software side, the meal exceeded expectations in taste.
The cabin crew worked very efficient too. The entire journey was very smooth, and I hope to try other international routes in the future~ Have you ever flown with Starlux Airlines?
What’s your opinion of them? Let me know in the comments! Thanks for watching, see you in the next video, bye bye!

with warm wood tones and soft lighting The natural light and design make it a pleasant place to wait A self-serve bar includes wine, beer, and a range of soft drinks The lounge's large windows overlook the tarmac A buffet area offers a selection

who want to freshen up before a long flight It’s time to head to the gate for boarding This is the Singapore Airlines A350 that will fly us to Singapore The aircraft has registration number 9V-SMO (built in 2017) Singapore Airlines has 65 Airbus A350s
(the world's largest fleet of 350s) Singapore Airlines operates several versions of the A350,
including the A350-900ULR ('ultra-long-range' model) Singapore Airlines was the A350-900ULR's launch customer
and remains the only airline to operate it Singapore Airlines’ A350-900ULR operates the world’s longest
scheduled commercial nonstop route (Singapore to New York) The A350 is one of the quietest jets in the sky The A350’s sleek carbon-fiber design also makes 
it lighter and more fuel-efficient The A350’s wings are elegantly curved
and flexible, improving aerodynamics It’s time to board the aircraft Singapore Airlines’ A350 features 42 Business Class seats The seats are spread over two cabins
and arranged in a 1-2-1 layout A larger cabin in the front of the plane
holds the bulk of the Business Class seats (26 in total) The remaining 16 seats are located in a smaller
and more intimate Business Class cabin over the wings The cabin design was created by James Parker Associated,
the company that also created the interiors of the Orient Express  Center seats include a partition screen
that can be raised for extra privacy All seats along the windows are single seats Singapore Airlines' Business Class seat 
is one of the widest seats in the sky Seat pitch is 153 cm (60 inches), and width is 71 cm (28 inches) The crew welcomes passengers with a drink and hot towel The pilot welcomes the passengers Singapore Airlines’ hospitality is
world-renowned, and it’s easy to see why Once boarding is complete, the safety video is shown It’s a beautifully produced film (not just a safety briefing) The video blends essential safety instructions
with Singapore’s cultural landmarks The famous Singapore Girl gracefully
guides passengers through each instruction Her presence symbolizes the airline’s
heritage of service and professionalism We’re leaving the gate (on time departure at 12 pm) Brussels Airport has three runways:
one north-south and two parallel east-west runways Singapore Airlines’ A350s are powered by
Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines Have you ever flown with Singapore Airlines?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment Let’s explore Singapore Airlines’ A350 Business Class seat A reading light sits at eye level for easy use during night flights Seat adjustments are made through
a control panel in the armrest by the aisle In front of the seat is a large 18-inch HD screen A small compartment with vanity mirror sits beside the screen The entertainment screen can be tilted The seat features a large ottoman (foot rest) A console next to the seat holds another reading light,
the power outlets and some storage space Next to the console sits the handheld remote
for the inflight entertainment system A storage box in the armrest is perfect
for a bottle of water or small personal items The tray table is stored in the armrest
and can be adjusted in height and position The bulkhead seats in rows 11 & 19 feature full-width ottomans In the other seats, the footwell is tucked
diagonally into the side of the seat ahead When the seat converts into a bed,
your legs extend into this angled cubby In Singapore Airlines' Business Class, amenity kits 
are available upon request rather than automatically provided The amenity kit is designed in collaboration with
Le Labo, the boutique fragrance house from New York The kit holds a selection of
Le Labo Bergamote 22 skincare essentials Singapore Airlines sometimes gives Business Class 
passengers a collectible plush bear as a keepsake Slippers, socks and eye-masks are offered A large pillow and soft duvet are provided Noise-cancelling headphones are provided,
ensuring an immersive experience Flying through high clouds shows just how fast we’re moving Let’s explore the inflight menu Singapore Airlines partners with world-class chefs
to create its Business and First Class menus The airline’s “Book the Cook” service lets passengers
pre-select main courses before departure Canape : Singapore chicken satay,
with onion, cucumber, and spicy peanut sauce Cocktail: Singapore Sling Appetizer: Vitello Tonnato (thinly sliced veal), with creamy
tuna sauce, capers, tomato, caviars and snow pea tendril Main course: classic beef stew in beer sauce,
Brussels sprouts, carrots, shallot and roasted grenaille potatoes Dessert: Oreo ice cream, raspberry bavarois
and a selection of cheese and sliced fresh fruits Singapore Airlines' Airbus A350 features 
three lavatories for Business Class passengers Payot hand lotion and facial mist
are available in the lavatories during the flight We can enjoy some beautiful views along the way The IFE system is controlled using a handheld remote Called KrisWorld, Singapore Airlines' IFE system includes
hundreds of movies, TV shows, and curated playlists Singapore Airlines offers its Business Class passengers
complimentary onboard Wi-Fi during the entire flight The flight can be tracked
in real-time using an interactive 3D map The sun sets as we fly over Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan A light bite is served mid-flight: vegetarian rice noodles,
with lettuce, black mushrooms, and Chinese greens Snacks are also available in the galley throughout the flight It’s time for some rest:
the cabin crew assists in setting up the bed When fully flat, the bed measures 198 cm or 78 inches in length I am lucky during this flight: one seat can be used for sitting,
while the other is fully converted into my bed The full-width ottoman of the bulkhead seat allows
for a natural sleeping position and unrestricted legroom A few hours later: we're crossing the Bay of Bengal As dawn approaches, the cabin lighting
gradually brightens to mimic sunrise Breakfast starts with a selection of sliced fresh fruits,
Bircher muesli, flavored yoghurt, and assorted bread rolls Main breakfast course: Dutch mini fluffy pancakes
with pineapple compote, strawberry and butter We're encountering some moderate turbulence near Phuket Turbulence can feel unsettling, 
but the plane is designed to handle it safely How do you feel about turbulence — calm or anxious? I’m a nervous flyer, but it helps  
to be on a reputable airline like Singapore Airlines A crew member, curious about my blog, shared 
this lovely note before we landed We’re approaching the Singapore Airlines airspace Unfortunately, thunderstorms are building up
over Singapore, so we have to circle before landing The sky over Singapore is stormy as we approach the airport Thunder rumbles in the distance,
and lightning flashes across the clouds Singapore Airlines is one of the world’s most awarded airlines Singapore Airlines' story began in 1947
when Malayan Airways operated its very first flight The airline was founded with a twin-engined Airspeed Consul In 1966, it became Malaysia-Singapore Airlines, known as MSA When MSA split in 1972, two national carriers were born:
Malaysia Airlines and Singapore Airlines Singapore Airlines quickly established
itself as a global carrier with high standards The airline built a reputation for reliability and premium comfort Singapore Airlines has often led the way in aviation innovation It was the first airline to offer free headsets,
choice of meals, and drinks in Economy Class In 2007, Singapore Airlines was the launch customer
for the Airbus A380, the world’s largest passenger aircraft The carrier is part of the Star Alliance network,
connecting passengers to over 1,000 destinations The company’s commitment to quality extends
beyond its cabins — to training, safety, and sustainability The Singapore Airlines brand stands for
precision, warmth, and world-class service Would you be scared to land in a thunderstorm? Despite the storm, the aircraft touches
down smoothly on the wet runway Thank you for watching this
