reviews.transcript_full: [Music] Welcome back. In this video, we're stepping on board Delta Airlines in business class aboard an Airbus A330 flying from Madrid, Spain to Atlanta, Georgia in the USA. Is this old and dated Delta 1 cabin worth the hefty price tag? Stay tuned to find out why Delta's recent retrofit of this aircraft missed the mark. We'll also tell you what you need to look for if you're looking to book Delta's business class product in order to make sure you know what you're booking before you board. So, join us as we explore the seat, service, and experience on board this 9 and 1/2 hour daytime flight. And stick around to learn about Delta's plans for these aircraft. Welcome to Travel at Random. We're Trevor and Ryan. This channel started out of a love of travel. We're here to share unbiased and self-funded trip reports, hotel and flight reviews, and travel advice. We hope we inspire your next getaway. Check out our playlist in the description and browse the channel. If you enjoy this video, please hit that like button and subscribe to keep up with our latest content. Thank you for watching. Now, let's head to the airport. [Applause] [Music] Welcome to Madrid, the capital of Spain. We are just wrapping up a week of exploring several historic Spanish cities. Check out our playlist at the end of the video to see more from our trip. We'll have new videos in this series over the next few months, so make sure you subscribe to stay uptodate. Today we're flying Delta out of Adulo Suarez Madrid Barahas International Airport, Barahas or MAD for short. Last year over 66 million passengers made their way through this airport, making it one of the busiest in Europe. MAD is located about 7 mi or 11 km from the city center, about 15 minutes by train or 30 minutes by car or taxi. The airport is connected to Madrid's public transit. Metro line 8 has stops at all four terminals and the commuter train system has a train station at terminal 4. There are five terminals in total. Terminals 1, 2, and three are older and are connected. Terminal 4 and 4S are newer and about 5 km from the other terminals. You can take a shuttle to move between 4, 4S, and the older terminals. Delta operates out of terminal 1 along with most of the other major international carriers. Except for one world alliance members like Iberia and American Airlines which are out of terminal 4. We're traveling in Delta 1 today. So there's a dedicated baggage drop and check-in line just for business class passengers. If you're flying Delta, enter through door 1 at terminal 1 and head to the right. Just look for the Delta 1 sign. Check-in was rather quick and we were off to security and passport control. There is fasttrack security at this airport and it was included with the Delta 1 ticket. The passport control line was pretty quick at this time of the morning and we were through in a few minutes. As part of your Delta 1 ticket, you also have access to the Seless VIP lounge which is located near gate B29 up the escalators just past the duty-free shop. This is also a priority pass lounge and is the only lounge in terminal 1. There are no Delta or Sky Team specific lounges in this airport. The Seless Lounge is large and there was plenty of seating available the morning of our flight. Most seats are set up at tables. This club also features a large outdoor terrace that wraps around the building, offering 180° views of the runway, remote stands, and gates. [Music] There are a lot of seating options out here, including some elevated sections with sofas. In the center was the main food and drink buffet. For breakfast, it had pastries, fruits, cold cuts, and salad items available. [Music] On the back wall are pairs of grabandgo refrigerators with items like packaged sandwiches, fruit cups, and bottled drinks. [Music] In the middle are two self-service espresso style drink machines. On the far side of the lounge is a large bar with wine, cocktails, soda, and beer on offer, even at 8:00 a.m. The club had showers available, which you can request. Since we were leaving first thing in the morning and we came from our hotel, we skipped the showers. The lounge also has pretty nice and clean bathrooms. Near the entrance, there's a quiet room with some tables where you can get some work done. Reviews online of this lounge are mixed with some reporting long entry lines and picked over food offerings. As far as lines go, there's always a customer arguing about access at any club we go to these days. But there were multiple agents working it, so it was less than five minutes. The food on offer looked fine, but was pretty basic for breakfast with the only hot option being a toaster for the bread. Overall, the lounge was a nice space to spend a little bit of time and grab a drink. The terrace was unexpected, and we always appreciate being able to get some fresh air while traveling. Otherwise, it's a pretty standard international priority pass lounge. Our daytime flight today takes us 9 and a half hours from MAD to ATL, about 4,300 miles. Delta flies this route once daily. Boarding started on time and was orderly. There were clearly marked cues for each zone. After scanning our boarding passes, we were surprised to be heading down some stairs. [Music] We then found out that we were on a remote stand this morning. This caused the actual boarding to be a bit chaotic as they loaded several zones into the bus before sending it off and everyone rushed the single set of air stairs at the same time. This Airbus A330300 features 282 seats across four classes. 34 Delta 1 seats, 21 premium select seats, 24 comfort plus seats, and 208 economy seats. Delta 1 seats on this A330 are arranged in a one 121 reverse herring bone configuration. We're in seats 2A and 2J today. The bulkhead on opposite sides of the plane. Privacy was reasonable, but mainly due to having your back facing the aisle, not due to the walls of the seat. Be aware, these are not Delta's newer suites, and the seats do not feature closing doors. If a door is important to you, make sure you look for flights operated by Delta's A350s and A330900 Neos. When booking, look at the more details to see the aircraft type. Delta 767s have a variant of the Delta 1 suite, but don't feature closing doors due to the narrower cabin width. Delta will also eventually have closing door suites on their upcoming A321 Neos that feature Delta 1. These A330 Delta 1 cabin seats are 19.6 7 in wide and are fully lie flat. There was plenty of room to lay down, even for Trevor at 6'4. [Music] Each seat features a 15.4 in touchscreen if that swings out, as well as USBA and universal power outlets. The tray table extends from the side console and folds open. It's a good size for both dining and getting some work done. While in seat mode, the seat has great leg room. I'm 6 foot for reference. There's also an adjustable armrest on the aisle side. Delta's A33300's underwent interior refits in 2021. In 2022, a new premium select cabin with 21 seats in a 232 configuration were added. The Comfort Plus cabin was downsized from 40 to 24 seats in a 242 arrangement. They also refreshed the lavatories and even added an espresso machine. Delta 1 and economy cabins got new upholstery, but otherwise went unchanged. These current seats are rather dated and are not as private or modern as Delta's other widebody Delta 1 seats. Delta must agree because they've announced they're going to refit these aircraft in 2026. They plan to start taking the 42 aircraft back into refit to replace the business class cabin with the latest Delta 1 seats. Each seat had a Mason branded bedding pack that includes a pretty substantial pillow and a good quality duvet. This flight also featured Delta's brand new mattress toppers which are now available on all Delta 1 flights. At this seat were also noiseancelling headphones, a large bottle of water, and an amenity kit. Delta's current amenity kit is from a Sony. It has a dark blue soft leatherrett bag with a zipper and contains a small card for the brand, an eye mask, and some of the nicest airplane socks we've seen. Normally, these things are like tissue paper, but these were decidedly thick and even had a nice Delta logo on the back. Rounding out the kit are earplugs, Grown Alchemist brand hand cream and lip balm, a dental kit, and a cardboard pen. Prior to departure, we were served a welcome drink. The standard sparkling wine, orange juice, or a mimosa. We had a lengthy taxi this morning to get out to the runway, but once we were there, we were off. [Music] [Applause] There have been a number of wildfires in Spain this summer, so the skies are a little bit hazy. [Music] Now that we're up in the air, let's take a look at the onboard entertainment. One area where these seats really show their age is the if system. The screen swings out when you push a button to release it from the seat in front of you. My screen was not very bright, and the touch is not responsive. There is a remote, but in our experience, it takes a little getting used to, as the arrows work almost 90 degrees to what you would expect. The selection of movies and TV shows was similar to older Delta planes and was decent, but the more modern IF systems have more content. The flight tracker and moving map are almost completely useless and show just how much better the newer systems are on other aircraft. Just look at this graphic. As mentioned earlier, the seats also have a universal power outlet near your shoulder, and there's a USB port. These aircraft are also equipped with Wi-Fi, which is free for all Sky Miles members in all cabins. It worked fairly well and was relatively consistent across the flight. Shortly after takeoff, the flight attendants were up and hard at work. Service started with a hot towel, followed by a drink service, and nuts. Trevor and I both opted for a glass of the Bordeaux red wine. It was decent. However, in our experience, the red wines in Delta 1 aren't very premium. Delta does also offer real champagne in Delta 1. Delta allows you to pre-order your meal a week ahead of the flight. Here's a look at the menu for today's route. I opted for the seafood paella and Trevor ordered the duck.com fee. [Music] following drinks and nuts, the starters arrived. The starter was a Thai coconut curry soup, chilled shrimp with herb crimp fish, a garden salad with roasted tomatoes, and a warm roll. The salad was actually the best part. The shrimp were good and tender, but we think the version with the aioli on some other routes is better. The soup was pretty good, but would have benefited from a little bit more curry flavor. The crew then moved on to mains. Their service was friendly and efficient on this flight. One thing to keep in mind is that the galley for Delta 1 on these A330s is at the back of the cabin, so they served rear to front. The paella included fish and shrimp. The fish was moist and not overcooked. The shrimp were also well prepared. The dish was a good take on paella, but after a few days in Valencia on this trip, not terribly authentic. The duckcomb feet came with spiced poached pears, carrots, kale, and mashed potatoes. The dish overall was good, but a little bland. The sauce didn't have much flavor, but when all mixed together, it was decent. It was nice to have the fresh veggies, which were well cooked and still had some texture, which is nice, and it wasn't overly heavy. The duck was shredded and served as sort of a ball wrapped in the skin. The duck was a little dry, and there was a tiny bone fragment, so this was a miss, we'd say. For dessert, the options were fruit and cheese, ice cream sundaes, or a Sarrento lemon cake. I opted for the ice cream. Trevor had the lemon cake. The cake was a dome of whipped cream with a thin slice of cake with lemon filling and coated with a thin layer of chocolate. This was light, fresh, and enjoyable. The entire main meal service was completed about 2 hours after departure. During the flight, the crew made themselves available for drink refills. They set up snacks and bottled water in the forward galley, and passengers were welcome to help themselves. Mid-flight, the crew baked cookies. This is one of our favorite features of Delta 1, and the flight attendants often take pride in the fresh baked chocolate chip cookies at 36,000 ft. During the flight, we came down the East Coast and had some great views in New York. About 90 minutes before arrival, the crew came around with a hot snack. The options were a pizza or a cheeseburger. I opted for the burger and requested the cheese be removed before they heated it up, and the person was happy to oblige. I made this request earlier in the flight since I don't eat cheese. Trevor was offered a tomato and basil pizza. They had run out of the burger by the time they reached midc cabin. He reported that the pizza was actually really good. The crust was crisp and soft, not soggy at all. The pizza came with roasted vegetables and pesto and a very dense chocolate cake. After the snack, it was about time to descend into Atlanta. Enjoy the landing and we'll be back to wrap things up. [Music] We landed from the west and then taxied to gate F1. So that's the Delta 1 experience on the A330 from Madrid to Atlanta. While these seats are definitely not as private as some of Delta's newer seats, the flight was comfortable and the crew was great. While old, the seats are definitely spacious. Delta excels at the soft product with a friendly and responsive crew and decent food. The hard product is inconsistent. Delta has too many aircraft with different Delta 1 seats, but they are working to bring the fleet closer to alignment. These A330s are some of the oldest business class seats in Delta's lineup, but that should start to disappear next year. To recall a bit, if you want to fly Delta's latest product, look for the A330 900 Neo or A350 aircraft. You'll also find upgraded Delta 1 seats on the 767s. They just won't have closing doors. A few months ago, we flew Delta 1 to Lima, Peru on an Airbus A350. We'll link that review down in the description. That plane had a unique configuration that's about to disappear. Also, make sure you check out our entire Spain playlist. We'll be releasing new content over the next few months, including hotel reviews, city tours, and Spain by highspeed rail. If you enjoy this video, please give it a thumbs up and make sure you subscribe to keep up with our latest content. Both of these are a great way you can help out the channel. We really appreciate it. Thank you for watching. We'll see you on the next adventure.

reviews.transcript_full:
Today I'm flying to Taipei, but this time my lovely
wife and daughter are joining me. We are in Munich and we are going to fly
with EVA air on their 787-9 to Taipei in the newest
business class cabin or Royal Laurel class as EVA air calls its premium product. Since EVA Air doesn't have a lounge in Munich, we opted for a Lufthansa Senator lounge G 24. Access is for Star Alliance Gold members
Or member with Lufthansa Senator status. Other elite and premium travelers
can use Lufthansa Business Class Lounge. The lounge is small and quiet, which was
perfect for us traveling with a toddler. Our natural light is limited
with only source being a narrow glass wall behind the bar. Our gate was located outside the Schengen area,
So we have to go through immigration, Make sure to allow enough
time as it can take a while Traveling with a toddler meant
we had priority boarding, allowing us to be among the first
to board a plane. We were warmly greeted and guided to our seats. The first impression of the EVA Air 787 Dreamliner cabin was stunning It is a significant upgrade
from their business class cabin on the Boeing 777 we tried last year. EVA Air 787-9 seats 304 passengers 26 in Business Class and 278 Economy Class Economy Class seats are in rows 20 to 55 configured in a 3-3-3 layout except for row 37, 40, and 50 he business class cabin featured 26 business class seats in a 1-2-1 staggered layout across a single cabin eat 1A & 1K are the most private However, it is closer to the galley,
So it might be noisier. Solo passenger’s should opt for windows seat for best privacy but since its staggered configuration seats with row 2, 5 and 7 are closer to the window and are more shielded While row 1, 3, 6 and 8 are closer to the aisle and more exposed The middle seat are the best choice for who is traveling together But keep in mind that someone will be in a more exposed seat given the staggered configuration and with the Vantage XL seat the seat console will create a gap between the seats It's also worth noting that the seats in Row 7 only have 1 window and there is no row 4 its because the word 4 is pronounced similar to “death” in Chinese The design of the seats are very futuristic and clean. EVA Air use Thompson Aero Vantage XL Seats n their business class on their 787-9 Same as Scandinavian use on their A330. Check out my review if you're interested. But the seats on EVA Air was much better
and offers more privacy. In the front of your seat,
you'll find an 18 inch HD IFE screen. Next to that is a larger literature pocket. The space underneath the footwell was made
into a slope surface to rest your feet Instead of a space for luggage storage, so a larger carry ons items would need
to be stored in the overhead bins. The side console in the middle seats
offer extra storage space, Which were nice to store your shoes
and slippers. The middle seats feature a small privacy
divider that can be laid back and forth. The side console offer a large white surface space with a control panel Here you find the seat controls which included three preset positions Separate buttons for adjusting
the leg rest, a do not disturb button, Massage function and light adjustment. And on the left side
you'll find a headphone jack. universal power outlet with an USB A port and the IFE remote controller Behind that was the enclosed storage compartment with two decent sized storage units,
one for the headphone. And the other one for smaller items. There were also a vanity mirror inside And right next to the storage
compartment was a flip out reading light. Underneath the console surface. there's a simpler set of seat controls Above that is a push button for the tray table. which swings out as a single wooden surface from within the console It's not particularly large, but
it's well-built and it can be adjusted Forward and backward Since we sat in the middle seat, we had an additional small privacy divider. It provides some privacy. But not as much as the newer business
class seats on the market. Since this is a staggered configuration,
my wife was more exposed to the aisle. On this side there was an adjustable armrest. It's worth mentioning that there isn't a private divider on the aisle side so you are quite exposed in a seat. And it's also worth noting that the 787 cabin on EVA Air doesn't have individual air nozzles. Upon boarding pillow, blanket and a amenity kit was already placed at our seats.  A moment after settling in, we were offered pre-departure drinks with a choice of champagne, sparkling water or juice. We both opted for orange juice. We both opted for orange juice so Sky could drink with us We were also served a warm towel Later on we got offered pajamas and slippers by Jason Wu. Last but not least, we was given a full menu and wine list. Just right before takeoff, the flight
attendant took food and drink orders. Along with the amenity kit, we received a small chocolate bar and a poem on a printed card,
Which was a very unique touch. Soon after takeoff, the meal service began. The meal service on this flight features a six course meal. And here's what was on food and drink menu for today's flight. There's also possibility to preorder your meal online ahead of the flight. The online menu showed the standard meal choices, along with handful choices that are only available online. This is similar to the book option offered by Singapore Airlines, except EVA Air has fewer choices. Nonetheless, selecting a meal is always
appreciated and adds a nice premium touch. For the amuse-bouche we got served Puff with Austrian bacon. Goat cheese wrapped with zucchini. Our rating 8/10 Next up was Hors D´oeuvre which was Grilled Prawn and Octopus with Quinoa Salad The dish was a bit strange for our taste. Our rating 5/10 Next up was carrot and ginger soup. The soup was creamy and delicious even Sky liked it very much Our rating 8/10 After the soup we got served Garden vegetable Salad with Balsamic olive oil It’s salad, nothing special about this Sky passed on the salad and continued with her yoghurt. For my main course, I opted for one of the online exclusive option.  Lobster with ginger scallion sauce. The lobster was delicious and sweet. And generously sized. I really enjoyed the noodles as well. My rating 8/10 Wifey also opted for one of the online exclusive option. Grilled teriyaki glazed salmon filet. Her rating 9/10 It was good to see Sky enjoy the food, especially since it's a bit
challenging to get a toddler to eat while traveling. For dessert,
I opted for cheese plate and ice cream. The cheese plate was quite good and
the ice cream was absolutely delicious. My rating 8/10 All three of us was now stuffed
and ready to dry off the bed. But before that, let's
check out the lavatory. For business class passengers. There are three lavatories in total. Two lavatories are behind the cabin
and one in front. The laboratory was a standard industry
sized but very clean. There's a larger lavatory located
on the right side behind the cabin. It also had a nice amenities
like earplugs, mouthwash, a dental kit and toiletries from 4711 Aqua Colonia. One of the flight attendent offered wifey turndown service So it was perfect. Time to change into pajamas. The pajamas was very comfortable and cozy,
and we got pajamas in different colors. In lie flat bed mode. the business class seat has a pretty standard width And it was wide enough for wifey and Sky
to sleep together. The footwell was wide and we had enough space both at the feet and in the knee area which was noticeable since both of us
liked to sleep on the side. One thing worth mentioning that my seat in lie-flat bed mode feels quite cocooned compared to to wifey seat If you tend to feel claustrophobic, a seat closer to the aisle might be a better fit for you The cabin light was swiftly dimmed
completely. Leaving all this soft glow. EVA Air signature starry night
lighting on the ceiling. All right lets check out the amenity kit EVA Air amenity kits are from a collaboration with Giorgio Armani And it is the most impressive amenity kit I every gotten a business class flight. For outbound flights from Taipei. Passenger will receive a champagne colored
hardcase adorned with pebble patterned. And passenger will receive a black soft
bag overnight kit bearing a Japanese Tatami mat pattern on a flight to Taipei. Amenity kits contains
a coin purse, eye mask, branded keychain. Discount code. Dental kit. Earplugs. Weirdo murderer. Lip balm. Facial mist. Hand and body lotion. I didn’t use the IFE much during this flight but I did spend a few minutes browsing through EVA Air’s Star Gallery in-flight entertainment system. The user interface was well-designed
and easy to use, and the selection of movies and television
shows was varied and plentiful, but it was very laggy during my flight. The IFE can also be controlled
via remote control. Which has its own small touchscreen. If you like, you can also watch movies
From the remote control screen. EVA Air also provides noise
canceling headphones. I didn't try them on this flight but Sky did, and she seemed happy and calm with them 787 also features Wi-Fi from Panasonic
with the following pricing. The Wi-Fi had a limited data cap
and it seems quite expensive. So I didn't find it
necessary to purchase it. I only tested the complimentary wifi
and the speed was just okay. It's made me feel better
about not paying for it. Sky woke up about two hours before the second meal service. And thankfully EVA Air has a snack menu available. Known as Leisure Delights. So we decided to try it out. We ordered a stir fried rice cake
with Chinese sausage and instant noodles. Both of the dishes was just okay. The second meal service
started two hours before landing. Starting off with hot towel service and some fruits For breakfast. I opted for Chinese style
and wifey for Western style. Chinese style breakfast was congee
with typical Chinese side dishes Our rating 7/10 And a western side breakfast contain
bread and yogurt, for starters. And for the main course wifey opted for the sweet option  sweet curd crepe with raspberry sauce Our rating 9/10 After being very impressed
by our previous flight on EVA Air Boeing 777. We had some expectation for the premium
cabin experience on EVA Air. New Dreamliner cabin. I'm happy to say that those expectations were fully met The new business class seats on the 787 are very well-designed, combining all the important elements
into a cohesive unit. Although it is not very private
compared to newer business class products like Qatar Qsuites or ANA The Room. But it's offer even better experience than the reverse herringbone seats on the Boeing 777. Eva Air's in-flight service was topnotch. The crew on our flight
were always friendly and attentive. Taking good care of us during the meal and
checking in on us throughout the flight. And they were extremely quick
and efficient during the meal service. Speaking of meal service. Really are impressed that there's a six
course meal on this flight. The food was quite good, But it didn't reach the same level
of quality as Qatar Airways. The option to preorder meals from a wide
ranging menu was a nice feature. even though the option isn’t wide as Singapore Book the cook.  And of course, the amenity
kit is one of the best I received from a business class flight. he dust bag and the coin purse are nice extra touches that enhance the luxury feeling Overall, this flight to Taipei was incredibly comfortable While there are few business class products I'd prefer over EVA Air I highly recommend you to experience their 787 business class if you have the opportunity—you won't regret it! e hope you enjoyed watching our video and sharing in our incredible flight with EVA Air business class Royal Laurel on their 787-9 Consider the
like or subscribe to our channel, and we'll look forward to bring you more
amazing content in the future. Until then, take
care and see you next time.

reviews.transcript_full: With more screens, on more aircraft than any airline in the world, Delta is known for its continued investment and seat back entertainment.  Today, Delta raises the bar again with the next step in the evolution of its groundbreaking wireless inflight entertainment system.  Beginning with a welcome screen personalized to your cabin, the Delta Flight Products Design Interface brings a feature rich entertainment experience that is both familiar and cutting edge.  The intuitive navigation system lets you explore content with the same ease of use you are accustomed to at home and on your mobile devices.  Techie extras bring the flying experience to life and offer opportunities to engage with the world around you.  And it's all showcased on brilliant oversized screens. Some of the largest seat back screens you'll find anywhere.  The biggest entertainment studio in the sky is now one of the most immersive and most engaging in the sky.  With the launch of Delta's first Airbus A330 Neo, this next-generation entertainment system takes flight.  It's part of Delta's commitment to elevating the customer experience and it's only the beginning.  We know you live every day to the fullest and with thoughtful innovation, we're making sure your journey with us is just as memorable as the destination.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to the TALA exhibition at the Dubai Show in 2011. Today we're here demonstrating  some equipment from the Inflight Entertainment and Connectivity Group, based in Erlinon,  California. We're showing examples of equipment which will be installed on various aircraft  times from 2012 onwards and forms part of our next generation Inflight Entertainment  platform which is known as top series avont. We're showing examples of the economy seat  screen which is a 12 inch capacitive touch screen interface and supports high definition  video, MPAC 4 and a very very wide range of applications delivered through the use of  the Android operating software and the Android market. As you can see it's a very  responsive interface. We have swipe capability which is very much in line with the latest  consumer electronics devices which are available in the marketplace. The viewing experience  for the passenger is a very rich and high quality video stream and again integrates the  latest in high definition close caption capabilities. All of the passenger interface functions  are integrated into the screen itself which means we can avoid the need for a control  handset which is particularly valuable in economy class configurations in terms of reducing  weight and minimizing maintenance. We're also integrating what we call smart passenger  interface modules and each of these modules is independently changeable so we can have  a combination of audio, Apple device connectivity USB and then we've also got an example here  of an early prototype of a webcam for barcode reader technology. We also have moving  map and information services which we take from the aircraft location based information  and for the first time we're showing use of the Android operating system which means  for the first time we can integrate games directly from the Android marketplace. Here's  an example of a very popular application we've taken directly from the Android marketplace.  This is a much more consumer oriented experience than current systems are capable of offering.  It's a very graphically rich and extremely responsive solution. Obviously we don't necessarily  supply the headset to our airline clients they're usually selecting those themselves.  What we have been able to do is introduce some new software based solutions which are independent  of the hardware itself independent of the headset. A good example of this is a 3D audio  technology that we launched earlier this year on an Air China and this enables a very  similar experience to a surround sound home theatre entertainment offering without any  changes to the hardware or the headset. Independent of the hardware independence of the headset  itself we're able to greatly improve the audio experience for the passengers.  But today you interface with an iP system with a touchscreen or the actual controller but  we've actually introduced a third interface which is gesture control. So basically with  my hand I can actually easily navigate through the screen without ever touching the screen.  So I have truly a unique experience for a passenger to be able to navigate through movies  and be able to launch movies as well. So in addition to that experience you can also  have controls over the player controls. So I can actually pause this movie. I can go back  to the beginning to something else all with the navigation of a hand. I can go to Album  Art and be able to navigate through my selection of Album Art that I may have. I'm  able to listen to music as well. We actually have some airlines that are very interested.  We're still in the ghostings with them. We're hoping to bring this in the next year at  least to the market. It's not something that would replace the current Avant system but  an enhancement to the experience for the passenger. Everything that we're trying to do is really  trying to evolve the experience. What you do on the ground, the passenger to expect to be  able to do it the air. So now that they have Xbox and Wii's on the ground, you now can  bring that experience up into the air and have games and transfer that experience. We don't  have to touch the screen. If you're in a lay down bed seat, you don't have to hunt for your  controller. You can just navigate and it just creates a different experience when you're  interfacing as well. I'm interested in we've had some germophobes that said this is great  because they don't actually have to touch the screen.

reviews.transcript_full:
Hello! As you know, you take a plane
when you want to travel quickly. Yet, the trip can still be long
if you’re going half way around the world! On long-haul flights, especially,
it‘s important to travel in comfort and not just have to count
the passing clouds for entertainment. So airline companies have made
passenger satisfaction a priority. In particular, via two key
pieces of equipment: the seats and the entertainment systems. More than just something to sit on,
the aircraft seat blends design with safety, thanks to prototypes
developed in top secrecy. Made from light materials to guarantee
minimum weight and maximum solidity, it's designed to absorb shocks and to keep the passenger firmly in place,
even in case of turbulence. And because passengers spend most
of their journey sitting or lying down, aircraft seats have to be comfortable,
whatever class they happen to be in. So, on long haul flights,
you find 4 types of seats, a different seat
equipping each travel class: Economy Class... Premium Economy Class... Business Class... and First Class. For airlines, the choice of seat is a way
of differentiating their company. They choose its design, its covering and its color. But also the LOPA,
the Layout of Passenger Accommodations. Basically, how the seats
are positioned in the cabin. Other accessories possibly integrated
into the seat are up to the airlines. For example, the headrest, the provision of electrical power sockets, or even stowage. But airline companies also focus
their attention on another key element: the choice of screen. User-friendly interfaces, diversity
and quality of content, reliability... Indeed, airlines pay special attention
to their choice of IFE: In-Flight Entertainment systems. The most recent feature:
a touch-screen... that lets you watch movies, listen to music, play games, pull up a flight plan, check out the meal menus, or even order duty-free merchandise. Usually, all content is hosted
on one or several servers that then feeds all the screens. But Safran has developed a revolutionary
new IFE system called RAVE: a stand-alone system,
equipped with broadband connectivity, integrated into
a high-resolution 4K screen that hosts the content independently. The beauty of this system
is its ease of maintenance, because,
as opposed to other systems, here,
if one screen goes down, the other passenger screens
are not impacted. What’s more, RAVE is equipped
with a very high performance, interference-free
Bluetooth audio connection that provides the passenger
with superb listening comfort when synchronized with their own headset. And so... this system allows passengers
to personalize their content according to their areas of interest. In short, trips have never seemed shorter, even when you’re flying
half way around the world! There, now you know everything,

reviews.transcript_excerpt:

captions.text:
additional forms of entertainment

reviews.transcript_full:
For most passengers, long-haul flights are 
a matter of endurance aided by a few drinks,   inflight entertainment, and trying to get some 
sleep between meal services. It is an entirely   different matter for the people flying the plane 
as there are still plenty of things to do even   after takeoff. Let’s look at what’s happening 
on the flight deck during these longer flights… Even though flight paths are decided upon 
before departure, pilots have to monitor   weather conditions and decide whether 
or not to alter them during the flight.   On long-haul flights, weather conditions are 
more likely to change from initial forecasts,   with aircraft often encountering multiple 
weather systems. These systems can vary in   intensity from slight turbulence to dangerous 
thunderstorms. Traveling at high speeds,   pilots must be prepared at all times 
to alter the flight path if necessary. If, for example, they see a 
thunderstorm on the radar,   they must first get the OK from air traffic 
control (ATC) to change their route. Clear air turbulence is another worry, and 
because it cannot be seen on the radar,   pilots rely upon the information provided by 
pilots flying the same route ahead of them. When   flying across oceans such as the Atlantic, one 
pilot's job is to communicate with the ATC while   the other monitors a common air-to-air frequency 
that pilots use to communicate with each other. The entire time a flight is 
in the air, the pilots monitor   all kinds of gauges to ensure that the 
plane performs how it is supposed to. Making sure that the temperature of the fuel 
is not too cold is another thing pilots must   monitor. If the fuel cools down too much, 
its flow can be restricted due to waxing.   If this happens, pilots can rectify 
the situation by descending, or by   increasing the aircraft's speed (and, 
thus, its skin temperature). However,   this isn't a particularly frequent occurrence, 
as engine oil helps fuel to retain heat. While one of the pilots monitors all the 
gauges, the other will be busy taking care   of the paperwork. Before the flight, the 
pilots are given a written flight plan.   Anything that deviates from this 
must be written down as notes. Outside of these important activities, 
long-haul flying can be very boring for pilots.   During cruise phases, pilots will often pass 
the time by making small talk with one another,   or doing some reading. Smartphone games and 
good old fashioned crossword puzzles might be   additional forms of entertainment 
found on the flight deck. Finally, just like passengers, 
enjoying inflight meals   is another part of the long-haul pilot experience. The pilots typically wait until the passengers 
have been served and then eat separately.   They do this so that there is 
always one person at the controls. For long flights over twelve hours, there 
are one or two relief pilots onboard   so that the two pilots who performed the 
takeoff can take a break and get some rest. There are just two pilots on shorter 
long-haul flights of eight or nine   hours. The only opportunity they get to 
leave their seats and stretch their legs   is when they go to the bathroom. Did you know about these long-haul duties and 
activities? Let us know by leaving a comment.

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Chicago Hair International Airport.  Today you'll join me on a business class journey to Munich aboard Lufthansa's A350.  This flight is part of my return trip between Vienna and Chicago, initially booked an economy  for 751 euros, then upgraded using e-vouchers from my mouse and more senator's status.  Unlike Austrian Airlines and Swiss, which operate out of Terminal 5, Lufthansa shares Terminal  1 with United Airlines.  We arrived at the airport just before 5pm, only to discover that the check-in desks wouldn't  open until 10 past 6.  Anticipating this, we queued up at 550 as the staff began to appear and the desks opened  slightly ahead of schedule.  Check-in and priority security were remarkably efficient and we found ourselves at the  sea gates in no time.  Traveling through O'Hare's iconic tunnel, a brief 3-minute walk brought us to the highlight  of our early arrival, the United Polaris Lounge.  Exclusively available to international, star alliance, business or first class passengers,  the Polaris Lounge offers the finest lounge experience in Chicago.  Even if your flight departs from a different terminal, you can switch terminals airside  to indulge in this unparalleled oasis of comfort and luxury.  Feeling hungry, we bypassed the drinks counter and the inviting seating pods and headed straight  for the dining room, the Allacard restaurant of the lounge.  While reservations are possible during busy times, we were fortunate to find the lounge  almost empty, securing a table immediately.  The menu, though small, was perfectly curated.  In a business class lounge, quality over quantity is key and a limited selection ensured each  dish was of top-notch quality.  We settled into a cozy booth with a view of the dining area and enjoyed a delightful meal.  I opted for the signature burger, customizable with a variety of toppings and it exceeded  my expectations.  For those in a hurry or seeking a quick snack, the expansive buffet offers a variety of options.  The lounge also features a manned bar for alcoholic beverages.  As a huge fan of cocktails, I eagerly ordered an old-fashioned but was disappointed by how  overly sweet it was.  I decided to switch to champagne for the rest of our stay, which proved to be a much better  choice.  It's worth noting that the bar expects you to tip, which I find a bit off-putting in  a lounge setting.  The lounge provides excellent apron views, though there wasn't much activity to observe  during our visit.  As our time in the lounge drew to the close, we learned that the showers and nap rooms  were already closed as well, which was a minor disappointment.  However, the all-gender restrooms were plentiful, spacious and impeccably clean, adding to  the overall comfort of our lounge experience.  After a delightful stay in the lounge, we made our way back through the tunnel and headed  to the B gates, where two Lufthansa flights, one to Frankfurt and our Sumeunik, were scheduled  to depart from neighboring gates in quick succession.  These convergence created a somewhat chaotic scene, with passengers crowding the area.  However, when priority boarding commenced, we swiftly left the crowd behind and joined  the queue to board our aircraft, an Airbus A350-900.  The A350 features eight rows in a 2-2-2 business class configuration.  The larger cabin spans rows 1-2-6, while a more intimate mini cabin occupies rows 7-8.  For this flight, we selected Seats 7 Hotel and 7 Kilo in the bulkhead row of the smaller  cabin, seeking a bit more privacy.  We were warmly greeted at the door, and again, as we made our way down the aisle, but unfortunately,  that was the extent of the warm hospitality we had anticipated.  Currently, the most common business class product in Lufthansa's fleet is starting to see  a change with the introduction of their new Aliegris business class, which debuted on  the Munich-Tubank Uber route on May 1, 2024.  While this older configuration is certainly outdated and lacks privacy, it does offer an  advantage for couples like us who enjoy sharing a window seat.  Here's a clear view of row 8, along with a look at the bulkhead footwell, which was  unfortunately smaller than I had hoped for.  However, this was not the biggest issue I encountered with the seat.  More on that later.  We had ample time to settle in, as the crew assigned to our cabin was noticeably absent.  It wasn't until long after the left side of our cabin had been served the welcome drinks  that we were finally offered a glass of champagne.  Let's take a closer look at the seat.  Unfortunately, there are no individual air vents.  The aisle seat offers a bit more storage space than the window seat, thanks to the litter  richer pocket positioned between the footwells.  The closed cubby initially housed the amenity kit and a water bottle.  Head folds outwards in the middle.  Between the seats there are two universal power outlets.  The whole next to them housed the AKG on ear headphones and the headphone jack.  On top of the consoles are the controls for the air cushioned seat and a flap opens up  to reveal the tray table and IFE remote.  Underneath the console is a USB-A port.  The tray table is released by pushing on it and folds out to double the surface area.  Although there was some flex, it felt sturdy overall.  The remote uses a D pad instead of the cursor found on other Loftanza planes.  My left armrest could be lowered to widen the bed or make it easier to leave the seat  with the table deployed.  The headrest which also houses a reading lamp is adjustable as well.  Here you can see the amenity kit, a pouch from Portia design containing the bar essentials  and a few lotions from Lotsitun.  Next to the IFE screen there is a coat hook and a holder for your glasses.  After take off the meal service began with a hot towel.  As is typical with overnight flights from the US, the selection was somewhat limited and  the meal was served on one tray to save time.  If you're eager to get to sleep you can opt for the Express service.  Nuts were handed out with the drink service.  For my main course I chose the surf and turf which was easily the best dish I enjoyed  on this flight.  The appetizer salad wasn't too my liking but the ice cream provided a satisfying conclusion  to the meal as I decided to skip the cheese course.  The restroom was a standard A350 bathroom featuring a full body mirror and a few amenities  stocked on the counter.  In addition to soap there was also lotion available.  As for the seats they are slightly angled towards the fuselage unlike the bulkhead.  The IFE screens fold out slightly but unfortunately cannot be angled downwards when you're in  bed mode which can't be inconvenient.  The entertainment selection was just okay.  I found a few movies that caught my interest but frequent flyers might quickly exhaust the  available content.  The user interface worked well with the remote but the limitations of the system became  apparent when trying to scroll with a finger.  The TV show selection was a significant letdown.  While waiting for the flight map to load I checked out the Wi-Fi prices.  25 euros gets you unlimited data with the highest speed for the entire flight.  The plane is equipped with three cameras providing different views during the journey.  Lufcans are offers unpackaged headphones for their business class customers with ear  pad covers available in the amenity kit.  As usual I opted to use my AirFlight Pro Bluetooth transmitter in conjunction with my AirPods  Max.  Before bed the crew handed out a small box of pre-leens a delightful touch to end the evening.  As I mentioned before the seat is air cushioned theoretically allowing you to adjust the firmness  of the mattress.  Unfortunately an hour after I managed to fall asleep I awoke with hip pain because the  bottom half of the seat had completely deflated leaving me lying on the metal frame.  The crew had to partially disassemble the seat to check all the hoses and restart it.  Luckily this fixed the issue but it still disrupted my sleep.  Unlike on other long haul flights to Asia for example no mattress pads slippers or sleeping  shirts were provided on this flight.  Breakfast was served on a single tray which was perfectly fine.  The Greek yogurt bowl was into my liking but the rest of the breakfast dish was okay.  I was left a bit underwhelmed by this flight.  The crew member attending to us throughout the journey neither greeted us nor smiled during  any interaction.  It is heartening to feel like a burden to the crew especially when you are being friendly  and not making any special requests. Your author recently experienced his first actual, real-world 4K video on board a Cathay Pacific A321neo this month, in conjunction with Cathay’s launch of 4K HDR content last month (for which, full disclosure, he was a guest of the airline), and the experience was an absolute joy.

Safran Passenger Innovations (SPI) has enjoyed an impressive trajectory in embedded inflight entertainment and today is seen as delivering proverbial ‘Cadillac’ IFE systems to airlines around the globe.

And a joint ideation project between SPI and Lufthansa led to the launch of new docked companion tablets that enable Allegris business class passengers to control their IFE, seat functionality, lighting and thermal environment with the device.
But SPI is also focused on what it says is a more sustainable approach to embedded IFE.

And so, when it set about to design its next-generation system, it didn’t just adopt new display and processor technology — 4K miniLED HDR 10+ Liquid Crystal Displays for the former and Snapdragon for the latter — it also worked to slash weight to reduce CO2 emissions.

Also driving weight savings is a decision by SPI to tuck a lightweight DC power system into the seat leg to power its RAVE Ultra plus 13.3″ displays in economy class and provide up to 60W of USB charging per passenger.

SPI also developed a product that allows AC power in economy to be selected as an option, explaining thusly: “The solution is deployed by distributing AC power directly to AC outlets located in every seat from a small number of power distribution points located throughout the cabin.

For example, below each 13.3″ display sits what Asmar calls “the little pill at the front” which features the USB ports and the audio socket, presently available in four combos (including USB-A and/or USB-C).

yt_comments.text: Pretty good overall — a comfortable, sleep-focused flight rather than a “wow” luxury experience ✈ The big wins were the Qantas A380 business seat, mattress pad, quiet/smooth ride, and crew. He apparently slept about 9 hours, which is basically the holy grail on a 16h48m flight. The weak points were pretty clear: Food: dinner was decent, but snack/breakfast sounded poor — lots of commenters also thought the catering looked below business-class standard. Entertainment/tech: limited IFE and no Wi-Fi, so the product feels dated. Ground experience: denied Flagship Lounge access, then ended up in a crowded Admirals Club. So: great bed, great crew, mediocre food, outdated tech. For a 17-hour Dallas–Sydney flight, I’d call it a successful flight — just not a top-tier business class experience like Singapore, Emirates, Qatar, etc. 😄

yt_comments.text: Qantas chose Viasat, not Starlink, and its long-haul retrofit is moving slowly — especially on the A380. ✈ On that Dallas–Sydney QF8 A380, the main reasons are: 1. Qantas already committed to Viasat Qantas announced its international Wi-Fi rollout using Viasat’s next-generation satellite network, with A330, 787 and A380 aircraft to be progressively retrofitted. That means they are not simply installing Starlink like Qatar or United. 2. A380 retrofits are hard Qantas said older A380s are especially challenging because they were built before modern onboard internet infrastructure was common. Installing Wi-Fi means adding antennas/radomes and aircraft wiring — basically physical surgery on the aircraft roof. Qantas specifically said the A380 is the most challenging fleet to retrofit. 3. Qantas is doing it during maintenance, not all at once The first international Wi-Fi aircraft were A330s, mainly for Asia routes. Qantas said 787, A380 and A330-300 installations would follow later, so the A380 fleet is behind the smaller/easier aircraft. 4. Coverage over the Pacific is still a weak spot for Qantas Qantas’ own Wi-Fi page says international connectivity can vary, and it lists areas where coverage is not available, including the South Pacific Ocean — exactly the kind of region a Dallas–Sydney flight crosses. 5. Other airlines moved faster with Starlink Qatar Airways, for example, has already equipped nearly 120 widebody aircraft with Starlink and completed its A350 rollout. That is why Starlink feels “already here” on some airlines while Qantas still feels behind. So basically: Qantas bet on Viasat, the A380 is difficult to retrofit, and the Pacific coverage/rollout is lagging. Starlink may be faster, but switching providers is expensive and disruptive once an airline has contracts, hardware plans and maintenance schedules in place. Reuters also notes that changing satellite providers is costly because aircraft need provider-specific equipment and downtime for installation.

yt_comments.author: @high-reshallucinations
yt_comments.text: Other airlines moved faster with Starlink mainly because they had stronger urgency, easier rollout paths, and better timing than Qantas. 1. They picked Starlink early, while Qantas picked Viasat Qatar, United, Hawaiian and others committed to Starlink as their next big Wi-Fi upgrade. Qantas instead committed its international A330, 787 and A380 fleet to Viasat’s satellite network, so it is locked into a different hardware and provider path. 2. Starlink installations got faster after the first fleets Qatar is the best example. It said its Boeing 777 Starlink retrofit time dropped from three days to 9.5 hours per aircraft, letting it finish the 777 rollout in nine months, about 50% faster than planned. That kind of process improvement makes a rollout much faster once the airline, installer and regulator have the aircraft type figured out. 3. Some airlines made Wi-Fi a headline competitive feature United is using Starlink as a big customer-experience weapon. It completed Starlink installation on 300+ regional aircraft and said more than 25% of its daily departures had Starlink by February 2026, with plans for 500+ mainline aircraft by the end of 2026. 4. Regional/narrow-body aircraft are easier to roll out first United started with regional jets and then moved to mainline aircraft. That is easier than starting with huge long-haul widebodies. Qantas’ problem is the opposite: its most painful gap is on international widebodies, especially A380s. 5. Qantas’ A380s are especially difficult Qantas has said retrofitting older international aircraft is complex, and that the A380s are the most challenging aircraft in its fleet to retrofit. Even the first international A330-200 Wi-Fi retrofit took around three weeks in the hangar. 6. Starlink had momentum and hardware scale Reuters reported that Starlink now has contracts on more than 7,000 aircraft, and airlines are rushing to upgrade because fast/free Wi-Fi has become a premium-cabin expectation. Once many airlines choose the same supplier, certifications, installation know-how and supply chains improve quickly. So the simple version: Qatar and United treated Starlink like a strategic priority and scaled the retrofit fast. Qantas chose Viasat, has older hard-to-retrofit long-haul aircraft, and is moving more cautiously. 🛰✈

Sain later continued along those same lines, noting that it was the job of IFE manufacturers to “make it easy for airlines to deploy” the solutions, both hardware and software.
Dominic Green, Director of IFE at United Airlines , in a later conversation, confirmed this challenge and also the progress that has been made in addressing it.
We now have the ability to do stuff quickly, which historically was not a great feature of inflight entertainment systems.
Green further noted that the company pulls significantly more data off the aircraft now, and far more quickly than in the prior generations of the IFE platforms.
Sain also shared a vision where each IFE screen on board ties in to the on-board connectivity solution – likely LEO satellites – to deliver a personalized passenger experience.

I'm trying my best to continuously improve the quality of our videos and I recently  got a special filter for my camera lens to allow me to capture these stunning time-lapse  shots with motion blur and I'll incorporate them into more videos in the future.  And since not just our equipment, but also the animations and the flights themselves are  pricey, we rely on various types of support to run this channel.  As you might know, we rarely promote other companies and products here at SimpliViation  because I simply won't lend my credibility to shady VPNs and risky investment products.  But there is a company we have been working with for almost two years of which product  I am a very satisfied user which is sponsoring today's video.  Holtzcan is a jewelry brand with a special focus on watches offering a wide variety of  products to both men and women, headquartered right here where we live in beautiful Vienna,  Austria.  Myself own three different Holtzcan watches and love each of them individually for their  unique designs.  All of Holtzcan's products are made from natural materials like wood, stone or even leaves  and peacock feathers.  If you can't make up your mind of what to gift to that special someone for Christmas  this year, Holtzcan has designs for everyone from elegant to business eve, to casual and  modern and with their free worldwide express shipping you can place orders until December  19th for the product to still arrive in time for Christmas.  If I could interest you with that, go to Holtzcan.com.com.  SimpliViation and use coupon code aviation for 15% off your order, using this specific link  will make it more likely for Holtzcan to help us put more effort into our videos in the  future too.  Before we board our aircraft, let me also briefly give you some information on booking this  flight.  On JetBlue's website you can easily see the features and amenities offered on each flight,  plus the different bundles they offer where I'm going with blue as it allows me to pick  a window seat in advance which is always a priority for me when recording these reviews.  There are options to pre-order special meals for free and when selecting the seat you  may also opt for extra legroom or emergency exodrome seats for an additional fee.  For my regular seats I always consult a website called erolopa.com which is also kind  enough to allow me to use their seat maps in our videos to better illustrate the layouts  of the planes we're flying on.  Lopa by the way means layout or location of passenger accommodations and is an industry  term for seating charts.  The flight itself wasn't expensive at all, but I paid even less than that thanks to  a friend of mine who still had a jet blue voucher left over.  So special thanks to Keishi for helping me out.  I know Keishi from being a nerd for aviation and Japan and he runs a fantastic English language  block and aviation and aviation related news in Japan called K&A where he also regularly  posts great in-depth flight and hotel reviews and I highly recommend you give him a follow  and check out his blog.  The first of Amsterdam's two daily jet blue flights is departing to Boston right now  with our rights to JFK coming in as we speak.  Today we will be traveling aboard November 4076 Juliet, a brand new 2023 build Airbus 8321  NOL.  Generally speaking the 8321 NOL is the same plane as the regular 8321 NOL, the capacity  limits for seats and fuel are a bit different but apart from that the planes are almost identical  which is why Airbus was able to bring it to market that quickly.  The new 8321 XLR on the other hand has structural differences that took years of work to get  right and certified by authorities which is why it is only now starting to get delivered  to airlines.  Jet Blue has ordered a bunch of these as well which will allow the airline to launch flights  further into Europe but due to their recent poor financial performance jet blue has decided  to defer the deliveries of their 8321 XLRs beyond 2030 so it will be a while until we potentially  see jet blue planes in places like Milan or Zurich.  Jet Blue currently operates 11 Airbus 8321 NOL which is quite hard to find out because  as I mentioned the LRs are so similar to the regular Nios there is no official separate  type code for the LR which means most websites list them all together.  However it is easy to spot that the two sets of 8321 Nios at Jet Blue carry slightly  different registrations.  The ones starting with N2 are the regular 8321 Nios and the ones with N4 are the LRs.  Keep that in mind that information will be relevant towards the end of the video again.  Since I did an air site transit I wasn't able to drop off my suitcase but they were looking  for volunteers to check their bags anyway which gave me another option to get rid of it  for the flight.  Jet Blue's Airbus 8321 NOL Rs are equipped with two classes.  Up front there is the Mint Cabin featuring 24 Thompson Vantage solo seats in a 11 herring  bone layout.  This is followed by the 8321's standard 333 layout and economy class where Jet Blue  offers additional leg room for the first 5 rows recognizable by an orange headrest outline  but we want to see what an average seat is like so we are back here in 20F.  Jet Blue installed Collins Aerospace Meridian seats in economy class which come with adjustable  headrests both vertically as well as on the sides.  And we've also got a blanket but unfortunately no pillow.  This is standard on Jet Blue Transatlantic flights and even during booking we got the  information that a blanket would be offered but no mention of a pillow.  Seeing a 180cm tall the leg room is very impressive and I love that the seat back pockets  come with these handy little extra pockets for things like your phone.  Beneath the seats you will find universal power ports as well as USB-C ports offering  fast charging which were even fast enough to power my laptop.  There are two of each per every 3 seats.  We've also got a standard tray table as well as a non-adjustable entertainment touch screen  with the audio port and a USB-A port at the bottom.  In the ceiling above you will find both non-adjustable personal reading lights as well as adjustable  private airweds.  Code hooks are not installed.  Now here's where the journey gets interesting.  Before departure you need to select what you want to eat using the entertainment screen.  You can choose between one of three different main courses, all of which sounding really  tasty and then you can pick two out of three side dishes.  But there are some changes coming to this unique kind of service structure soon so stick  around until the end when I talk a bit more about that.  You can also choose which drink you want to have with your meal and I really like this  in particular because it gives a much better overview of what's even an offer.  Often times when I'm asked what I want to drink I don't even think that they would  have things like ginger ale.  On transatlantic flights both hot and cold, non-alcoholic as well as alcoholic drinks are  offered at no extra charge.  While we're at it let's also take a closer look at the entertainment system as a whole.  JetBlue uses Tali's Avent in flight entertainment system and while you can connect your phone  through the Wi-Fi with the system to use it as a remote control it sucks that such a  modern system does not support Bluetooth headphones.  Earbuds are provided by JetBlue but given how modern this brain is it would have been  better to include Bluetooth instead of the phone as a remote control thingy which let's  be honest is mostly just a gimmick.  And entertainment wise JetBlue offers a solid selection of movies and TV shows to stream  on demand as well as a small number of live TV channels.  Within the US JetBlue is known for offering dozens of live TV channels and the reason why  they don't on transatlantic flights is likely that it's a licensing issue.  US TV channels license content to show it to US audiences so an airline flying outside  of the US is likely not able to show these channels.  JetBlue more than makes up for that by offering tons of content and multiple episodes of  popular TV shows in addition to games and audio and a high quality in flight map application.  With that it's finally time to head out.  Given that JetBlue has inflated entertainment screens on all of their planes it does  surprise me that they still do manual safety demos as opposed to having a fun safety  game.  After take off the crew immediately began with their first round of service consisting  of just beverages.  As on all JetBlue flights sweet and savory snacks were available for free throughout the  entire flight but for now I was just craving a coffee and some sparkling water.  As we're leaving Ireland behind it's finally time for that main meal service.  It served in these uniform reusable containers and the crew puts together the meal from a few  large boxes they have on their meal cart checking their tablet computer for what you have  ordered.  I went with meatballs with tomato fero, the kale quinoa salad and the cucumber with vegan  ranch dressing.  It was served alongside a bottle of water and a bit of sweet and sour sauce.  All in all this was superb.  It was beautifully presented and very tasty and I highly appreciate how inventive and  healthy these dishes appear to be.  That's not a standard chicken or pasta choice, this is a meal service somebody put thought  into and I love it.  I'll share some more thoughts about this towards the end of the video when I also have to inform  you that JetBlue is going to cut all of this from their service but there's more to  this story for now let's get on with our flight.  The meal chocolate ice cream was handed out by the crew.  T and coffee were offered too.  The cabin of this A321neo is absolutely stunning.  Airbus calls this set of innovations and designs in their newest cabin's airspace.  And as part of these airspace cabins the overhead bins are notably larger allowing for more  cabin sized suitcases to be stored in each of them.  It also comes with LED lighting and certain new materials and innovations beyond the passenger  site which help the airline operate more efficiently.  One downside to operating A321neos across the Atlantic is that they are quite bothersome  for crews.  The galleys are much smaller, there is less space for passengers to loiter meaning that  everybody is in closer proximity to each other than they normally would be on a widebody  aircraft.  Because of that crews also don't have regular crew rest areas which is what this curtain  is for.  Behind that are a few seats blocked for the crew for when they are on break.  And if the plane operates a flight where no crew rest is necessary the curtain just  stays open and the seats get sold.  Another unique thing to this plane but unique to JetBlue not to the A321neo is the pantry.  Aborted transcontinental and transatlantic flights JetBlue offers a snack bar where  you can serve yourself at any point during the flight.  We've got pop chips, plantain chips, pretzel sticks, bottled water and the crew will also  help you with any additional beverage needs.  The lavatories are quite small but I do love the New York style wallpaper and the  waistband and flush are touch free.  As you can see with my shoes I'm a person who wears a lot of brown tones and these wooden  harts can watches fit my style phenomenally.  And by the way while the company designs the outside the inner clockwork are still manufactured  by renowned companies like Japanese watchmaker Seiko ensuring they last.  I can genuinely vouch for Haltscan's quality and reliability and can guarantee their products  will make great Christmas presents.  I got myself some snacks and drinks to enjoy the rest of the flight.  This is my personal favorite beverage combo on US Airlines.  This cranberry apple juice mixed with sparkling water so refreshing.  Another really cool thing about JetBlue is that they offer free unlimited wifi on transatlantic  flights and a usably fast one at that.  Before landing another hot snack is offered.  This time a slice of cheese pizza and some more water always stay hydrated on long haul  flights.  After a long flight half of the drowsiness you feel is simply dehydration.  The drier cabin air combined with sitting for prolonged periods of times and not drinking  enough liquids it strains your body more than any time difference usually does.  As we're starting our descent into New York there are quite a few things we still need  to address.  First, let's recap the good things because there are a lot.  Free unlimited wifi is such a handy component to this flight especially with the speeds  it offers as I was able to get a decent amount of work done on this flight.  I also love the main meal service not just where the dish is inventive, healthy and  balanced.  I also found them to be delicious and in a world where plenty of airlines just try to  make the cheapest pasta with cheese they can I appreciate JetBlue putting so much thought  and effort into their economy class meals.  The beverage selection also left nothing to be desired and I'm a big fan of the pantry  being there as a standard feature not just a will they won't they have snacks in the  back which for many airlines you don't know until you check.  But there are all the things that bothered me mainly because I'm unable to understand  the reasonings behind them.  Front and center being that the ive system does not support Bluetooth headphones either  tollies does not offer this feature yet or JetBlue opted against it both not good for  a plane that will remain flying with this cabin for probably another decade.  Bluetooth headphones are ubiquitous already and will only increase in adoption further  down the road.  I also believe it would be in JetBlue's own interest to provide pillows.  If I think about this journey and which service elements gave me the least return in terms  of comfort compared to their price to the airline, a pillow simply wouldn't be the  first thing I would cut.  Since the main meal was so substantial and the pantry being offered on all transatlantic  flights, I would argue it's the cheap slice of pizza that brought the least additional  comfort relative to its price.  So I would say JetBlue should think about cutting that and instead give everyone pillows.  But JetBlue has put some additional thought into their transatlantic product and they  have made a decision regarding their main meal service.  Being right now they will cut the hot main dish meaning it'll be just a cold meal.  Now calm down.  I know there have been heated reactions to this and people calling JetBlue cheap skates  and whatnot but after researching these changes and even reaching out to JetBlue directly,  I believe the airline actually deserves to be cut some slack here.  First, the main meal service will still feature various high quality items.  They're not going down to doing cheap mass produced wraps and sandwiches but rather  still offer thoughtfully crafted dishes that I would argue sound still better cold than  what you might find on other airline served warm.  The current menus can be found on their website and while the selection got smaller, only  offering two main dishes as opposed to three and just two sides, the inventiveness seems  to still be there, although it is undeniably disappointing that the cool select your  sides and main dish is no more.  JetBlue gave us the following statement saying that this change is part of our effort  to ensure we can continue to provide a great experience at JetBlue's competitive fairs  on these routes.  In addition to our dig meals, our transatlantic flights offer fast and free fly-fi and  seatback entertainment at every seat.  Pre-landing light bites vary based on route and aircraft and have not changed with the  new menus, JetBlue continues to provide free unlimited snacks and drinks available during  the InFlight service and self-service from the JetBlue pantry.  Which raises the question, why?  Why would JetBlue do that?  They did mention their effort to provide competitive fairs which puts a financial reasoning behind  that, and while I'm sure that is the case with reducing the number of options, I don't  think that it is necessarily cheaper to provide a high quality cold dish as opposed to a  high quality hot dish.  There is something else a hot dish needs though, and that's galley space and ovens  to heat it up.  And that's where the different registration is for regular A321 Nios and LRs I mentioned  earlier in the video coming.  So my personal assumption as to why the meals are now served cold is that due to delivery  delays at Airbus as well as the persistent issues with preten Whitney Geert's Tourbuffin  engines, JetBlue was forced to send their regular A321 Nios across the Atlantic on selected  flights last season, replacing the originally scheduled A321 Nios LRs.  Now the A321 Nios can do those routes, likely somewhat weight restricted but they have the  same type of seats so it doesn't matter too much from the perspective of the passenger.  Or so it seems, you see if you look closely you'll see that the regular A321 Nios have  less galley space in the back than the A321 Nios LRs.  That's because JetBlue ordered their regular A321 Nios with fewer ovens because they  don't need them.  There are no hot meals on transcon flights, so when you substitute the LRs with regular  Nios you end up with too few ovens to offer hot meals to all passengers which is why I assume  they decided to just offer cold meals on all flights across the Atlantic.  JetBlue has said this change is not temporary but I do think they will keep their options  open.  If passenger satisfaction does not decline too much they might keep it this way.  If the A321 Nios LRs and later XLRs come into service maybe they'll go back to hot  meals.  All we know right now is that the free Wi-Fi, the snack bar, the beverage selection, the  pre-landing snack all that will stay the same.  Only the main meal will now have a cold main dish as opposed to a hot main dish which  I would argue in the grand scheme of things is much less of a quality decline that some  people made it out to be.  While I love the concept of the meal I had and it's disappointing to see it change I would  say that even with a cold main course, the overall experience flying transatlantic with  JetBlue is a good one.  Very good in fact.  They offer a superb value for money at the moment and their service is almost over  the top for the length of their flights.  After all JetBlue only connects the very northeast of North America with the very west of  Europe so their transatlantic flights are comparably short anyway ranging in the roughly  six hours eastbound and seven hours westbound.  So with everything we saw in experience then my endless monologues we had finally made  it to New York's John of Kennedy International Airport.  One underrated advantage of flying JetBlue into JFK is that you arrive in Terminal 5 which  at this time of day is a breeze to go through immigration at taking me less than 10 minutes  today.  I hope you enjoyed another one of our hopelessly long and egregiously detailed flight reviews.  If that's exactly what you're longing for make sure you are subscribed to our channel  as we have plenty more where that came from.  Special thanks to Kishi once again for letting me use his JetBlue credit to all of our fantastic  channel sponsors who through their financial contributions help us dedicate more time and  resources to this channel and every single one of you for watching InstaKillaround until  the end.  Of course thank you to Holtscam for sponsoring this video, go to Holtscam.com slash simply  and use coupon code aviation for 15% of your order.  I will see you again for a new video next week and until then, safe travels.  And go get yourself a calendar for 2025.

chapters.title: Why does Brisbane need a metro?

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Brisbane! When we think of a metro, we often associate it with rapid transit train systems like the Sydney Metro, London Underground, or Singapore's MRT. Today, Brisbane is launching its own metro, though it's not what you might expect from the name. Let's go and take a closer look! Since September 2000, Brisbane has developed a Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) network, mainly through the construction of dedicated busways that run separately from regular traffic. These exclusive corridors have enhanced the efficiency and reliability of bus services, encouraging more residents to opt for public transportation. As a result, the city’s bus infrastructure quickly reached capacity in a number of areas and has led to congestion on some bus routes and at key interchanges. To address this, in 2016, the Brisbane City Council proposed the Brisbane Metro. Initially, the plan was to convert the busway from Woolloongabba to Herston into a track-based, rubber-tyred underground metro system similar to the Paris Metro. However, by March 2017, while keeping the same name, the project shifted to using high-capacity bi-articulated buses on the existing busway, reducing costs by $500 million. And this becomes the Brisbane Metro we see today! The first stage of the Metro consists of two routes covering 21 kilometres. Metro 1 will replace bus routes 111 and 160, connecting Eight Mile Plains to Roma Street with 11 stations. Metro 2 has 12 stops and will replace route 66, linking the Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital to the University of Queensland. The system will utilise the existing busways and was initially designed to offer turn-up-and-go services with three-minute intervals during peak times, though this was later scaled back to every five minutes. Full services for Metro 1 and Metro 2 are expected to commence by the end of the year. Today, Brisbane Metro is having a soft launch, running between UQ Lakes and Eight Mile Plains, replacing some regular buses on route 169. The 60 buses ordered for Brisbane Metro are built by the Swiss manufacturer HESS and are similar to the models operating in Basel, Switzerland, and Nantes, France. Each bus has three large double doors for efficient boarding, including one automated on-request ramp access at the first passenger door. Before we hop on board, do you know what this is for? Brisbane Metro buses are battery-electric and rely on charging facilities to operate. This is one of the end-of-route flash charging locations on the network, where each bus uses a pantograph that autonomously connects to the charger, recharging the bus in just six minutes. At the Rochedale Metro depot, slower overnight chargers are used to enhance battery lifespan and optimise energy efficiency. At 24.7 metres long, each bus can carry 150 passengers in comfort mode or up to 170 in event mode. There are three accessible spaces at the front with next stop audio and hearing loops in all compartments. As you'd expect from a modern bus, there are WiFi and USB charging ports throughout, along with real-time travel information screens. Brisbane-born actress Melanie Zanetti provides the voice for Brisbane Metro. The expected cost to deliver Brisbane Metro is $1.4 billion. It will reduce around 125 buses from the CBD during the morning peak while maintaining passenger capacity. Route 169 serves nine stations. Thanks to the dedicated busway, what typically takes 28 minutes by car in regular traffic only took 20 minutes on the metro. Overall, I found the ride enjoyable. It's more flexible than a tram line while offering similar capacity, making it the next best alternative to the original rubber-tyred metro design. Given that most people associate "metro" with trains, I do believe names such as Brisbane Electric Rapid Transit (BERT) would be more fitting for this new public transport option. Thank you so much for watching! If you find this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more train and flight reviews. See you all in my next video!
